"""
Purpose: Implement advanced search capabilities across catalog
"""

class SearchField(Enum):
    """Searchable fields"""
    TABLE_NAME = "table_name"
    COLUMN_NAME = "column_name"
    DESCRIPTION = "description"
    OWNER = "owner"
    TAG = "tag"
    ALL = "all"


@dataclass
class SearchResult:
    """Represents a search result"""
    asset_id: str
    asset_type: str
    name: str
    description: str
    relevance_score: float
    matched_fields: List[str]
    metadata: Dict[str, Any]


class CatalogSearchEngine:
    """
    Implements the Catalog Search Pattern
    Provides advanced search capabilities
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.catalog_index: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
        self.inverted_index: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
    
    def index_asset(
        self,
        asset_id: str,
        asset_type: str,
        name: str,
        description: str = "",
        columns: Optional[List[str]] = None,
        tags: Optional[Dict[str, str]] = None,
        metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None
    ):
        """
        Index an asset for searching
        
        Args:
            asset_id: Unique asset identifier
            asset_type: Type of asset (table, view, etc.)
            name: Asset name
            description: Asset description
            columns: List of column names
            tags: Asset tags
            metadata: Additional metadata
        """
        asset_data = {
            'asset_id': asset_id,
            'asset_type': asset_type,
            'name': name,
            'description': description,
            'columns': columns or [],
            'tags': tags or {},
            'metadata': metadata or {},
            'indexed_at': datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        self.catalog_index[asset_id] = asset_data
        
        # Build inverted index
        self._update_inverted_index(asset_id, name, 'name')
        self._update_inverted_index(asset_id, description, 'description')
        
        for column in (columns or []):
            self._update_inverted_index(asset_id, column, 'column')
        
        for tag_key, tag_value in (tags or {}).items():
            self._update_inverted_index(asset_id, f"{tag_key}:{tag_value}", 'tag')
        
        print(f"📇 Indexed asset: {asset_id}")
    
    def _update_inverted_index(
        self,
        asset_id: str,
        text: str,
        field_type: str
    ):
        """Update inverted index with tokenized text"""
        if not text:
            return
        
        # Simple tokenization
        tokens = self._tokenize(text)
        
        for token in tokens:
            key = f"{field_type}:{token}"
            if key not in self.inverted_index:
                self.inverted_index[key] = []
            if asset_id not in self.inverted_index[key]:
                self.inverted_index[key].append(asset_id)
    
    def _tokenize(self, text: str) -> List[str]:
        """Tokenize text for indexing"""
        # Convert to lowercase and split
        text = text.lower()
        # Remove special characters except underscore
        text = ''.join(c if c.isalnum() or c in [' ', '_'] else ' ' for c in text)
        # Split and filter
        tokens = [t.strip() for t in text.split() if len(t.strip()) > 2]
        return tokens
    
    def search(
        self,
        query: str,
        search_fields: List[SearchField] = None,
        filters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
        limit: int = 10
    ) -> List[SearchResult]:
        """
        Search catalog assets
        
        Args:
            query: Search query string
            search_fields: Fields to search in
            filters: Additional filters (asset_type, tags, etc.)
            limit: Maximum results to return
            
        Returns:
            List of SearchResult objects
        """
        print(f"🔍 Searching for: '{query}'")
        
        if search_fields is None:
            search_fields = [SearchField.ALL]
        
        # Tokenize query
        query_tokens = self._tokenize(query)
        
        # Find matching assets
        candidate_assets = set()
        matched_fields = {}
        
        for token in query_tokens:
            # Search in different fields
            if SearchField.ALL in search_fields or SearchField.TABLE_NAME in search_fields:
                key = f"name:{token}"
                if key in self.inverted_index:
                    for asset_id in self.inverted_index[key]:
                        candidate_assets.add(asset_id)
                        matched_fields.setdefault(asset_id, []).append('name')
            
            if SearchField.ALL in search_fields or SearchField.DESCRIPTION in search_fields:
                key = f"description:{token}"
                if key in self.inverted_index:
                    for asset_id in self.inverted_index[key]:
                        candidate_assets.add(asset_id)
                        matched_fields.setdefault(asset_id, []).append('description')
            
            if SearchField.ALL in search_fields or SearchField.COLUMN_NAME in search_fields:
                key = f"column:{token}"
                if key in self.inverted_index:
                    for asset_id in self.inverted_index[key]:
                        candidate_assets.add(asset_id)
                        matched_fields.setdefault(asset_id, []).append('column')
            
            if SearchField.ALL in search_fields or SearchField.TAG in search_fields:
                key = f"tag:{token}"
                if key in self.inverted_index:
                    for asset_id in self.inverted_index[key]:
                        candidate_assets.add(asset_id)
                        matched_fields.setdefault(asset_id, []).append('tag')
        
        # Score and rank results
        results = []
        for asset_id in candidate_assets:
            if asset_id not in self.catalog_index:
                continue
            
            asset = self.catalog_index[asset_id]
            
            # Apply filters
            if filters:
                if 'asset_type' in filters and asset['asset_type'] != filters['asset_type']:
                    continue
                if 'tags' in filters:
                    asset_tags = asset.get('tags', {})
                    filter_tags = filters['tags']
                    if not all(asset_tags.get(k) == v for k, v in filter_tags.items()):
                        continue
            
            # Calculate relevance score
            score = self._calculate_relevance_score(
                query_tokens,
                asset,
                matched_fields.get(asset_id, [])
            )
            
            result = SearchResult(
                asset_id=asset_id,
                asset_type=asset['asset_type'],
                name=asset['name'],
                description=asset['description'],
                relevance_score=score,
                matched_fields=list(set(matched_fields.get(asset_id, []))),
                metadata=asset.get('metadata', {})
            )
            
            results.append(result)
        
        # Sort by relevance score
        results.sort(key=lambda x: x.relevance_score, reverse=True)
        
        print(f"✓ Found {len(results)} results")
        return results[:limit]
    
    def _calculate_relevance_score(
        self,
        query_tokens: List[str],
        asset: Dict[str, Any],
        matched_fields: List[str]
    ) -> float:
        """Calculate relevance score for search result"""
        score = 0.0
        
        # Field weights
        field_weights = {
            'name': 10.0,
            'column': 5.0,
            'description': 3.0,
            'tag': 2.0
        }
        
        # Score based on matched fields
        for field in matched_fields:
            score += field_weights.get(field, 1.0)
        
        # Bonus for exact matches
        name_lower = asset['name'].lower()
        query_lower = ' '.join(query_tokens)
        
        if query_lower in name_lower:
            score += 20.0
        
        # Bonus for multiple token matches
        token_matches = sum(1 for token in query_tokens if token in name_lower)
        score += token_matches * 2.0
        
        return score
    
    def faceted_search(
        self,
        query: str,
        facets: List[str] = None
    )
```python
    def faceted_search(
        self,
        query: str,
        facets: List[str] = None
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Perform faceted search with aggregations
        
        Args:
            query: Search query
            facets: List of facet fields (asset_type, owner, tags, etc.)
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with search results and facet counts
        """
        if facets is None:
            facets = ['asset_type', 'tags']
        
        # Get base search results
        results = self.search(query, limit=1000)
        
        # Calculate facets
        facet_counts = {}
        
        for facet in facets:
            facet_counts[facet] = {}
            
            for result in results:
                asset = self.catalog_index.get(result.asset_id, {})
                
                if facet == 'asset_type':
                    value = asset.get('asset_type', 'unknown')
                    facet_counts[facet][value] = facet_counts[facet].get(value, 0) + 1
                
                elif facet == 'tags':
                    tags = asset.get('tags', {})
                    for tag_key, tag_value in tags.items():
                        tag_str = f"{tag_key}:{tag_value}"
                        facet_counts[facet][tag_str] = facet_counts[facet].get(tag_str, 0) + 1
                
                elif facet in asset.get('metadata', {}):
                    value = asset['metadata'][facet]
                    facet_counts[facet][value] = facet_counts[facet].get(value, 0) + 1
        
        return {
            'results': results[:10],  # Return top 10
            'total_results': len(results),
            'facets': facet_counts
        }
    
    def suggest_completions(
        self,
        partial_query: str,
        field: SearchField = SearchField.TABLE_NAME,
        limit: int = 5
    ) -> List[str]:
        """
        Suggest query completions based on partial input
        
        Args:
            partial_query: Partial query string
            field: Field to search for completions
            limit: Maximum suggestions to return
            
        Returns:
            List of suggested completions
        """
        partial_lower = partial_query.lower()
        suggestions = set()
        
        field_prefix = {
            SearchField.TABLE_NAME: 'name',
            SearchField.COLUMN_NAME: 'column',
            SearchField.DESCRIPTION: 'description',
            SearchField.TAG: 'tag'
        }.get(field, 'name')
        
        # Search inverted index for matching tokens
        for key in self.inverted_index.keys():
            if key.startswith(f"{field_prefix}:"):
                token = key.split(':', 1)[1]
                if token.startswith(partial_lower):
                    suggestions.add(token)
        
        # Also search asset names directly
        for asset in self.catalog_index.values():
            if field == SearchField.TABLE_NAME:
                name = asset['name'].lower()
                if name.startswith(partial_lower):
                    suggestions.add(asset['name'])
            elif field == SearchField.COLUMN_NAME:
                for column in asset.get('columns', []):
                    if column.lower().startswith(partial_lower):
                        suggestions.add(column)
        
        return sorted(list(suggestions))[:limit]
    
    def advanced_search(
        self,
        criteria: Dict[str, Any]
    ) -> List[SearchResult]:
        """
        Perform advanced search with multiple criteria
        
        Args:
            criteria: Dictionary with search criteria
                {
                    'query': str,
                    'asset_type': str,
                    'columns_contain': List[str],
                    'has_tags': Dict[str, str],
                    'created_after': str,
                    'owner': str
                }
        
        Returns:
            List of SearchResult objects
        """
        print(f"🔍 Advanced search with {len(criteria)} criteria")
        
        # Start with all assets
        candidate_assets = set(self.catalog_index.keys())
        
        # Apply text query if provided
        if 'query' in criteria and criteria['query']:
            text_results = self.search(criteria['query'], limit=1000)
            query_assets = {r.asset_id for r in text_results}
            candidate_assets &= query_assets
        
        # Filter by asset type
        if 'asset_type' in criteria:
            type_assets = {
                asset_id for asset_id, asset in self.catalog_index.items()
                if asset['asset_type'] == criteria['asset_type']
            }
            candidate_assets &= type_assets
        
        # Filter by columns
        if 'columns_contain' in criteria:
            required_columns = set(criteria['columns_contain'])
            column_assets = {
                asset_id for asset_id, asset in self.catalog_index.items()
                if required_columns.issubset(set(asset.get('columns', [])))
            }
            candidate_assets &= column_assets
        
        # Filter by tags
        if 'has_tags' in criteria:
            required_tags = criteria['has_tags']
            tag_assets = {
                asset_id for asset_id, asset in self.catalog_index.items()
                if all(asset.get('tags', {}).get(k) == v 
                      for k, v in required_tags.items())
            }
            candidate_assets &= tag_assets
        
        # Filter by owner
        if 'owner' in criteria:
            owner_assets = {
                asset_id for asset_id, asset in self.catalog_index.items()
                if asset.get('metadata', {}).get('owner') == criteria['owner']
            }
            candidate_assets &= owner_assets
        
        # Build results
        results = []
        for asset_id in candidate_assets:
            asset = self.catalog_index[asset_id]
            
            result = SearchResult(
                asset_id=asset_id,
                asset_type=asset['asset_type'],
                name=asset['name'],
                description=asset['description'],
                relevance_score=1.0,  # Could calculate based on criteria match
                matched_fields=['advanced_criteria'],
                metadata=asset.get('metadata', {})
            )
            results.append(result)
        
        print(f"✓ Found {len(results)} assets matching criteria")
        return results
    
    def export_search_index(self) -> DataFrame:
        """Export search index as DataFrame"""
        if not self.catalog_index:
            schema = StructType([
                StructField("asset_id", StringType(), True),
                StructField("asset_type", StringType(), True),
                StructField("name", StringType(), True),
                StructField("description", StringType(), True),
                StructField("column_count", IntegerType(), True),
                StructField("indexed_at", StringType(), True)
            ])
            return self.spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
        
        index_data = []
        for asset_id, asset in self.catalog_index.items():
            index_data.append({
                'asset_id': asset_id,
                'asset_type': asset['asset_type'],
                'name': asset['name'],
                'description': asset['description'],
                'column_count': len(asset.get('columns', [])),
                'tag_count': len(asset.get('tags', {})),
                'indexed_at': asset['indexed_at']
            })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(index_data)

This comprehensive PySpark program implements all 6 Data Catalog Integration Patterns with the following features:

## **Pattern 1: Catalog Synchronization**
- Extracts metadata from source catalogs
- Synchronizes across different catalog types (Hive, Glue, Unity)
- Supports full, schema-only, and properties-only sync modes
- Tracks synchronization history

## **Pattern 2: Catalog Discovery**
- Automatically discovers datasets in specified paths
- Supports multiple file
```python
## **Pattern 2: Catalog Discovery** (continued)
- Automatically discovers datasets in specified paths
- Supports multiple file formats (Parquet, CSV, JSON, ORC)
- Infers schema and partitioning information
- Auto-registers discovered assets
- Generates discovery reports

## **Pattern 3: Catalog Metadata**
- Manages technical, business, quality, and usage metadata
- Enriches catalog with business context
- Calculates data quality metrics (completeness, validity)
- Tracks ownership and classification
- Exports comprehensive metadata catalogs

## **Pattern 4: Catalog Lineage**
- Tracks data lineage across transformations
- Builds lineage graphs with upstream/downstream relationships
- Supports impact analysis for change management
- Records transformation logic and dependencies
- Visualizes data flow through the pipeline

## **Pattern 5: Catalog Tagging**
- Implements flexible tagging system with categories
- Supports bulk tagging operations
- Enables tag-based search and filtering
- Creates tag hierarchies
- Provides tag usage statistics

## **Pattern 6: Catalog Search**
- Advanced search with relevance scoring

# ============================================================================
# CONFIGURATION AND CUSTOMIZATION
# ============================================================================

class CatalogConfig:
    """
    Configuration class for catalog integration patterns
    Allows customization of behavior across all patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        # Synchronization settings
        self.sync_batch_size = 100
        self.sync_retry_attempts = 3
        self.sync_timeout_seconds = 300
        
        # Discovery settings
        self.discovery_max_depth = 5
        self.discovery_file_size_limit_mb = 1000
        self.discovery_sample_size = 1000
        
        # Metadata settings
        self.metadata_cache_ttl_seconds = 3600
        self.metadata_quality_threshold = 0.95
        self.metadata_profiling_enabled = True
        
        # Lineage settings
        self.lineage_max_depth = 10
        self.lineage_track_column_level = False
        self.lineage_store_transformations = True
        
        # Tagging settings
        self.tagging_max_tags_per_asset = 50
        self.tagging_allow_duplicates = False
        self.tagging_enforce_hierarchy = True
        
        # Search settings
        self.search_max_results = 100
        self.search_min_score_threshold = 0.1
        self.search_enable_fuzzy = True
        self.search_fuzzy_distance = 2
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Export configuration as dictionary"""
        return {k: v for k, v in self.__dict__.items() 
                if not k.startswith('_')}
    
    @classmethod
    def from_dict(cls, config_dict: Dict[str, Any]) -> 'CatalogConfig':
        """Create configuration from dictionary"""
        config = cls()
        for key, value in config_dict.items():
            if hasattr(config, key):
                setattr(config, key, value)
        return config
    
    def validate(self) -> List[str]:
        """Validate configuration settings"""
        errors = []
        
        if self.sync_batch_size <= 0:
            errors.append("sync_batch_size must be positive")
        
        if self.discovery_max_depth <= 0:
            errors.append("discovery_max_depth must be positive")
        
        if not 0 <= self.metadata_quality_threshold <= 1:
            errors.append("metadata_quality_threshold must be between 0 and 1")
        
        if self.search_fuzzy_distance < 0:
            errors.append("search_fuzzy_distance must be non-negative")
        
        return errors

class CatalogMetrics:
    """
    Collects and reports metrics across all catalog patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.metrics = {
            'synchronization': {
                'total_syncs': 0,
                'successful_syncs': 0,
                'failed_syncs': 0,
                'avg_sync_time_ms': 0
            },
            'discovery': {
                'total_discoveries': 0,
                'assets_discovered': 0,
                'avg_discovery_time_ms': 0
            },
            'metadata': {
                'total_enrichments': 0,
                'quality_checks_performed': 0,
                'avg_quality_score': 0
            },
            'lineage': {
                'total_nodes': 0,
                'total_edges': 0,
                'max_depth': 0
            },
            'tagging': {
                'total_tags': 0,
                'unique_tag_keys': 0,
                'assets_tagged': 0
            },
            'search': {
                'total_searches': 0,
                'avg_search_time_ms': 0,
                'avg_results_per_search': 0
            }
        }
        self.start_time = datetime.now()
    
    def record_sync(self, success: bool, duration_ms: float):
        """Record synchronization metrics"""
        self.metrics['synchronization']['total_syncs'] += 1
        if success:
            self.metrics['synchronization']['successful_syncs'] += 1
        else:
            self.metrics['synchronization']['failed_syncs'] += 1
        
        # Update average
        total = self.metrics['synchronization']['total_syncs']
        current_avg = self.metrics['synchronization']['avg_sync_time_ms']
        self.metrics['synchronization']['avg_sync_time_ms'] = \
            (current_avg * (total - 1) + duration_ms) / total
    
    def record_discovery(self, assets_found: int, duration_ms: float):
        """Record discovery metrics"""
        self.metrics['discovery']['total_discoveries'] += 1
        self.metrics['discovery']['assets_discovered'] += assets_found
        
        total = self.metrics['discovery']['total_discoveries']
        current_avg = self.metrics['discovery']['avg_discovery_time_ms']
        self.metrics['discovery']['avg_discovery_time_ms'] = \
            (current_avg * (total - 1) + duration_ms) / total
    
    def record_search(self, results_count: int, duration_ms: float):
        """Record search metrics"""
        self.metrics['search']['total_searches'] += 1
        
        total = self.metrics['search']['total_searches']
        current_avg = self.metrics['search']['avg_search_time_ms']
        self.metrics['search']['avg_search_time_ms'] = \
            (current_avg * (total - 1) + duration_ms) / total
        
        current_results_avg = self.metrics['search']['avg_results_per_search']
        self.metrics['search']['avg_results_per_search'] = \
            (current_results_avg * (total - 1) + results_count) / total
    
    def get_summary(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get metrics summary"""
        uptime = (datetime.now() - self.start_time).total_seconds()
        
        return {
            'uptime_seconds': uptime,
            'metrics': self.metrics,
            'generated_at': datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
    
    def export_metrics(self, spark: SparkSession) -> DataFrame:
        """Export metrics as DataFrame"""
        metrics_data = []
        
        for category, category_metrics in self.metrics.items():
            for metric_name, metric_value in category_metrics.items():
                metrics_data.append({
                    'category': category,
                    'metric_name': metric_name,
                    'metric_value': float(metric_value),
                    'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
                })
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(metrics_data)


class CatalogValidator:
    """
    Validates catalog integrity and consistency
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.validation_results = []
    
    def validate_metadata_completeness(
        self,
        metadata_manager: CatalogMetadataManager
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate metadata completeness"""
        results = {
            'total_assets': len(metadata_manager.metadata_store),
            'missing_owner': 0,
            'missing_description': 0,
            'missing_classification': 0,
            'completeness_score': 0
        }
        
        for table_name, metadata in metadata_manager.metadata_store.items():
            if metadata.business_metadata.get('owner') == 'unknown':
                results['missing_owner'] += 1
            
            if not metadata.business_metadata.get('description') or \
               metadata.business_metadata.get('description') == 'No description':
                results['missing_description'] += 1
            
            if metadata.business_metadata.get('classification') == 'unclassified':
                results['missing_classification'] += 1
        
        # Calculate completeness score
        total_fields = results['total_assets'] * 3  # owner, description, classification
        missing_fields = (results['missing_owner'] + 
                         results['missing_description'] + 
                         results['missing_classification'])
        
        results['completeness_score'] = \
            ((total_fields - missing_fields) / total_fields * 100) if total_fields > 0 else 0
        
        self.validation_results.append({
            'validation_type': 'metadata_completeness',
            'results': results,
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
        })
        
        return results
    
    def validate_lineage_integrity(
        self,
        lineage_tracker: CatalogLineageTracker
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate lineage graph integrity"""
        results = {
            'total_nodes': len(lineage_tracker.nodes),
            'total_edges': len(lineage_tracker.edges),
            'orphaned_nodes': 0,
            'circular_dependencies': 0,
            'integrity_score': 0
        }
        
        # Check for orphaned nodes (no upstream or downstream)
        for node_id, connections in lineage_tracker.lineage_graph.items():
            if not connections['upstream'] and not connections['downstream']:
                results['orphaned_nodes'] += 1
        
        # Check for circular dependencies
        def has_cycle(node_id: str, visited: set, rec_stack: set) -> bool:
            visited.add(node_id)
            rec_stack.add(node_id)
            
            if node_id in lineage_tracker.lineage_graph:
                for downstream_id in lineage_tracker.lineage_graph[node_id]['downstream']:
                    if downstream_id not in visited:
                        if has_cycle(downstream_id, visited, rec_stack):
                            return True
                    elif downstream_id in rec_stack:
                        return True
            
            rec_stack.remove(node_id)
            return False
        
        visited = set()
        for node_id in lineage_tracker.nodes.keys():
            if node_id not in visited:
                if has_cycle(node_id, visited, set()):
                    results['circular_dependencies'] += 1
        
        # Calculate integrity score
        issues = results['orphaned_nodes'] + results['circular_dependencies']
        total_nodes = results['total_nodes']
        results['integrity_score'] = \
            ((total_nodes - issues) / total_nodes * 100) if total_nodes > 0 else 0
        
        self.validation_results.append({
            'validation_type': 'lineage_integrity',
            'results': results,
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
        })
        
        return results
    
    def validate_tag_consistency(
        self,
        tagging_system: CatalogTaggingSystem
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate tag consistency"""
        results = {
            'total_assets': len(tagging_system.tags_store),
            'total_tags': sum(len(tags) for tags in tagging_system.tags_store.values()),
            'duplicate_tags': 0,
            'invalid_categories': 0,
            'consistency_score': 0
        }
        
        valid_categories = {cat.value for cat in TagCategory}
        
        for asset_id, tags in tagging_system.tags_store.items():
            # Check for duplicates
            seen = set()
            for tag in tags:
                tag_key = (tag.key, tag.category.value)
                if tag_key in seen:
                    results['duplicate_tags'] += 1
                seen.add(tag_key)
                
                # Check for invalid categories
                if tag.category.value not in valid_categories:
                    results['invalid_categories'] += 1
        
        # Calculate consistency score
        issues = results['duplicate_tags'] + results['invalid_categories']
        total_tags = results['total_tags']
        results['consistency_score'] = \
            ((total_tags - issues) / total_tags * 100) if total_tags > 0 else 100
        
        self.validation_results.append({
            'validation_type': 'tag_consistency',
            'results': results,
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
        })
        
        return results
    
    def validate_search_index(
        self,
        search_engine: CatalogSearchEngine
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Validate search index integrity"""
        results = {
            'total_indexed_assets': len(search_engine.catalog_index),
            'total_index_entries': len(search_engine.inverted_index),
            'broken_references': 0,
            'index_score': 0
        }
        
        # Check for broken references in inverted index
        for key, asset_ids in search_engine.inverted_index.items():
            for asset_id in asset_ids:
                if asset_id not in search_engine.catalog_index:
                    results['broken_references'] += 1
        
        # Calculate index score
        total_refs = sum(len(refs) for refs in search_engine.inverted_index.values())
        broken = results['broken_references']
        results['index_score'] = \
            ((total_refs - broken) / total_refs * 100) if total_refs > 0 else 100
        
        self.validation_results.append({
            'validation_type': 'search_index',
            'results': results,
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
        })
        
        return results
    
    def generate_validation_report(self, spark: SparkSession) -> DataFrame:
        """Generate comprehensive validation report"""
        if not self.validation_results:
            schema = StructType([
                StructField("validation_type", StringType(), True),
                StructField("score", DoubleType(), True),
                StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True)
            ])
            return spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
        
        report_data = []
        for validation in self.validation_results:
            results = validation['results']
            score_key = [k for k in results.keys() if 'score' in k][0]
            
            report_data.append({
                'validation_type': validation['validation_type'],
                'score': results[score_key],
                'details': json.dumps(results),
                'timestamp': validation['timestamp']
            })
        
        return spark.createDataFrame(report_data)

class CatalogExporter:
    """
    Export catalog data to various formats
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def export_to_json(
        self,
        output_path: str,
        metadata_manager: CatalogMetadataManager,
        tagging_system: CatalogTaggingSystem,
        lineage_tracker: CatalogLineageTracker
    ):
        """Export complete catalog to JSON"""
        catalog_export = {
            'export_metadata': {
                'exported_at': datetime.now().isoformat(),
                'version': '1.0',
                'exporter': 'CatalogExporter'
            },
            'metadata': {},
            'tags': {},
            'lineage': {
                'nodes': {},
                'edges': []
            }
        }
        
        # Export metadata
        for table_name, metadata in metadata_manager.metadata_store.items():
            catalog_export['metadata'][table_name] = {
                'technical': metadata.technical_metadata,
                
```python
                'technical': metadata.technical_metadata,
                'business': metadata.business_metadata,
                'quality': metadata.quality_metadata,
                'usage': metadata.usage_metadata
            }
        
        # Export tags
        for asset_id, tags in tagging_system.tags_store.items():
            catalog_export['tags'][asset_id] = [
                {
                    'key': tag.key,
                    'value': tag.value,
                    'category': tag.category.value,
                    'created_by': tag.created_by,
                    'created_at': tag.created_at
                }
                for tag in tags
            ]
        
        # Export lineage
        for node_id, node in lineage_tracker.nodes.items():
            catalog_export['lineage']['nodes'][node_id] = {
                'node_type': node.node_type,
                'name': node.name,
                'metadata': node.metadata
            }
        
        for edge in lineage_tracker.edges:
            catalog_export['lineage']['edges'].append({
                'source_id': edge.source_id,
                'target_id': edge.target_id,
                'transformation_type': edge.transformation_type,
                'created_at': edge.created_at
            })
        
        # Write to file
        with open(output_path, 'w') as f:
            json.dump(catalog_export, f, indent=2)
        
        print(f"✓ Catalog exported to {output_path}")
    
    def export_to_parquet(
        self,
        output_path: str,
        metadata_manager: CatalogMetadataManager,
        tagging_system: CatalogTaggingSystem
    ):
        """Export catalog to Parquet format"""
        
        # Export metadata
        metadata_df = metadata_manager.export_metadata_catalog()
        metadata_df.write.mode('overwrite').parquet(f"{output_path}/metadata")
        
        # Export tags
        tags_df = tagging_system.export_tags_catalog()
        tags_df.write.mode('overwrite').parquet(f"{output_path}/tags")
        
        print(f"✓ Catalog exported to {output_path} (Parquet)")
    
    def export_to_delta(
        self,
        output_path: str,
        metadata_manager: CatalogMetadataManager,
        tagging_system: CatalogTaggingSystem,
        lineage_tracker: CatalogLineageTracker
    ):
        """Export catalog to Delta Lake format"""
        
        # Export metadata
        metadata_df = metadata_manager.export_metadata_catalog()
        metadata_df.write.format('delta').mode('overwrite') \
            .save(f"{output_path}/metadata")
        
        # Export tags
        tags_df = tagging_system.export_tags_catalog()
        tags_df.write.format('delta').mode('overwrite') \
            .save(f"{output_path}/tags")
        
        # Export lineage
        lineage_df = lineage_tracker.export_lineage_graph()
        lineage_df.write.format('delta').mode('overwrite') \
            .save(f"{output_path}/lineage")
        
        print(f"✓ Catalog exported to {output_path} (Delta)")


class CatalogImporter:
    """
    Import catalog data from various formats
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def import_from_json(
        self,
        input_path: str,
        metadata_manager: CatalogMetadataManager,
        tagging_system: CatalogTaggingSystem,
        lineage_tracker: CatalogLineageTracker
    ):
        """Import complete catalog from JSON"""
        
        with open(input_path, 'r') as f:
            catalog_data = json.load(f)
        
        # Import metadata
        for table_name, metadata_dict in catalog_data.get('metadata', {}).items():
            enriched = EnrichedMetadata(
                technical_metadata=metadata_dict['technical'],
                business_metadata=metadata_dict['business'],
                quality_metadata=metadata_dict['quality'],
                usage_metadata=metadata_dict['usage']
            )
            metadata_manager.metadata_store[table_name] = enriched
        
        # Import tags
        for asset_id, tags_list in catalog_data.get('tags', {}).items():
            for tag_dict in tags_list:
                tag = Tag(
                    key=tag_dict['key'],
                    value=tag_dict['value'],
                    category=TagCategory(tag_dict['category']),
                    created_by=tag_dict['created_by'],
                    created_at=tag_dict['created_at']
                )
                if asset_id not in tagging_system.tags_store:
                    tagging_system.tags_store[asset_id] = []
                tagging_system.tags_store[asset_id].append(tag)
        
        # Import lineage
        lineage_data = catalog_data.get('lineage', {})
        
        for node_id, node_dict in lineage_data.get('nodes', {}).items():
            node = LineageNode(
                node_id=node_id,
                node_type=node_dict['node_type'],
                name=node_dict['name'],
                metadata=node_dict['metadata']
            )
            lineage_tracker.nodes[node_id] = node
            lineage_tracker.lineage_graph[node_id] = {'upstream': [], 'downstream': []}
        
        for edge_dict in lineage_data.get('edges', []):
            edge = LineageEdge(
                source_id=edge_dict['source_id'],
                target_id=edge_dict['target_id'],
                transformation_type=edge_dict['transformation_type'],
                created_at=edge_dict['created_at']
            )
            lineage_tracker.edges.append(edge)
            
            # Update graph
            source_id = edge.source_id
            target_id = edge.target_id
            if source_id in lineage_tracker.lineage_graph:
                lineage_tracker.lineage_graph[source_id]['downstream'].append(target_id)
            if target_id in lineage_tracker.lineage_graph:
                lineage_tracker.lineage_graph[target_id]['upstream'].append(source_id)
        
        print(f"✓ Catalog imported from {input_path}")
    
    def import_from_parquet(
        self,
        input_path: str,
        metadata_manager: CatalogMetadataManager,
        tagging_system: CatalogTaggingSystem
    ):
        """Import catalog from Parquet format"""
        
        # Import metadata
        metadata_df = self.spark.read.parquet(f"{input_path}/metadata")
        print(f"✓ Imported {metadata_df.count()} metadata entries")
        
        # Import tags
        tags_df = self.spark.read.parquet(f"{input_path}/tags")
        print(f"✓ Imported {tags_df.count()} tags")
        
        print(f"✓ Catalog imported from {input_path} (Parquet)")

class CatalogMonitor:
    """
    Monitor catalog health and trigger alerts
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, config: CatalogConfig):
        self.spark = spark
        self.config = config
        self.alerts = []
    
    def check_metadata_quality(
        self,
        metadata_manager: CatalogMetadataManager
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Check metadata quality and generate alerts"""
        alerts = []
        
        for table_name, metadata in metadata_manager.metadata_store.items():
            quality_metrics = metadata.quality_metadata
            
            # Check completeness
            if 'completeness' in quality_metrics:
                for column, completeness_pct in quality_metrics['completeness'].items():
                    if completeness_pct < self.config.metadata_quality_threshold * 100:
                        alerts.append({
                            'severity': 'WARNING',
                            'type': 'LOW_COMPLETENESS',
                            'table': table_name,
                            'column': column,
                            'value': completeness_pct,
                            'threshold': self.config.metadata_quality_threshold * 100,
                            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
                        })
            
            # Check validity
            if 'validity' in quality_metrics:
                for rule, validity_pct in quality_metrics['validity'].items():
                    if isinstance(validity_pct, (int, float)) and \
                       validity_pct < self.config.metadata_quality_threshold * 100:
                        alerts.append({
                            'severity': 'ERROR',
                            'type': 'VALIDATION_FAILURE',
                            'table': table_name,
                            'rule': rule,
                            'value': validity_pct,
                            'threshold': self.config.metadata_quality_threshold * 100,
                            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
                        })
        
        self.alerts.extend(alerts)
        return alerts
    
    def check_lineage_health(
        self,
        lineage_tracker: CatalogLineageTracker
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Check lineage graph health"""
        alerts = []
        
        # Check for orphaned nodes
        for node_id, connections in lineage_tracker.lineage_graph.items():
            if not connections['upstream'] and not connections['downstream']:
                node = lineage_tracker.nodes.get(node_id)
                alerts.append({
                    'severity': 'WARNING',
                    'type': 'ORPHANED_NODE',
                    'node_id': node_id,
                    'node_name': node.name if node else 'unknown',
                    'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
                })
        
        # Check lineage depth
        for node_id in lineage_tracker.nodes.keys():
            upstream = lineage_tracker.get_upstream_lineage(node_id)
            if len(upstream) > self.config.lineage_max_depth:
                alerts.append({
                    'severity': 'INFO',
                    'type': 'DEEP_LINEAGE',
                    'node_id': node_id,
                    'depth': len(upstream),
                    'max_depth': self.config.lineage_max_depth,
                    'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
                })
        
        self.alerts.extend(alerts)
        return alerts
    
    def check_tag_compliance(
        self,
        tagging_system: CatalogTaggingSystem,
        required_tags: List[str]
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Check tag compliance"""
        alerts = []
        
        for asset_id, tags in tagging_system.tags_store.items():
            tag_keys = {tag.key for tag in tags}
            
            # Check for required tags
            missing_tags = set(required_tags) - tag_keys
            if missing_tags:
                alerts.append({
                    'severity': 'WARNING',
                    'type': 'MISSING_REQUIRED_TAGS',
                    'asset_id': asset_id,
                    'missing_tags': list(missing_tags),
                    'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
                })
            
            # Check tag limits
            if len(tags) > self.config.tagging_max_tags_per_asset:
                alerts.append({
                    'severity': 'WARNING',
                    'type': 'EXCESSIVE_TAGS',
                    'asset_id': asset_id,
                    'tag_count': len(tags),
                    'max_allowed': self.config.tagging_max_tags_per_asset,
                    'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat()
                })
        
        self.alerts.extend(alerts)
        return alerts
    
    def get_alert_summary(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get alert summary"""
        if not self.alerts:
            return {
                'total_alerts': 0,
                'by_severity': {},
                'by_type': {}
            }
        
        by_severity = {}
        by_type = {}
        
        for alert in self.alerts:
            severity = alert['severity']
            alert_type = alert['type']
            
            by_severity[severity] = by_severity.get(severity, 0) + 1
            by_type[alert_type] = by_type.get(alert_type, 0) + 1
        
        return {
            'total_alerts': len(self.alerts),
            'by_severity': by_severity,
            'by_type': by_type,
            'latest_alerts': self.alerts[-5:]  # Last 5 alerts
        }
    
    def export_alerts(self) -> DataFrame:
        """Export alerts as DataFrame"""
        if not self.alerts:
            schema = StructType([
                StructField("severity", StringType(), True),
                StructField("type", StringType(), True),
                StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True)
            ])
            return self.spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(self.alerts)

class GovernancePolicy(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for governance policies"""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def evaluate(self, asset_metadata: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """
        Evaluate policy against asset metadata
        Returns: (compliant, reason)
        """
        pass


class PIIDetectionPolicy(GovernancePolicy):
    """Policy to detect and flag PII data"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.pii_patterns = [
            r'email',
            r'ssn',
            r'social_security',
            r'phone',
            r'credit_card',
            r'passport',
            r'driver_license',
            r'address',
            r'date_of_birth',
            r'dob'
        ]
    
    def evaluate(self, asset_metadata: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Check if asset contains PII columns"""
        import re
        
        columns = asset_metadata.get('columns', [])
        pii_columns = []
        
        for column in columns:
            column_lower = column.lower()
            for pattern in self.pii_patterns:
                if re.search(pattern, column_lower):
                    pii_columns.append(column)
                    break
        
        if pii_columns:
            return False, f"PII detected in columns: {', '.join(pii_columns)}"
        
        return True, "No PII detected"


class DataClassificationPolicy(GovernancePolicy):
    """Policy to enforce data classification"""
    
    def __init__(self, required_classification: bool = True):
        self.required_classification = required_classification
        self.valid_classifications = ['public', 'internal', 'confidential', 'restricted']
    
    def evaluate(self, asset_metadata: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Check if asset has valid classification"""
        classification = asset_metadata.get('classification', '').lower()
        
        if self.required_classification and not classification:
            return False, "Classification is required but missing"
        
        if classification and classification not in self.valid_classifications:
            return False, f"Invalid classification: {classification}"
        
```python

            return False, f"Invalid classification: {classification}"
        
        return True, f"Valid classification: {classification}"


class OwnershipPolicy(GovernancePolicy):
    """Policy to enforce asset ownership"""
    
    def __init__(self, required_owner: bool = True, valid_teams: List[str] = None):
        self.required_owner = required_owner
        self.valid_teams = valid_teams or []
    
    def evaluate(self, asset_metadata: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Check if asset has valid owner"""
        owner = asset_metadata.get('owner', '').lower()
        
        if self.required_owner and (not owner or owner == 'unknown'):
            return False, "Owner is required but missing"
        
        if self.valid_teams and owner not in [t.lower() for t in self.valid_teams]:
            return False, f"Owner '{owner}' not in valid teams: {self.valid_teams}"
        
        return True, f"Valid owner: {owner}"


class RetentionPolicy(GovernancePolicy):
    """Policy to enforce data retention rules"""
    
    def __init__(self, max_age_days: int = 365):
        self.max_age_days = max_age_days
    
    def evaluate(self, asset_metadata: Dict[str, Any]) -> Tuple[bool, str]:
        """Check if asset exceeds retention period"""
        created_time = asset_metadata.get('created_time', '')
        
        if not created_time:
            return True, "Creation time not available"
        
        try:
            created_date = datetime.fromisoformat(created_time.replace('Z', '+00:00'))
            age_days = (datetime.now() - created_date).days
            
            if age_days > self.max_age_days:
                return False, f"Asset age ({age_days} days) exceeds retention policy ({self.max_age_days} days)"
            
            return True, f"Asset age ({age_days} days) within retention policy"
        
        except Exception as e:
            return True, f"Could not evaluate retention: {str(e)}"


class CatalogGovernanceEngine:
    """
    Engine to enforce governance policies across catalog
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.policies: List[GovernancePolicy] = []
        self.policy_results = []
    
    def add_policy(self, policy: GovernancePolicy):
        """Add a governance policy"""
        self.policies.append(policy)
        print(f"✓ Added policy: {policy.__class__.__name__}")
    
    def evaluate_asset(
        self,
        asset_id: str,
        asset_metadata: Dict[str, Any]
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Evaluate all policies against an asset"""
        results = {
            'asset_id': asset_id,
            'evaluated_at': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'compliant': True,
            'policy_results': []
        }
        
        for policy in self.policies:
            compliant, reason = policy.evaluate(asset_metadata)
            
            policy_result = {
                'policy': policy.__class__.__name__,
                'compliant': compliant,
                'reason': reason
            }
            
            results['policy_results'].append(policy_result)
            
            if not compliant:
                results['compliant'] = False
        
        self.policy_results.append(results)
        return results
    
    def evaluate_catalog(
        self,
        metadata_manager: CatalogMetadataManager,
        tagging_system: CatalogTaggingSystem
    ) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """Evaluate all policies across entire catalog"""
        print(f"\n🔍 Evaluating {len(self.policies)} policies across catalog...")
        
        all_results = []
        
        for table_name, metadata in metadata_manager.metadata_store.items():
            # Combine metadata and tags
            asset_metadata = {
                'columns': list(metadata.technical_metadata.get('schema', {}).keys()),
                'classification': metadata.business_metadata.get('classification', ''),
                'owner': metadata.business_metadata.get('owner', ''),
                'created_time': metadata.technical_metadata.get('created_time', ''),
                'tags': {}
            }
            
            # Add tags
            if table_name in tagging_system.tags_store:
                for tag in tagging_system.tags_store[table_name]:
                    asset_metadata['tags'][tag.key] = tag.value
            
            # Evaluate policies
            result = self.evaluate_asset(table_name, asset_metadata)
            all_results.append(result)
        
        # Print summary
        compliant_count = sum(1 for r in all_results if r['compliant'])
        total_count = len(all_results)
        
        print(f"✓ Evaluation complete: {compliant_count}/{total_count} assets compliant")
        
        return all_results
    
    def get_compliance_report(self) -> DataFrame:
        """Generate compliance report"""
        if not self.policy_results:
            schema = StructType([
                StructField("asset_id", StringType(), True),
                StructField("compliant", BooleanType(), True),
                StructField("policy_count", IntegerType(), True),
                StructField("evaluated_at", StringType(), True)
            ])
            return self.spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
        
        report_data = []
        for result in self.policy_results:
            failed_policies = [p['policy'] for p in result['policy_results'] if not p['compliant']]
            
            report_data.append({
                'asset_id': result['asset_id'],
                'compliant': result['compliant'],
                'total_policies': len(result['policy_results']),
                'failed_policies': ', '.join(failed_policies) if failed_policies else 'None',
                'evaluated_at': result['evaluated_at']
            })
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(report_data)

class CatalogAutomation:
    """
    Automate catalog operations on schedule
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, config: CatalogConfig):
        self.spark = spark
        self.config = config
        self.scheduled_jobs = []
        self.job_history = []
    
    def schedule_discovery(
        self,
        base_path: str,
        schedule: str = "daily",
        auto_register: bool = True
    ):
        """Schedule automatic dataset discovery"""
        job = {
            'job_id': f"discovery_{len(self.scheduled_jobs)}",
            'job_type': 'discovery',
            'schedule': schedule,
            'config': {
                'base_path': base_path,
                'auto_register': auto_register
            },
            'created_at': datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        self.scheduled_jobs.append(job)
        print(f"✓ Scheduled discovery job: {job['job_id']}")
    
    def schedule_metadata_refresh(
        self,
        tables: List[str],
        schedule: str = "hourly"
    ):
        """Schedule metadata refresh"""
        job = {
            'job_id': f"metadata_refresh_{len(self.scheduled_jobs)}",
            'job_type': 'metadata_refresh',
            'schedule': schedule,
            'config': {
                'tables': tables
            },
            'created_at': datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        self.scheduled_jobs.append(job)
        print(f"✓ Scheduled metadata refresh job: {job['job_id']}")
    
    def schedule_quality_checks(
        self,
        quality_rules: Dict[str, Dict[str, str]],
        schedule: str = "daily"
    ):
        """Schedule data quality checks"""
        job = {
            'job_id': f"quality_check_{len(self.scheduled_jobs)}",
            'job_type': 'quality_check',
            'schedule': schedule,
            'config': {
                'quality_rules': quality_rules
            },
            'created_at': datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        self.scheduled_jobs.append(job)
        print(f"✓ Scheduled quality check job: {job['job_id']}")
    
    def schedule_compliance_scan(
        self,
        policies: List[str],
        schedule: str = "weekly"
    ):
        """Schedule compliance scanning"""
        job = {
            'job_id': f"compliance_scan_{len(self.scheduled_jobs)}",
            'job_type': 'compliance_scan',
            'schedule': schedule,
            'config': {
                'policies': policies
            },
            'created_at': datetime.now().isoformat()
        }
        
        self.scheduled_jobs.append(job)
        print(f"✓ Scheduled compliance scan job: {job['job_id']}")
    
    def execute_job(self, job_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Execute a scheduled job"""
        job = next((j for j in self.scheduled_jobs if j['job_id'] == job_id), None)
        
        if not job:
            return {'status': 'error', 'message': f"Job {job_id} not found"}
        
        execution_result = {
            'job_id': job_id,
            'job_type': job['job_type'],
            'started_at': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'status': 'running'
        }
        
        try:
            # Simulate job execution
            print(f"⚙️  Executing job: {job_id} ({job['job_type']})")
            
            # Job-specific logic would go here
            if job['job_type'] == 'discovery':
                print(f"   Discovering datasets in {job['config']['base_path']}")
            elif job['job_type'] == 'metadata_refresh':
                print(f"   Refreshing metadata for {len(job['config']['tables'])} tables")
            elif job['job_type'] == 'quality_check':
                print(f"   Running quality checks")
            elif job['job_type'] == 'compliance_scan':
                print(f"   Scanning for compliance")
            
            execution_result['status'] = 'success'
            execution_result['completed_at'] = datetime.now().isoformat()
            
        except Exception as e:
            execution_result['status'] = 'failed'
            execution_result['error'] = str(e)
            execution_result['completed_at'] = datetime.now().isoformat()
        
        self.job_history.append(execution_result)
        return execution_result
    
    def get_job_status(self) -> DataFrame:
        """Get status of all scheduled jobs"""
        if not self.scheduled_jobs:
            schema = StructType([
                StructField("job_id", StringType(), True),
                StructField("job_type", StringType(), True),
                StructField("schedule", StringType(), True),
                StructField("created_at", StringType(), True)
            ])
            return self.spark.createDataFrame([], schema)
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(self.scheduled_jobs)

"""
Platform Abstraction Pattern
Provides a unified interface for different storage platforms (HDFS, S3, Azure Blob, Local)
"""

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from typing import Dict, Any, Optional
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class StoragePlatform(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for storage platforms"""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def read_data(self, path: str, format: str = "parquet", **options) -> DataFrame:
        """Read data from storage platform"""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def write_data(self, df: DataFrame, path: str, format: str = "parquet", 
                   mode: str = "overwrite", **options) -> None:
        """Write data to storage platform"""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def list_files(self, path: str) -> list:
        """List files in the given path"""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def delete_path(self, path: str) -> bool:
        """Delete path from storage"""
        pass


class HDFSPlatform(StoragePlatform):
    """HDFS Storage Platform Implementation"""
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, namenode: str = "hdfs://namenode:9000"):
        self.spark = spark
        self.namenode = namenode
        logger.info(f"Initialized HDFS Platform with namenode: {namenode}")
    
    def read_data(self, path: str, format: str = "parquet", **options) -> DataFrame:
        full_path = f"{self.namenode}{path}"
        logger.info(f"Reading from HDFS: {full_path}")
        return self.spark.read.format(format).options(**options).load(full_path)
    
    def write_data(self, df: DataFrame, path: str, format: str = "parquet", 
                   mode: str = "overwrite", **options) -> None:
        full_path = f"{self.namenode}{path}"
        logger.info(f"Writing to HDFS: {full_path}")
        df.write.format(format).mode(mode).options(**options).save(full_path)
    
    def list_files(self, path: str) -> list:
        full_path = f"{self.namenode}{path}"
        hadoop_conf = self.spark._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
        fs = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(
            self.spark._jvm.java.net.URI(self.namenode), hadoop_conf
        )
        file_path = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(full_path)
        files = fs.listStatus(file_path)
        return [str(f.getPath()) for f in files]
    
    def delete_path(self, path: str) -> bool:
        full_path = f"{self.namenode}{path}"
        logger.info(f"Deleting from HDFS: {full_path}")
        hadoop_conf = self.spark._jsc.hadoopConfiguration()
        fs = self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.FileSystem.get(
            self.spark._jvm.java.net.URI(self.namenode), hadoop_conf
        )
        return fs.delete(self.spark._jvm.org.apache.hadoop.fs.Path(full_path), True)

class LocalPlatform(StoragePlatform):
    """Local File System Platform Implementation"""
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, base_path: str = "/tmp"):
        self.spark = spark
        self.base_path = base_path
        logger.info(f"Initialized Local Platform with base path: {base_path}")
    
    def read_data(self, path: str, format: str = "parquet", **options) -> DataFrame:
        full_path = f"file://{self.base_path}/{path.lstrip('/')}"
        logger.info(f"Reading from Local FS: {full_path}")
        return self.spark.read.format(format).options(**options).load(full_path)
    
    def write_data(self, df: DataFrame, path: str, format: str = "parquet", 
                   mode: str = "overwrite", **options) -> None:
        full_path = f"file://{self.base_path}/{path.lstrip('/')}"
        logger.info(f"Writing to Local FS: {full_path}")
        df.write.format(format).mode(mode).options(**options).save(full_path)
    
    def list_files(self, path: str) -> list:
        import os
        full_path = f"{self.base_path}/{path.lstrip('/')}"
        if os.path.exists(full_path):
            return [os.path.join(full_path, f) for f in os.listdir(full_path)]
        return []
    
    def delete_path(self, path: str) -> bool:
        import shutil
        full_path = f"{self.base_path}/{path.lstrip('/')}"
        logger.info(f"Deleting from Local FS: {full_path}")
        try:
            if os.path.isdir(full_path):
                shutil.rmtree(full_path)
            else:
                os.remove(full_path)
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Error deleting path: {e}")
            return False

    ]

    # Use different platforms interchangeably
    platforms = {
        "local": LocalPlatform(spark, "/tmp/data"),
        # "hdfs": HDFSPlatform(spark),
        # "s3": S3Platform(spark, "my-bucket"),
        # "azure": AzureBlobPlatform(spark, "myaccount", "mycontainer")
    }
    
    # Write to all platforms using the same interface
    for platform_name, platform in platforms.items():
        logger.info(f"\n--- Using {platform_name} platform ---")
        
        # Write data
        platform.write_data(df, "employees/data", format="parquet")
        
        # Read data back
        read_df = platform.read_data("employees/data", format="parquet")
        read_df.show()
        
        # List files
        files = platform.list_files("employees/data")
        logger.info(f"Files: {files}")
    
    spark.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    platform_abstraction_example()

## 2. Adapter Pattern (Refined)

```python
"""
Adapter Pattern
Adapts different data source formats to a unified DataFrame interface
"""

from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType
import json
import xml.etree.ElementTree as ET


class DataSourceAdapter(ABC):
    """Abstract adapter for different data sources"""
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    @abstractmethod
    def read(self, source: str, schema: Optional[StructType] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """Read data from source and return DataFrame"""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def validate(self, source: str) -> bool:
        """Validate if the source can be read"""
        pass


class CSVAdapter(DataSourceAdapter):
    """Adapter for CSV files"""
    
    def read(self, source: str, schema: Optional[StructType] = None) -> DataFrame:
        logger.info(f"Reading CSV from: {source}")
        
        options = {
            "header": "true",
            "inferSchema": "true" if schema is None else "false"
        }
        
        reader = self.spark.read.options(**options)
        
        if schema:
            reader = reader.schema(schema)
        
        return reader.csv(source)
    
    def validate(self, source: str) -> bool:
        try:
            # Try to read first row
            self.spark.read.option("header", "true").csv(source).limit(1).count()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"CSV validation failed: {e}")
            return False


class JSONAdapter(DataSourceAdapter):
    """Adapter for JSON files"""
    
    def read(self, source: str, schema: Optional[StructType] = None) -> DataFrame:
        logger.info(f"Reading JSON from: {source}")
        
        reader = self.spark.read
        
        if schema:
            reader = reader.schema(schema)
        
        return reader.json(source)
    
    def validate(self, source: str) -> bool:
        try:
            self.spark.read.json(source).limit(1).count()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"JSON validation failed: {e}")
            return False


class ParquetAdapter(DataSourceAdapter):
    """Adapter for Parquet files"""
    
    def read(self, source: str, schema: Optional[StructType] = None) -> DataFrame:
        logger.info(
```python
        logger.info(f"Reading Parquet from: {source}")
        
        # Parquet has embedded schema, but we can still apply schema if needed
        reader = self.spark.read
        
        if schema:
            reader = reader.schema(schema)
        
        return reader.parquet(source)
    
    def validate(self, source: str) -> bool:
        try:
            self.spark.read.parquet(source).limit(1).count()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Parquet validation failed: {e}")
            return False


class AvroAdapter(DataSourceAdapter):
    """Adapter for Avro files"""
    
    def read(self, source: str, schema: Optional[StructType] = None) -> DataFrame:
        logger.info(f"Reading Avro from: {source}")
        
        reader = self.spark.read.format("avro")
        
        if schema:
            reader = reader.schema(schema)
        
        return reader.load(source)
    
    def validate(self, source: str) -> bool:
        try:
            self.spark.read.format("avro").load(source).limit(1).count()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Avro validation failed: {e}")
            return False


class XMLAdapter(DataSourceAdapter):
    """Adapter for XML files"""
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, row_tag: str = "row"):
        super().__init__(spark)
        self.row_tag = row_tag
    
    def read(self, source: str, schema: Optional[StructType] = None) -> DataFrame:
        logger.info(f"Reading XML from: {source}")
        
        reader = self.spark.read \
            .format("com.databricks.spark.xml") \
            .option("rowTag", self.row_tag)
        
        if schema:
            reader = reader.schema(schema)
        
        return reader.load(source)
    
    def validate(self, source: str) -> bool:
        try:
            self.spark.read \
                .format("com.databricks.spark.xml") \
                .option("rowTag", self.row_tag) \
                .load(source).limit(1).count()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"XML validation failed: {e}")
            return False


class DatabaseAdapter(DataSourceAdapter):
    """Adapter for JDBC database sources"""
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, jdbc_url: str, 
                 properties: Dict[str, str]):
        super().__init__(spark)
        self.jdbc_url = jdbc_url
        self.properties = properties
    
    def read(self, source: str, schema: Optional[StructType] = None) -> DataFrame:
        """Source parameter is the table name for database adapter"""
        logger.info(f"Reading from database table: {source}")
        
        return self.spark.read \
            .jdbc(url=self.jdbc_url, 
                  table=source, 
                  properties=self.properties)
    
    def validate(self, source: str) -> bool:
        try:
            self.spark.read \
                .jdbc(url=self.jdbc_url, 
                      table=f"(SELECT * FROM {source} LIMIT 1) AS tmp", 
                      properties=self.properties).count()
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Database validation failed: {e}")
            return False


class DataSourceFactory:
    """Factory to create appropriate adapters based on source type"""
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_adapter(spark: SparkSession, source_type: str, 
                      **kwargs) -> DataSourceAdapter:
        """Create appropriate adapter based on source type"""
        
        adapters = {
            "csv": CSVAdapter,
            "json": JSONAdapter,
            "parquet": ParquetAdapter,
            "avro": AvroAdapter,
            "xml": XMLAdapter,
            "database": DatabaseAdapter
        }
        
        adapter_class = adapters.get(source_type.lower())
        
        if not adapter_class:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported source type: {source_type}")
        
        if adapter_class == DatabaseAdapter:
            return adapter_class(spark, **kwargs)
        elif adapter_class == XMLAdapter:
            return adapter_class(spark, kwargs.get("row_tag", "row"))
        else:
            return adapter_class(spark)


class UnifiedDataReader:
    """Unified interface to read from multiple data sources"""
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.adapters: Dict[str, DataSourceAdapter] = {}
    
    def register_adapter(self, name: str, adapter: DataSourceAdapter):
        """Register a custom adapter"""
        self.adapters[name] = adapter
        logger.info(f"Registered adapter: {name}")
    
    def read(self, source: str, source_type: str, 
             schema: Optional[StructType] = None, **kwargs) -> DataFrame:
        """Read data using appropriate adapter"""
        
        # Check if adapter is already registered
        if source_type not in self.adapters:
            adapter = DataSourceFactory.create_adapter(
                self.spark, source_type, **kwargs
            )
            self.adapters[source_type] = adapter
        
        adapter = self.adapters[source_type]
        
        # Validate source
        if not adapter.validate(source):
            raise ValueError(f"Source validation failed: {source}")
        
        # Read data
        return adapter.read(source, schema)


# Example Usage
def adapter_pattern_example():
    """Example demonstrating Adapter Pattern"""
    
    spark = SparkSession.builder \
        .appName("AdapterPattern") \
        .config("spark.jars.packages", "com.databricks:spark-xml_2.12:0.14.0") \
        .getOrCreate()
    
    # Create unified data reader
    reader = UnifiedDataReader(spark)
    
    # Create sample data in different formats
    sample_data = [
        (1, "Alice", 30, 75000.0),
        (2, "Bob", 35, 85000.0),
        (3, "Charlie", 28, 70000.0)
    ]
    df = spark.createDataFrame(sample_data, ["id", "name", "age", "salary"])
    
    # Write to different formats
    df.write.mode("overwrite").csv("/tmp/data/employees.csv", header=True)
    df.write.mode("overwrite").json("/tmp/data/employees.json")
    df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet("/tmp/data/employees.parquet")
    
    # Read from different sources using unified interface
    logger.info("\n--- Reading CSV ---")
    csv_df = reader.read("/tmp/data/employees.csv", "csv")
    csv_df.show()
    
    logger.info("\n--- Reading JSON ---")
    json_df = reader.read("/tmp/data/employees.json", "json")
    json_df.show()
    
    logger.info("\n--- Reading Parquet ---")
    parquet_df = reader.read("/tmp/data/employees.parquet", "parquet")
    parquet_df.show()
    
    # All DataFrames have the same interface regardless of source
    for df_name, df_obj in [("CSV", csv_df), ("JSON", json_df), ("Parquet", parquet_df)]:
        logger.info(f"\n{df_name} Schema:")
        df_obj.printSchema()
        logger.info(f"{df_name} Count: {df_obj.count()}")
    
    spark.stop()


if __name__ == "__main__":
    adapter_pattern_example()
