# Example 2: Custom Adapter for Proprietary Format
class CustomFormatAdapter(DataSourceAdapter):
    """Adapter for custom data format"""
    
    def read(self, source: str, schema: Optional[StructType] = None) -> DataFrame:
        logger.info(f"Reading custom format from: {source}")
        
        # Implement custom parsing logic
        # This is a simplified example
        rdd = self.spark.sparkContext.textFile(source)
        
        # Parse custom format
        def parse_line(line):
            # Your custom parsing logic
            parts = line.split("|")
            return tuple(parts)
        
        parsed_rdd = rdd.map(parse_line)
        
        if schema:
            return self.spark.createDataFrame(parsed_rdd, schema)
        else:
            return self.spark.createDataFrame(parsed_rdd)
    
    def validate(self, source: str) -> bool:
        try:
            # Implement validation logic
            self.spark.sparkContext.textFile(source).take(1)
            return True
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"Validation failed: {e}")
            return False


# Example 3: Custom Transformation with Bridge Pattern
class CustomTransformationProcessor(DataProcessor):
    """Custom business logic processor"""
    
    def __init__(self, platform: ExecutionPlatform, config: Dict[str, Any]):
        super().__init__(platform)
        self.config = config
    
    def process(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        logger.info("Applying custom business transformations")
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, udf
        from pyspark.sql.types import StringType
        
        # Custom UDF
        @udf(returnType=StringType())
        def custom_logic(value):
            # Your custom business logic
            return f"processed_{value}"
        
        # Apply transformations based on config
        result = df
        
        if self.config.get("apply_filter"):
            result = result.filter(col(self.config["filter_column"]) > self.config["filter_value"])
        
        if self.config.get("apply_enrichment"):
            result = result.withColumn(
                self.config["new_column"],
                custom_logic(col(self.config["source_column"]))
            )
        
        if self.config.get("apply_aggregation"):
            result = result.groupBy(self.config["group_columns"]) \
                .agg(self.config["agg_expressions"])
        
        return result


# Example 4: Multi-Cloud Disaster Recovery
class MultiCloudDisasterRecovery:
    """Advanced disaster recovery across multiple clouds"""
    
    def __init__(self, data_lake: CloudAgnosticDataLake):
        self.data_lake = data_lake
        self.recovery_points: Dict[str, List[Dict[str, Any]]] = {}
    
    def create_recovery_point(self, dataset_name: str, 
                             df: DataFrame,
                             locations: List[StorageLocation],
                             metadata: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None):
        """Create a recovery point across multiple clouds"""
        
        import datetime
        timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()
        
        recovery_point = {
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "record_count": df.count(),
            "schema": df.schema.json(),
            "locations": [],
            "metadata": metadata or {}
        }
        
        # Write to all locations
        for location in locations:
            try:
                # Add timestamp to path for versioning
                versioned_location = StorageLocation(
                    provider=location.provider,
                    bucket_or_container=location.bucket_or_container,
                    path=f"{location.path}/{timestamp}",
                    region=location.region
                )
                
                self.data_lake.write(df, versioned_location)
                
                recovery_point["locations"].append({
                    "provider": location.provider.value,
                    "path": versioned_location.get_full_path(),
                    "status": "success"
                })
                
                logger.info(f"Created recovery point on {location.provider.value}")
                
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"Failed to create recovery point on {location.provider.value}: {e}")
                recovery_point["locations"].append({
                    "provider": location.provider.value,
                    "status": "failed",
                    "error": str(e)
                })
        
        # Store recovery point metadata
        if dataset_name not in self.recovery_points:
            self.recovery_points[dataset_name] = []
        
        self.recovery_points[dataset_name].append(recovery_point)
        
        return recovery_point
    
    def list_recovery_points(self, dataset_name: str) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """List all recovery points for a dataset"""
        return self.recovery_points.get(dataset_name, [])
    
    def restore_from_recovery_point(self, dataset_name: str,
                                   timestamp: str,
                                   target_location: StorageLocation) -> DataFrame:
        """Restore data from a specific recovery point"""
        
        recovery_points = self.recovery_points.get(dataset_name, [])
        recovery_point = next(
            (rp for rp in recovery_points if rp["timestamp"] == timestamp),
            None
        )
        
        if not recovery_point:
            raise ValueError(f"Recovery point not found: {timestamp}")
        
        # Try to restore from each location until successful
        for location_info in recovery_point["locations"]:
            if location_info["status"] != "success":
                continue
            
            try:
                # Parse the location
                provider = CloudProvider(location_info["provider"])
                path = location_info["path"]
                
                # Create temporary location object
                temp_location = StorageLocation(
                    provider=provider,
                    bucket_or_container="",  # Extracted from path
                    path=path
                )
                
                # Read from recovery point
                df = self.data_lake.read(temp_location)
                
                # Write to target location
                self.data_lake.write(df, target_location)
                
                logger.info(f"Successfully restored from {provider.value}")
                return df
                
            except Exception as e:
                logger.warning(f"Failed to restore from {location_info['provider']}: {e}")
                continue
        
        raise Exception("Failed to restore from any recovery point location")

class CrossPlatformBenchmark:
    """Benchmark performance across different platforms"""
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.results: List[Dict[str, Any]] = []
    
    def benchmark_read(self, platforms: Dict[str, StoragePlatform],
                      path: str, iterations: int = 3) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Benchmark read operations across platforms"""
        
        import time
        
        results = {}
        
        for platform_name, platform in platforms.items():
            timings = []
            
            for i in range(iterations):
                start_time = time.time()
                df = platform.read_data(path)
                count = df.count()  # Force execution
                end_time = time.time()
                
                timings.append(end_time - start_time)
                logger.info(f"{platform_name} iteration {i+1}: {timings[-1]:.3f}s")
            
            results[platform_name] = {
                "avg_time": sum(timings) / len(timings),
                "min_time": min(timings),
                "max_time": max(timings),
                "record_count": count
            }
        
        self.results.append({
            "operation": "read",
            "path": path,
            "results": results
        })
        
        return results
    
    def benchmark_write(self, platforms: Dict[str, StoragePlatform],
                       df: DataFrame, base_path: str,
                       iterations: int = 3) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Benchmark write operations across platforms"""
        
        import time
        
        results = {}
        
        for platform_name, platform in platforms.items():
            timings = []
            
            for i in range(iterations):
                path = f"{base_path}/iteration_{i}"
                
                start_time = time.time()
                platform.write_data(df, path)
                end_time = time.time()
                
                timings.append(end_time - start_time)
                logger.info(f"{platform_name} iteration {i+1}: {timings[-1]:.3f}s")
            
            results[platform_name] = {
                "avg_time": sum(timings) / len(timings),
                "min_time": min(timings),
                "max_time": max(timings),
                "record_count": df.count()
            }
        
        self.results.append({
            "operation": "write",
            "base_path": base_path,
            "results": results
        })
        
        return results
    
    def generate_report(self) -> str:
        """Generate benchmark report"""
        
        report = "CROSS-PLATFORM BENCHMARK REPORT\n"
        report += "=" * 80 + "\n\n"
        
        for result in self.results:
            report += f"Operation: {result['operation'].upper()}\n"
            report += f"Path: {result.get('path', result.get('base_path'))}\n\n"
            
            for platform, metrics in result['results'].items():
                report += f"  {platform}:\n"
                report += f"    Average Time: {metrics['avg_time']:.3f}s\n"
                report += f"    Min Time: {metrics['min_time']:.3f}s\n"
                report += f"    Max Time: {metrics['max_time']:.3f}s\n"
                report += f"    Records: {metrics['record_count']}\n\n"
        
        return report

# Example 6: Cross-Platform Data Lineage Tracker
class DataLineageTracker:
    """Track data lineage across platforms and transformations"""
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.lineage_graph: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
    
    def record_read(self, dataset_id: str, 
                   source_location: StorageLocation,
                   timestamp: str = None):
        """Record a read operation"""
        
        import datetime
        if timestamp is None:
            timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()
        
        if dataset_id not in self.lineage_graph:
            self.lineage_graph[dataset_id] = {
                "operations": [],
                "sources": [],
                "targets": []
            }
        
        self.lineage_graph[dataset_id]["operations"].append({
            "type": "read",
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "location": {
                "provider": source_location.provider.value,
                "path": source_location.get_full_path()
            }
        })
        
        self.lineage_graph[dataset_id]["sources"].append({
            "provider": source_location.provider.value,
            "path": source_location.get_full_path()
        })
    
    def record_transformation(self, dataset_id: str,
                            transformation_name: str,
                            input_datasets: List[str],
                            parameters: Optional[Dict[str, Any]] = None,
                            timestamp: str = None):
        """Record a transformation operation"""
        
        import datetime
        if timestamp is None:
            timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()
        
        if dataset_id not in self.lineage_graph:
            self.lineage_graph[dataset_id] = {
                "operations": [],
                "sources": [],
                "targets": []
            }
        
        self.lineage_graph[dataset_id]["operations"].append({
            "type": "transformation",
            "name": transformation_name,
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "inputs": input_datasets,
            "parameters": parameters or {}
        })
    
    def record_write(self, dataset_id: str,
                    target_location: StorageLocation,
                    record_count: int,
                    timestamp: str = None):
        """Record a write operation"""
        
        import datetime
        if timestamp is None:
            timestamp = datetime.datetime.now().isoformat()
        
        if dataset_id not in self.lineage_graph:
            self.lineage_graph[dataset_id] = {
                "operations": [],
                "sources": [],
                "targets": []
            }
        
        self.lineage_graph[dataset_id]["operations"].append({
            "type": "write",
            "timestamp": timestamp,
            "location": {
                "provider": target_location.provider.value,
                "path": target_location.get_full_path()
            },
            "record_count": record_count
        })
        
        self.lineage_graph[dataset_id]["targets"].append({
            "provider": target_location.provider.value,
            "path": target_location.get_full_path(),
            "record_count": record_count
        })
    
    def get_lineage(self, dataset_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get complete lineage for a dataset"""
        return self.lineage_graph.get(dataset_id, {})
    
    def trace_upstream(self, dataset_id: str) -> List[str]:
        """Trace all upstream datasets"""
        
        upstream = set()
        to_process = [dataset_id]
        
        while to_process:
            current = to_process.pop(0)
            lineage = self.lineage_graph.get(current, {})
            
            for operation in lineage.get("operations", []):
                if operation["type"] == "transformation":
                    for input_dataset in operation.get("inputs", []):
                        if input_dataset not in upstream:
                            upstream.add(input_dataset)
                            to_process.append(input_dataset)
        
        return list(upstream)
    
    def trace_downstream(self, dataset_id: str) -> List[str]:
        """Trace all downstream datasets"""
        
        downstream = set()
        
        for ds_id, lineage in self.lineage_graph.items():
            for operation in lineage.get("operations", []):
                if operation["type"] == "transformation":
                    if dataset_id in operation.get("inputs", []):
                        downstream.add(ds_id)
        
        return list(downstream)
    
    def export_lineage_graph(self, format: str = "json") -> str:
        """Export lineage graph in specified format"""
        
        if format == "json":
            import json
            return json.dumps(self.lineage_graph, indent=2)
        
        elif format == "dot":
            # Generate GraphViz DOT format
            dot = "digraph lineage {\n"
            dot += "  rankdir=LR;\n"
            dot += "  node [shape=box];\n\n"
            
            for dataset_id, lineage in self.lineage_graph.items():
                for operation in lineage.get("operations", []):
                    if operation["type"] == "transformation":
                        for input_dataset in operation.get("inputs", []):
                            dot += f'  "{input_dataset}" -> "{dataset_id}" [label="{operation["name"]}"];\n'
            
            dot += "}\n"
            return dot
        
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unsupported format: {format}")

        )
    ]
    
    recovery_point = dr_manager.create_recovery_point(
        "employees_raw",
        employees_df,
        recovery_locations,
        metadata={"purpose": "initial_backup", "team": "data_engineering"}
    )

    # Step 3: Complex transformation with lineage
    logger.info("\nStep 3: Performing transformations with lineage tracking")
    
    # Read source data
    lineage_tracker.record_read("employees_raw", employees_location)
    lineage_tracker.record_read("departments_raw", departments_location)
    
    employees_read = spark.read.parquet(employees_location.path)
    departments_read = spark.read.parquet(departments_location.path)
    
    # Transformation 1: Filter and enrich employees
    from pyspark.sql.functions import col, when, upper
    
    enriched_employees = employees_read.filter(col("salary") > 65000) \
        .withColumn(
            "salary_band",
            when(col("salary") >= 80000, "High")
            .when(col("salary") >= 70000, "Medium")
            .otherwise("Low")
        ) \
        .withColumn("name_upper", upper(col("name")))
    
    lineage_tracker.record_transformation(
        "employees_enriched",

        }
    )
    
    # Transformation 2: Join with departments
    joined_df = enriched_employees.join(

    )

        "employees_with_departments",
        "join_departments",

            "join_type": "inner",
            "join_key": "department"
        }
    )
    
    # Transformation 3: Aggregate by department
    from pyspark.sql.functions import avg, count as spark_count, max as spark_max
    
    department_summary = joined_df.groupBy("department", "location", "manager") \
        .agg(
            spark_count("id").alias("employee_count"),
            avg("salary").alias("avg_salary"),
            spark_max("salary").alias("max_salary"),
            avg("age").alias("avg_age")
        )
    
    lineage_tracker.record_transformation(
        "department_summary",
        "aggregate_by_department",

    # Step 5: Display results

class ConfigurationManager:
    """Manage configurations for cross-platform deployments"""
    
    def __init__(self, environment: str = "development"):
        self.environment
```python
        self.environment = environment
        self.configs: Dict[str, Any] = {}
        self._load_default_configs()
    
    def _load_default_configs(self):
        """Load default configurations based on environment"""
        
        base_config = {
            "spark": {
                "app_name": "CrossPlatformApp",
                "master": "local[*]",
                "shuffle_partitions": 200,
                "dynamic_allocation": True
            },
            "storage": {
                "default_format": "parquet",
                "compression": "snappy",
                "write_mode": "overwrite"
            },
            "quality": {
                "enable_validation": True,
                "enable_profiling": True,
                "null_threshold": 0.1,
                "duplicate_threshold": 0.05
            },
            "performance": {
                "cache_enabled": True,
                "broadcast_threshold": 10485760,  # 10MB
                "adaptive_query_enabled": True
            },
            "monitoring": {
                "log_level": "INFO",
                "metrics_enabled": True,
                "alert_on_failure": True
            }
        }
        
        # Environment-specific overrides
        if self.environment == "production":
            production_overrides = {
                "spark": {
                    "master": "yarn",
                    "shuffle_partitions": 400,
                    "executor_memory": "8g",
                    "executor_cores": 4
                },
                "storage": {
                    "compression": "gzip"
                },
                "monitoring": {
                    "log_level": "WARN",
                    "alert_on_failure": True,
                    "send_notifications": True
                }
            }
            self._deep_merge(base_config, production_overrides)
        
        elif self.environment == "staging":
            staging_overrides = {
                "spark": {
                    "master": "yarn",
                    "shuffle_partitions": 200,
                    "executor_memory": "4g"
                },
                "monitoring": {
                    "log_level": "INFO"
                }
            }
            self._deep_merge(base_config, staging_overrides)
        
        self.configs = base_config
    
    def _deep_merge(self, base: Dict, override: Dict):
        """Deep merge override dict into base dict"""
        for key, value in override.items():
            if key in base and isinstance(base[key], dict) and isinstance(value, dict):
                self._deep_merge(base[key], value)
            else:
                base[key] = value
    
    def get(self, key_path: str, default: Any = None) -> Any:
        """Get configuration value using dot notation"""
        keys = key_path.split(".")
        value = self.configs
        
        for key in keys:
            if isinstance(value, dict) and key in value:
                value = value[key]
            else:
                return default
        
        return value
    
    def set(self, key_path: str, value: Any):
        """Set configuration value using dot notation"""
        keys = key_path.split(".")
        config = self.configs
        
        for key in keys[:-1]:
            if key not in config:
                config[key] = {}
            config = config[key]
        
        config[keys[-1]] = value
    
    def get_spark_configs(self) -> Dict[str, str]:
        """Get Spark-specific configurations"""
        spark_config = self.configs.get("spark", {})
        
        return {
            f"spark.{k}": str(v) 
            for k, v in spark_config.items() 
            if k not in ["app_name", "master"]
        }
    
    def get_platform_config(self, platform: CloudProvider) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Get platform-specific configuration"""
        platform_configs = self.configs.get("platforms", {})
        return platform_configs.get(platform.value, {})
    
    def load_from_file(self, filepath: str):
        """Load configuration from file (JSON or YAML)"""
        import json
        
        with open(filepath, 'r') as f:
            if filepath.endswith('.json'):
                file_config = json.load(f)
            elif filepath.endswith('.yaml') or filepath.endswith('.yml'):
                try:
                    import yaml
                    file_config = yaml.safe_load(f)
                except ImportError:
                    raise ImportError("PyYAML required for YAML config files")
            else:
                raise ValueError(f"Unsupported file format: {filepath}")
        
        self._deep_merge(self.configs, file_config)
    
    def export_config(self, filepath: str):
        """Export current configuration to file"""
        import json
        
        with open(filepath, 'w') as f:
            if filepath.endswith('.json'):
                json.dump(self.configs, f, indent=2)
            elif filepath.endswith('.yaml') or filepath.endswith('.yml'):
                try:
                    import yaml
                    yaml.dump(self.configs, f, default_flow_style=False)
                except ImportError:
                    raise ImportError("PyYAML required for YAML config files")

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from typing import List, Callable
import logging

# Configure logging
logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class DataTransformationChainPatterns:
    """
    Comprehensive implementation of Data Transformation Chain Patterns in PySpark.
    Demonstrates various chaining techniques for data processing pipelines.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, app_name: str = "TransformationChainPatterns"):
        """Initialize Spark Session with optimized configurations."""
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName(app_name) \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        logger.info(f"Spark Session initialized: {app_name}")
    
    def create_sample_data(self):
        """Create sample datasets for demonstration."""
        # Sample e-commerce transaction data
        transactions_data = [
            (1, "John", "Electronics", 1200.50, "2024-01-15", "New York"),
            (2, "Alice", "Clothing", 85.00, "2024-01-16", "California"),
            (3, "Bob", "Electronics", 2500.00, "2024-01-17", "Texas"),
            (4, "Charlie", "Books", 45.50, "2024-01-18", "New York"),
            (5, "Diana", "Electronics", 899.99, "2024-01-19", "California"),
            (6, "Eve", "Clothing", 120.00, "2024-01-20", "Texas"),
            (7, "Frank", "Books", 32.50, "2024-01-21", "New York"),
            (8, "Grace", "Electronics", 1750.00, "2024-01-22", "California"),
            (9, "Henry", "Clothing", 95.00, "2024-01-23", "Texas"),
            (10, "Ivy", "Books", 28.00, "2024-01-24", "New York")
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("transaction_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("customer_name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("category", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("transaction_date", StringType(), False),
            StructField("state", StringType(), False)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(transactions_data, schema)
    
    # ============================================================
    # PATTERN 1: Map Chain Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def map_chain_pattern(self):
        """
        Map Chain Pattern: Apply a series of transformation functions sequentially.
        Each transformation maps the data to a new form.
        
        Use Case: Sequential data enrichment and standardization
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("PATTERN 1: Map Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        # Chain of map transformations
        result = df \
            .withColumn("amount_rounded", round(col("amount"), 2)) \
            .withColumn("customer_upper", upper(col("customer_name"))) \
            .withColumn("category_lower", lower(col("category"))) \
            .withColumn("transaction_year", year(to_date(col("transaction_date")))) \
            .withColumn("transaction_month", month(to_date(col("transaction_date")))) \
            .withColumn("amount_category", 
                when(col("amount") < 50, "Low")
                .when(col("amount") < 500, "Medium")
                .when(col("amount") < 1000, "High")
                .otherwise("Premium")) \
            .withColumn("state_code", 
                when(col("state") == "New York", "NY")
                .when(col("state") == "California", "CA")
                .when(col("state") == "Texas", "TX")
                .otherwise("OTHER"))
        
        logger.info("Map Chain: Applied 7 sequential transformations")
        result.show(5, truncate=False)
        result.printSchema()
        
        return result
    
    # ============================================================
    # PATTERN 2: Filter Chain Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def filter_chain_pattern(self):
        """
        Filter Chain Pattern: Apply multiple filter conditions in sequence.
        Each filter narrows down the dataset progressively.
        
        Use Case: Multi-criteria data filtering and quality checks
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("PATTERN 2: Filter Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        # Progressive filtering chain
        logger.info(f"Initial record count: {df.count()}")
        
        # Filter 1: Amount threshold
        filtered_1 = df.filter(col("amount") > 50)
        logger.info(f"After amount > 50 filter: {filtered_1.count()}")
        
        # Filter 2: Category filter
        filtered_2 = filtered_1.filter(col("category").isin(["Electronics", "Clothing"]))
        logger.info(f"After category filter: {filtered_2.count()}")
        
        # Filter 3: State filter
        filtered_3 = filtered_2.filter(col("state") != "Texas")
        logger.info(f"After state filter: {filtered_3.count()}")
        
        # Filter 4: Date range filter
        filtered_4 = filtered_3.filter(
            to_date(col("transaction_date")) >= lit("2024-01-16")
        )
        logger.info(f"After date filter: {filtered_4.count()}")
        
        # Combined filter chain (alternative approach)
        result = df.filter(
            (col("amount") > 50) &
            (col("category").isin(["Electronics", "Clothing"])) &
            (col("state") != "Texas") &
            (to_date(col("transaction_date")) >= lit("2024-01-16"))
        )
        
        logger.info("Filter Chain: Applied 4 sequential filters")
        result.show(truncate=False)
        
        return result
    
    # ============================================================
    # PATTERN 3: FlatMap Chain Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def flatmap_chain_pattern(self):
        """
        FlatMap Chain Pattern: Transform and explode data in multiple stages.
        Each stage can produce multiple records from single input.
        
        Use Case: Data expansion, tokenization, and multi-level normalization
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("PATTERN 3: FlatMap Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        # Create data with nested structures
        nested_data = [
            (1, "John Doe", "Electronics,Books", ["email", "sms", "push"]),
            (2, "Alice Smith", "Clothing", ["email", "phone"]),
            (3, "Bob Johnson", "Electronics,Clothing,Books", ["sms"])
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("categories", StringType(), False),
            StructField("contact_methods", ArrayType(StringType()), False)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(nested_data, schema)
        
        logger.info("Original Data:")
        df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # FlatMap Chain Stage 1: Split categories
        stage1 = df.withColumn("category", explode(split(col("categories"), ",")))
        logger.info("\nStage 1 - Categories exploded:")
        stage1.show(truncate=False)
        
        # FlatMap Chain Stage 2: Explode contact methods
        stage2 = stage1.withColumn("contact_method", explode(col("contact_methods")))
        logger.info("\nStage 2 - Contact methods exploded:")
        stage2.show(truncate=False)
        
        # FlatMap Chain Stage 3: Generate additional derived records
        stage3 = stage2.withColumn(
            "name_parts", 
            split(col("name"), " ")
        ).withColumn(
            "name_part",
            explode(col("name_parts"))
        )
        
        logger.info("\nStage 3 - Name parts exploded:")
        stage3.select("id", "name", "category", "contact_method", "name_part").show(truncate=False)
        
        return stage3
    
    # ============================================================
    # PATTERN 4: Reduce Chain Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def reduce_chain_pattern(self):
        """
        Reduce Chain Pattern: Progressive aggregation and reduction operations.
        Each stage reduces data dimensionality or aggregates information.
        
        Use Case: Multi-level aggregation and hierarchical summarization
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("PATTERN 4: Reduce Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        logger.info("Original Data:")
        df.show(5)
        
        # Reduction Stage 1: Aggregate by category
        stage1 = df.groupBy("category").agg(
            count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
            max("amount").alias("max_amount"),
            min("amount").alias("min_amount")
        )
        
        logger.info("\nStage 1 - Reduced by category:")
        stage1.show()
        
        # Reduction Stage 2: Further reduce to summary statistics
        stage2 = stage1.agg(
            sum("transaction_count").alias("total_transactions"),
            sum("total_amount").alias("grand_total"),
            avg("avg_amount").alias("overall_avg"),
            max("max_amount").alias("global_max"),
            min("min_amount").alias("global_min"),
            count("*").alias("category_count")
        )
        
        logger.info("\nStage 2 - Overall summary:")
        stage2.show()
        
        # Reduction Stage 3: Multi-dimensional reduction
        stage3 = df.groupBy("state", "category").agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total")
        ).groupBy("state").agg(
            sum("count").alias("total_transactions"),
            sum("total").alias("total_revenue"),
            count("*").alias("category_diversity")
        )
        
        logger.info("\nStage 3 - Multi-dimensional reduction by state:")
        stage3.show()
        
        return stage3
    
    # ============================================================
    # PATTERN 5: Transform Chain Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def transform_chain_pattern(self):
        """
        Transform Chain Pattern: Use DataFrame.transform() for composable transformations.
        Enables reusable transformation functions and clean pipeline composition.
        
        Use Case: Modular, reusable transformation pipelines
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("PATTERN 5: Transform Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        # Define reusable transformation functions
        def add_date_features(df):
            """Add date-related features."""
            return df \
                .withColumn("year", year(to_date(col("transaction_date")))) \
                .withColumn("month", month(to_date(col("transaction_date")))) \
                .withColumn("day_of_week", dayofweek(to_date(col("transaction_date"))))
        
        def add_amount_features(df):
            """Add amount-related features."""
            return df \
                .withColumn("amount_tier", 
                    when(col("amount") < 100, "Tier1")
                    .when(col("amount") < 500, "Tier2")
                    .when(col("amount") < 1000, "Tier3")
                    .otherwise("Tier4")) \
                .withColumn("is_high_value", col("amount") > 1000)
        
        def add_customer_features(df):
            """Add customer-related features."""
            return df \
                .withColumn("customer_initials", 
                    concat(substring(col("customer_name"), 1, 1), lit("."))) \
                .withColumn("name_length", length(col("customer_name")))
        
        def add_location_features(df):
            """Add location-related features."""
            return df \
                .withColumn("region",
                    when(col("state").isin(["New York", "California"]), "Coastal")
                    .otherwise("Inland")) \
                .withColumn("state_abbr",
                    when(col("state") == "New York", "NY")
                    .when(col("state") == "California", "CA")
                    .when(col("state") == "Texas", "TX")
                    .otherwise("OTHER"))
        
        # Apply transformation chain
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        result = df \
            .transform(add_date_features) \
            .transform(add_amount_features) \
            .transform(add_customer_features) \
            .transform(add_location_features)
        
        logger.info("Transform Chain: Applied 4 modular transformation functions")
        result.show(5, truncate=False)
        result.printSchema()
        
        # Demonstrate conditional transformation chain
        def apply_conditional_transforms(df, include_advanced=True):
            """Apply transformations conditionally."""
            df = df.transform(add_date_features)
            df = df.transform(add_amount_features)
            
            if include_advanced:
                df = df.transform(add_customer_features)
                df = df.transform(add_location_features)
            
            return df
        
        logger.info("\nConditional Transform Chain (advanced=False):")
        conditional_result = apply_conditional_transforms(
            self.create_sample_data(), 
            include_advanced=False
        )
        conditional_result.show(3)
        
        return result
    
    # ============================================================
    # PATTERN 6: Multi-Stage Transformation Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def multi_stage_transformation_pattern(self):
        """
        Multi-Stage Transformation Pattern: Complex pipeline with multiple stages
        combining different transformation types (map, filter, reduce, etc.).
        
        Use Case: End-to-end ETL pipelines with quality checks and enrichment
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("PATTERN 6: Multi-Stage Transformation Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        # STAGE 1: Data Validation and Cleaning
        logger.info("\nSTAGE 1: Data Validation and Cleaning")
        stage1 = df \
            .filter(col("amount").isNotNull()) \
            .filter(col("amount") > 0) \
            .filter(col("customer_name").isNotNull()) \
            .withColumn("customer_name", trim(col("customer_name"))) \
            .withColumn("category", trim(col("category")))
        
        logger.info(f"Records
```python
        logger.info(f"Records after validation: {stage1.count()}")
        
        # STAGE 2: Feature Engineering
        logger.info("\nSTAGE 2: Feature Engineering")
        stage2 = stage1 \
            .withColumn("transaction_date_parsed", to_date(col("transaction_date"))) \
            .withColumn("year", year(col("transaction_date_parsed"))) \
            .withColumn("month", month(col("transaction_date_parsed"))) \
            .withColumn("quarter", quarter(col("transaction_date_parsed"))) \
            .withColumn("amount_category",
                when(col("amount") < 50, "Low")
                .when(col("amount") < 500, "Medium")
                .when(col("amount") < 1000, "High")
                .otherwise("Premium")) \
            .withColumn("customer_segment",
                when(col("amount") > 1000, "VIP")
                .when(col("amount") > 500, "Premium")
                .otherwise("Standard"))
        
        stage2.show(5)
        
        # STAGE 3: Aggregation and Metrics
        logger.info("\nSTAGE 3: Aggregation and Metrics")
        stage3 = stage2.groupBy("category", "state", "amount_category").agg(
            count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_revenue"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction"),
            max("amount").alias("max_transaction"),
            min("amount").alias("min_transaction"),
            countDistinct("customer_name").alias("unique_customers")
        )
        
        stage3.show()
        
        # STAGE 4: Enrichment with Window Functions
        logger.info("\nSTAGE 4: Enrichment with Window Functions")
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(col("total_revenue").desc())
        
        stage4 = stage3 \
            .withColumn("rank_by_revenue", rank().over(window_spec)) \
            .withColumn("revenue_percentile", 
                percent_rank().over(window_spec)) \
            .withColumn("cumulative_revenue",
                sum("total_revenue").over(
                    window_spec.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
                ))
        
        stage4.show()
        
        # STAGE 5: Final Filtering and Selection
        logger.info("\nSTAGE 5: Final Filtering and Selection")
        stage5 = stage4 \
            .filter(col("transaction_count") >= 1) \
            .filter(col("total_revenue") > 0) \
            .select(
                "category",
                "state",
                "amount_category",
                "transaction_count",
                round("total_revenue", 2).alias("total_revenue"),
                round("avg_transaction", 2).alias("avg_transaction"),
                "unique_customers",
                "rank_by_revenue",
                round("revenue_percentile", 4).alias("revenue_percentile")
            ) \
            .orderBy(col("total_revenue").desc())
        
        logger.info("Final Result:")
        stage5.show(20, truncate=False)
        
        # STAGE 6: Quality Metrics
        logger.info("\nSTAGE 6: Quality Metrics")
        quality_metrics = {
            "total_records": df.count(),
            "valid_records": stage1.count(),
            "final_aggregated_records": stage5.count(),
            "total_revenue": stage5.agg(sum("total_revenue")).collect()[0][0],
            "categories_processed": stage5.select("category").distinct().count(),
            "states_processed": stage5.select("state").distinct().count()
        }
        
        logger.info("Pipeline Quality Metrics:")
        for metric, value in quality_metrics.items():
            logger.info(f"  {metric}: {value}")
        
        return stage5
    
    # ============================================================
    # Advanced Pattern: Composite Chain Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def composite_chain_pattern(self):
        """
        Composite Chain Pattern: Combines all transformation patterns
        into a comprehensive data processing pipeline.
        
        Use Case: Production-grade ETL with multiple transformation strategies
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("ADVANCED: Composite Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        # Define transformation functions
        def validate_data(df):
            """Validation stage."""
            return df.filter(
                (col("amount") > 0) & 
                (col("customer_name").isNotNull()) &
                (col("category").isNotNull())
            )
        
        def enrich_features(df):
            """Feature enrichment stage."""
            return df \
                .withColumn("date_parsed", to_date(col("transaction_date"))) \
                .withColumn("year_month", date_format(col("date_parsed"), "yyyy-MM")) \
                .withColumn("amount_log", log10(col("amount") + 1)) \
                .withColumn("is_weekend", 
                    dayofweek(col("date_parsed")).isin([1, 7]))
        
        def apply_business_rules(df):
            """Business logic stage."""
            return df \
                .withColumn("discount_eligible",
                    (col("amount") > 1000) | (col("category") == "Electronics")) \
                .withColumn("priority_customer",
                    col("amount") > 500) \
                .withColumn("fraud_risk_score",
                    when(col("amount") > 2000, 0.8)
                    .when(col("amount") > 1000, 0.5)
                    .otherwise(0.1))
        
        def calculate_metrics(df):
            """Metrics calculation stage."""
            from pyspark.sql.window import Window
            
            customer_window = Window.partitionBy("customer_name")
            category_window = Window.partitionBy("category")
            
            return df \
                .withColumn("customer_total_spend",
                    sum("amount").over(customer_window)) \
                .withColumn("customer_transaction_count",
                    count("*").over(customer_window)) \
                .withColumn("category_avg_amount",
                    avg("amount").over(category_window)) \
                .withColumn("amount_vs_category_avg",
                    col("amount") / col("category_avg_amount"))
        
        # Execute composite chain
        result = df \
            .transform(validate_data) \
            .transform(enrich_features) \
            .transform(apply_business_rules) \
            .transform(calculate_metrics)
        
        logger.info("Composite Chain: Applied 4 transformation stages")
        result.show(10, truncate=False)
        
        # Summary statistics
        logger.info("\nSummary Statistics:")
        result.select(
            count("*").alias("total_records"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            avg("fraud_risk_score").alias("avg_fraud_risk"),
            sum(when(col("discount_eligible"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("discount_eligible_count"),
            sum(when(col("priority_customer"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("priority_customer_count")
        ).show()
        
        return result
    
    # ============================================================
    # Performance Optimized Chain Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def optimized_chain_pattern(self):
        """
        Optimized Chain Pattern: Demonstrates performance optimization
        techniques in transformation chains.
        
        Use Case: High-performance data processing with caching and partitioning
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("ADVANCED: Optimized Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        # Cache frequently accessed intermediate results
        logger.info("\nStep 1: Cache base dataset")
        base_df = df \
            .filter(col("amount") > 0) \
            .cache()
        
        logger.info(f"Cached records: {base_df.count()}")
        
        # Optimized transformation with repartitioning
        logger.info("\nStep 2: Optimized transformation chain")
        
        # Repartition by frequently used grouping key
        optimized_df = base_df \
            .repartition(4, "category") \
            .withColumn("processing_date", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("amount_bucket", 
                (col("amount") / 100).cast("int") * 100)
        
        # Perform aggregation on partitioned data
        aggregated = optimized_df.groupBy("category", "amount_bucket").agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total"),
            avg("amount").alias("average")
        )
        
        logger.info("Aggregated results:")
        aggregated.show()
        
        # Broadcast join optimization for small lookup tables
        logger.info("\nStep 3: Broadcast join optimization")
        
        # Create small lookup table
        category_config = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            ("Electronics", 0.15, "High"),
            ("Clothing", 0.10, "Medium"),
            ("Books", 0.05, "Low")
        ], ["category", "commission_rate", "priority"])
        
        # Broadcast join
        from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
        
        enriched = optimized_df.join(
            broadcast(category_config),
            "category",
            "left"
        ).withColumn("commission",
            col("amount") * col("commission_rate"))
        
        enriched.show(5)
        
        # Unpersist cache when done
        base_df.unpersist()
        
        logger.info("\nOptimization complete - cache cleared")
        
        return enriched
    
    # ============================================================
    # Error Handling Chain Pattern
    # ============================================================
    
    def error_handling_chain_pattern(self):
        """
        Error Handling Chain Pattern: Robust transformation chain
        with comprehensive error handling and data quality checks.
        
        Use Case: Production pipelines requiring fault tolerance
        """
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        logger.info("ADVANCED: Error Handling Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        # Create data with potential errors
        error_prone_data = [
            (1, "John", "Electronics", 1200.50, "2024-01-15", "New York"),
            (2, "Alice", "Clothing", -50.00, "2024-01-16", "California"),  # Negative amount
            (3, "Bob", None, 2500.00, "2024-01-17", "Texas"),  # Null category
            (4, "Charlie", "Books", None, "2024-01-18", "New York"),  # Null amount
            (5, None, "Electronics", 899.99, "2024-01-19", "California"),  # Null name
            (6, "Eve", "Clothing", 120.00, "invalid-date", "Texas"),  # Invalid date
            (7, "Frank", "Books", 32.50, "2024-01-21", None),  # Null state
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("transaction_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("customer_name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("category", StringType(), True),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("transaction_date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("state", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(error_prone_data, schema)
        
        logger.info("Original data with errors:")
        df.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Error detection and flagging
        error_flagged = df \
            .withColumn("error_flags", array()) \
            .withColumn("error_flags",
                when(col("customer_name").isNull(), 
                    array_union(col("error_flags"), array(lit("NULL_CUSTOMER"))))
                .otherwise(col("error_flags"))) \
            .withColumn("error_flags",
                when(col("category").isNull(),
                    array_union(col("error_flags"), array(lit("NULL_CATEGORY"))))
                .otherwise(col("error_flags"))) \
            .withColumn("error_flags",
                when(col("amount").isNull(),
                    array_union(col("error_flags"), array(lit("NULL_AMOUNT"))))
                .otherwise(col("error_flags"))) \
            .withColumn("error_flags",
                when(col("amount") < 0,
                    array_union(col("error_flags"), array(lit("NEGATIVE_AMOUNT"))))
                .otherwise(col("error_flags"))) \
            .withColumn("error_flags",
                when(col("state").isNull(),
                    array_union(col("error_flags"), array(lit("NULL_STATE"))))
                .otherwise(col("error_flags"))) \
            .withColumn("has_errors", size(col("error_flags")) > 0)
        
        logger.info("\nData with error flags:")
        error_flagged.select("transaction_id", "customer_name", "amount", "error_flags", "has_errors").show(truncate=False)
        
        # Split into valid and invalid records
        valid_records = error_flagged.filter(~col("has_errors"))
        invalid_records = error_flagged.filter(col("has_errors"))
        
        logger.info(f"\nValid records: {valid_records.count()}")
        logger.info(f"Invalid records: {invalid_records.count()}")
        
        # Process valid records with safe transformations
        processed = valid_records \
            .withColumn("amount_safe", coalesce(col("amount"), lit(0.0))) \
            .withColumn("category_safe", coalesce(col("category"), lit("Unknown"))) \
            .withColumn("state_safe", coalesce(col("state"), lit("Unknown"))) \
            .withColumn("processing_status", lit("SUCCESS"))
        
        logger.info("\nProcessed valid records:")
        processed.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Error summary
        error_summary = invalid_records \
            .withColumn("error_flag", explode(col("error_flags"))) \
            .groupBy("error_flag") \
            .agg(count("*").alias("error_count")) \
            .orderBy(col("error_count").desc())
        
        logger.info("\nError Summary:")
        error_summary.show()
        
        return {
            "valid": processed,
            "invalid": invalid_records,
            "error_summary": error_summary
        }
    
    # ============================================================
    # Main Execution Method
    # ============================================================
    
    def run_all_patterns(self):
        """Execute all transformation chain patterns."""
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 60)
        logger.info("EXECUTING ALL TRANSFORMATION CHAIN PATTERNS")
        logger.info("=" * 60 + "\n")
        
        patterns = [
            ("Map Chain Pattern", self.map_chain_pattern),
            ("Filter Chain Pattern", self.filter_chain_pattern),
            ("FlatMap Chain Pattern", self.flatmap_chain_pattern),
            ("Reduce Chain Pattern", self.reduce_chain_pattern),
            ("Transform Chain Pattern", self.transform_chain_pattern),
            ("Multi-Stage Transformation Pattern", self.multi_stage_transformation_pattern),
            ("Composite Chain Pattern", self.composite_chain_pattern),
```python
            ("Composite Chain Pattern", self.composite_chain_pattern),
            ("Optimized Chain Pattern", self.optimized_chain_pattern),
            ("Error Handling Chain Pattern", self.error_handling_chain_pattern)
        ]
        
        results = {}
        
        for pattern_name, pattern_func in patterns:
            try:
                logger.info(f"\n{'=' * 60}")
                logger.info(f"Executing: {pattern_name}")
                logger.info(f"{'=' * 60}")
                results[pattern_name] = pattern_func()
                logger.info(f"✓ {pattern_name} completed successfully\n")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"✗ {pattern_name} failed: {str(e)}\n")
                results[pattern_name] = None
        
        # Summary report
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 60)
        logger.info("EXECUTION SUMMARY")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        successful = sum(1 for v in results.values() if v is not None)
        total = len(patterns)
        
        logger.info(f"Total Patterns: {total}")
        logger.info(f"Successful: {successful}")
        logger.info(f"Failed: {total - successful}")
        logger.info(f"Success Rate: {(successful/total)*100:.1f}%")
        
        return results
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Clean up Spark session."""
        logger.info("\nCleaning up Spark session...")
        self.spark.stop()
        logger.info("Spark session stopped successfully")


# ============================================================
# Additional Utility Functions for Chain Patterns
# ============================================================

class ChainPatternUtilities:
    """
    Utility functions to support transformation chain patterns.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_transformation_pipeline(transformations: List[Callable]):
        """
        Create a composable transformation pipeline.
        
        Args:
            transformations: List of transformation functions
            
        Returns:
            A single function that applies all transformations in sequence
        """
        def pipeline(df):
            result = df
            for transform in transformations:
                result = result.transform(transform)
            return result
        return pipeline
    
    @staticmethod
    def log_transformation_stats(df, stage_name: str):
        """
        Log statistics for a transformation stage.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to analyze
            stage_name: Name of the transformation stage
        """
        logger.info(f"\n--- {stage_name} Statistics ---")
        logger.info(f"Record Count: {df.count()}")
        logger.info(f"Column Count: {len(df.columns)}")
        logger.info(f"Partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        
        # Show schema
        logger.info("Schema:")
        df.printSchema()
        
        return df
    
    @staticmethod
    def validate_chain_output(df, validations: dict):
        """
        Validate transformation chain output against rules.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to validate
            validations: Dictionary of validation rules
            
        Returns:
            Validation results
        """
        results = {}
        
        for rule_name, rule_func in validations.items():
            try:
                results[rule_name] = rule_func(df)
                logger.info(f"✓ Validation '{rule_name}': PASSED")
            except Exception as e:
                results[rule_name] = False
                logger.error(f"✗ Validation '{rule_name}': FAILED - {str(e)}")
        
        return results

class TransformationChainExamples:
    """
    Real-world examples demonstrating transformation chain patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def customer_360_pipeline(self):
        """
        Example: Customer 360 view using multiple chain patterns.
        
        Combines customer data from multiple sources using various
        transformation chains.
        """
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 60)
        logger.info("EXAMPLE: Customer 360 Pipeline")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        # Sample customer transaction data
        transactions = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1, "C001", "2024-01-15", 150.00, "Electronics"),
            (2, "C001", "2024-01-20", 75.00, "Books"),
            (3, "C002", "2024-01-18", 200.00, "Clothing"),
            (4, "C001", "2024-01-25", 300.00, "Electronics"),
            (5, "C003", "2024-01-22", 50.00, "Books"),
        ], ["transaction_id", "customer_id", "date", "amount", "category"])
        
        # Sample customer profile data
        profiles = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            ("C001", "John Doe", "john@email.com", "2023-01-01", "Gold"),
            ("C002", "Jane Smith", "jane@email.com", "2023-06-15", "Silver"),
            ("C003", "Bob Johnson", "bob@email.com", "2024-01-01", "Bronze"),
        ], ["customer_id", "name", "email", "join_date", "tier"])
        
        # Chain Pattern 1: Aggregate transaction metrics
        transaction_metrics = transactions.groupBy("customer_id").agg(
            count("*").alias("total_transactions"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_spent"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction"),
            max("amount").alias("max_transaction"),
            countDistinct("category").alias("categories_purchased"),
            max("date").alias("last_transaction_date")
        )
        
        # Chain Pattern 2: Enrich with profile data
        customer_360 = profiles.join(transaction_metrics, "customer_id", "left") \
            .withColumn("days_since_join", 
                datediff(current_date(), to_date(col("join_date")))) \
            .withColumn("total_spent", coalesce(col("total_spent"), lit(0.0))) \
            .withColumn("total_transactions", coalesce(col("total_transactions"), lit(0))) \
            .withColumn("customer_value_score",
                (col("total_spent") / 100) + (col("total_transactions") * 10)) \
            .withColumn("engagement_level",
                when(col("total_transactions") >= 3, "High")
                .when(col("total_transactions") >= 1, "Medium")
                .otherwise("Low"))
        
        logger.info("Customer 360 View:")
        customer_360.show(truncate=False)
        
        return customer_360
    
    def real_time_analytics_pipeline(self):
        """
        Example: Real-time analytics using optimized chain patterns.
        
        Demonstrates streaming-ready transformation chains.
        """
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 60)
        logger.info("EXAMPLE: Real-time Analytics Pipeline")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        # Simulated streaming data
        events = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            ("E001", "page_view", "2024-01-15 10:00:00", "user1", "/home"),
            ("E002", "click", "2024-01-15 10:01:00", "user1", "/products"),
            ("E003", "page_view", "2024-01-15 10:02:00", "user2", "/home"),
            ("E004", "purchase", "2024-01-15 10:03:00", "user1", "/checkout"),
            ("E005", "click", "2024-01-15 10:04:00", "user2", "/products"),
        ], ["event_id", "event_type", "timestamp", "user_id", "page"])
        
        # Transformation chain for real-time processing
        processed = events \
            .withColumn("timestamp_parsed", to_timestamp(col("timestamp"))) \
            .withColumn("hour", hour(col("timestamp_parsed"))) \
            .withColumn("minute", minute(col("timestamp_parsed"))) \
            .withColumn("event_value",
                when(col("event_type") == "purchase", 100)
                .when(col("event_type") == "click", 10)
                .when(col("event_type") == "page_view", 1)
                .otherwise(0))
        
        # Windowed aggregation
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        
        user_window = Window.partitionBy("user_id").orderBy("timestamp_parsed")
        
        analytics = processed \
            .withColumn("event_sequence", row_number().over(user_window)) \
            .withColumn("cumulative_value", 
                sum("event_value").over(
                    user_window.rowsBetween(Window.unboundedPreceding, Window.currentRow)
                )) \
            .withColumn("session_events",
                count("*").over(user_window))
        
        logger.info("Real-time Analytics:")
        analytics.show(truncate=False)
        
        return analytics
    
    def data_quality_pipeline(self):
        """
        Example: Data quality assessment using filter and validation chains.
        
        Implements comprehensive data quality checks.
        """
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 60)
        logger.info("EXAMPLE: Data Quality Pipeline")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        # Sample data with quality issues
        data = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1, "Product A", 100.00, "2024-01-15", "Electronics", "USA"),
            (2, "Product B", -50.00, "2024-01-16", "Clothing", "USA"),  # Negative price
            (3, "", 200.00, "2024-01-17", "Electronics", "UK"),  # Empty name
            (4, "Product D", 150.00, "invalid", "Books", "USA"),  # Invalid date
            (5, "Product E", 75.00, "2024-01-19", None, "Canada"),  # Null category
            (6, "Product F", 300.00, "2024-01-20", "Electronics", "USA"),
        ], ["id", "name", "price", "date", "category", "country"])
        
        # Quality check chain
        quality_checks = data \
            .withColumn("qc_empty_name", col("name") == "") \
            .withColumn("qc_negative_price", col("price") < 0) \
            .withColumn("qc_null_category", col("category").isNull()) \
            .withColumn("qc_invalid_date", 
                col("date").rlike("^\\d{4}-\\d{2}-\\d{2}$") == False) \
            .withColumn("quality_score",
                100 - (
                    (col("qc_empty_name").cast("int") * 25) +
                    (col("qc_negative_price").cast("int") * 25) +
                    (col("qc_null_category").cast("int") * 25) +
                    (col("qc_invalid_date").cast("int") * 25)
                )) \
            .withColumn("quality_status",
                when(col("quality_score") == 100, "PASS")
                .when(col("quality_score") >= 75, "WARNING")
                .otherwise("FAIL"))
        
        logger.info("Data Quality Assessment:")
        quality_checks.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Quality summary
        summary = quality_checks.groupBy("quality_status").agg(
            count("*").alias("record_count"),
            avg("quality_score").alias("avg_quality_score")
        )
        
        logger.info("\nQuality Summary:")
        summary.show()
        
        return quality_checks

# Performance Benchmarking for Chain Patterns
# ============================================================

class ChainPatternBenchmark:
    """
    Benchmark different chain pattern implementations.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def benchmark_chain_approaches(self, record_count: int = 10000):
        """
        Compare performance of different chaining approaches.
        """
        import time
        
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 60)
        logger.info("BENCHMARK: Chain Pattern Performance")
        logger.info("=" * 60)
        
        # Generate large dataset
        from random import randint, choice
        
        data = [(i, f"Customer{i}", choice(["A", "B", "C"]), 
                 randint(10, 1000), f"2024-01-{randint(1,28):02d}")
                for i in range(record_count)]
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            data, 
            ["id", "name", "category", "amount", "date"]
        )
        
        # Approach 1: Sequential withColumn
        start = time.time()
        result1 = df \
            .withColumn("col1", col("amount") * 2) \
            .withColumn("col2", col("amount") * 3) \
            .withColumn("col3", col("amount") * 4) \
            .withColumn("col4", col("amount") * 5) \
            .withColumn("col5", col("amount") * 6)
        result1.count()  # Trigger execution
        time1 = time.time() - start
        
        # Approach 2: Using select with multiple expressions
        start = time.time()
        result2 = df.select(
            "*",
            (col("amount") * 2).alias("col1"),
            (col("amount") * 3).alias("col2"),
            (col("amount") * 4).alias("col3"),
            (col("amount") * 5).alias("col4"),
            (col("amount") * 6).alias("col5")
        )
        result2.count()  # Trigger execution
        time2 = time.time() - start
        
        # Approach 3: Using transform
        def add_columns(df):
            return df \
                .withColumn("col1", col("amount") * 2) \
                .withColumn("col2", col("amount") * 3) \
                .withColumn("col3", col("amount") * 4) \
                .withColumn("col4", col("amount") * 5) \
                .withColumn("col5", col("amount") * 6)
        
        start = time.time()
        result3 = df.transform(add_columns)
        result3.count()  # Trigger execution
        time3 = time.time() - start
        
        # Results
        logger.info(f"\nRecords processed: {record_count:,}")
        logger.info(f"Sequential withColumn: {time1:.4f} seconds")
        logger.info(f"Single select: {time2:.4f} seconds")
        logger.info(f"Transform function: {time3:.4f} seconds")
        logger.info(f"\nFastest approach: ", end="")
        
        min_time = min(time1, time2, time3)
        if min_time == time1:
            logger.info("Sequential withColumn")
        elif min_time == time2:
            logger.info("Single select")
        else:
            logger.info("Transform function")

def demo_utilities(spark: SparkSession):
    """
    Demonstrate utility functions for chain patterns.
    """
    logger.info("Demonstrating Chain Pattern Utilities")
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (1, "Alice", 100),
        (2, "Bob", 200),
        (3, "Charlie", 300)
    ], ["id", "name", "value"])
    
    # Define transformation functions
    def double_value(df):
        return df.withColumn("value", col("value") * 2)
    
    def add_category(df):
        return df.withColumn("category",
            when(col("value") < 200, "Low")
            .when(col("value") < 400, "Medium")
            .otherwise("High"))
    
    def add_timestamp(df):
        return df.withColumn("processed_at", current_timestamp())
    
    # Create pipeline using utility
    transformations = [double_value, add_category, add_timestamp]
    pipeline = ChainPatternUtilities.create_transformation_pipeline(transformations)
    
    # Apply pipeline
    logger.info("\nApplying transformation pipeline:")
    result = pipeline(df)
    result.show(truncate=False)
    
    # Log transformation stats
    ChainPatternUtilities.log_transformation_stats(result, "Final Pipeline Stage")
    
    # Validate output
    validations = {
        "has_records": lambda df: df.count() > 0,
        "has_required_columns": lambda df: all(
            col in df.columns for col in ["id", "name", "value", "category", "processed_at"]
        ),
        "no_null_values": lambda df: df.filter(
            col("value").isNull() | col("category").isNull()
        ).count() == 0
    }
    
    logger.info("\nRunning validations:")
    validation_results = ChainPatternUtilities.validate_chain_output(result, validations)
    
    logger.info("\nValidation Results:")
    for rule, passed in validation_results.items():
        status = "✓ PASSED" if passed else "✗ FAILED"
        logger.info(f"  {rule}: {status}")


# ============================================================
# Advanced Pattern: Dynamic Chain Builder
# ============================================================

class DynamicChainBuilder:
    """
    Build transformation chains dynamically based on configuration.
    Useful for configurable ETL pipelines.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.transformations = []
    
    def add_filter(self, condition):
        """Add a filter transformation to the chain."""
        def filter_transform(df):
            return df.filter(condition)
        self.transformations.append(("filter", filter_transform))
        return self
    
    def add_column(self, col_name, expression):
        """Add a column transformation to the chain."""
        def column_transform(df):
            return df.withColumn(col_name, expression)
        self.transformations.append(("add_column", column_transform))
        return self
    
    def add_aggregation(self, group_cols, agg_exprs):
        """Add an aggregation transformation to the chain."""
        def agg_transform(df):
            return df.groupBy(*group_cols).agg(*agg_exprs)
        self.transformations.append(("aggregation", agg_transform))
        return self
    
    def add_join(self, other_df, join_cols, join_type="inner"):
        """Add a join transformation to the chain."""
        def join_transform(df):
            return df.join(other_df, join_cols, join_type)
        self.transformations.append(("join", join_transform))
        return self
    
    def add_custom(self, transform_func, name="custom"):
        """Add a custom transformation to the chain."""
        self.transformations.append((name, transform_func))
        return self
    
    def build(self):
        """Build and return the complete transformation chain."""
        def execute_chain(df):
            result = df
            for name, transform in self.transformations:
                logger.info(f"Applying transformation: {name}")
                result = transform(result)
            return result
        return execute_chain
    
    def execute(self, df):
        """Build and execute the chain on the given DataFrame."""
        chain = self.build()
        return chain(df)
    
    def get_chain_summary(self):
        """Get a summary of the transformation chain."""
        logger.info("\nTransformation Chain Summary:")
        logger.info(f"Total transformations: {len(self.transformations)}")
        for idx, (name, _) in enumerate(self.transformations, 1):
            logger.info(f"  {idx}. {name}")

# Example: Using Dynamic Chain Builder
# ============================================================

def demo_dynamic_chain_builder(spark: SparkSession):
    """
    Demonstrate the Dynamic Chain Builder pattern.
    """
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 60)
    logger.info("DEMO: Dynamic Chain Builder")
    logger.info("=" * 60)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (1, "Alice", "Engineering", 95000, "2024-01-15"),
        (2, "Bob", "Sales", 75000, "2024-01-16"),
        (3, "Charlie", "Engineering", 105000, "2024-01-17"),
        (4, "Diana", "Marketing", 85000, "2024-01-18"),
        (5, "Eve", "Engineering", 98000, "2024-01-19"),
        (6, "Frank", "Sales", 72000, "2024-01-20"),
    ], ["id", "name", "department", "salary", "hire_date"])
    
    logger.info("Original Data:")
    df.show()
    
    # Build dynamic chain
    builder = DynamicChainBuilder(spark)
    
    chain = builder \
        .add_filter(col("salary") > 70000) \
        .add_column("salary_category",
            when(col("salary") < 80000, "Junior")
            .when(col("salary") < 100000, "Mid")
            .otherwise("Senior")) \
        .add_column("hire_year", year(to_date(col("hire_date")))) \
        .add_column("annual_bonus", col("salary") * 0.1) \
        .build()
    
    # Show chain summary
    builder.get_chain_summary()
    
    # Execute chain
    result = chain(df)
    
    logger.info("\nTransformed Data:")
    result.show(truncate=False)
    
    return result

def print_best_practices():
    """
    Print best practices for transformation chain patterns.
    """
    best_practices = """
    
    ╔════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║         TRANSFORMATION CHAIN PATTERNS - BEST PRACTICES             ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    1. MAP CHAIN PATTERN
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✓ Use for sequential data transformations
    ✓ Keep transformations pure and idempotent
    ✓ Consider using .select() for multiple columns at once
    ✓ Avoid excessive withColumn() calls - combine when possible
    
    2. FILTER CHAIN PATTERN
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✓ Apply most selective filters first
    ✓ Combine filters with & and | operators when possible
    ✓ Cache intermediate results if reused multiple times
    ✓ Use .explain() to verify filter pushdown optimization
    
    3. FLATMAP CHAIN PATTERN
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✓ Use explode() judiciously - can cause data explosion
    ✓ Consider lateral view for multiple explode operations
    ✓ Monitor partition sizes after explosion
    ✓ Use explode_outer() to preserve null values
    
    4. REDUCE CHAIN PATTERN
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✓ Group by high-cardinality columns first
    ✓ Use appropriate aggregation functions
    ✓ Consider partial aggregations for large datasets
    ✓ Leverage adaptive query execution
    
    5. TRANSFORM CHAIN PATTERN
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✓ Create reusable transformation functions
    ✓ Keep functions focused and single-purpose
    ✓ Document transformation logic clearly
    ✓ Test transformations independently
    
    6. MULTI-STAGE TRANSFORMATION PATTERN
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    ✓ Break complex pipelines into logical stages
    ✓ Add validation between stages
    ✓ Log metrics at each stage
    ✓ Consider checkpointing for long pipelines
    
    PERFORMANCE OPTIMIZATION
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    • Cache frequently accessed DataFrames
    • Repartition before expensive operations
    • Use broadcast joins for small tables
    • Avoid UDFs when possible - use built-in functions
    • Monitor and tune shuffle partitions
    • Use column pruning - select only needed columns
    • Leverage predicate pushdown
    
    ERROR HANDLING
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    • Validate input data early in the chain
    • Use coalesce() for null handling
    • Implement data quality checks
    • Separate valid and invalid records
    • Log errors and warnings appropriately
    
    TESTING
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    • Unit test individual transformation functions
    • Integration test complete chains
    • Validate output schemas
    • Test with edge cases and null values
    • Benchmark performance with realistic data volumes
    
    MAINTAINABILITY
    ────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
    • Use meaningful variable names
    • Add comments for complex logic
    • Version control transformation functions
    • Document expected input/output schemas
    • Keep transformation functions pure
    
    """
    print(best_practices)
