class ECommerceAnalyticsPipeline:
    """
    Complete real-world example: E-commerce analytics using all chain patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def create_sample_ecommerce_data(self):
        """Create comprehensive e-commerce sample data."""
        
        # Orders data
        orders = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1001, 501, "2024-01-15 10:30:00", 250.00, "completed", "CA"),
            (1002, 502, "2024-01-15 11:45:00", 150.00, "completed", "NY"),
            (1003, 501, "2024-01-16 09:15:00", 350.00, "pending", "CA"),
            (1004, 503, "2024-01-16 14:20:00", 75.00, "completed", "TX"),
            (1005, 504, "2024-01-17 16:30:00", 500.00, "completed", "CA"),
            (1006, 502, "2024-01-17 12:00:00", 200.00, "cancelled", "NY"),
            (1007, 505, "2024-01-18 10:00:00", 125.00, "completed", "FL"),
            (1008, 501, "2024-01-18 15:30:00", 450.00, "completed", "CA"),
        ], ["order_id", "customer_id", "order_timestamp", "order_total", "status", "state"])
        
        # Order items data
        order_items = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1001, "P001", "Electronics", 2, 100.00),
            (1001, "P002", "Books", 1, 50.00),
            (1002, "P003", "Clothing", 3, 50.00),
            (1003, "P001", "Electronics", 1, 100.00),
            (1003, "P004", "Home", 2, 125.00),
            (1004, "P002", "Books", 1, 50.00),
            (1004, "P005", "Sports", 1, 25.00),
            (1005, "P001", "Electronics", 5, 100.00),
            (1007, "P003", "Clothing", 2, 50.00),
            (1007, "P005", "Sports", 1, 25.00),
            (1008, "P001", "Electronics", 3, 100.00),
            (1008, "P004", "Home", 1, 125.00),
        ], ["order_id", "product_id", "category", "quantity", "unit_price"])
        
        # Customer data
        customers = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (501, "Alice Johnson", "alice@email.com", "2023-01-15", "Premium"),
            (502, "Bob Smith", "bob@email.com", "2023-06-20", "Standard"),
            (503, "Charlie Brown", "charlie@email.com", "2024-01-10", "Standard"),
            (504, "Diana Prince", "diana@email.com", "2022-12-01", "Premium"),
            (505, "Eve Davis", "eve@email.com", "2023-09-15", "Standard"),
        ], ["customer_id", "customer_name", "email", "signup_date", "tier"])
        
        return orders, order_items, customers
    
    def run_complete_pipeline(self):
        """
        Execute complete e-commerce analytics pipeline using all patterns.
        """
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
        logger.info(" E-COMMERCE ANALYTICS PIPELINE - COMPLETE EXAMPLE")
        logger.info("=" * 70)
        
        orders, order_items, customers = self.create_sample_ecommerce_data()
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 1: Data Validation (Filter Chain Pattern)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[STAGE 1] Data Validation - Filter Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("-" * 70)
        
        validated_orders = orders \
            .filter(col("order_total") > 0) \
            .filter(col("status").isNotNull()) \
            .filter(col("customer_id").isNotNull())
        
        validated_items = order_items \
            .filter(col("quantity") > 0) \
            .filter(col("unit_price") > 0)
        
        logger.info(f"Valid orders: {validated_orders.count()}")
        logger.info(f"Valid items: {validated_items.count()}")
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 2: Feature Engineering (Map Chain Pattern)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[STAGE 2] Feature Engineering - Map Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("-" * 70)
        
        enriched_orders = validated_orders \
            .withColumn("order_date", to_date(col("order_timestamp"))) \
            .withColumn("order_hour", hour(col("order_timestamp"))) \
            .withColumn("order_day_of_week", dayofweek(col("order_date"))) \
            .withColumn("is_weekend", col("order_day_of_week").isin([1, 7])) \
            .withColumn("order_month", month(col("order_date"))) \
            .withColumn("order_value_tier",
                when(col("order_total") < 100, "Low")
                .when(col("order_total") < 300, "Medium")
                .when(col("order_total") < 500, "High")
                .otherwise("Premium")) \
            .withColumn("is_completed", col("status") == "completed")
        
        enriched_orders.show(5, truncate=False)
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 3: Item-Level Aggregation (Reduce Chain Pattern)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[STAGE 3] Item Aggregation - Reduce Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("-" * 70)
        
        item_metrics = validated_items \
            .withColumn("line_total", col("quantity") * col("unit_price")) \
            .groupBy("order_id").agg(
                count("*").alias("item_count"),
                sum("quantity").alias("total_quantity"),
                sum("line_total").alias("items_total"),
                countDistinct("category").alias("category_diversity"),
                collect_set("category").alias("categories")
            )
        
        item_metrics.show(5, truncate=False)
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 4: Order Enrichment (Transform Chain Pattern)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[STAGE 4] Order Enrichment - Transform Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("-" * 70)
        
        def add_customer_info(df):
            """Join with customer data."""
            return df.join(customers, "customer_id", "left")
        
        def add_item_metrics(df):
            """Join with item metrics."""
            return df.join(item_metrics, "order_id", "left")
        
        def calculate_customer_metrics(df):
            """Calculate customer-level metrics."""
            from pyspark.sql.window import Window
            customer_window = Window.partitionBy("customer_id")
            
            return df \
                .withColumn("customer_order_count", 
                    count("*").over(customer_window)) \
                .withColumn("customer_total_spend",
                    sum("order_total").over(customer_window)) \
                .withColumn("customer_avg_order",
                    avg("order_total").over(customer_window))
        
        def add_business_flags(df):
            """Add business logic flags."""
            return df \
                .withColumn("high_value_customer", col("customer_total_spend") > 500) \
                .withColumn("repeat_customer", col("customer_order_count") > 1) \
                .withColumn("multi_category_order", col("category_diversity") > 1)
        
        # Apply transformation chain
        complete_orders = enriched_orders \
            .transform(add_customer_info) \
            .transform(add_item_metrics) \
            .transform(calculate_customer_metrics) \
            .transform(add_business_flags)
        
        complete_orders.select(
            "order_id", "customer_name", "order_total", "item_count",
            "customer_order_count", "high_value_customer", "repeat_customer"
        ).show(10, truncate=False)
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 5: Category Analysis (FlatMap Chain Pattern)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[STAGE 5] Category Analysis - FlatMap Chain Pattern")
        logger.info("-" * 70)
        
        category_analysis = validated_items \
            .withColumn("line_total", col("quantity") * col("unit_price")) \
            .join(validated_orders.select("order_id", "status", "state"), "order_id") \
            .filter(col("status") == "completed")
        
        category_metrics = category_analysis.groupBy("category", "state").agg(
            count("*").alias("item_count"),
            sum("quantity").alias("total_units_sold"),
            sum("line_total").alias("category_revenue"),
            avg("unit_price").alias("avg_unit_price")
        )
        
        category_metrics.show(truncate=False)
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 6: Multi-Dimensional Analytics (Multi-Stage Pattern)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[STAGE 6] Multi-Dimensional Analytics - Multi-Stage Pattern")
        logger.info("-" * 70)
        
        # Dimension 1: Time-based analysis
        daily_metrics = complete_orders \
            .filter(col("is_completed")) \
            .groupBy("order_date").agg(
                count("*").alias("orders"),
                sum("order_total").alias("revenue"),
                avg("order_total").alias("avg_order_value"),
                countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers")
            ) \
            .orderBy("order_date")
        
        logger.info("\nDaily Metrics:")
        daily_metrics.show()
        
        # Dimension 2: Customer segment analysis
        customer_segments = complete_orders \
            .filter(col("is_completed")) \
            .groupBy("tier", "order_value_tier").agg(
                count("*").alias("orders"),
                sum("order_total").alias("revenue"),
                avg("item_count").alias("avg_items_per_order")
            ) \
            .orderBy("tier", "order_value_tier")
        
        logger.info("\nCustomer Segment Analysis:")
        customer_segments.show()
        
        # Dimension 3: Geographic analysis
        state_metrics = complete_orders \
            .filter(col("is_completed")) \
            .groupBy("state").agg(
                count("*").alias("orders"),
                sum("order_total").alias("revenue"),
                countDistinct("customer_id").alias("customers"),
                avg("order_total").alias("avg_order_value")
            ) \
            .withColumn("revenue_rank", 
                rank().over(Window.orderBy(col("revenue").desc()))) \
            .orderBy("revenue_rank")
        
        logger.info("\nState Performance:")
        state_metrics.show()
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 7: Final Summary Report
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[STAGE 7] Final Summary Report")
        logger.info("-" * 70)
        
        # Overall KPIs
        kpis = complete_orders.filter(col("is_completed")).agg(
            count("*").alias("total_orders"),
            sum("order_total").alias("total_revenue"),
            avg("order_total").alias("avg_order_value"),
            countDistinct("customer_id").alias("unique_customers"),
            sum(when(col("high_value_customer"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("high_value_customers"),
            sum(when(col("repeat_customer"), 1).otherwise(0)).alias("repeat_customers"),
            avg("item_count").alias("avg_items_per_order")
        )
        
        logger.info("\n📊 OVERALL KPIs:")
        kpis.show(vertical=True, truncate=False)
        
        # Top customers
        top_customers = complete_orders \
            .filter(col("is_completed")) \
            .groupBy("customer_id", "customer_name", "tier").agg(
                count("*").alias("orders"),
                sum("order_total").alias("total_spent"),
                avg("order_total").alias("avg_order")
            ) \
            .orderBy(col("total_spent").desc()) \
            .limit(5)
        
        logger.info("\n🏆 TOP 5 CUSTOMERS:")
        top_customers.show(truncate=False)
        
        # Category performance
        category_performance = validated_items \
            .join(validated_orders.filter(col("status") == "completed"), "order_id") \
            .withColumn("line_total", col("quantity") * col("unit_price")) \
            .groupBy("category").agg(
                count("*").alias("items_sold"),
                sum("quantity").alias("units_sold"),
                sum("line_total").alias("revenue"),
                avg("unit_price").alias("avg_price")
            ) \
            .orderBy(col("revenue").desc())
        
        logger.info("\n📦 CATEGORY PERFORMANCE:")
        category_performance.show(truncate=False)
        
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
        logger.info(" PIPELINE EXECUTION COMPLETED SUCCESSFULLY")
        logger.info("=" * 70)
        
        return {
            "complete_orders": complete_orders,
            "daily_metrics": daily_metrics,
            "customer_segments": customer_segments,
            "state_metrics": state_metrics,
            "kpis": kpis,
            "top_customers": top_customers,
            "category_performance": category_performance
        }

        df = self.spark.createDataFrame([(1, 10), (2, 20)], ["id", "value"])
        
        result = df \
            .withColumn("value_x2", col("value") * 2) \
            .withColumn("value_x3", col("value") * 3)
        
        expected_count = 2
        actual_count = result.count()
        expected_cols = 4  
```python
        expected_cols = 4  # id, value, value_x2, value_x3
        actual_cols = len(result.columns)
        
        test_passed = (expected_count == actual_count) and (expected_cols == actual_cols)
        
        self.test_results.append({
            "test": "Map Chain Pattern",
            "passed": test_passed,
            "details": f"Count: {actual_count}/{expected_count}, Cols: {actual_cols}/{expected_cols}"
        })
        
        logger.info(f"✓ PASSED" if test_passed else "✗ FAILED")

    def test_filter_chain(self):

        df = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1, 10), (2, 20), (3, 30), (4, 40)
        ], ["id", "value"])
        
        result = df \
            .filter(col("value") > 15) \
            .filter(col("value") < 35)

        actual_count = result.count()
        
        test_passed = expected_count == actual_count
        
        self.test_results.append({
            "test": "Filter Chain Pattern",
            "passed": test_passed,

        })
        
        logger.info(f"✓ PASSED" if test_passed else "✗ FAILED")
        return test_passed
    
    def test_flatmap_chain(self):
        """Test flatmap chain pattern."""
        logger.info("\n[TEST] FlatMap Chain Pattern")
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (1, "a,b,c"),
            (2, "d,e")
        ], ["id", "values"])
        
        result = df.withColumn("value", explode(split(col("values"), ",")))
        
        expected_count = 5  # Total elements after explosion
        actual_count = result.count()
        
        test_passed = expected_count == actual_count
        
        self.test_results.append({
            "test": "FlatMap Chain Pattern",
            "passed": test_passed,
            "details": f"Exploded count: {actual_count}/{expected_count}"
        })
        
        logger.info(f"✓ PASSED" if test_passed else "✗ FAILED")
        return test_passed
    
    def test_reduce_chain(self):
        """Test reduce chain pattern."""
        logger.info("\n[TEST] Reduce Chain Pattern")
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            ("A", 10), ("A", 20), ("B", 30)
        ], ["category", "value"])
        
        result = df.groupBy("category").agg(sum("value").alias("total"))
        
        expected_count = 2  # Two categories
        actual_count = result.count()
        
        # Verify aggregation correctness
        category_a_total = result.filter(col("category") == "A").select("total").collect()[0][0]
        test_passed = (expected_count == actual_count) and (category_a_total == 30)
        
        self.test_results.append({
            "test": "Reduce Chain Pattern",
            "passed": test_passed,
            "details": f"Groups: {actual_count}/{expected_count}, Sum A: {category_a_total}/30"
        })
        
        logger.info(f"✓ PASSED" if test_passed else "✗ FAILED")
        return test_passed
    
    def test_transform_chain(self):
        """Test transform chain pattern."""
        logger.info("\n[TEST] Transform Chain Pattern")
        
        def add_doubled(df):
            return df.withColumn("doubled", col("value") * 2)
        
        def add_tripled(df):
            return df.withColumn("tripled", col("value") * 3)
        
        df = self.spark.createDataFrame([(1, 10)], ["id", "value"])
        
        result = df.transform(add_doubled).transform(add_tripled)
        
        expected_cols = 4  # id, value, doubled, tripled
        actual_cols = len(result.columns)
        
        test_passed = expected_cols == actual_cols
        
        self.test_results.append({
            "test": "Transform Chain Pattern",
            "passed": test_passed,
            "details": f"Columns: {actual_cols}/{expected_cols}"
        })
        
        logger.info(f"✓ PASSED" if test_passed else "✗ FAILED")
        return test_passed
    
    def run_all_tests(self):
        """Run all tests and print summary."""
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
        logger.info(" RUNNING TRANSFORMATION CHAIN PATTERN TESTS")
        logger.info("=" * 70)
        
        tests = [
            self.test_map_chain,
            self.test_filter_chain,
            self.test_flatmap_chain,
            self.test_reduce_chain,
            self.test_transform_chain
        ]
        
        for test in tests:
            test()
        
        # Print summary
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
        logger.info(" TEST SUMMARY")
        logger.info("=" * 70)
        
        passed = sum(1 for r in self.test_results if r["passed"])
        total = len(self.test_results)
        
        for result in self.test_results:
            status = "✓ PASSED" if result["passed"] else "✗ FAILED"
            logger.info(f"{status} - {result['test']}")
            logger.info(f"  Details: {result['details']}")
        
        logger.info(f"\nTotal: {passed}/{total} tests passed ({(passed/total)*100:.1f}%)")
        
        return self.test_results


# ============================================================
# Configuration-Driven Chain Pattern
# ============================================================

class ConfigurableChainPattern:
    """
    Create transformation chains from configuration.
    Useful for dynamic, configuration-driven ETL pipelines.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def build_from_config(self, df, config):
        """
        Build transformation chain from configuration dictionary.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            config: Configuration dictionary with transformation specs
            
        Example config:
        {
            "filters": [
                {"column": "amount", "operator": ">", "value": 100},
                {"column": "status", "operator": "==", "value": "active"}
            ],
            "transformations": [
                {"type": "add_column", "name": "amount_doubled", "expr": "amount * 2"},
                {"type": "add_column", "name": "category_upper", "expr": "upper(category)"}
            ],
            "aggregations": {
                "group_by": ["category"],
                "agg_exprs": [
                    {"func": "sum", "column": "amount", "alias": "total_amount"},
                    {"func": "count", "column": "*", "alias": "count"}
                ]
            }
        }
        """
        result = df
        
        # Apply filters
        if "filters" in config:
            logger.info("Applying filters from config...")
            for filter_spec in config["filters"]:
                col_name = filter_spec["column"]
                operator = filter_spec["operator"]
                value = filter_spec["value"]
                
                if operator == ">":
                    result = result.filter(col(col_name) > value)
                elif operator == "<":
                    result = result.filter(col(col_name) < value)
                elif operator == "==":
                    result = result.filter(col(col_name) == value)
                elif operator == "!=":
                    result = result.filter(col(col_name) != value)
                elif operator == ">=":
                    result = result.filter(col(col_name) >= value)
                elif operator == "<=":
                    result = result.filter(col(col_name) <= value)
                
                logger.info(f"  Applied filter: {col_name} {operator} {value}")
        
        # Apply transformations
        if "transformations" in config:
            logger.info("Applying transformations from config...")
            for trans_spec in config["transformations"]:
                if trans_spec["type"] == "add_column":
                    result = result.withColumn(
                        trans_spec["name"],
                        expr(trans_spec["expr"])
                    )
                    logger.info(f"  Added column: {trans_spec['name']}")
        
        # Apply aggregations
        if "aggregations" in config:
            logger.info("Applying aggregations from config...")
            agg_config = config["aggregations"]
            
            group_cols = agg_config.get("group_by", [])
            agg_exprs = []
            
            for agg_spec in agg_config.get("agg_exprs", []):
                func_name = agg_spec["func"]
                col_name = agg_spec["column"]
                alias_name = agg_spec["alias"]
                
                if func_name == "sum":
                    agg_exprs.append(sum(col_name).alias(alias_name))
                elif func_name == "count":
                    agg_exprs.append(count(col_name).alias(alias_name))
                elif func_name == "avg":
                    agg_exprs.append(avg(col_name).alias(alias_name))
                elif func_name == "max":
                    agg_exprs.append(max(col_name).alias(alias_name))
                elif func_name == "min":
                    agg_exprs.append(min(col_name).alias(alias_name))
            
            if group_cols and agg_exprs:
                result = result.groupBy(*group_cols).agg(*agg_exprs)
                logger.info(f"  Grouped by: {group_cols}")
        
        return result


def demo_configurable_chain(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate configuration-driven chain pattern."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Configuration-Driven Chain Pattern")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (1, "Electronics", 150.00, "active"),
        (2, "Books", 25.00, "active"),
        (3, "Electronics", 300.00, "active"),
        (4, "Clothing", 75.00, "inactive"),
        (5, "Books", 40.00, "active"),
    ], ["id", "category", "amount", "status"])
    
    logger.info("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show()
    
    # Define configuration
    config = {
        "filters": [
            {"column": "amount", "operator": ">", "value": 30},
            {"column": "status", "operator": "==", "value": "active"}
        ],
        "transformations": [
            {"type": "add_column", "name": "amount_doubled", "expr": "amount * 2"},
            {"type": "add_column", "name": "category_upper", "expr": "upper(category)"}
        ],
        "aggregations": {
            "group_by": ["category_upper"],
            "agg_exprs": [
                {"func": "sum", "column": "amount", "alias": "total_amount"},
                {"func": "count", "column": "*", "alias": "count"},
                {"func": "avg", "column": "amount", "alias": "avg_amount"}
            ]
        }
    }
    
    # Build and execute pipeline
    pipeline = ConfigurableChainPattern(spark)
    result = pipeline.build_from_config(df, config)
    
    logger.info("\nResult after applying configuration:")
    result.show()
    
    return result


# ============================================================
# Monitoring and Logging for Chain Patterns
# ============================================================

class ChainPatternMonitor:
    """
    Monitor and log transformation chain execution metrics.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.metrics = []
    
    def monitor_transformation(self, stage_name):
        """
        Decorator to monitor transformation execution.
        """
        def decorator(func):
            def wrapper(df, *args, **kwargs):
                import time
                
                start_time = time.time()
                input_count = df.count()
                input_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
                
                logger.info(f"\n[MONITOR] Starting stage: {stage_name}")
                logger.info(f"  Input records: {input_count:,}")
                logger.info(f"  Input partitions: {input_partitions}")
                
                # Execute transformation
                result = func(df, *args, **kwargs)
                
                output_count = result.count()
                output_partitions = result.rdd.getNumPartitions()
                execution_time = time.time() - start_time
                
                # Calculate metrics
                record_change = output_count - input_count
                record_change_pct = (record_change / input_count * 100) if input_count > 0 else 0
                
                logger.info(f"  Output records: {output_count:,}")
                logger.info(f"  Output partitions: {output_partitions}")
                logger.info(f"  Record change: {record_change:+,} ({record_change_pct:+.1f}%)")
                logger.info(f"  Execution time: {execution_time:.2f}s")
                
                # Store metrics
                self.metrics.append({
                    "stage": stage_name,
                    "input_records": input_count,
                    "output_records": output_count,
                    "record_change": record_change,
                    "record_change_pct": record_change_pct,
                    "input_partitions": input_partitions,
                    "output_partitions": output_partitions,
                    "execution_time": execution_time
                })
                
                return result
            
            return wrapper
        return decorator
    
    def get_metrics_summary(self):
        """Get summary of all monitored transformations."""
        if not self.metrics:
            logger.info("No metrics available")
            return None
        
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
        logger.info(" TRANSFORMATION CHAIN METRICS SUMMARY")
        logger.info("=" * 70)
        
        total_time = sum(m["execution_time"] for m in self.metrics)
        
        logger.info(f"\nTotal stages: {len(self.metrics)}")
        logger.info(f"Total execution time: {total_time:.2f}s")
        logger.info("\nPer-Stage Metrics:")
        logger.info("-" * 70)
        
        for i, metric in enumerate(self.metrics, 1):
            logger.info(f"\n{i}. {metric['stage']}")
            logger.info(f"   Records: {metric['input_records']:,} → {metric['output_records']:,} "
                       f"({metric['record_change_pct']:+.1f}%)")
            logger.info(f"   Partitions: {metric['input_partitions']} → {metric['output_partitions']}")
            logger.
```python
            logger.info(f"   Partitions: {metric['input_partitions']} → {metric['output_partitions']}")
            logger.info(f"   Time: {metric['execution_time']:.2f}s "
                       f"({metric['execution_time']/total_time*100:.1f}% of total)")
        
        return self.metrics


def demo_monitoring(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate chain pattern monitoring."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Chain Pattern Monitoring")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    monitor = ChainPatternMonitor()
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (i, f"Customer{i}", i * 10, "Category" + str(i % 3))
        for i in range(1, 1001)
    ], ["id", "name", "amount", "category"])
    
    # Define monitored transformations
    @monitor.monitor_transformation("Initial Filtering")
    def filter_stage(df):
        return df.filter(col("amount") > 100)
    
    @monitor.monitor_transformation("Feature Engineering")
    def feature_stage(df):
        return df \
            .withColumn("amount_tier", 
                when(col("amount") < 300, "Low")
                .when(col("amount") < 600, "Medium")
                .otherwise("High")) \
            .withColumn("name_length", length(col("name")))
    
    @monitor.monitor_transformation("Aggregation")
    def aggregation_stage(df):
        return df.groupBy("category", "amount_tier").agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
        )
    
    # Execute monitored pipeline
    result = df
    result = filter_stage(result)
    result = feature_stage(result)
    result = aggregation_stage(result)
    
    logger.info("\nFinal Result:")
    result.show()
    
    # Get metrics summary
    monitor.get_metrics_summary()
    
    return result


# ============================================================
# Advanced: Lazy Evaluation Chain Pattern
# ============================================================

class LazyEvaluationChain:
    """
    Implement lazy evaluation pattern for complex transformation chains.
    Optimizes execution by combining operations before execution.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, df):
        self.df = df
        self.operations = []
    
    def add_operation(self, op_name, op_func):
        """Add an operation to the chain without executing."""
        self.operations.append((op_name, op_func))
        logger.info(f"[LAZY] Queued operation: {op_name}")
        return self
    
    def filter(self, condition):
        """Add filter operation."""
        def filter_op(df):
            return df.filter(condition)
        return self.add_operation(f"filter({condition})", filter_op)
    
    def withColumn(self, col_name, expression):
        """Add column operation."""
        def column_op(df):
            return df.withColumn(col_name, expression)
        return self.add_operation(f"withColumn({col_name})", column_op)
    
    def groupBy(self, *cols):
        """Add groupBy operation (returns new chain context)."""
        self.group_cols = cols
        return self
    
    def agg(self, *exprs):
        """Add aggregation operation."""
        def agg_op(df):
            return df.groupBy(*self.group_cols).agg(*exprs)
        return self.add_operation(f"groupBy+agg", agg_op)
    
    def execute(self):
        """Execute all queued operations."""
        logger.info("\n[LAZY] Executing transformation chain...")
        logger.info(f"[LAZY] Total operations queued: {len(self.operations)}")
        
        result = self.df
        for op_name, op_func in self.operations:
            logger.info(f"[LAZY] Executing: {op_name}")
            result = op_func(result)
        
        logger.info("[LAZY] Chain execution completed")
        return result
    
    def explain_plan(self):
        """Show the planned operations without executing."""
        logger.info("\n[LAZY] Planned Execution Chain:")
        for i, (op_name, _) in enumerate(self.operations, 1):
            logger.info(f"  {i}. {op_name}")
        return self


def demo_lazy_evaluation(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate lazy evaluation chain pattern."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Lazy Evaluation Chain Pattern")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (1, "Product A", 100, "Electronics"),
        (2, "Product B", 200, "Books"),
        (3, "Product C", 300, "Electronics"),
        (4, "Product D", 150, "Books"),
    ], ["id", "name", "price", "category"])
    
    logger.info("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show()
    
    # Build lazy chain
    chain = LazyEvaluationChain(df) \
        .filter(col("price") > 100) \
        .withColumn("price_doubled", col("price") * 2) \
        .withColumn("category_upper", upper(col("category")))
    
    # Show plan without executing
    chain.explain_plan()
    
    # Execute the chain
    result = chain.execute()
    
    logger.info("\nResult after execution:")
    result.show()
    
    return result


# ============================================================
# Pattern: Conditional Chain Execution
# ============================================================

class ConditionalChainExecutor:
    """
    Execute different transformation chains based on conditions.
    Useful for dynamic pipeline behavior.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def execute_conditional_chain(self, df, condition_field, chains):
        """
        Execute different transformation chains based on field values.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            condition_field: Field to check for conditions
            chains: Dictionary mapping condition values to transformation functions
        """
        results = []
        
        for condition_value, transform_func in chains.items():
            logger.info(f"\n[CONDITIONAL] Processing condition: {condition_field} == {condition_value}")
            
            # Filter data for this condition
            filtered = df.filter(col(condition_field) == condition_value)
            count = filtered.count()
            
            if count > 0:
                logger.info(f"[CONDITIONAL] Records matching: {count}")
                # Apply transformation
                transformed = transform_func(filtered)
                results.append(transformed)
            else:
                logger.info(f"[CONDITIONAL] No records matching, skipping")
        
        # Union all results
        if results:
            from functools import reduce
            final_result = reduce(lambda df1, df2: df1.union(df2), results)
            logger.info(f"\n[CONDITIONAL] Combined result count: {final_result.count()}")
            return final_result
        else:
            logger.info("[CONDITIONAL] No results to combine")
            return None


def demo_conditional_chain(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate conditional chain execution."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Conditional Chain Execution")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (1, "Electronics", 1000, "Premium"),
        (2, "Books", 50, "Standard"),
        (3, "Electronics", 1500, "Premium"),
        (4, "Clothing", 200, "Standard"),
        (5, "Books", 30, "Budget"),
    ], ["id", "category", "amount", "tier"])
    
    logger.info("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show()
    
    # Define different transformations for different tiers
    def premium_transform(df):
        return df \
            .withColumn("discount", lit(0.20)) \
            .withColumn("final_amount", col("amount") * 0.80) \
            .withColumn("priority", lit("HIGH"))
    
    def standard_transform(df):
        return df \
            .withColumn("discount", lit(0.10)) \
            .withColumn("final_amount", col("amount") * 0.90) \
            .withColumn("priority", lit("MEDIUM"))
    
    def budget_transform(df):
        return df \
            .withColumn("discount", lit(0.05)) \
            .withColumn("final_amount", col("amount") * 0.95) \
            .withColumn("priority", lit("LOW"))
    
    # Execute conditional chains
    executor = ConditionalChainExecutor(spark)
    
    chains = {
        "Premium": premium_transform,
        "Standard": standard_transform,
        "Budget": budget_transform
    }
    
    result = executor.execute_conditional_chain(df, "tier", chains)
    
    logger.info("\nResult after conditional transformations:")
    result.orderBy("id").show()
    
    return result


# ============================================================
# Pattern: Parallel Chain Execution
# ============================================================

class ParallelChainExecutor:
    """
    Execute multiple independent transformation chains in parallel.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def execute_parallel_chains(self, df, chains):
        """
        Execute multiple transformation chains and return all results.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            chains: Dictionary of chain_name -> transformation_function
        """
        results = {}
        
        logger.info(f"\n[PARALLEL] Executing {len(chains)} parallel chains")
        
        for chain_name, transform_func in chains.items():
            logger.info(f"\n[PARALLEL] Executing chain: {chain_name}")
            try:
                result = transform_func(df)
                results[chain_name] = result
                logger.info(f"[PARALLEL] Chain '{chain_name}' completed: {result.count()} records")
            except Exception as e:
                logger.error(f"[PARALLEL] Chain '{chain_name}' failed: {str(e)}")
                results[chain_name] = None
        
        return results


def demo_parallel_chains(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate parallel chain execution."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Parallel Chain Execution")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (1, "Alice", 1000, "2024-01-15", "Electronics"),
        (2, "Bob", 500, "2024-01-16", "Books"),
        (3, "Charlie", 1500, "2024-01-17", "Electronics"),
        (4, "Diana", 200, "2024-01-18", "Clothing"),
        (5, "Eve", 800, "2024-01-19", "Electronics"),
    ], ["id", "customer", "amount", "date", "category"])
    
    logger.info("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show()
    
    # Define parallel transformation chains
    def customer_analysis_chain(df):
        """Analyze customer metrics."""
        return df.groupBy("customer").agg(
            count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_spent"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_transaction")
        )
    
    def category_analysis_chain(df):
        """Analyze category metrics."""
        return df.groupBy("category").agg(
            count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
            sum("amount").alias("category_revenue"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
        )
    
    def daily_analysis_chain(df):
        """Analyze daily metrics."""
        return df.groupBy("date").agg(
            count("*").alias("transactions"),
            sum("amount").alias("daily_revenue"),
            countDistinct("customer").alias("unique_customers")
        )
    
    def high_value_chain(df):
        """Filter and analyze high-value transactions."""
        return df.filter(col("amount") > 500) \
            .select("*") \
            .withColumn("value_tier", lit("HIGH"))
    
    # Execute parallel chains
    executor = ParallelChainExecutor(spark)
    
    chains = {
        "customer_analysis": customer_analysis_chain,
        "category_analysis": category_analysis_chain,
        "daily_analysis": daily_analysis_chain,
        "high_value_transactions": high_value_chain
    }
    
    results = executor.execute_parallel_chains(df, chains)
    
    # Display results
    for chain_name, result_df in results.items():
        if result_df is not None:
            logger.info(f"\n{'='*70}")
            logger.info(f" Result: {chain_name}")
            logger.info(f"{'='*70}")
            result_df.show()
    
    return results

# Additional Utility: Chain Pattern Visualizer
# ============================================================

class ChainPatternVisualizer:
    """
    Visualize transformation chain execution flow.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def visualize_chain(chain_steps):
        """
        Create ASCII visualization of transformation chain.
        
        Args:
            chain_steps: List of tuples (step_name, record_count)
        """
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print(" TRANSFORMATION CHAIN VISUALIZATION")
        print("=" * 70 + "\n")
        
        max_width = 50
        max_count = max(count for _, count in chain_steps)
        
        for i, (step_name, record_count) in enumerate(chain_steps):
            # Calculate bar width
            bar_width = int((record_count / max_count) * max_width) if max_count > 0 else 0
            bar = "█" * bar_width
            
            # Arrow between steps
            if i > 0:
                print("    │")
                print("    ▼")
            
            # Step visualization
            print(f"{i+1}. {step_name}")
            print(f"   Records: {record_count:,}")
            print(f"   {bar} ({record_count})")
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)


def demo_chain_visualization(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate chain visualization."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Chain Pattern Visualization")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (i, f"Customer{i}", i * 10, "Category" + str(i % 3))
        for i in range(1, 101)
    ], ["id", "name", "amount", "category"])
    
    # Track chain execution
    chain_steps = []
    
    # Step 1: Initial data
    chain_steps.append(("Initial Data Load", df.count()))
    
    # Step 2: Filter
    df_filtered = df.filter(col("amount") > 200)
    chain_steps.append(("Filter (amount > 200)", df_filtered.count()))
    
    # Step 3: Add columns
    df_enriched = df_filtered.withColumn("tier", 
        when(col("amount") < 500, "Low")
        .when(col("amount") < 700, "Medium")
        .otherwise("High"))
    chain_steps.append(("Add Tier Column", df_enriched.count()))
    
    # Step 4: Aggregation
    df_aggregated = df_enriched.groupBy("category", "tier").agg(
        count("*").alias("count")
    )
    chain_steps.append(("Group By & Aggregate", df_aggregated.count()))
    
    # Visualize the chain
    ChainPatternVisualizer.visualize_chain(chain_steps)
    
    return df_aggregated


# ============================================================
# Pattern: Error Recovery Chain
# ============================================================

class ErrorRecoveryChain:
    """
    Implement error recovery mechanisms in transformation chains.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.error_log = []
    
    def safe_transform(self, df, transform_func, transform_name, fallback_func=None):
        """
        Execute transformation with error handling and optional fallback.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            transform_func: Primary transformation function
            transform_name: Name of transformation for logging
            fallback_func: Optional fallback function if primary fails
        """
        try:
            logger.info(f"[RECOVERY] Attempting: {transform_name}")
            result = transform_func(df)
            logger.info(f"[RECOVERY] ✓ Success: {transform_name}")
            return result
        
        except Exception as e:
            error_msg = f"Error in {transform_name}: {str(e)}"
            logger.error(f"[RECOVERY] ✗ Failed: {error_msg}")
            self.error_log.append({
                "transform": transform_name,
                "error": str(e),
                "timestamp": str(pd.Timestamp.now())
            })
            
            if fallback_func:
                logger.info(f"[RECOVERY] Attempting fallback for: {transform_name}")
                try:
                    result = fallback_func(df)
                    logger.info(f"[RECOVERY] ✓ Fallback succeeded: {transform_name}")
                    return result
                except Exception as fallback_error:
                    logger.error(f"[RECOVERY] ✗ Fallback failed: {str(fallback_error)}")
                    return df  # Return original DataFrame
            else:
                logger.warning(f"[RECOVERY] No fallback available, returning original DataFrame")
                return df
    
    def get_error_report(self):
        """Generate error report."""
        if not self.error_log:
            logger.info("[RECOVERY] No errors encountered")
            return None
        
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
        logger.info(" ERROR RECOVERY REPORT")
        logger.info("=" * 70)
        
        for i, error in enumerate(self.error_log, 1):
            logger.info(f"\n{i}. Transform: {error['transform']}")
            logger.info(f"   Error: {error['error']}")
            logger.info(f"   Time: {error['timestamp']}")
        
        return self.error_log


def demo_error_recovery(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate error recovery chain."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Error Recovery Chain Pattern")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    # Create sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (1, "Product A", 100),
        (2, "Product B", 200),
        (3, "Product C", 300),
    ], ["id", "name", "price"])
    
    logger.info("\nOriginal Data:")
    df.show()
    
    recovery = ErrorRecoveryChain(spark)
    
    # Define transformations (some will fail)
    def good_transform(df):
        return df.withColumn("price_doubled", col("price") * 2)
    
    def bad_transform(df):
        # This will fail - invalid column name
        return df.withColumn("invalid", col("nonexistent_column") * 2)
    
    def fallback_transform(df):
        # Fallback: add a default column
        return df.withColumn("invalid", lit(0))
    
    def another_good_transform(df):
        return df.withColumn("name_upper", upper(col("name")))
    
    # Execute chain with error recovery
    result = df
    result = recovery.safe_transform(result, good_transform, "Double Price")
    result = recovery.safe_transform(result, bad_transform, "Invalid Transform", fallback_transform)
    result = recovery.safe_transform(result, another_good_transform, "Uppercase Name")
    
    logger.info("\nFinal Result (with error recovery):")
    result.show()
    
    # Get error report
    recovery.get_error_report()
    
    return result


# ============================================================
# Pattern: Incremental Chain Processing
# ============================================================

class IncrementalChainProcessor:
    """
    Process data incrementally through transformation chains.
    Useful for streaming or large batch processing.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, checkpoint_dir="/tmp/checkpoints"):
        self.spark = spark
        self.checkpoint_dir = checkpoint_dir
    
    def process_incrementally(self, df, batch_size, transform_chain):
        """
        Process DataFrame in batches through transformation chain.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            batch_size: Number of records per batch
            transform_chain: Transformation function to apply
        """
        logger.info(f"\n[INCREMENTAL] Starting incremental processing")
        logger.info(f"[INCREMENTAL] Batch size: {batch_size}")
        
        # Add row number for batching
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        
        df_with_batch = df.withColumn(
            "row_num",
            row_number().over(Window.orderBy(lit(1)))
        ).withColumn(
            "batch_id",
            ((col("row_num") - 1) / batch_size).cast("int")
        )
        
        total_batches = df_with_batch.select(max("batch_id")).collect()[0][0] + 1
        logger.info(f"[INCREMENTAL] Total batches: {total_batches}")
        
        results = []
        
        for batch_id in range(total_batches):
            logger.info(f"\n[INCREMENTAL] Processing batch {batch_id + 1}/{total_batches}")
            
            # Get batch data
            batch_df = df_with_batch.filter(col("batch_id") == batch_id) \
                .drop("row_num", "batch_id")
            
            batch_count = batch_df.count()
            logger.info(f"[INCREMENTAL] Batch records: {batch_count}")
            
            # Apply transformation
            transformed_batch = transform_chain(batch_df)
            results.append(transformed_batch)
        
        # Combine results
        from functools import reduce
        final_result = reduce(lambda df1, df2: df1.union(df2), results)
        
        logger.info(f"\n[INCREMENTAL] Processing complete")
        logger.info(f"[INCREMENTAL] Total output records: {final_result.count()}")
        
        return final_result


def demo_incremental_processing(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate incremental chain processing."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Incremental Chain Processing")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    # Create larger sample data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (i, f"Customer{i}", i * 10, f"Category{i % 3}")
        for i in range(1, 51)
    ], ["id", "name", "amount", "category"])
    
    logger.info(f"\nOriginal Data: {df.count()} records")
    
    # Define transformation chain
    def transform_chain(df):
        return df \
            .withColumn("amount_doubled", col("amount") * 2) \
            .withColumn("tier",
                when(col("amount") < 200, "Low")
                .when(col("amount") < 400, "Medium")
                .otherwise("High"))
    
    # Process incrementally
    processor = IncrementalChainProcessor(spark)
    result = processor.process_incrementally(df, batch_size=10, transform_chain=transform_chain)
    
    logger.info("\nFinal Result (first 10 rows):")
    result.show(10)
    
    return result

# ============================================================
# Quick Reference Guide
# ============================================================

"""
QUICK REFERENCE: TRANSFORMATION CHAIN PATTERNS
===============================================

1. MAP CHAIN PATTERN
--------------------
Purpose: Sequential field transformations
Example:
    df.withColumn("col1", expr1) \
      .withColumn("col2", expr2) \
      .withColumn("col3", expr3)

Best For:
    - Data enrichment
    - Feature engineering
    - Type conversions

2. FILTER CHAIN PATTERN
-----------------------
Purpose: Progressive data filtering
Example:
    df.filter(condition1) \
      .filter(condition2) \
      .filter(condition3)

Best For:
    - Data quality checks
    - Multi-criteria filtering
    - Outlier removal

3. FLATMAP CHAIN PATTERN
------------------------
Purpose: Data explosion and normalization
Example:
    df.withColumn("items", explode(col("array_col"))) \
      .withColumn("subitems", explode(col("nested_array")))

Best For:
    - Array/map explosion
    - Tokenization
    - One-to-many transformations

4. REDUCE CHAIN PATTERN
-----------------------
Purpose: Progressive aggregation
Example:
    df.groupBy("col1").agg(...) \
      .groupBy("col2").agg(...)

Best For:
    - Multi-level aggregation
    - Hierarchical summarization
    - Dimensional reduction

5. TRANSFORM CHAIN PATTERN
--------------------------
Purpose: Modular, reusable transformations
Example:
    df.transform(func1) \
      .transform(func2) \
      .transform(func3)

Best For:
    - Clean code architecture
    - Reusable pipelines
    - Configuration-driven ETL

6. MULTI-STAGE TRANSFORMATION PATTERN
-------------------------------------
Purpose: Complex end-to-end pipelines
Example:
    df.transform(validate) \
      .transform(enrich) \
      .transform(aggregate) \
      .transform(finalize)

Best For:
    - Production ETL
    - Complex business logic
    - Multi-source integration

PERFORMANCE TIPS
================
✓ Cache intermediate results if reused
✓ Use broadcast joins for small tables
✓ Avoid UDFs when possible
✓ Repartition before expensive operations
✓ Monitor shuffle operations
✓ Use column pruning early
✓ Leverage predicate pushdown

ERROR HANDLING
==============
✓ Validate input data early
✓ Use coalesce() for null handling
✓ Implement data quality checks
✓ Separate valid/invalid records
✓ Log errors appropriately
✓ Provide fallback mechanisms

TESTING
=======
✓ Unit test individual transformations
✓ Integration test complete chains
✓ Validate output schemas
✓ Test edge cases and nulls
✓ Benchmark with realistic data

"""

class TransformationChainExamplesQuickRef:
    """
    Quick reference examples for each pattern.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_map_chain():
        """Quick example of Map Chain Pattern."""
        code = """
# Map Chain Pattern Example
df = df.withColumn("amount_usd", col("amount") * exchange_rate) \\
       .withColumn("amount_rounded", round(col("amount_usd"), 2)) \\
       .withColumn("amount_category", 
           when(col("amount_usd") < 100, "Low")
           .when(col("amount_usd") < 1000, "Medium")
           .otherwise("High")) \\
       .withColumn("processed_date", current_timestamp())
        """
        return code
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_filter_chain():
        """Quick example of Filter Chain Pattern."""
        code = """
# Filter Chain Pattern Example
df = df.filter(col("amount") > 0) \\
       .filter(col("status") == "active") \\
       .filter(col("created_date") >= "2024-01-01") \\
       .filter(col("category").isin(["A", "B", "C"]))
        """
        return code
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_flatmap_chain():
        """Quick example of FlatMap Chain Pattern."""
        code = """
# FlatMap Chain Pattern Example
df = df.withColumn("tag", explode(split(col("tags"), ","))) \\
       .withColumn("word", explode(split(col("description"), " "))) \\
       .filter(length(col("word")) > 3)
        """
        return code
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_reduce_chain():
        """Quick example of Reduce Chain Pattern."""
        code = """
# Reduce Chain Pattern Example
df = df.groupBy("category", "region").agg(
           sum("amount").alias("total"),
           count("*").alias("count")
       ).groupBy("category").agg(
           sum("total").alias("category_total"),
           avg("count").alias("avg_count")
       )
        """
        return code
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_transform_chain():
        """Quick example of Transform Chain Pattern."""
        code = """
# Transform Chain Pattern Example
def add_date_features(df):
    return df.withColumn("year", year(col("date"))) \\
             .withColumn("month", month(col("date")))

def add_amount_features(df):
    return df.withColumn("amount_tier", 
               when(col("amount") < 100, "Low").otherwise("High"))

df = df.transform(add_date_features) \\
       .transform(add_amount_features)
        """
        return code
    
    @staticmethod
    def example_multistage_chain():
        """Quick example of Multi-Stage Transformation Pattern."""
        code = """
# Multi-Stage Transformation Pattern Example
# Stage 1: Validation
validated = df.filter(col("amount") > 0).filter(col("id").isNotNull())

# Stage 2: Enrichment
enriched = validated.join(lookup_table, "id") \\
                     .withColumn("calculated_field", col("a") * col("b"))

# Stage 3: Aggregation
aggregated = enriched.groupBy("category").agg(sum("amount").alias("total"))

# Stage 4: Final Processing
final = aggregated.withColumn("rank", rank().over(window_spec))
        """
        return code

class TroubleshootingGuide:
    """
    Common issues and solutions for transformation chains.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_guide():
        guide = """
╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
║              TRANSFORMATION CHAIN TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE          ║
╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝

ISSUE: Out of Memory Errors
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptoms: Job fails with OOM exceptions
Solutions:
  ✓ Increase executor memory
  ✓ Reduce partition size
  ✓ Use .persist() with MEMORY_AND_DISK
  ✓ Avoid collect() on large DataFrames
  ✓ Use sampling for development/testing
  
Example:
  df = df.repartition(100)  # Increase partitions
  df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE: Slow Performance
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptoms: Jobs take too long to complete
Solutions:
  ✓ Check for data skew
  ✓ Optimize shuffle operations
  ✓ Use broadcast joins for small tables
  ✓ Enable adaptive query execution
  ✓ Avoid UDFs, use built-in functions
  
Example:
  spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
  df.join(broadcast(small_df), "key")

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE: NULL Values Causing Errors
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptoms: NullPointerException or unexpected results
Solutions:
  ✓ Use coalesce() to provide defaults
  ✓ Filter out nulls early
  ✓ Use null-safe operators
  ✓ Add explicit null checks
  
Example:
  df.withColumn("safe_value", coalesce(col("value"), lit(0)))
  df.filter(col("important_field").isNotNull())

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE: Schema Mismatch in Union
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptoms: AnalysisException during union operations
Solutions:
  ✓ Ensure column order matches
  ✓ Use unionByName instead of union
  ✓ Add missing columns with null values
  ✓ Cast columns to same types
  
Example:
  df1.unionByName(df2, allowMissingColumns=True)

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE: Excessive Shuffling
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptoms: Many shuffle stages, slow performance
Solutions:
  ✓ Reduce number of groupBy operations
  ✓ Use repartition strategically
  ✓ Combine filters before groupBy
  ✓ Use window functions instead of self-joins
  
Example:
  # Bad: Multiple groupBy operations
  df.groupBy("a").agg(...).groupBy("b").agg(...)
  
  # Better: Single groupBy with window functions
  df.withColumn("metric", sum("value").over(window_spec))

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE: Column Not Found Errors
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptoms: AnalysisException: cannot resolve column
Solutions:
  ✓ Check for typos in column names
  ✓ Use df.columns to verify available columns
  ✓ Check if column was dropped in previous step
  ✓ Verify case sensitivity
  
Example:
  print(df.columns)  # Check available columns
  df.select([col(c) for c in df.columns if c.startswith("prefix")])

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
ISSUE: Data Skew
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
Symptoms: Some tasks take much longer than others
Solutions:
  ✓ Use salting technique for skewed keys
  ✓ Repartition by different column
  ✓ Filter outliers if appropriate
  ✓ Use adaptive query execution
  
Example:
  # Add salt to skewed key
  df.withColumn("salted_key", 
      concat(col("key"), lit("_"), (rand() * 10).cast("int")))

────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
DEBUGGING TIPS
────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
1. Use .explain() to understand query plan
2. Check Spark UI for bottlenecks
3. Add .cache() to inspect intermediate results
4. Use .show() and .printSchema() frequently
5. Start with small data samples
6. Monitor resource usage
7. Check executor logs for detailed errors

Example Debugging Workflow:
  df.explain(True)  # See execution plan
  df.cache()        # Cache for inspection
  df.show(5)        # Preview data
  df.printSchema()  # Verify schema
  print(f"Count: {df.count()}")  # Verify record count
"""
        print(guide)

# Performance Profiler
# ============================================================

class ChainPerformanceProfiler:
    """
    Profile performance of transformation chains.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.profiles = []
    
    def profile_chain(self, df, chain_func, chain_name):
        """
        Profile a transformation chain.
        
        Returns detailed performance metrics.
        """
        import time
        import gc
        
        logger.info(f"\n[PROFILER] Profiling: {chain_name}")
        
        # Force garbage collection before profiling
        gc.collect()
        
        # Initial metrics
        start_time = time.time()
        start_count = df.count()
        start_partitions = df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        
        # Get query plan before execution
        logger.info("[PROFILER] Analyzing query plan...")
        explain_str = df._jdf.queryExecution().toString()
        
        # Execute transformation
        logger.info("[PROFILER] Executing transformation...")
        result = chain_func(df)
        
        # Trigger action to measure actual execution
        end_count = result.count()
        
        # End metrics
        end_time = time.time()
        end_partitions = result.rdd.getNumPartitions()
        execution_time = end_time - start_time
        
        # Calculate statistics
        records_per_second = end_count / execution_time if execution_time > 0 else 0
        
        profile = {
            "chain_name": chain_name,
            "input_records": start_count,
            "output_records": end_count,
            "record_change": end_count - start_count,
            "input_partitions": start_partitions,
            "output_partitions": end_partitions,
            "execution_time": execution_time,
            "records_per_second": records_per_second,
            "timestamp": time.strftime("%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S")
        }
        
        self.profiles.append(profile)
        
        # Print summary
        logger.info(f"[PROFILER] Completed: {chain_name}")
        logger.info(f"  Records: {start_count:,} → {end_count:,}")
        logger.info(f"  Time: {execution_time:.2f}s")
        logger.info(f"  Throughput: {records_per_second:,.0f} records/sec")
        
        return result, profile
    
    def compare_profiles(self):
        """Compare all profiled chains."""
        if not self.profiles:
            logger.info("[PROFILER] No profiles to compare")
            return
        
        logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
        logger.info(" PERFORMANCE COMPARISON")
        logger.info("=" * 70)
        
        # Sort by execution time
        sorted_profiles = sorted(self.profiles, key=lambda x: x['execution_time'])
        
        print("\n{:<30} {:>15} {:>15} {:>15}".format(
            "Chain", "Time (s)", "Records/sec", "Output Rows"
        ))
        print("-" * 70)
        
        for profile in sorted_profiles:
            print("{:<30} {:>15.2f} {:>15,.0f} {:>15,}".format(
                profile['chain_name'][:28],
                profile['execution_time'],
                profile['records_per_second'],
                profile['output_records']
            ))
        
        # Fastest and slowest
        fastest = sorted_profiles[0]
        slowest = sorted_profiles[-1]
        
        print("\n" + "=" * 70)
        print(f"Fastest: {fastest['chain_name']} ({fastest['execution_time']:.2f}s)")
        print(f"Slowest: {slowest['chain_name']} ({slowest['execution_time']:.2f}s)")
        
        if slowest['execution_time'] > 0:
            speedup = slowest['execution_time'] / fastest['execution_time']
            print(f"Speedup: {speedup:.2f}x")


def demo_performance_profiling(spark: SparkSession):
    """Demonstrate performance profiling."""
    logger.info("\n" + "=" * 70)
    logger.info(" DEMO: Performance Profiling")
    logger.info("=" * 70)
    
    # Create test data
    df = spark.createDataFrame([
        (i, f"Name{i}", i * 10, f"Cat{i % 5}")
        for i in range(1, 10001)
    ], ["id", "name", "value", "category"])
    
    profiler = ChainPerformanceProfiler()
    
    # Define different transformation approaches
    def approach1_sequential_withcolumn(df):
        return df \
            .withColumn("val1", col("value") * 2) \
            .withColumn("val2", col("value") * 3) \
            .withColumn("val3", col("value") * 4)
    
    def approach2_single_select(df):
        return df.select(
            "*",
            (col("value") * 2).alias("val1"),
            (col("value") * 3).alias("val2"),
            (col("value") * 4).alias("val3")
        )
    
    def approach3_with_aggregation(df):
        return df.groupBy("category").agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            sum("value").alias("total"),
            avg("value").alias("average")
        )
    
    # Profile each approach
    result1, _ = profiler.profile_chain(df, approach1_sequential_withcolumn, "Sequential withColumn")
    result2, _ = profiler.profile_chain(df, approach2_single_select, "Single select")
    result3, _ = profiler.profile_chain(df, approach3_with_aggregation, "With aggregation")
    
    # Compare results
    profiler.compare_profiles()
    
    return profiler

# Export Utilities

class ChainPatternExporter:
    """
    Export transformation chain results to various formats.
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def export_to_parquet(df, path, partition_by=None):
        """Export DataFrame to Parquet format."""
        logger.info(f"[EXPORT] Writing to Parquet: {path}")
        
        writer = df.write.mode("overwrite")
        
        if partition_by:
            writer = writer.partitionBy(partition_by)
        
        writer.parquet(path)
        logger.info(f"[EXPORT] Successfully wrote to: {path}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def export_to_csv(df, path, header=True):
        """Export DataFrame to CSV format."""
        logger.info(f"[EXPORT] Writing to CSV: {path}")
        
        df.write.mode("overwrite") \
            .option("header", header) \
            .csv(path)
        
        logger.info(f"[EXPORT] Successfully wrote to: {path}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def export_to_json(df, path):
        """Export DataFrame to JSON format."""
        logger.info(f"[EXPORT] Writing to JSON: {path}")
        
        df.write.mode("overwrite").json(path)
        
        logger.info(f"[EXPORT] Successfully wrote to: {path}")
    
    @staticmethod
    def export_summary_to_text(df, path, sample_size=10):
        """Export DataFrame summary to text file."""
        logger.info(f"[EXPORT] Writing summary to: {path}")
        
        with open(path, 'w') as f:
            f.write("=" * 70 + "\n")
            f.write("DATAFRAME SUMMARY\n")
            f.write("=" * 70 + "\n\n")
            
            f.write(f"Total Records: {df.count():,}\n")
            f.write(f"Total Columns: {len(df.columns)}\n")
            f.write(f"Partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}\n\n")
            
            f.write("Schema:\n")
            f.write("-" * 70 + "\n")
            for field in df.schema.fields:
                f.write(f"{field.name}: {field.dataType}\n")
            
            f.write("\n" + "=" * 70 + "\n")
            f.write(f"Sample Data (first {sample_size} rows):\n")
            f.write("=" * 70 + "\n\n")
            
            # Get sample data
            sample = df.limit(sample_size).collect()
            for row in sample:
                f.write(str(row) + "\n")
        
        logger.info(f"[EXPORT] Successfully wrote summary to: {path}")

class CompleteETLPipeline:
    """
    Complete ETL pipeline demonstrating all transformation chain patterns
    with monitoring, error handling, and export capabilities.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.monitor = ChainPatternMonitor()
        self.profiler = ChainPerformanceProfiler()
        self.recovery = ErrorRecoveryChain(spark)
    
    def run_complete_pipeline(self, input_path=None, output_path="/tmp/pipeline_output"):
        """
        Execute complete ETL pipeline with all features.
        """
        logger.info("\n" + "╔" + "═" * 68 + "╗")
        logger.info("║" + " COMPLETE ETL PIPELINE - ALL FEATURES ".center(68) + "║")
        logger.info("╚" + "═" * 68 + "╝")
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 1: Data Ingestion
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] STAGE 1: Data Ingestion")
        
        if input_path:
            df = self.spark.read.parquet(input_path)
        else:
            # Create sample data
            df = self.spark.createDataFrame([
                (i, f"Customer{i}", f"Product{i%10}", i * 10.5, 
                 f"2024-01-{(i%28)+1:02d}", f"Category{i%5}")
                for i in range(1, 1001)
            ], ["id", "customer", "product", "amount", "date", "category"])
        
        logger.info(f"[PIPELINE] Loaded {df.count():,} records")
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 2: Data Validation (with monitoring)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] STAGE 2: Data Validation")
        
        @self.monitor.monitor_transformation("Data Validation")
        def validate_data(df):
            return df \
                .filter(col("amount") > 0) \
                .filter(col("id").isNotNull()) \
                .filter(col("customer").isNotNull())
        
        df_validated = validate_data(df)
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 3: Feature Engineering (with error recovery)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] STAGE 3: Feature Engineering")
        
        def add_features(df):
            return df \
                .withColumn("date_parsed", to_date(col("date"))) \
                .withColumn("year", year(col("date_parsed"))) \
                .withColumn("month", month(col("date_parsed"))) \
                .withColumn("amount_tier",
                    when(col("amount") < 50, "Low")
                    .when(col("amount") < 200, "Medium")
                    .otherwise("High"))
        
        df_enriched = self.recovery.safe_transform(
            df_validated, 
            add_features, 
            "Feature Engineering"
        )
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 4: Aggregation (with profiling)
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] STAGE 4: Aggregation")
        
        def aggregate_data(df):
            return df.groupBy("category", "amount_tier", "month").agg(
                count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
                sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
                avg("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
                countDistinct("customer").alias("unique_customers")
            )
        
        df_aggregated, _ = self.profiler.profile_chain(
            df_enriched,
            aggregate_data,
            "Aggregation Stage"
        )
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 5: Final Transformations
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] STAGE 5: Final Transformations")
        
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(col("total_amount").desc())
        
        df_final = df_aggregated \
            .withColumn("rank", rank().over(window_spec)) \
            .withColumn("processing_timestamp", current_timestamp()) \
            .withColumn("pipeline_version", lit("1.0"))
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 6: Quality Checks
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] STAGE 6: Quality Checks")
        
        quality_metrics = {
            "total_records": df_final.count(),
            "null_check": df_final.filter(
                col("transaction_count").isNull() | 
                col("total_amount").isNull()
            ).count(),
            "categories": df_final.select("category").distinct().count(),
            "date_range": {
                "min_month": df_final.agg(min("month")).collect()[0][0],
                "max_month": df_final.agg(max("month")).collect()[0][0]
            }
        }
        
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] Quality Metrics:")
        for metric, value in quality_metrics.items():
            logger.info(f"  {metric}: {value}")
```python
            logger.info(f"  {metric}: {value}")
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 7: Export Results
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] STAGE 7: Export Results")
        
        exporter = ChainPatternExporter()
        
        # Export to multiple formats
        try:
            exporter.export_to_parquet(
                df_final, 
                f"{output_path}/parquet",
                partition_by=["category"]
            )
            
            exporter.export_to_csv(
                df_final.limit(100),
                f"{output_path}/csv_sample"
            )
            
            exporter.export_summary_to_text(
                df_final,
                f"{output_path}/summary.txt"
            )
            
            logger.info("[PIPELINE] All exports completed successfully")
            
        except Exception as e:
            logger.error(f"[PIPELINE] Export error: {str(e)}")
        
        # ============================================================
        # STAGE 8: Generate Reports
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n[PIPELINE] STAGE 8: Generate Reports")
        
        # Monitoring report
        self.monitor.get_metrics_summary()
        
        # Performance report
        self.profiler.compare_profiles()
        
        # Error report
        self.recovery.get_error_report()
        
        # ============================================================
        # PIPELINE SUMMARY
        # ============================================================
        logger.info("\n" + "╔" + "═" * 68 + "╗")
        logger.info("║" + " PIPELINE EXECUTION SUMMARY ".center(68) + "║")
        logger.info("╚" + "═" * 68 + "╝")
        
        summary = f"""

Execution Date: {pd.Timestamp.now()}

Input Records: {df.count():,}
Output Records: {df_final.count():,}
Processing Success Rate: {(df_final.count()/df.count()*100):.2f}%

Stages Completed: 8
Errors Encountered: {len(self.recovery.error_log)}

Output Location: {output_path}

Quality Metrics:

  - Null Records: {quality_metrics['null_check']}
  - Month Range: {quality_metrics['date_range']['min_month']} to {quality_metrics['date_range']['max_month']}
        """

        logger.info(f"\n[PIPELINE] Summary saved to: {output_path}/pipeline_summary.txt")
        
        return {
            "final_data": df_final,

        }
