## 4. Code Review Pattern

```python
"""
Code Review Pattern for PySpark
Demonstrates automated code review, quality checks, and review workflow management.

This module provides a comprehensive framework for conducting code reviews on
PySpark applications, including automated checks, review tracking, and
feedback management.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType, BooleanType, TimestampType
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Set, Callable, Any
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime
from enum import Enum
import re
import ast
import inspect
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class ReviewSeverity(Enum):
    """Severity levels for code review findings"""
    CRITICAL = "critical"
    MAJOR = "major"
    MINOR = "minor"
    INFO = "info"


class ReviewCategory(Enum):
    """Categories of code review findings"""
    PERFORMANCE = "performance"
    MAINTAINABILITY = "maintainability"
    SECURITY = "security"
    BEST_PRACTICES = "best_practices"
    DOCUMENTATION = "documentation"
    TESTING = "testing"


class ReviewStatus(Enum):
    """Status of review items"""
    OPEN = "open"
    ADDRESSED = "addressed"
    ACKNOWLEDGED = "acknowledged"
    WONT_FIX = "wont_fix"


@dataclass
class ReviewFinding:
    """
    Represents a single code review finding.
    
    Attributes:
        finding_id: Unique identifier for the finding
        category: Category of the finding
        severity: Severity level
        title: Brief title of the finding
        description: Detailed description
        location: Code location (file, line number, function)
        recommendation: Suggested fix or improvement
        status: Current status of the finding
        reviewer: Person who identified the finding
        created_at: Timestamp of finding creation
    """
    finding_id: str
    category: ReviewCategory
    severity: ReviewSeverity
    title: str
    description: str
    location: str
    recommendation: str
    status: ReviewStatus = ReviewStatus.OPEN
    reviewer: str = "AutoReviewer"
    created_at: datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.now)
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert finding to dictionary"""
        return {
            "finding_id": self.finding_id,
            "category": self.category.value,
            "severity": self.severity.value,
            "title": self.title,
            "description": self.description,
            "location": self.location,
            "recommendation": self.recommendation,
            "status": self.status.value,
            "reviewer": self.reviewer,
            "created_at": self.created_at.isoformat()
        }


class CodeReviewEngine:
    """
    Automated code review engine for PySpark applications.
    
    Performs automated checks on PySpark code including:
    - Performance anti-patterns
    - Security vulnerabilities
    - Best practice violations
    - Code quality issues
    - Documentation completeness
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession) -> None:
        """
        Initialize the code review engine.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
        """
        self.spark: SparkSession = spark
        self.findings: List[ReviewFinding] = []
        self.review_rules: Dict[str, Callable] = self._initialize_review_rules()
        self.finding_counter: int = 0
    
    def _initialize_review_rules(self) -> Dict[str, Callable]:
        """Initialize review rule checkers"""
        return {
            "performance_check": self._check_performance_patterns,
            "security_check": self._check_security_issues,
            "best_practices_check": self._check_best_practices,
            "documentation_check": self._check_documentation,
        }
    
    def _generate_finding_id(self) -> str:
        """Generate unique finding ID"""
        self.finding_counter += 1
        return f"FIND-{self.finding_counter:04d}"
    
    def review_dataframe_operation(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        operation_name: str,
        operation_code: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> List[ReviewFinding]:
        """
        Review a DataFrame operation for potential issues.
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame being operated on
            operation_name: Name of the operation
            operation_code: Optional source code of the operation
            
        Returns:
            List of review findings
        """
        operation_findings: List[ReviewFinding] = []
        
        # Check for wide transformations
        plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().toString()
        
        if "Exchange" in plan and "hashpartitioning" in plan.lower():
            operation_findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.PERFORMANCE,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.MAJOR,
                title="Shuffle Operation Detected",
                description=f"Operation '{operation_name}' triggers a shuffle which may impact performance",
                location=operation_name,
                recommendation="Consider repartitioning data beforehand or using broadcast joins if applicable"
            ))
        
        # Check for Cartesian products
        if "CartesianProduct" in plan:
            operation_findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.PERFORMANCE,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL,
                title="Cartesian Product Detected",
                description=f"Operation '{operation_name}' performs a Cartesian product",
                location=operation_name,
                recommendation="Add explicit join conditions to avoid Cartesian product"
            ))
        
        # Check column count
        if len(df.columns) > 100:
            operation_findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.PERFORMANCE,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
                title="Excessive Column Count",
                description=f"DataFrame has {len(df.columns)} columns which may impact performance",
                location=operation_name,
                recommendation="Consider selecting only necessary columns"
            ))
        
        self.findings.extend(operation_findings)
        return operation_findings
    
    def _check_performance_patterns(self, code: str, context: str) -> List[ReviewFinding]:
        """
        Check for performance anti-patterns in code.
        
        Args:
            code: Source code to review
            context: Context information
            
        Returns:
            List of performance-related findings
```python
        """
        findings: List[ReviewFinding] = []
        
        # Check for collect() usage
        if re.search(r'\.collect\(\)', code):
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.PERFORMANCE,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.MAJOR,
                title="Collect() Usage Detected",
                description="Using collect() brings all data to driver which may cause OOM",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Use take(n) for sampling or process data in distributed manner"
            ))
        
        # Check for iterative collect in loops
        if re.search(r'for.*\.collect\(\)', code, re.DOTALL):
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.PERFORMANCE,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL,
                title="Collect in Loop",
                description="Calling collect() inside a loop causes multiple actions",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Refactor to use DataFrame operations instead of loops"
            ))
        
        # Check for count() after filter
        if re.search(r'\.filter\([^)]+\)\.count\(\)', code):
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.PERFORMANCE,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.INFO,
                title="Filter Before Count",
                description="Counting after filter may be expensive on large datasets",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Consider caching if the filtered DataFrame is reused"
            ))
        
        # Check for multiple actions without caching
        action_pattern = r'\.(count|collect|show|write|save)\(\)'
        actions = re.findall(action_pattern, code)
        if len(actions) > 2 and 'cache' not in code and 'persist' not in code:
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.PERFORMANCE,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.MAJOR,
                title="Multiple Actions Without Caching",
                description=f"Found {len(actions)} actions without caching intermediate results",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Use cache() or persist() for DataFrames used multiple times"
            ))
        
        # Check for UDF usage
        if re.search(r'@udf|F\.udf\(', code):
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.PERFORMANCE,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
                title="UDF Usage",
                description="Python UDFs have performance overhead due to serialization",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Consider using built-in Spark functions or Pandas UDFs for better performance"
            ))
        
        return findings
    
    def _check_security_issues(self, code: str, context: str) -> List[ReviewFinding]:
        """
        Check for security vulnerabilities.
        
        Args:
            code: Source code to review
            context: Context information
            
        Returns:
            List of security-related findings
        """
        findings: List[ReviewFinding] = []
        
        # Check for hardcoded credentials
        credential_patterns = [
            (r'password\s*=\s*["\'][^"\']+["\']', "Hardcoded Password"),
            (r'api_key\s*=\s*["\'][^"\']+["\']', "Hardcoded API Key"),
            (r'secret\s*=\s*["\'][^"\']+["\']', "Hardcoded Secret"),
            (r'token\s*=\s*["\'][^"\']+["\']', "Hardcoded Token"),
        ]
        
        for pattern, title in credential_patterns:
            if re.search(pattern, code, re.IGNORECASE):
                findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                    finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                    category=ReviewCategory.SECURITY,
                    severity=ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL,
                    title=title,
                    description="Credentials should not be hardcoded in source code",
                    location=context,
                    recommendation="Use environment variables or secure credential management systems"
                ))
        
        # Check for SQL injection risks
        if re.search(r'spark\.sql\([^)]*\+[^)]*\)', code):
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.SECURITY,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL,
                title="Potential SQL Injection",
                description="String concatenation in SQL queries may lead to SQL injection",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Use parameterized queries or DataFrame API"
            ))
        
        # Check for insecure file operations
        if re.search(r'\.load\(["\']file:///', code):
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.SECURITY,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
                title="Local File Access",
                description="Direct local file access may pose security risks",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Validate file paths and use appropriate access controls"
            ))
        
        return findings
    
    def _check_best_practices(self, code: str, context: str) -> List[ReviewFinding]:
        """
        Check for best practice violations.
        
        Args:
            code: Source code to review
            context: Context information
            
        Returns:
            List of best practice findings
        """
        findings: List[ReviewFinding] = []
        
        # Check for proper error handling
        if 'try:' in code and 'except:' in code:
            if re.search(r'except\s*:', code):
                findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                    finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                    category=ReviewCategory.BEST_PRACTICES,
                    severity=ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
                    title="Bare Except Clause",
                    description="Using bare 'except:' catches all exceptions including system exits",
                    location=context,
                    recommendation="Catch specific exception types"
                ))
        
        # Check for magic numbers
        magic_numbers = re.findall(r'\b(\d{2,})\b', code)
        if len(magic_numbers) > 3:
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.BEST_PRACTICES,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
                title="Magic Numbers",
                description="Multiple numeric literals found in code",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Define constants with meaningful names"
            ))
        
        # Check for proper column naming
        if re.search(r'withColumn\(["\'][A-Z]', code):
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.BEST_PRACTICES,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
                title="Column Naming Convention",
                description="Column names should follow snake_case convention",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Use lowercase with underscores for column names"
            ))
        
        # Check for deprecated functions
        deprecated_patterns = [
            (r'\.na\.fill\(0\)', "Use fillna() with specific columns"),
            (r'\.dropna\(\)', "Specify subset of columns for dropna()"),
        ]
        
        for pattern, recommendation in deprecated_patterns:
            if re.search(pattern, code):
                findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                    finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                    category=ReviewCategory.BEST_PRACTICES,
                    severity=ReviewSeverity.INFO,
                    title="Suboptimal Function Usage",
                    description="Function usage could be more specific",
                    location=context,
                    recommendation=recommendation
                ))
        
        return findings
    
    def _check_documentation(self, code: str, context: str) -> List[ReviewFinding]:
        """
        Check for documentation completeness.
        
        Args:
            code: Source code to review
            context: Context information
            
        Returns:
            List of documentation-related findings
        """
        findings: List[ReviewFinding] = []
        
        # Check for function docstrings
        function_pattern = r'def\s+(\w+)\s*\([^)]*\):'
        functions = re.findall(function_pattern, code)
        
        for func_name in functions:
            if not func_name.startswith('_'):  # Public functions
                # Check if docstring exists after function definition
                func_block = re.search(
                    rf'def\s+{func_name}\s*\([^)]*\):\s*"""',
                    code
                )
                if not func_block:
                    findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                        finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                        category=ReviewCategory.DOCUMENTATION,
                        severity=ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
                        title=f"Missing Docstring: {func_name}",
                        description=f"Public function '{func_name}' lacks documentation",
                        location=f"{context}.{func_name}",
                        recommendation="Add docstring with description, args, and returns"
                    ))
        
        # Check for class docstrings
        class_pattern = r'class\s+(\w+)'
        classes = re.findall(class_pattern, code)
        
        for class_name in classes:
            class_block = re.search(
                rf'class\s+{class_name}[^:]*:\s*"""',
                code
            )
            if not class_block:
                findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                    finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                    category=ReviewCategory.DOCUMENTATION,
                    severity=ReviewSeverity.MINOR,
                    title=f"Missing Class Docstring: {class_name}",
                    description=f"Class '{class_name}' lacks documentation",
                    location=f"{context}.{class_name}",
                    recommendation="Add class docstring describing purpose and usage"
                ))
        
        # Check for TODO comments
        todos = re.findall(r'#\s*TODO:?\s*(.+)', code)
        if todos:
            findings.append(ReviewFinding(
                finding_id=self._generate_finding_id(),
                category=ReviewCategory.DOCUMENTATION,
                severity=ReviewSeverity.INFO,
                title="TODO Comments Found",
                description=f"Found {len(todos)} TODO items that need attention",
                location=context,
                recommendation="Address or track TODO items in issue tracker"
            ))
        
        return findings
    
    def review_code(
        self,
        code: str,
        context: str = "code_review"
    ) -> List[ReviewFinding]:
        """
        Perform comprehensive code review.
        
        Args:
            code: Source code to review
            context: Context identifier
            
        Returns:
            List of all findings
        """
        logger.info(f"Starting code review for: {context}")
        
        all_findings: List[ReviewFinding] = []
        
        for rule_name, rule_func in self.review_rules.items():
            findings = rule_func(code, context)
            all_findings.extend(findings)
            logger.info(f"{rule_name}: Found {len(findings)} issues")
        
        self.findings.extend(all_findings)
        return all_findings
    
    def generate_review_report(self) -> str:
        """
        Generate comprehensive review report.
        
        Returns:
            Formatted review report
        """
        report_lines: List[str] = [
            "=" * 80,
            "CODE REVIEW REPORT",
            "=" * 80,
            f"\nGenerated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}",
            f"Total Findings: {len(self.findings)}\n"
        ]
        
        # Summary by severity
        severity_counts: Dict[ReviewSeverity, int] = {}
        for finding in self.findings:
            severity_counts[finding.severity] = severity_counts.get(finding.severity, 0) + 1
        
        report_lines.append("SUMMARY BY SEVERITY:")
        report_lines.append("-" * 40)
        for severity in ReviewSeverity:
            count = severity_counts.get(severity, 0)
            report_lines.append(f"  {severity.value.upper()}: {count}")
        
        # Summary by category
        category_counts: Dict[ReviewCategory, int] = {}
        for finding in self.findings:
            category_counts[finding.category] = category_counts.get(finding.category, 0) + 1
        
        report_lines.append("\nSUMMARY BY CATEGORY:")
        report_lines.append("-" * 40)
        for category in ReviewCategory:
            count = category_counts.get(category, 0)
            report_lines.append(f"  {category.value.upper()}: {count}")
        
        # Detailed findings
        report_lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
        report_lines.append("DETAILED FINDINGS")
        report_lines.append("=" * 80)
        
        # Group by severity
        for severity in [ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL, ReviewSeverity.MAJOR, 
                        ReviewSeverity.MINOR, ReviewSeverity.INFO]:
            severity_findings = [f for f in self.findings if f.severity == severity]
            
            if severity_findings:
                report_lines.append(f"\n{severity.value.upper()} ISSUES ({len(severity_findings)}):")
                report_lines.append("-" * 80)
                
                for finding in severity_findings:
                    report_lines.append(f"\n[{finding.finding_id}] {finding.title}")
                    report_lines.append(f"Category: {finding.category.value}")
                    report_lines.append(f"Location: {finding.location}")
                    report_lines.append(f"Description: {finding.description}")
                    report_lines.append(f"Recommendation: {finding.recommendation}")
                    report_lines.append(f"Status: {finding.status.value}")
        
        report_lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
        
        return "\n".join(report_lines)
    
    def get_findings_by_severity(
        self,
        severity: ReviewSeverity
    ) -> List[ReviewFinding]:
        """
        Get findings filtered by severity.
        
        Args:
            severity: Severity level to filter by
            
        Returns:
            List of findings with specified severity
        """
        return [f for f in self.findings if f.severity == severity]
    
    def get_findings_by_category(
        self,
        category: ReviewCategory
    ) -> List[ReviewFinding]:
        """
        Get findings filtered by category.
        
        Args:
            category: Category to filter by
            
        Returns:
            List of findings in specified category
        """
        return [f for f in self.findings if f.category == category]
    
    def update_finding_status(

            comment: Optional comment
            
        Returns:
            True if updated successfully
        """
        for finding in self.findings:
            if finding.finding_id == finding_id:

class ReviewWorkflow:
    """
    Manages the code review workflow and approval process.
    
    Tracks review assignments, approvals, and feedback cycles.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession) -> None:
        """
        Initialize review workflow manager.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
        """
        self.spark: SparkSession = spark
        self.review_engine: CodeReviewEngine = CodeReviewEngine(spark)
        self.approvers: Set[str] = set()
        self.approvals: Dict[str, List[str]] = {}
        self.required_approvals: int = 2
    
    def add_approver(self, approver_name: str) -> None:
        """
        Add an approver to the workflow.
        
        Args:
            approver_name: Name of the approver
        """
        self.approvers.add(approver_name)
        logger.info(f"Added approver: {approver_name}")
    
    def submit_for_review(
        self,
        code: str,
        author: str,
        description: str
    ) -> str:
        """
        Submit code for review.
        
        Args:
            code: Code to review
            author: Code author
            description: Description of changes
            
        Returns:
            Review ID
        """
        review_id = f"REV-{datetime.now().strftime('%Y%m%d%H%M%S')}"
        
        logger.info(f"Submitting code for review: {review_id}")
        logger.info(f"Author: {author}")
        logger.info(f"Description: {description}")
        
        # Perform automated review
        findings = self.review_engine.review_code(code, review_id)
        
        # Initialize approval tracking
        self.approvals[review_id] = []
        
        logger.info(f"Review {review_id} submitted with {len(findings)} findings")
        
        return review_id
    
    def add_approval(
        self,
        review_id: str,
        approver: str,
        comments: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Add approval from a reviewer.
        
        Args:
            review_id: Review identifier
            approver: Name of approver
            comments: Optional comments
            
        Returns:
            True if approval added successfully
        """
        if approver not in self.approvers:
            logger.warning(f"{approver} is not a registered approver")
            return False
        
        if review_id not in self.approvals:
            logger.warning(f"Review {review_id} not found")
            return False
        
        if approver in self.approvals[review_id]:
            logger.warning(f"{approver} has already approved {review_id}")
            return False
        
        self.approvals[review_id].append(approver)
        logger.info(f"{approver} approved {review_id}")
        
        if comments:
            logger.info(f"Comments: {comments}")
        
        return True
    
    def is_approved(self, review_id: str) -> bool:
        """
        Check if review has sufficient approvals.
        
        Args:
            review_id: Review identifier
            
        Returns:
            True if review is approved
        """
        if review_id not in self.approvals:
            return False
        
        approval_count = len(self.approvals[review_id])
        is_approved = approval_count >= self.required_approvals
        
        # Also check for critical findings
        critical_findings = self.review_engine.get_findings_by_severity(
            ReviewSeverity.CRITICAL
        )
        
        if critical_findings:
            logger.warning(f"Review {review_id} has {len(critical_findings)} critical findings")
            return False
        
        return is_approved
    
    def get_review_status(self, review_id: str) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Get comprehensive review status.
        
        Args:
            review_id: Review identifier
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with review status information
        """
        if review_id not in self.approvals:
            return {"error": "Review not found"}
        
        approval_count = len(self.approvals[review_id])
        findings_by_severity = {
            severity.value: len(self.review_engine.get_findings_by_severity(severity))
            for severity in ReviewSeverity
        }
        
        return {
            "review_id": review_id,
            "approvals": {
                "count": approval_count,
                "required": self.required_approvals,
                "approvers": self.approvals[review_id]
            },
            "findings": findings_by_severity,
            "is_approved": self.is_approved(review_id),
            "timestamp": datetime.now().isoformat()
        }

## 5. Refactoring Pattern

```python
"""
Refactoring Pattern for PySpark
Demonstrates systematic code refactoring techniques, before/after comparisons,
and refactoring safety checks.

This module provides a framework for safely refactoring PySpark code while
maintaining functionality and improving quality.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType, DateType
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Callable, Tuple, Any
from dataclasses import dataclass
from datetime import datetime, date
from abc import ABC, abstractmethod
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


@dataclass
class RefactoringMetrics:
    """
    Metrics for measuring refactoring impact.
    
    Attributes:
        code_complexity_before: Complexity score before refactoring
        code_complexity_after: Complexity score after refactoring
        performance_before: Execution time before (seconds)
        performance_after: Execution time after (seconds)
        lines_of_code_before: LOC before refactoring
        lines_of_code_after: LOC after refactoring
        maintainability_score: Subjective maintainability improvement
    """
    code_complexity_before: int
    code_complexity_after: int
    performance_before: float
    performance_after: float
    lines_of_code_before: int
    lines_of_code_after: int
    maintainability_score: float
    
    def improvement_percentage(self, metric: str) -> float:
        """Calculate improvement percentage for a metric"""
        before = getattr(self, f"{metric}_before")
        after = getattr(self, f"{metric}_after")
        
        if before == 0:
            return 0.0
        
        return ((before - after) / before) * 100


class RefactoringStrategy(ABC):
    """Abstract base class for refactoring strategies"""
    
    @abstractmethod
    def refactor(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """Apply refactoring to DataFrame"""
        pass
    
    @abstractmethod
    def get_description(self) -> str:
        """Get description of refactoring"""
        pass


class ExtractMethodRefactoring(RefactoringStrategy):
    """
    Extract Method refactoring pattern.
    
    Extracts complex logic into separate, reusable methods.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def refactor(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Refactor by extracting methods.
        
        Before: All logic in one place
        After: Separated into focused methods
        """
        # Apply extracted methods
        df = self._add_calculated_fields(df)
        df = self._apply_business_rules(df)
        df = self._add_quality_flags(df)
        
        return df
    
    def _add_calculated_fields(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """Extract: Add calculated fields"""
        return df.withColumn(
            "total_with_tax",
            F.col("amount") * 1.08
        ).withColumn(
            "discount_percentage",
            (F.col("original_price") - F.col("amount")) / F.col("original_price") * 100
        )
    
    def _apply_business_rules(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """Extract: Apply business rules"""
        return df.withColumn(
            "is_vip_transaction",
            (F.col("customer_tier") == "VIP") & (F.col("amount") > 1000)
        )
    
    def _add_quality_flags(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """Extract: Add data quality flags"""
        return df.withColumn(
            "has_complete_data",
            F.col("customer_id").isNotNull() & 
            F.col("amount").isNotNull() & 
            F.col("transaction_date").isNotNull()
        )
    
    def get_description(self) -> str:
        return "Extract Method: Separated complex logic into focused, reusable methods"


class SimplifyConditionalRefactoring(RefactoringStrategy):
    """
    Simplify Conditional refactoring pattern.
    
    Simplifies complex conditional logic using better patterns.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def refactor(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Refactor complex conditionals.
        
        Before: Nested when().otherwise() chains
        After: Clear, maintainable conditional logic
        """
        # BEFORE (complex):
        # df = df.withColumn("category",
        #     F.when((F.col("age") < 18), "Minor")
        #      .when((F.col("age") >= 18) & (F.col("age") < 25), "Young Adult")
        #      .when((F.col("age") >= 25) & (F.col("age") < 40), "Adult")
        #      .when((F.col("age") >= 40) & (F.col("age") < 60), "Middle Age")
        #      .otherwise("Senior"))
        
        # AFTER (simplified using case expression):
        return df.withColumn(
            "age_category",
            self._categorize_age(F.col("age"))
        )
    
    def _categorize_age(self, age_col: F.Column) -> F.Column:
        """Simplified age categorization"""
        return (
            F.when(age_col < 18, "Minor")
            .when(age_col < 25, "Young Adult")
            .when(age_col < 40,
```python
            .when(age_col < 40, "Adult")
            .when(age_col < 60, "Middle Age")
            .otherwise("Senior")
        )
    
    def get_description(self) -> str:
        return "Simplify Conditional: Replaced complex nested conditions with clearer logic"


class ReplaceLoopWithDataFrameOpsRefactoring(RefactoringStrategy):
    """
    Replace Loop with DataFrame Operations refactoring.
    
    Converts imperative loops to declarative DataFrame operations.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def refactor_before(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        BEFORE: Using loops (anti-pattern in Spark)
        
        This is what we're refactoring FROM
        """
        # Anti-pattern: Collecting and looping
        collected_data = df.collect()
        results = []
        
        for row in collected_data:
            if row['amount'] > 100:
                new_amount = row['amount'] * 1.1
                results.append((row['customer_id'], new_amount))
        
        # Convert back to DataFrame (inefficient!)
        result_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(
            results, 
            ["customer_id", "adjusted_amount"]
        )
        
        return result_df
    
    def refactor(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        AFTER: Using DataFrame operations (best practice)
        
        This is what we're refactoring TO
        """
        # Efficient: Using DataFrame transformations
        return df.filter(
            F.col("amount") > 100
        ).select(
            F.col("customer_id"),
            (F.col("amount") * 1.1).alias("adjusted_amount")
        )
    
    def get_description(self) -> str:
        return "Replace Loop: Converted imperative loops to declarative DataFrame operations"


class IntroduceParameterObjectRefactoring(RefactoringStrategy):
    """
    Introduce Parameter Object refactoring.
    
    Groups related parameters into cohesive objects.
    """
    
    @dataclass
    class TransformationConfig:
        """Parameter object for transformation configuration"""
        filter_threshold: float
        tax_rate: float
        discount_rate: float
        include_inactive: bool
        date_format: str
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, config: TransformationConfig):
        self.spark = spark
        self.config = config
    
    def refactor_before(
        self, 
        df: DataFrame,
        filter_threshold: float,
        tax_rate: float,
        discount_rate: float,
        include_inactive: bool,
        date_format: str
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        BEFORE: Many individual parameters (hard to maintain)
        """
        # Complex parameter list makes function hard to use
        pass
    
    def refactor(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        AFTER: Using parameter object (clean interface)
        """
        # Filter based on config
        if not self.config.include_inactive:
            df = df.filter(F.col("is_active") == True)
        
        # Apply transformations using config
        return df.filter(
            F.col("amount") > self.config.filter_threshold
        ).withColumn(
            "amount_with_tax",
            F.col("amount") * (1 + self.config.tax_rate)
        ).withColumn(
            "discounted_amount",
            F.col("amount") * (1 - self.config.discount_rate)
        )
    
    def get_description(self) -> str:
        return "Parameter Object: Grouped related parameters into cohesive configuration object"


class DecomposeComplexExpressionRefactoring(RefactoringStrategy):
    """
    Decompose Complex Expression refactoring.
    
    Breaks down complex expressions into intermediate variables.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def refactor_before(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        BEFORE: Complex, hard-to-read expression
        """
        # Complex expression in one line (hard to understand)
        return df.withColumn(
            "complex_metric",
            ((F.col("revenue") - F.col("cost")) / F.col("revenue") * 100) * 
            F.when(F.col("customer_tier") == "VIP", 1.2).otherwise(1.0) *
            F.when(F.datediff(F.current_date(), F.col("last_purchase")) < 30, 1.1).otherwise(0.9)
        )
    
    def refactor(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        AFTER: Decomposed into clear, intermediate steps
        """
        # Step 1: Calculate profit margin
        df = df.withColumn(
            "profit_margin_pct",
            (F.col("revenue") - F.col("cost")) / F.col("revenue") * 100
        )
        
        # Step 2: Apply tier multiplier
        df = df.withColumn(
            "tier_multiplier",
            F.when(F.col("customer_tier") == "VIP", 1.2).otherwise(1.0)
        )
        
        # Step 3: Apply recency multiplier
        df = df.withColumn(
            "recency_multiplier",
            F.when(
                F.datediff(F.current_date(), F.col("last_purchase")) < 30, 
                1.1
            ).otherwise(0.9)
        )
        
        # Step 4: Combine into final metric
        df = df.withColumn(
            "customer_value_score",
            F.col("profit_margin_pct") * 
            F.col("tier_multiplier") * 
            F.col("recency_multiplier")
        )
        
        return df
    
    def get_description(self) -> str:
        return "Decompose Expression: Broke complex expression into clear intermediate steps"


class ReplaceNestedJoinsRefactoring(RefactoringStrategy):
    """
    Replace Nested Joins refactoring.
    
    Optimizes multiple joins for better performance and readability.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def refactor_before(
        self, 
        transactions_df: DataFrame,
        customers_df: DataFrame,
        products_df: DataFrame,
        stores_df: DataFrame
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        BEFORE: Nested joins (hard to read and potentially inefficient)
        """
        # Nested joins
        result = transactions_df.join(
            customers_df.join(
                stores_df,
                customers_df.store_id == stores_df.store_id
            ),
            transactions_df.customer_id == customers_df.customer_id
        ).join(
            products_df,
            transactions_df.product_id == products_df.product_id
        )
        
        return result
    
    def refactor(
        self,
        transactions_df: DataFrame,
        customers_df: DataFrame,
        products_df: DataFrame,
        stores_df: DataFrame
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """
        AFTER: Sequential joins with clear intent
        """
        # Join customers with stores first (dimension enrichment)
        customers_enriched = customers_df.join(
            stores_df,
            "store_id",
            "left"
        )
        
        # Join transactions with enriched customers
        result = transactions_df.join(
            customers_enriched,
            "customer_id",
            "left"
        )
        
        # Join with products
        result = result.join(
            products_df,
            "product_id",
            "left"
        )
        
        return result
    
    def get_description(self) -> str:
        return "Replace Nested Joins: Flattened nested joins into sequential, readable operations"


class RefactoringManager:
    """
    Manages refactoring operations and tracks improvements.
    
    Provides tools for safely refactoring PySpark code while
    measuring impact and maintaining quality.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        """
        Initialize refactoring manager.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.refactorings: List[Tuple[str, RefactoringStrategy]] = []
        self.metrics_history: List[RefactoringMetrics] = []
    
    def register_refactoring(
        self,
        name: str,
        strategy: RefactoringStrategy
    ) -> None:
        """
        Register a refactoring strategy.
        
        Args:
            name: Name of the refactoring
            strategy: Refactoring strategy instance
        """
        self.refactorings.append((name, strategy))
        logger.info(f"Registered refactoring: {name}")
    
    def apply_refactoring(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        refactoring_name: str
    ) -> Tuple[DataFrame, str]:
        """
        Apply a specific refactoring.
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            refactoring_name: Name of refactoring to apply
            
        Returns:
            Tuple of (refactored DataFrame, description)
        """
        for name, strategy in self.refactorings:
            if name == refactoring_name:
                logger.info(f"Applying refactoring: {name}")
                refactored_df = strategy.refactor(df)
                description = strategy.get_description()
                return refactored_df, description
        
        raise ValueError(f"Refactoring '{refactoring_name}' not found")
    
    def verify_refactoring(
        self,
        original_df: DataFrame,
        refactored_df: DataFrame,
        key_columns: List[str]
    ) -> Dict[str, bool]:
        """
        Verify that refactoring maintains correctness.
        
        Args:
            original_df: Original DataFrame
            refactored_df: Refactored DataFrame
            key_columns: Columns to use for comparison
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with verification results
        """
        logger.info("Verifying refactoring correctness...")
        
        results = {
            "row_count_match": False,
            "schema_compatible": False,
            "data_integrity": False
        }
        
        # Check row counts
        original_count = original_df.count()
        refactored_count = refactored_df.count()
        results["row_count_match"] = (original_count == refactored_count)
        
        # Check schema compatibility (common columns)
        common_columns = set(original_df.columns) & set(refactored_df.columns)
        results["schema_compatible"] = len(common_columns) > 0
        
        # Check data integrity on key columns
        if key_columns and all(col in common_columns for col in key_columns):
            # Compare sorted data on key columns
            original_sorted = original_df.select(key_columns).orderBy(key_columns)
            refactored_sorted = refactored_df.select(key_columns).orderBy(key_columns)
            
            # Simple check: compare first and last rows
            original_first = original_sorted.first()
            refactored_first = refactored_sorted.first()
            
            results["data_integrity"] = (original_first == refactored_first)
        
        return results
    
    def generate_refactoring_report(self) -> str:
        """
        Generate comprehensive refactoring report.
        
        Returns:
            Formatted report string
        """
        report_lines = [
            "=" * 80,
            "REFACTORING REPORT",
            "=" * 80,
            f"\nGenerated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}",
            f"\nTotal Refactorings Applied: {len(self.refactorings)}\n"
        ]
        
        report_lines.append("REGISTERED REFACTORINGS:")
        report_lines.append("-" * 80)
        
        for i, (name, strategy) in enumerate(self.refactorings, 1):
            report_lines.append(f"\n{i}. {name}")
            report_lines.append(f"   Description: {strategy.get_description()}")
        
        if self.metrics_history:
            report_lines.append("\n\nPERFORMANCE METRICS:")
            report_lines.append("-" * 80)
            
            for i, metrics in enumerate(self.metrics_history, 1):
                report_lines.append(f"\nRefactoring #{i}:")
                report_lines.append(f"  Code Complexity: {metrics.code_complexity_before} → {metrics.code_complexity_after}")
                report_lines.append(f"  Lines of Code: {metrics.lines_of_code_before} → {metrics.lines_of_code_after}")
                report_lines.append(f"  Performance: {metrics.performance_before:.2f}s → {metrics.performance_after:.2f}s")
                
                perf_improvement = metrics.improvement_percentage("performance")
                report_lines.append(f"  Performance Improvement: {perf_improvement:.1f}%")
        
        report_lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
        
        return "\n".join(report_lines)


class LegacyCodeRefactorer:
    """
    Example class demonstrating refactoring of legacy code.
    
    Shows before/after comparisons of common refactoring scenarios.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
    
    def legacy_process_sales(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        LEGACY CODE (Before Refactoring)
        
        Issues:
        - Complex nested logic
        - No separation of concerns
        - Hard to test
        - Poor performance (multiple actions)
        - Magic numbers
        """
        # All logic crammed together
        df = df.filter(F.col("amount") > 0)
        
        # Complex nested conditions
        df = df.withColumn("category",
            F.when((F.col("amount") < 50) & (F.col("customer_type") == "new"), "small_new")
             .when((F.col("amount") < 50) & (F.col("customer_type") == "existing"), "small_existing")
             .when((F.col("amount") >= 50) & (F.col("amount") < 200) & (F.col("customer_type") == "new"), "medium_new")
             .when((F.col("amount") >= 50) & (F.col("amount") < 200) & (F.col("customer_type") == "existing"), "medium_existing")
             .otherwise("large"))
        
        # Multiple actions without caching
        count1 = df.count()
        count2 = df.filter(F.col("category").like("%new%")).count()
        
        # Magic numbers everywhere
        df = df.withColumn("adjusted_amount", F.col("amount") * 1.08 * 0.95)
        
        return df
    
    def refactored_process_sales(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        REFACTORED CODE (After Refactoring)
        
        Improvements:
        - Clear separation of concerns
        - Named constants
        - Simplified logic
        - Better performance
        - Testable components
        """
        # Constants (no magic numbers)
        SMALL_THRESHOLD = 50
        MEDIUM_THRESHOLD = 200
        TAX_RATE = 1
```python
        TAX_RATE = 1.08
        DISCOUNT_RATE = 0.95
        
        # Clean data
        df = self._filter_valid_transactions(df)
        
        # Categorize transactions
        df = self._categorize_by_amount_and_type(df, SMALL_THRESHOLD, MEDIUM_THRESHOLD)
        
        # Apply pricing adjustments
        df = self._apply_pricing_adjustments(df, TAX_RATE, DISCOUNT_RATE)
        
        # Cache for reuse
        df = df.cache()
        
        return df
    
    def _filter_valid_transactions(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """Filter out invalid transactions"""
        return df.filter(F.col("amount") > 0)
    
    def _categorize_by_amount_and_type(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        small_threshold: float,
        medium_threshold: float
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """Categorize transactions by amount and customer type"""
        # Simplified logic using helper function
        return df.withColumn(
            "amount_category",
            F.when(F.col("amount") < small_threshold, "small")
             .when(F.col("amount") < medium_threshold, "medium")
             .otherwise("large")
        ).withColumn(
            "category",
            F.concat(
                F.col("amount_category"),
                F.lit("_"),
                F.col("customer_type")
            )
        )
    
    def _apply_pricing_adjustments(
        self,
        df: DataFrame,
        tax_rate: float,
        discount_rate: float
    ) -> DataFrame:
        """Apply tax and discount to amounts"""
        return df.withColumn(
            "adjusted_amount",
            F.col("amount") * tax_rate * discount_rate
        )

## 6. Technical Debt Management Pattern

```python
"""
Technical Debt Management Pattern for PySpark
Demonstrates tracking, measuring, and managing technical debt in PySpark applications.

This module provides a comprehensive framework for identifying, prioritizing,
and resolving technical debt in data engineering projects.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.types import StructType, StructField, StringType, IntegerType, DoubleType, TimestampType, BooleanType
from typing import List, Dict, Optional, Set, Any
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta
from enum import Enum
import logging

logging.basicConfig(level=logging.INFO)
logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)


class DebtType(Enum):
    """Types of technical debt"""
    CODE_QUALITY = "code_quality"
    PERFORMANCE = "performance"
    ARCHITECTURE = "architecture"
    DOCUMENTATION = "documentation"
    TESTING = "testing"
    SECURITY = "security"
    SCALABILITY = "scalability"


class DebtPriority(Enum):
    """Priority levels for technical debt"""
    CRITICAL = 1
    HIGH = 2
    MEDIUM = 3
    LOW = 4


class DebtStatus(Enum):
    """Status of technical debt items"""
    IDENTIFIED = "identified"
    PLANNED = "planned"
    IN_PROGRESS = "in_progress"
    RESOLVED = "resolved"
    WONT_FIX = "wont_fix"


@dataclass
class TechnicalDebtItem:
    """
    Represents a single technical debt item.
    
    Attributes:
        debt_id: Unique identifier
        title: Brief description
        description: Detailed description
        debt_type: Type of technical debt
        priority: Priority level
        status: Current status
        component: Affected component/module
        estimated_effort_hours: Estimated hours to resolve
        interest_rate: Cost accumulation rate (0-1)
        created_date: When debt was identified
        resolved_date: When debt was resolved (if applicable)
        assigned_to: Person/team responsible
        related_issues: List of related issue IDs
    """
    debt_id: str
    title: str
    description: str
    debt_type: DebtType
    priority: DebtPriority
    status: DebtStatus
    component: str
    estimated_effort_hours: float
    interest_rate: float  # 0.0 to 1.0
    created_date: datetime = field(default_factory=datetime.now)
    resolved_date: Optional[datetime] = None
    assigned_to: Optional[str] = None
    related_issues: List[str] = field(default_factory=list)
    
    def calculate_cost(self) -> float:
        """
        Calculate accumulated cost of technical debt.
        
        Cost increases over time based on interest rate.
        
        Returns:
            Accumulated cost in effort-hours
        """
        days_open = (datetime.now() - self.created_date).days
        accumulated_cost = self.estimated_effort_hours * (1 + self.interest_rate * days_open / 30)
        return accumulated_cost
    
    def to_dict(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """Convert to dictionary"""
        return {
            "debt_id": self.debt_id,
            "title": self.title,
            "description": self.description,
            "debt_type": self.debt_type.value,
            "priority": self.priority.value,
            "status": self.status.value,
            "component": self.component,
            "estimated_effort_hours": self.estimated_effort_hours,
            "interest_rate": self.interest_rate,
            "accumulated_cost": self.calculate_cost(),
            "created_date": self.created_date.isoformat(),
            "resolved_date": self.resolved_date.isoformat() if self.resolved_date else None,
            "assigned_to": self.assigned_to,
            "related_issues": self.related_issues
        }


class TechnicalDebtTracker:
    """
    Tracks and manages technical debt across PySpark projects.
    
    Provides tools for:
    - Identifying technical debt
    - Prioritizing debt items
    - Tracking resolution progress
    - Measuring debt impact
    - Generating reports
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession, project_name: str):
        """
        Initialize technical debt tracker.
        
        Args:
            spark: Active SparkSession
            project_name: Name of the project
        """
        self.spark = spark
        self.project_name = project_name
        self.debt_items: List[TechnicalDebtItem] = []
        self.debt_counter = 0
    
    def _generate_debt_id(self) -> str:
        """Generate unique debt ID"""
        self.debt_counter += 1
        return f"DEBT-{self.debt_counter:04d}"
    
    def add_debt_item(
        self,
        title: str,
        description: str,
        debt_type: DebtType,
        priority: DebtPriority,
        component: str,
        estimated_effort_hours: float,
        interest_rate: float = 0.1,
        assigned_to: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> TechnicalDebtItem:
        """
        Add a new technical debt item.
        
        Args:
            title: Brief title
            description: Detailed description
            debt_type: Type of debt
            priority: Priority level
            component: Affected component
            estimated_effort_hours: Estimated resolution effort
            interest_rate: Cost accumulation rate
            assigned_to: Assignee
            
        Returns:
            Created TechnicalDebtItem
        """
        debt_item = TechnicalDebtItem(
            debt_id=self._generate_debt_id(),
            title=title,
            description=description,
            debt_type=debt_type,
            priority=priority,
            status=DebtStatus.IDENTIFIED,
            component=component,
            estimated_effort_hours=estimated_effort_hours,
            interest_rate=interest_rate,
            assigned_to=assigned_to
        )
        
        self.debt_items.append(debt_item)
        logger.info(f"Added technical debt: {debt_item.debt_id} - {title}")
        
        return debt_item
    
    def update_debt_status(
        self,
        debt_id: str,
        new_status: DebtStatus,
        notes: Optional[str] = None
    ) -> bool:
        """
        Update status of a debt item.
        
        Args:
            debt_i
```python
            debt_id: Debt item ID
            new_status: New status
            notes: Optional notes
            
        Returns:
            True if updated successfully
        """
        for debt in self.debt_items:
            if debt.debt_id == debt_id:
                old_status = debt.status
                debt.status = new_status
                
                if new_status == DebtStatus.RESOLVED:
                    debt.resolved_date = datetime.now()
                
                logger.info(f"Updated {debt_id}: {old_status.value} → {new_status.value}")
                if notes:
                    logger.info(f"Notes: {notes}")
                
                return True
        
        logger.warning(f"Debt item {debt_id} not found")
        return False
    
    def get_debt_by_priority(self, priority: DebtPriority) -> List[TechnicalDebtItem]:
        """Get debt items by priority"""
        return [d for d in self.debt_items if d.priority == priority]
    
    def get_debt_by_type(self, debt_type: DebtType) -> List[TechnicalDebtItem]:
        """Get debt items by type"""
        return [d for d in self.debt_items if d.debt_type == debt_type]
    
    def get_debt_by_status(self, status: DebtStatus) -> List[TechnicalDebtItem]:
        """Get debt items by status"""
        return [d for d in self.debt_items if d.status == status]
    
    def get_debt_by_component(self, component: str) -> List[TechnicalDebtItem]:
        """Get debt items by component"""
        return [d for d in self.debt_items if d.component == component]
    
    def calculate_total_debt(self, include_resolved: bool = False) -> Dict[str, float]:
        """
        Calculate total technical debt metrics.
        
        Args:
            include_resolved: Whether to include resolved items
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with debt metrics
        """
        items = self.debt_items
        if not include_resolved:
            items = [d for d in items if d.status != DebtStatus.RESOLVED]
        
        total_estimated_hours = sum(d.estimated_effort_hours for d in items)
        total_accumulated_cost = sum(d.calculate_cost() for d in items)
        
        return {
            "total_items": len(items),
            "total_estimated_hours": total_estimated_hours,
            "total_accumulated_cost": total_accumulated_cost,
            "average_interest_rate": sum(d.interest_rate for d in items) / len(items) if items else 0,
            "average_age_days": sum((datetime.now() - d.created_date).days for d in items) / len(items) if items else 0
        }
    
    def prioritize_debt(self) -> List[TechnicalDebtItem]:
        """
        Prioritize debt items based on multiple factors.
        
        Considers:
        - Priority level
        - Accumulated cost
        - Component criticality
        - Dependencies
        
        Returns:
            Sorted list of debt items
        """
        # Calculate priority score for each item
        scored_items = []
        
        for debt in self.debt_items:
            if debt.status in [DebtStatus.IDENTIFIED, DebtStatus.PLANNED]:
                # Priority score components
                priority_score = (5 - debt.priority.value) * 100  # Higher priority = higher score
                cost_score = debt.calculate_cost()
                age_score = (datetime.now() - debt.created_date).days
                
                # Combined score
                total_score = priority_score + cost_score + (age_score * 0.5)
                
                scored_items.append((total_score, debt))
        
        # Sort by score (descending)
        scored_items.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
        
        return [debt for score, debt in scored_items]
    
    def generate_debt_report(self, report_type: str = "summary") -> str:
        """
        Generate technical debt report.
        
        Args:
            report_type: Type of report ('summary', 'detailed', 'dashboard')
            
        Returns:
            Formatted report string
        """
        if report_type == "summary":
            return self._generate_summary_report()
        elif report_type == "detailed":
            return self._generate_detailed_report()
        elif report_type == "dashboard":
            return self._generate_dashboard_report()
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"Unknown report type: {report_type}")
    
    def _generate_summary_report(self) -> str:
        """Generate summary report"""
        lines = [
            "=" * 80,
            f"TECHNICAL DEBT SUMMARY - {self.project_name}",
            "=" * 80,
            f"\nGenerated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n"
        ]
        
        # Overall metrics
        metrics = self.calculate_total_debt()
        lines.append("OVERALL METRICS:")
        lines.append("-" * 40)
        lines.append(f"Total Debt Items: {metrics['total_items']}")
        lines.append(f"Estimated Effort: {metrics['total_estimated_hours']:.1f} hours")
        lines.append(f"Accumulated Cost: {metrics['total_accumulated_cost']:.1f} hours")
        lines.append(f"Average Age: {metrics['average_age_days']:.1f} days")
        
        # By priority
        lines.append("\n\nBY PRIORITY:")
        lines.append("-" * 40)
        for priority in DebtPriority:
            items = self.get_debt_by_priority(priority)
            if items:
                total_cost = sum(d.calculate_cost() for d in items)
                lines.append(f"{priority.name}: {len(items)} items ({total_cost:.1f} hours)")
        
        # By type
        lines.append("\n\nBY TYPE:")
        lines.append("-" * 40)
        for debt_type in DebtType:
            items = self.get_debt_by_type(debt_type)
            if items:
                lines.append(f"{debt_type.value}: {len(items)} items")
        
        # By status
        lines.append("\n\nBY STATUS:")
        lines.append("-" * 40)
        for status in DebtStatus:
            items = self.get_debt_by_status(status)
            lines.append(f"{status.value}: {len(items)} items")
        
        lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
        
        return "\n".join(lines)
    
    def _generate_detailed_report(self) -> str:
        """Generate detailed report"""
        lines = [
            "=" * 80,
            f"TECHNICAL DEBT DETAILED REPORT - {self.project_name}",
            "=" * 80,
            f"\nGenerated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n"
        ]
        
        # Prioritized list
        prioritized = self.prioritize_debt()
        
        lines.append("PRIORITIZED DEBT ITEMS:")
        lines.append("-" * 80)
        
        for i, debt in enumerate(prioritized, 1):
            lines.append(f"\n{i}. [{debt.debt_id}] {debt.title}")
            lines.append(f"   Priority: {debt.priority.name}")
            lines.append(f"   Type: {debt.debt_type.value}")
            lines.append(f"   Component: {debt.component}")
            lines.append(f"   Status: {debt.status.value}")
            lines.append(f"   Estimated Effort: {debt.estimated_effort_hours:.1f} hours")
            lines.append(f"   Accumulated Cost: {debt.calculate_cost():.1f} hours")
            lines.append(f"   Age: {(datetime.now() - debt.created_date).days} days")
            if debt.assigned_to:
                lines.append(f"   Assigned To: {debt.assigned_to}")
            lines.append(f"   Description: {debt.description}")
        
        lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
        
        return "\n".join(lines)
    
    def _generate_dashboard_report(self) -> str:
        """Generate dashboard-style report"""
        lines = [
            "=" * 80,
            f"TECHNICAL DEBT DASHBOARD - {self.project_name}",
            "=" * 80,
            f"\nGenerated: {datetime.now().strftime('%Y-%m-%d %H:%M:%S')}\n"
        ]
        
        metrics = self.calculate_total_debt()
        
        # Key metrics
        lines.append("KEY METRICS:")
        lines.append("┌" + "─" * 78 + "┐")
        lines.append(f"│ Total Items: {metrics['total_items']:>10} │ Accumulated Cost: {metrics['total_accumulated_cost']:>10.1f} hours │")
        lines.append(f"│ Est. Effort: {metrics['total_estimated_hours']:>10.1f} hrs │ Avg Age: {metrics['average_age_days']:>18.1f} days │")
        lines.append("└" + "─" * 78 + "┘")
        
        # Top 5 critical items
        critical_items = sorted(
            [d for d in self.debt_items if d.status != DebtStatus.RESOLVED],
            key=lambda x: x.calculate_cost(),
            reverse=True
        )[:5]
        
        lines.append("\n\nTOP 5 CRITICAL ITEMS:")
        lines.append("-" * 80)
        for i, debt in enumerate(critical_items, 1):
            lines.append(f"{i}. {debt.title} ({debt.calculate_cost():.1f} hrs)")
        
        # Components with most debt
        component_debt: Dict[str, float] = {}
        for debt in self.debt_items:
            if debt.status != DebtStatus.RESOLVED:
                component_debt[debt.component] = component_debt.get(debt.component, 0) + debt.calculate_cost()
        
        lines.append("\n\nCOMPONENTS WITH MOST DEBT:")
        lines.append("-" * 80)
        sorted_components = sorted(component_debt.items(), key=lambda x: x[1], reverse=True)[:5]
        for component, cost in sorted_components:
            lines.append(f"{component}: {cost:.1f} hours")
        
        # Trend analysis
        recent_items = [d for d in self.debt_items if (datetime.now() - d.created_date).days <= 30]
        resolved_recent = [d for d in recent_items if d.status == DebtStatus.RESOLVED]
        
        lines.append("\n\n30-DAY TREND:")
        lines.append("-" * 80)
        lines.append(f"New Items: {len(recent_items)}")
        lines.append(f"Resolved Items: {len(resolved_recent)}")
        lines.append(f"Net Change: {len(recent_items) - len(resolved_recent):+d}")
        
        lines.append("\n" + "=" * 80)
        
        return "\n".join(lines)
    
    def export_to_dataframe(self) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Export debt items to Spark DataFrame.
        
        Returns:
            DataFrame with all debt items
        """
        data = [debt.to_dict() for debt in self.debt_items]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("debt_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("title", StringType(), False),
            StructField("description", StringType(), True),
            StructField("debt_type", StringType(), False),
            StructField("priority", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("status", StringType(), False),
            StructField("component", StringType(), False),
            StructField("estimated_effort_hours", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("interest_rate", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("accumulated_cost", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("created_date", StringType(), False),
            StructField("resolved_date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("assigned_to", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Convert dict list to DataFrame-compatible format
        records = []
        for d in data:
            records.append((
                d['debt_id'],
                d['title'],
                d['description'],
                d['debt_type'],
                d['priority'],
                d['status'],
                d['component'],
                d['estimated_effort_hours'],
                d['interest_rate'],
                d['accumulated_cost'],
                d['created_date'],
                d['resolved_date'],
                d['assigned_to']
            ))
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(records, schema)


class DebtAnalyzer:
    """
    Analyzes technical debt patterns and provides insights.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, tracker: TechnicalDebtTracker):
        """
        Initialize debt analyzer.
        
        Args:
            tracker: TechnicalDebtTracker instance
        """
        self.tracker = tracker
    
    def analyze_debt_trends(self) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Analyze debt accumulation trends.
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary with trend analysis
        """
        items = self.tracker.debt_items
        
        if not items:
            return {"error": "No debt items to analyze"}
        
        # Group by month
        monthly_data: Dict[str, List[TechnicalDebtItem]] = {}
        for debt in items:
            month_key = debt.created_date.strftime("%Y-%m")
            if month_key not in monthly_data:
                monthly_data[month_key] = []
            monthly_data[month_key].append(debt)
        
        # Calculate monthly metrics
        monthly_metrics = {}
        for month, debts in sorted(monthly_data.items()):
            monthly_metrics[month] = {
                "new_items": len(debts),
                "total_effort": sum(d.estimated_effort_hours for d in debts),
                "avg_priority": sum(d.priority.value for d in debts) / len(debts)
            }
        
        return {
            "monthly_trends": monthly_metrics,
            "total_months": len(monthly_data),
            "average_new_per_month": len(items) / len(monthly_data)
        }
    
    def identify_hotspots(self) -> List[Dict[str, Any]]:
        """
        Identify components with highest debt concentration.
        
        Returns:
            List of hotspot components
        """
        component_analysis: Dict[str, Dict[str, Any]] = {}
        
        for debt in self.tracker.debt_items:
            if debt.status != DebtStatus.RESOLVED:
                if debt.component not in component_analysis:
                    component_analysis[debt.component] = {
                        "component": debt.component,
                        "item_count": 0,
                        "total_cost": 0.0,
                        "critical_count": 0
                    }
                
                component_analysis[debt.component]["item_count"] += 1
                component_analysis[debt.component]["total_cost"] += debt.calculate_cost()
                
                if debt.priority == DebtPriority.CRITICAL:
                    component_analysis[debt.component]["critical_count"] += 1
        
        #
```python
        # Sort by total cost
        hotspots = sorted(
            component_analysis.values(),
            key=lambda x: x["total_cost"],
            reverse=True
        )
        
        return hotspots
    
    def recommend_resolution_order(self) -> List[TechnicalDebtItem]:
        """
        Recommend order for resolving debt items.
        
        Uses multiple factors:
        - ROI (return on investment)
        - Priority
        - Dependencies
        - Effort required
        
        Returns:
            Ordered list of debt items
        """
        unresolved = [
            d for d in self.tracker.debt_items 
            if d.status not in [DebtStatus.RESOLVED, DebtStatus.WONT_FIX]
        ]
        
        # Calculate ROI score for each item
        scored_items = []
        for debt in unresolved:
            # ROI = (accumulated_cost - effort) / effort
            # Higher accumulated cost and lower effort = better ROI
            accumulated_cost = debt.calculate_cost()
            effort = debt.estimated_effort_hours
            
            if effort > 0:
                roi = (accumulated_cost - effort) / effort
            else:
                roi = 0
            
            # Adjust for priority
            priority_multiplier = {
                DebtPriority.CRITICAL: 3.0,
                DebtPriority.HIGH: 2.0,
                DebtPriority.MEDIUM: 1.5,
                DebtPriority.LOW: 1.0
            }
            
            final_score = roi * priority_multiplier[debt.priority]
            scored_items.append((final_score, debt))
        
        # Sort by score
        scored_items.sort(key=lambda x: x[0], reverse=True)
        
        return [debt for score, debt in scored_items]
    
    def calculate_payback_period(
        self,
        debt_item: TechnicalDebtItem,
        team_velocity_hours_per_week: float = 40
    ) -> Dict[str, Any]:
        """
        Calculate payback period for resolving a debt item.
        
        Args:
            debt_item: Debt item to analyze
            team_velocity_hours_per_week: Team's available hours per week
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with payback analysis
        """
        effort = debt_item.estimated_effort_hours
        current_cost = debt_item.calculate_cost()
        weekly_interest = debt_item.estimated_effort_hours * debt_item.interest_rate / 4
        
        # Calculate weeks to payback
        if weekly_interest > 0:
            payback_weeks = effort / weekly_interest
        else:
            payback_weeks = float('inf')
        
        # Calculate time to resolve
        resolution_weeks = effort / team_velocity_hours_per_week
        
        return {
            "debt_id": debt_item.debt_id,
            "title": debt_item.title,
            "effort_hours": effort,
            "current_cost_hours": current_cost,
            "weekly_interest_hours": weekly_interest,
            "payback_weeks": payback_weeks,
            "resolution_weeks": resolution_weeks,
            "is_worthwhile": payback_weeks < 52  # Payback within a year
        }

"""
PySpark Data Comparison Patterns
Comprehensive implementation of various data comparison techniques
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql import functions as F
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from pyspark.sql.window import Window
from typing import Dict, List, Tuple, Optional
import hashlib
from datetime import datetime

# Initialize Spark Session
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("DataComparisonPatterns") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
    .getOrCreate()

spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")

# 1. SCHEMA COMPARISON PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class SchemaComparison:
    """
    Compares schemas of two DataFrames to identify structural differences
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_schemas(df1: DataFrame, df2: DataFrame, 
                       df1_name: str = "DF1", 
                       df2_name: str = "DF2") -> Dict:
        """
        Comprehensive schema comparison
        
        Args:
            df1: First DataFrame
            df2: Second DataFrame
            df1_name: Name identifier for first DataFrame
            df2_name: Name identifier for second DataFrame
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary containing schema comparison results
        """
        schema1 = {field.name: field for field in df1.schema.fields}
        schema2 = {field.name: field for field in df2.schema.fields}
        
        # Find columns only in df1
        only_in_df1 = set(schema1.keys()) - set(schema2.keys())
        
        # Find columns only in df2
        only_in_df2 = set(schema2.keys()) - set(schema1.keys())
        
        # Find common columns
        common_columns = set(schema1.keys()) & set(schema2.keys())
        
        # Check data type differences in common columns
        type_differences = {}
        nullable_differences = {}
        
        for col in common_columns:
            if schema1[col].dataType != schema2[col].dataType:
                type_differences[col] = {
                    df1_name: str(schema1[col].dataType),
                    df2_name: str(schema2[col].dataType)
                }
            
            if schema1[col].nullable != schema2[col].nullable:
                nullable_differences[col] = {
                    df1_name: schema1[col].nullable,
                    df2_name: schema2[col].nullable
                }
        
        # Create comparison report
        comparison_result = {
            "schemas_match": len(only_in_df1) == 0 and 
                           len(only_in_df2) == 0 and 
                           len(type_differences) == 0,
            "column_count": {
                df1_name: len(schema1),
                df2_name: len(schema2)
            },
            "columns_only_in_" + df1_name: list(only_in_df1),
            "columns_only_in_" + df2_name: list(only_in_df2),
            "common_columns": list(common_columns),
            "type_differences": type_differences,
            "nullable_differences": nullable_differences
        }
        
        return comparison_result
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_schema_comparison(comparison_result: Dict):
        """Pretty print schema comparison results"""
        print("=" * 80)
        print("SCHEMA COMPARISON REPORT")
        print("=" * 80)
        print(f"\nSchemas Match: {comparison_result['schemas_match']}")
        print(f"\nColumn Counts: {comparison_result['column_count']}")
        
        for key, value in comparison_result.items():
            if key.startswith("columns_only_in_"):
                if value:
                    print(f"\n{key}: {value}")
            elif key == "type_differences" and value:
                print("\nData Type Differences:")
                for col, types in value.items():
                    print(f"  {col}: {types}")
            elif key == "nullable_differences" and value:
                print("\nNullable Differences:")
                for col, nullable in value.items():
                    print(f"  {col}: {nullable}")
