# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: INTERACTIVE MODE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Ad-hoc queries and exploratory data analysis
# Use Case: Data exploration, debugging, prototyping

class InteractiveModePattern:
    """
    Interactive Mode Pattern for ad-hoc data exploration and analysis.
    Typically used in notebooks (Jupyter, Databricks) for quick insights.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("InteractiveModePattern") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "4") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
    
    def create_sample_data(self):
        """Create sample data for interactive exploration"""
        data = [
            (1, "Alice", "Engineering", 75000, "2020-01-15"),
            (2, "Bob", "Marketing", 65000, "2019-03-20"),
            (3, "Charlie", "Engineering", 85000, "2018-07-10"),
            (4, "Diana", "HR", 60000, "2021-02-28"),
            (5, "Eve", "Engineering", 90000, "2017-11-05"),
            (6, "Frank", "Marketing", 70000, "2020-06-12"),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("name", StringType(), True),
            StructField("department", StringType(), True),
            StructField("salary", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("hire_date", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def interactive_analysis(self):
        """Demonstrate interactive analysis capabilities"""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("PATTERN 1: INTERACTIVE MODE PATTERN")
        print("="*60)
        
        df = self.create_sample_data()
        
        # Quick data exploration
        print("\n1. Quick Data Preview:")
        df.show(5)
        
        # Schema inspection
        print("\n2. Schema Inspection:")
        df.printSchema()
        
        # Summary statistics
        print("\n3. Summary Statistics:")
        df.describe().show()
        
        # Ad-hoc queries
        print("\n4. Department-wise Analysis:")
        dept_analysis = df.groupBy("department") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("employee_count"),
                avg("salary").alias("avg_salary"),
                max("salary").alias("max_salary")
            ) \
            .orderBy(desc("avg_salary"))
        
        dept_analysis.show()
        
        # Interactive filtering
        print("\n5. High Earners (>70000):")
        high_earners = df.filter(col("salary") > 70000) \
            .select("name", "department", "salary")
        high_earners.show()
        
        # Quick visualization data preparation
        print("\n6. Data for Visualization:")
        viz_data = df.groupBy("department") \
            .count() \
            .toPandas()  # Convert to pandas for easy plotting
        print(viz_data)
        
        return df
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Stop the Spark session"""
        self.spark.stop()


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 2: BATCH MODE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Process large volumes of data in scheduled batches
# Use Case: ETL jobs, daily reports, data warehousing

class BatchModePattern:
    """
    Batch Mode Pattern for processing large datasets in scheduled intervals.
    Optimized for throughput over latency.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("BatchModePattern") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "8") \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
    
    def create_large_dataset(self):
        """Create a larger dataset simulating batch processing"""
        # Simulate transaction data
        from random import randint, choice
        
        departments = ["Sales", "Engineering", "Marketing", "HR", "Finance"]
        products = ["Product_A", "Product_B", "Product_C", "Product_D"]
        
        data = [
            (
                i,
                f"2024-01-{(i % 28) + 1:02d}",
                choice(departments),
                choice(products),
                randint(100, 10000),
                randint(1, 100)
            )
            for i in range(1, 10001)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("transaction_id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("department", StringType(), True),
            StructField("product", StringType(), True),
            StructField("amount", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("quantity", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def batch_processing_job(self):
        """Execute a complete batch processing job"""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("PATTERN 2: BATCH MODE PATTERN")
        print("="*60)
        
        start_time = time.time()
        
        # Step 1: Extract
        print("\n1. EXTRACT: Loading data...")
        df = self.create_large_dataset()
        print(f"   Loaded {df.count()} records")
        
        # Step 2: Transform
        print("\n2. TRANSFORM: Processing data...")
        
        # Add calculated columns
        transformed_df = df.withColumn("total_value", col("amount") * col("quantity")) \
            .withColumn("date_parsed", to_date(col("date"), "yyyy-MM-dd")) \
            .withColumn("month", month(col("date_parsed"))) \
            .withColumn("year", year(col("date_parsed")))
        
        # Aggregate by department and product
        aggregated_df = transformed_df.groupBy("department", "product", "month") \
            .agg(
                sum("total_value").alias("total_revenue"),
                sum("quantity").alias("total_quantity"),
                count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
                avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
            )
        
        print("\n   Aggregated Results:")
        aggregated_df.orderBy(desc("total_revenue")).show(10)
        
        # Step 3: Load (simulate writing to storage)
        print("\n3. LOAD: Writing results...")
        output_path = "/tmp/batch_output"
        
        # Partition by department for efficient querying
        aggregated_df.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("department") \
            .parquet(output_path)
        
        print(f"   Data written to {output_path}")
        
        # Step 4: Quality Checks
        print("\n4. QUALITY CHECKS:")
        
        # Check for nulls
        null_counts = transformed_df.select(
            [sum(col(c).isNull().cast("int")).alias(c) 
             for c in transformed_df.columns]
        )
        print("   Null counts:")
        null_counts.show()
        
        # Data validation
        invalid_records = transformed_df.filter(
            (col("amount") <= 0) | (col("quantity") <= 0)
        ).count()
        print(f"   Invalid records: {invalid_records}")
        
        end_time = time.time()
        print(f"\n5. EXECUTION TIME: {end_time - start_time:.2f} seconds")
        
        return aggregated_df
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Stop the Spark session"""
        self.spark.stop()


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 3: STREAMING MODE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Continuous processing of data streams
# Use Case: Real-time analytics, event processing, monitoring

class StreamingModePattern:
    """
    Streaming Mode Pattern for continuous data processing.
    Uses Structured Streaming for fault-tolerant stream processing.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("StreamingModePattern") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .config("spark.sql.streaming.schemaInference", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
    
    def create_streaming_source(self):
        """Create a simulated streaming data source"""
        # Define schema for streaming data
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), True),
            StructField("user_id", IntegerType(), True),
            StructField("event_type", StringType(), True),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Create a rate source for demonstration
        # In production, this would be Kafka, Kinesis, etc.
        stream_df = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("rate") \
            .option("rowsPerSecond", 10) \
            .load() \
            .withColumn("user_id", (rand() * 1000).cast("int")) \
            .withColumn("event_type", 
                       when(col("value") % 3 == 0, "click")
                       .when(col("value") % 3 == 1, "view")
                       .otherwise("purchase")) \
            .withColumn("value", rand() * 100)
        
        return stream_df
    
    def streaming_processing(self):
        """Demonstrate streaming data processing"""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("PATTERN 3: STREAMING MODE PATTERN")
        print("="*60)
        
        stream_df = self.create_streaming_source()
        
        # Streaming aggregations with windowing
        print("\n1. Setting up streaming aggregations...")
        
        windowed_counts = stream_df \
            .withWatermark("timestamp", "10 seconds") \
            .groupBy(
                window(col("timestamp"), "10 seconds", "5 seconds"),
                col("event_type")
            ) \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("event_count"),
                avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
                max("value").alias("max_value")
            )
        
        # Start the streaming query with console output
        print("\n2. Starting streaming query (will run for 30 seconds)...")
        
        query = windowed_counts.writeStream \
            .outputMode("update") \
            .format("console") \
            .option("truncate", "false") \
            .option("numRows", 20) \
            .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        # Let it run for a short time
        query.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
        query.stop()
        
        print("\n3. Streaming query completed")
        
        return stream_df
    
    def stateful_streaming(self):
        """Demonstrate stateful streaming with state management"""
        print("\n4. Stateful Streaming Example:")
        
        stream_df = self.create_streaming_source()
        
        # Running aggregation (stateful)
        running_totals = stream_df \
            .groupBy("event_type") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("total_count"),
                sum("value").alias("total_value")
            )
        
        query = running_totals.writeStream \
            .outputMode("complete") \
            .format("console") \
            .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        query.awaitTermination(timeout=20)
        query.stop()
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Stop the Spark session"""
        self.spark.stop()

# PATTERN 4: HYBRID MODE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Combine batch and streaming processing
# Use Case: Lambda architecture, combining historical and real-time data

class HybridModePattern:
    """
    Hybrid Mode Pattern combining batch and streaming processing.
    Implements Lambda Architecture principles.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("HybridModePattern") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
    
    def create_batch_layer(self):
        """Create historical batch data (batch layer)"""
        # Historical data
        data = [
            ("2024-01-01", "user_1", "product_A", 100),
            ("2024-01-01", "user_2", "product_B", 150),
            ("2024-01-02", "user_1", "product_C", 200),
            ("2024-01-02", "user_3", "product_A", 120),
            ("2024-01-03", "user_2", "product_B", 180),
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("date", StringType(), True),
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("product", StringType(), True),
            StructField("amount", IntegerType(), True)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def create_speed_layer(self):
        """Create streaming data source (speed layer)"""
        # Simulated real-time data
        stream_df = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("rate") \
            .option("rowsPerSecond", 5) \
            .load() \
            .withColumn("user_id", concat(lit("user_"), (rand() * 5).cast("int"))) \
            .withColumn("product", concat(lit("product_"), 
                       when(col("value") % 3 == 0, "A")
                       .when(col("value") % 3 == 1, "B")
                       .otherwise("C"))) \
            .withColumn("amount", (rand() * 200).cast("int")) \
            .withColumn("date", current_date().cast("string")) \
            .select("date", "user_id", "product", "amount")
        
        return stream_df
    
    def hybrid_processing(self):
        """Demonstrate hybrid batch + streaming processing"""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("PATTERN 4: HYBRID MODE PATTERN")
        print("="*60)
        
        # Batch Layer Processing
        print("\n1. BATCH LAYER: Processing historical data...")
        batch_df = self.create_batch_layer()
        
        batch_aggregates = batch_df
```python
        batch_aggregates = batch_df.groupBy("product") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("historical_total"),
                count("*").alias("historical_count"),
                avg("amount").alias("historical_avg")
            )
        
        print("   Historical Aggregates:")
        batch_aggregates.show()
        
        # Speed Layer Processing
        print("\n2. SPEED LAYER: Processing real-time data...")
        stream_df = self.create_speed_layer()
        
        # Real-time aggregations
        stream_aggregates = stream_df \
            .groupBy("product") \
            .agg(
                sum("amount").alias("realtime_total"),
                count("*").alias("realtime_count"),
                avg("amount").alias("realtime_avg")
            )
        
        # Serving Layer - Combine both views
        print("\n3. SERVING LAYER: Starting hybrid query...")
        
        # Write streaming results to memory table
        query = stream_aggregates.writeStream \
            .outputMode("complete") \
            .format("memory") \
            .queryName("realtime_aggregates") \
            .trigger(processingTime="5 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        # Allow some data to accumulate
        time.sleep(15)
        
        # Query the in-memory table
        realtime_view = self.spark.sql("SELECT * FROM realtime_aggregates")
        
        print("\n   Real-time View:")
        realtime_view.show()
        
        # Combine batch and streaming results
        print("\n4. COMBINED VIEW (Batch + Streaming):")
        
        # Join batch and streaming aggregates
        combined = batch_aggregates.join(
            realtime_view,
            "product",
            "full_outer"
        ).fillna(0).withColumn(
            "total_amount",
            col("historical_total") + col("realtime_total")
        ).withColumn(
            "total_count",
            col("historical_count") + col("realtime_count")
        )
        
        print("   Combined Aggregates:")
        combined.show()
        
        query.stop()
        
        return combined
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Stop the Spark session"""
        self.spark.stop()

# PATTERN 5: REAL-TIME MODE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Ultra-low latency processing with immediate responses
# Use Case: Fraud detection, alerting, real-time recommendations

class RealTimeModePattern:
    """
    Real-Time Mode Pattern for ultra-low latency processing.
    Optimized for minimal latency with continuous processing.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("RealTimeModePattern") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .config("spark.sql.streaming.statefulOperator.checkCorrectness.enabled", "false") \
            .config("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "2") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
    
    def create_realtime_stream(self):
        """Create a high-frequency streaming source"""
        # Simulate IoT sensor data or transaction stream
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("sensor_id", StringType(), True),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), True),
            StructField("temperature", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("pressure", DoubleType(), True),
            StructField("status", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        stream_df = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("rate") \
            .option("rowsPerSecond", 100) \
            .load() \
            .withColumn("sensor_id", concat(lit("sensor_"), (rand() * 10).cast("int"))) \
            .withColumn("temperature", 20 + (rand() * 50)) \
            .withColumn("pressure", 100 + (rand() * 20)) \
            .withColumn("status", 
                       when(col("temperature") > 60, "CRITICAL")
                       .when(col("temperature") > 50, "WARNING")
                       .otherwise("NORMAL"))
        
        return stream_df
    
    def realtime_processing(self):
        """Demonstrate real-time processing with minimal latency"""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("PATTERN 5: REAL-TIME MODE PATTERN")
        print("="*60)
        
        stream_df = self.create_realtime_stream()
        
        # Real-time alerting - detect critical conditions immediately
        print("\n1. REAL-TIME ALERTING: Monitoring critical conditions...")
        
        critical_alerts = stream_df \
            .filter(col("status") == "CRITICAL") \
            .select(
                col("timestamp"),
                col("sensor_id"),
                col("temperature"),
                col("pressure"),
                col("status")
            )
        
        # Process with continuous trigger (lowest latency)
        print("\n2. Starting continuous processing (30 seconds)...")
        
        alert_query = critical_alerts.writeStream \
            .outputMode("append") \
            .format("console") \
            .option("truncate", "false") \
            .trigger(continuous="1 second") \
            .start()
        
        # Real-time aggregations with micro-batching
        realtime_stats = stream_df \
            .groupBy(
                window(col("timestamp"), "5 seconds"),
                col("sensor_id")
            ) \
            .agg(
                avg("temperature").alias("avg_temp"),
                max("temperature").alias("max_temp"),
                count("*").alias("reading_count")
            ) \
            .filter(col("max_temp") > 55)
        
        stats_query = realtime_stats.writeStream \
            .outputMode("update") \
            .format("console") \
            .option("truncate", "false") \
            .trigger(processingTime="2 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        # Run for demonstration
        alert_query.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
        alert_query.stop()
        stats_query.stop()
        
        print("\n3. Real-time processing completed")
    
    def realtime_enrichment(self):
        """Demonstrate real-time stream enrichment"""
        print("\n4. REAL-TIME ENRICHMENT:")
        
        stream_df = self.create_realtime_stream()
        
        # Static reference data for enrichment
        sensor_metadata = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            ("sensor_0", "Building A", "Floor 1"),
            ("sensor_1", "Building A", "Floor 2"),
            ("sensor_2", "Building B", "Floor 1"),
            ("sensor_3", "Building B", "Floor 2"),
            ("sensor_4", "Building C", "Floor 1"),
        ], ["sensor_id", "building", "floor"])
        
        # Enrich stream with static data
        enriched_stream = stream_df.join(
            broadcast(sensor_metadata),
            "sensor_id",
            "left"
        )
        
        query = enriched_stream.writeStream \
            .outputMode("append") \
            .format("console") \
            .option("truncate", "false") \
            .trigger(processingTime="3 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        query.awaitTermination(timeout=20)
        query.stop()
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Stop the Spark session"""
        self.spark.stop()

# PATTERN 6: NEAR REAL-TIME MODE PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Balance between latency and throughput
# Use Case: Dashboard updates, periodic aggregations, micro-batch processing

class NearRealTimeModePattern:
    """
    Near Real-Time Mode Pattern for balanced latency and throughput.
    Uses micro-batching with configurable intervals.
    """
    
    def __init__(self):
        self.spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("NearRealTimeModePattern") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .config("spark.sql.streaming.metricsEnabled", "true") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        self.spark.sparkContext.setLogLevel("WARN")
    
    def create_microbatch_stream(self):
        """Create a streaming source for micro-batch processing"""
        # Simulate e-commerce clickstream data
        stream_df = self.spark.readStream \
            .format("rate") \
            .option("rowsPerSecond", 50) \
            .load() \
            .withColumn("user_id", (rand() * 1000).cast("int")) \
            .withColumn("page", 
                       when(col("value") % 5 == 0, "home")
                       .when(col("value") % 5 == 1, "product")
                       .when(col("value") % 5 == 2, "cart")
                       .when(col("value") % 5 == 3, "checkout")
                       .otherwise("account")) \
            .withColumn("session_duration", (rand() * 300).cast("int")) \
            .withColumn("country", 
                       when(col("value") % 4 == 0, "US")
                       .when(col("value") % 4 == 1, "UK")
                       .when(col("value") % 4 == 2, "CA")
                       .otherwise("AU"))
        
        return stream_df
    
    def near_realtime_processing(self):
        """Demonstrate near real-time processing with micro-batches"""
        print("\n" + "="*60)
        print("PATTERN 6: NEAR REAL-TIME MODE PATTERN")
        print("="*60)
        
        stream_df = self.create_microbatch_stream()
        
        # Micro-batch aggregations (every 10 seconds)
        print("\n1. MICRO-BATCH PROCESSING: 10-second intervals...")
        
        page_analytics = stream_df \
            .withWatermark("timestamp", "30 seconds") \
            .groupBy(
                window(col("timestamp"), "10 seconds", "10 seconds"),
                col("page"),
                col("country")
            ) \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("page_views"),
                countDistinct("user_id").alias("unique_users"),
                avg("session_duration").alias("avg_session_duration")
            )
        
        # Write to memory for querying
        query1 = page_analytics.writeStream \
            .outputMode("update") \
            .format("memory") \
            .queryName("page_analytics") \
            .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        # Dashboard-style aggregations
        print("\n2. DASHBOARD METRICS: Real-time KPIs...")
        
        kpi_metrics = stream_df \
            .groupBy(
                window(col("timestamp"), "15 seconds", "5 seconds")
            ) \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("total_events"),
                countDistinct("user_id").alias("active_users"),
                avg("session_duration").alias("avg_duration"),
                sum(when(col("page") == "checkout", 1).otherwise(0)).alias("checkouts")
            ) \
            .withColumn("conversion_rate", 
                       (col("checkouts") / col("total_events") * 100))
        
        query2 = kpi_metrics.writeStream \
            .outputMode("update") \
            .format("console") \
            .option("truncate", "false") \
            .trigger(processingTime="15 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        # Let it accumulate data
        time.sleep(35)
        
        # Query the analytics table
        print("\n3. ANALYTICS QUERY RESULTS:")
        analytics_df = self.spark.sql("""
            SELECT 
                page,
                country,
                SUM(page_views) as total_views,
                SUM(unique_users) as total_users,
                AVG(avg_session_duration) as overall_avg_duration
            FROM page_analytics
            GROUP BY page, country
            ORDER BY total_views DESC
        """)
        
        analytics_df.show()
        
        query1.stop()
        query2.stop()
        
        print("\n4. Near real-time processing completed")
    
    def sliding_window_analytics(self):
        """Demonstrate sliding window analytics for trend analysis"""
        print("\n5. SLIDING WINDOW ANALYTICS:")
        
        stream_df = self.create_microbatch_stream()
        
        # Sliding window for trend detection
        sliding_trends = stream_df \
            .withWatermark("timestamp", "1 minute") \
            .groupBy(
                window(col("timestamp"), "30 seconds", "10 seconds"),
                col("page")
            ) \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("views"),
                countDistinct("user_id").alias("users")
            ) \
            .withColumn("views_per_user", col("views") / col("users"))
        
        query = sliding_trends.writeStream \
            .outputMode("update") \
            .format("console") \
            .option("truncate", "false") \
            .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        query.awaitTermination(timeout=30)
        query.stop()
    
    def stateful_session_tracking(self):
        """Demonstrate stateful processing for session tracking"""
        print("\n6. STATEFUL SESSION TRACKING:")
        
        stream_df = self.create_microbatch_stream()
        
        # Track user sessions with state
        user_sessions = stream_df \
            .groupBy("user_id") \
            .agg(
                count("*").alias("event_count"),
                max("timestamp").alias("last_seen"),
                sum("session_duration").alias("total_duration"),
                collect_set("page").alias("pages_visited")
            )
        
        query = user_sessions.writeStream \
            .outputMode("update") \
            .format("console") \
            .option("truncate", "false") \
            .option("numRows", 10) \
            .trigger(processingTime="10 seconds") \
            .start()
        
        query.awaitTermination(timeout=25)
        query.stop()
    
    def cleanup(self):
        """Stop the Spark session"""
        self.spark.stop()

class PatternComparison:
    """
    Utility class to compare different processing patterns
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_patterns():
        """Compare all patterns side by side"""
        
        comparison_data = [
            ("Interactive", "Low", "Medium", "On-demand", "Exploration"),
            ("Batch", "High", "Very High", "Scheduled", "ETL/Reports"),
            ("Streaming", "Low-Medium", "High", "Continuous", "Event Processing"),
            ("Hybrid", "Variable", "Very High", "Hybrid", "Lambda Architecture"),
            ("Real-Time", "Very Low", "Medium", "Continuous", "Alerting"),
            ("Near Real-Time", "Low", "High", "Periodic", "Dashboards")
        ]
        
        spark = SparkSession.builder \
            .appName("PatternComparison") \
            .master("local[*]") \
            .getOrCreate()
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("Pattern", StringType(), True),
            StructField("Latency", StringType(), True),
            StructField("Throughput", StringType(), True),
            StructField("Trigger", StringType(), True),
            StructField("Primary_Use_Case", StringType(), True)
        ])
        
        df = spark.createDataFrame(comparison_data, schema)
        
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print("PATTERN COMPARISON TABLE")
        print("="*70 + "\n")
        
        df.show(truncate=False)
        
        spark.stop()

class PatternSelector:
    """
    Helper class to guide pattern selection based on requirements
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def select_pattern(latency_requirement, data_volume, processing_frequency):
        """
        Recommend a pattern based on requirements
        
        Args:
            latency_requirement: 'milliseconds', 'seconds', 'minutes', 'hours'
            data_volume: 'small', 'medium', 'large', 'very_large'
            processing_frequency: 'continuous', 'frequent', 'periodic', 'scheduled'
        
        Returns:
            Recommended pattern name
        """
        
        recommendations = {
            ('milliseconds', 'small', 'continuous'): 'Real-Time Mode',
            ('milliseconds', 'medium', 'continuous'): 'Real-Time Mode',
            ('seconds', 'small', 'continuous'): 'Real-Time Mode',
            ('seconds', 'medium', 'continuous'): 'Streaming Mode',
            ('seconds', 'large', 'continuous'): 'Streaming Mode',
            ('seconds', 'small', 'frequent'): 'Near Real-Time Mode',
            ('seconds', 'medium', 'frequent'): 'Near Real-Time Mode',
            ('minutes', 'medium', 'frequent'): 'Near Real-Time Mode',
            ('minutes', 'large', 'frequent'): 'Near Real-Time Mode',
            ('minutes', 'small', 'periodic'): 'Interactive Mode',
            ('hours', 'large', 'scheduled'): 'Batch Mode',
            ('hours', 'very_large', 'scheduled'): 'Batch Mode',
        }
        
        key = (latency_requirement, data_volume, processing_frequency)
        
        if key in recommendations:
            return recommendations[key]
        else:
            # Default recommendation logic
            if latency_requirement in ['milliseconds', 'seconds'] and processing_frequency == 'continuous':
                if data_volume in ['small', 'medium']:
                    return 'Real-Time Mode'
                else:
                    return 'Streaming Mode'
            elif processing_frequency == 'scheduled':
                return 'Batch Mode'
            elif latency_requirement in ['minutes', 'seconds']:
                return 'Near Real-Time Mode'
            else:
                return 'Hybrid Mode (for complex requirements)'
    
    @staticmethod
    def print_selection_guide():
        """Print a decision tree for pattern selection"""
        
        guide = """
        
        ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║                    PATTERN SELECTION GUIDE                           ║
        ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        Start here and follow the decision tree:
        
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ What is your PRIMARY requirement?                                   │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                    │
                ┌───────────────────┼───────────────────┐
                │                   │                   │
                ▼                   ▼                   ▼
        ┌───────────────┐   ┌───────────────┐   ┌───────────────┐
        │ Ad-hoc        │   │ Low Latency   │   │ High          │
        │ Exploration   │   │ (<1 min)      │   │ Throughput    │
        └───────────────┘   └───────────────┘   └───────────────┘
                │                   │                   │
                ▼                   │                   ▼
        ┌───────────────┐           │           ┌───────────────┐
        │ INTERACTIVE   │           │           │ BATCH MODE    │
        │ MODE          │           │           │               │
        └───────────────┘           │           └───────────────┘
                                    │
                    ┌───────────────┼───────────────┐
                    │               │               │
                    ▼               ▼               ▼
            ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐
            │ Milliseconds │ │ Seconds      │ │ Minutes      │
            └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘
                    │               │               │
                    ▼               ▼               ▼
            ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐ ┌──────────────┐
            │ REAL-TIME    │ │ STREAMING    │ │ NEAR         │
            │ MODE         │ │ MODE         │ │ REAL-TIME    │
            └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘ └──────────────┘
        
        ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ Need BOTH historical AND real-time data?                            │
        │                                                                     │
        │                    ▼                                                │
        │            ┌──────────────┐                                         │
        │            │ HYBRID MODE  │                                         │
        │            └──────────────┘                                         │
        └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        
        """
        
        print(guide)
    
    @staticmethod
    def interactive_selector():
        """Interactive pattern selector"""
        
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print(" INTERACTIVE PATTERN SELECTOR")
        print("="*70)
        
        print("\n1. What is your latency requirement?")
        print("   a) Milliseconds (ultra-low latency)")
        print("   b) Seconds (low latency)")
        print("   c) Minutes (moderate latency)")
        print("   d) Hours (high latency acceptable)")
        
        print("\n2. What is your data volume?")
        print("   a) Small (< 1GB)")
        print("   b) Medium (1GB - 100GB)")
        print("   c) Large (100GB - 1TB)")
        print("   d) Very Large (> 1TB)")
        
        print("\n3. What is your processing frequency?")
        print("   a) Continuous (24/7 streaming)")
        print("   b) Frequent (every few seconds/minutes)")
        print("   c) Periodic (hourly/daily)")
        print("   d) Scheduled (batch jobs)")
        
        print("\n4. Do you need both historical and real-time data?")
        print("   a) Yes (hybrid approach)")
        print("   b) No (single mode)")
        
        # Example recommendations
        print("\n" + "="*70)
        print(" EXAMPLE RECOMMENDATIONS:")
        print("="*70)
        
        examples = [
            ("Fraud Detection", "milliseconds", "medium", "continuous", "Real-Time Mode"),
            ("Daily ETL Job", "hours", "very_large", "scheduled", "Batch Mode"),
            ("Dashboard Updates", "minutes", "medium", "frequent", "Near Real-Time Mode"),
            ("IoT Monitoring", "seconds", "large", "continuous", "Streaming Mode"),
            ("Customer 360", "seconds", "large", "continuous", "Hybrid Mode"),
            ("Data Exploration", "minutes", "small", "periodic", "Interactive Mode"),
        ]
        
        for use_case, latency, volume, frequency, recommendation in examples:
            print(f"\n{use_case}:")
            print(f"  Latency: {latency}, Volume: {volume}, Frequency: {frequency}")
            print(f"  → Recommended: {recommendation}")

# ============================================================================

# ============================================================================

def run_specific_pattern(pattern_name):
    """
    Run a specific pattern by name
    
    Args:
        pattern_name: Name of the pattern to run
    """
    
    patterns = {
        "interactive": InteractiveModePattern,
        "batch": BatchModePattern,
        "streaming": StreamingModePattern,
        "hybrid": HybridModePattern,
        "realtime": RealTimeModePattern,
        "nearrealtime": NearRealTimeModePattern
    }
    
    pattern_name_lower = pattern_name.lower().replace(" ", "").replace("-", "")
    
    if pattern_name_lower in patterns:
        print(f"\n{'='*70}")
        print(f" Running {pattern_name} Pattern")
        print(f"{'='*70}")
        
        pattern_class = patterns[pattern_name_lower]
        pattern_instance = pattern_class()
        
        try:
            if pattern_name_lower == "interactive":
                pattern_instance.interactive_analysis()
            elif pattern_name_lower == "batch":
                pattern_instance.batch_processing_job()
            elif pattern_name_lower == "streaming":
                pattern_instance.streaming_processing()
                pattern_instance.stateful_streaming()
            elif pattern_name_lower == "hybrid":
                pattern_instance.hybrid_processing()
            elif pattern_name_lower == "realtime":
                pattern_instance.realtime_processing()
                pattern_instance.realtime_enrichment()
            elif pattern_name_lower == "nearrealtime":
                pattern_instance.near_realtime_processing()
                pattern_instance.sliding_window_analytics()
                pattern_instance.stateful_session_tracking()
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"Error running {pattern_name}: {e}")
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
        finally:
            pattern_instance.cleanup()
    else:
        print(f"Pattern '{pattern_name}' not found.")
        print(f"Available patterns: {', '.join(patterns.keys())}")


def run_all_patterns_sequential():
    """Run all patterns sequentially with proper cleanup"""
    
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print(" RUNNING ALL PATTERNS SEQUENTIALLY")
    print("="*70)
    
    patterns = [
        ("Interactive", InteractiveModePattern, lambda p: p.interactive_analysis()),
        ("Batch", BatchModePattern, lambda p: p.batch_processing_job()),
        ("Streaming", StreamingModePattern, lambda p: [p.streaming_processing(), p.stateful_streaming()]),
        ("Hybrid", HybridModePattern, lambda p: p.hybrid_processing()),
        ("Real-Time", RealTimeModePattern, lambda p: [p.realtime_processing(), p.realtime_enrichment()]),
        ("Near Real-Time", NearRealTimeModePattern, lambda p: [
            p.near_realtime_processing(), 
            p.sliding_window_analytics(), 
            p.stateful_session_tracking()
        ])
    ]
    
    for pattern_name, pattern_class, execution_func in patterns:
        print(f"\n\n{'#'*70}")
        print(f"# PATTERN: {pattern_name}")
        print(f"{'#'*70}\n")
        
        pattern_instance = None
        try:
            pattern_instance = pattern_class()
            execution_func(pattern_instance)
            print(f"\n✓ {pattern_name} Pattern completed successfully")
        except Exception as e:
            print(f"\n✗ Error in {pattern_name} Pattern: {e}")
            import traceback
            traceback.print_exc()
        finally:
            if pattern_instance:
                pattern_instance.cleanup()
            time.sleep(2)  # Brief pause between patterns
    
    print("\n" + "="*70)
    print(" ALL PATTERNS COMPLETED")
    print("="*70)

def interactive_menu():
    """Interactive menu system"""
    
    while True:
        print_menu()
        
        try:
            choice = input("Enter your choice (0-14): ").strip()
            
            if choice == "0":
                print("\nExiting... Thank you!")
                break
            
            elif choice == "1":
                run_all_patterns_sequential()
            
            elif choice == "2":

COMPLETE USAGE EXAMPLES

1. INTERACTIVE MODE EXAMPLE
---------------------------
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("Interactive").getOrCreate()

# Quick exploration
df = spark.read.csv("data.csv", header=True, inferSchema=True)
df.show(10)
df.printSchema()
df.describe().show()

# Ad-hoc analysis
result = df.groupBy("category").agg(
    count("*").alias("count"),
    avg("price").alias("avg_price")
)
result.show()


2. BATCH MODE EXAMPLE
---------------------
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("BatchETL") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
    .getOrCreate()

# Extract
df = spark.read.parquet("s3://bucket/raw-data/")

# Transform
transformed = df \
    .filter(col("status") == "active") \
    .withColumn("processed_date", current_date()) \
    .withColumn("year", year(col("date"))) \
    .withColumn("month", month(col("date")))

# Aggregate
aggregated = transformed.groupBy("year", "month", "category") \
    .agg(
        sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
        count("*").alias("record_count")
    )

# Load
aggregated.write \
    .mode("overwrite") \
    .partitionBy("year", "month") \
    .parquet("s3://bucket/processed-data/")


3. STREAMING MODE EXAMPLE
--------------------------
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("Streaming").getOrCreate()

# Read from Kafka
df = spark.readStream \
    .format("kafka") \
    .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
    .option("subscribe", "events") \
    .load()

# Parse JSON
parsed = df.select(
    from_json(col("value").cast("string"), schema).alias("data")
).select("data.*")

# Aggregate with windowing
windowed = parsed \
    .withWatermark("timestamp", "10 minutes") \
    .groupBy(
        window(col("timestamp"), "5 minutes"),
        col("event_type")
    ) \
    .agg(count("*").alias("event_count"))

# Write to console (or another sink)
query = windowed.writeStream \
    .outputMode("update") \
    .format("console") \
    .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
    .start()

query.awaitTermination()


4. HYBRID MODE EXAMPLE
-----------------------
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("Hybrid").getOrCreate()

# Batch Layer - Historical data
batch_df = spark.read.parquet("s3://bucket/historical/")
batch_agg = batch_df.groupBy("product_id") \
    .agg(sum("sales").alias("historical_sales"))

# Speed Layer - Real-time data
stream_df = spark.readStream.format("kafka").load()
stream_agg = stream_df.groupBy("product_id") \
    .agg(sum("sales").alias("realtime_sales"))

# Write streaming to memory table
query = stream_agg.writeStream \
    .format("memory") \
    .queryName("realtime_sales") \
    .outputMode("update") \
    .start()

# Serving Layer - Combine both
def get_combined_view():
    realtime = spark.sql("SELECT * FROM realtime_sales")
    combined = batch_agg.join(realtime, "product_id", "full_outer")
    return combined.withColumn(
        "total_sales",
        coalesce(col("historical_sales"), lit(0)) + 
        coalesce(col("realtime_sales"), lit(0))
    )


5. REAL-TIME MODE EXAMPLE
--------------------------
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("RealTime").getOrCreate()

# High-frequency stream
stream_df = spark.readStream \
    .format("kafka") \
    .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
    .option("subscribe", "transactions") \
    .load()

# Real-time fraud detection
fraud_check = stream_df \
    .select(from_json(col("value").cast("string"), schema).alias("txn")) \
    .select("txn.*") \
    .filter(
        (col("amount") > 10000) | 
        (col("velocity") > 100)
    )

# Alert immediately with continuous trigger
alert_query = fraud_check.writeStream \
    .outputMode("append") \
    .format("kafka") \
    .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
    .option("topic", "fraud-alerts") \
    .trigger(continuous="1 second") \
    .start()


6. NEAR REAL-TIME MODE EXAMPLE
-------------------------------
from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *

spark = SparkSession.builder.appName("NearRealTime").getOrCreate()

# Dashboard metrics with micro-batching
stream_df = spark.readStream.format("kafka").load()

# 30-second micro-batches for dashboard
dashboard_metrics = stream_df \
    .withWatermark("timestamp", "1 minute") \
    .groupBy(
        window(col("timestamp"), "30 seconds"),
        col("metric_name")
    ) \
    .agg(
        avg("value").alias("avg_value"),
        max("value").alias("max_value"),
        count("*").alias("count")
    )

# Update dashboard every 30 seconds
query = dashboard_metrics.writeStream \
    .outputMode("update") \
    .format("memory") \
    .queryName("dashboard_metrics") \
    .trigger(processingTime="30 seconds") \
    .start()

# Query for dashboard
def get_dashboard_data():
    return spark.sql(\"\"\"
        SELECT 
            window.start as time_window,
            metric_name,
            avg_value,
            max_value,
            count
        FROM dashboard_metrics
        ORDER BY time_window DESC
        LIMIT 100
    \"\"\")

class AdvancedPatternFeatures:

    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_checkpointing():
        """Demonstrate checkpointing for fault tolerance"""
        
        checkpoint_demo = """
        
        ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║                    CHECKPOINTING GUIDE                               ║
        ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        Checkpointing is crucial for fault-tolerant streaming:
        
        # Set checkpoint location
        checkpoint_path = "s3://bucket/checkpoints/my-stream"
        
        # For Structured Streaming
        query = df.writeStream \
            .format("parquet") \
            .option("path", "s3://bucket/output") \
            .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_path) \
            .start()
        
        # For Batch (lineage truncation)
        df.checkpoint()  # Eager checkpoint
        
        BEST PRACTICES:
        ✓ Use reliable storage (S3, HDFS) for checkpoints
        ✓ Never delete checkpoint directories while query is running
        ✓ Set appropriate checkpoint intervals
        ✓ Monitor checkpoint size growth
        ✓ Plan for checkpoint recovery scenarios
        
        """
        
        print(checkpoint_demo)
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_state_management():
        """Demonstrate stateful operations"""
        
        state_demo = """
        
        ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║                    STATE MANAGEMENT GUIDE                            ║
        ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        Managing state in streaming applications:
        
        # Stateful aggregations
        from pyspark.sql.functions import *
        
        # 1. Simple aggregation (maintains state)
        counts = df.groupBy("user_id").count()
        
        # 2. Time-based state with watermark
        windowed = df \
            .withWatermark("timestamp", "10 minutes") \
            .groupBy(
                window("timestamp", "5 minutes"),
                "user_id"
            ) \
            .count()
        
        # 3. Custom stateful processing
        from pyspark.sql.streaming import GroupState, GroupStateTimeout
        
        def update_state(key, values, state):
            # Custom state logic
            if state.exists:
                old_count = state.get
            else:
                old_count = 0
            
            new_count = old_count + sum(1 for _ in values)
            state.update(new_count)
            
            return (key, new_count)
        
        result = df.groupByKey(lambda x: x.user_id) \
            .mapGroupsWithState(update_state, 
                               GroupStateTimeout.ProcessingTimeTimeout)
        
        STATE STORE CONFIGURATION:
        ✓ spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.providerClass = "RocksDB"
        ✓ spark.sql.streaming.stateStore.maintenanceInterval = "60s"
        ✓ Monitor state store size and memory usage
        ✓ Use watermarks to clean up old state
        
        """
        
        print(state_demo)

        ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        Achieving exactly-once processing guarantees:
        
        # 1. Idempotent Writes (for sinks that support it)
        query = df.writeStream \
            .format("delta")  # Delta Lake supports ACID transactions \
            .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_path) \

        # 2. Kafka with Idempotent Producer
        query = df.writeStream \
            .format("kafka") \
            .option("kafka.bootstrap.servers", "localhost:9092") \
            .option("topic", "output-topic") \
            .option("kafka.enable.idempotence", "true") \
            .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_path) \
            .start()
        
        # 3. Deduplication for at-least-once sources
        deduplicated = df \
            .withWatermark("timestamp", "10 minutes") \
            .dropDuplicates(["event_id", "timestamp"])
        
        # 4. Transactional Writes
        def write_batch(batch_df, batch_id):
            # Use database transactions
            batch_df.write \
                .format("jdbc") \
                .option("isolationLevel", "READ_COMMITTED") \
                .mode("append") \
                .save()
        
        query = df.writeStream \
            .foreachBatch(write_batch) \
            .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_path) \
            .start()
        
        KEY REQUIREMENTS:
        ✓ Enable checkpointing
        ✓ Use idempotent sinks (Delta, Iceberg, Hudi)
        ✓ Implement deduplication where needed
        ✓ Use transactional writes
        ✓ Handle failures gracefully
        
        """
        
        print(exactly_once_demo)

        1. BATCH MODE PARTITIONING

        # Write with partitioning
        df.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .partitionBy("year", "month", "day") \
            .parquet("s3://bucket/data/")
        
        # Read with partition pruning
        df = spark.read.parquet("s3://bucket/data/") \
            .filter("year = 2024 AND month = 1")
        
        # Dynamic partition overwrite
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode", "dynamic")
        
        
        2. STREAMING PARTITIONING
        ──────────────────────────
        
        # Partition streaming output
        query = df.writeStream \
            .format("parquet") \
            .partitionBy("date") \
            .option("path", "s3://bucket/stream-data/") \
            .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_path) \
            .start()
        
        # Repartition before writing
        df.repartition(10, "user_id") \
            .writeStream \
            .format("parquet") \
            .start()
        
        
        3. OPTIMAL PARTITION SIZING
        ────────────────────────────
        
        # Target: 128MB - 1GB per partition
        num_partitions = int(total_data_size_mb / 256)
        
        df_optimized = df.repartition(num_partitions)
        
        # Coalesce for reducing partitions
        df_coalesced = df.coalesce(50)
        
        
        BEST PRACTICES:
        ✓ Partition by commonly filtered columns
        ✓ Avoid over-partitioning (too many small files)
        ✓ Use Z-ordering for multi-dimensional queries (Delta Lake)
        ✓ Monitor partition sizes regularly
        ✓ Consider data skew when partitioning

        print(partitioning_guide)
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_caching_strategies():
        """Show caching strategies"""
        
        caching_guide = """
        
        ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║                    CACHING STRATEGIES                                ║
        ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        1. INTERACTIVE MODE CACHING
        ────────────────────────────
        
        # Cache frequently accessed data
        df.cache()  # or df.persist()
        
        # Use specific storage levels
        from pyspark import StorageLevel
        
        df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
        df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
        df.persist(StorageLevel.DISK_ONLY)
        
        # Unpersist when done
        df.unpersist()
        
        
        2. BATCH MODE CACHING
        ──────────────────────
        
        # Cache intermediate results
        intermediate = df.filter(...).groupBy(...).agg(...)
        intermediate.cache()
        
        # Use in multiple operations
        result1 = intermediate.filter(...)
        result2 = intermediate.join(...)
        
        # Clean up
        intermediate.unpersist()
        
        
        3. BROADCAST JOINS
        ──────────────────
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import broadcast
        
        # Broadcast small dimension table
        result = large_df.join(
            broadcast(small_df),
            "key"
        )
        
        # Configure broadcast threshold
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760")  # 10MB
        
        
        4. ADAPTIVE QUERY EXECUTION (AQE)
        ──────────────────────────────────
        
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
        spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
        
        
        WHEN TO CACHE:
        ✓ Data is accessed multiple times
        ✓ Expensive computations (joins, aggregations)
        ✓ Iterative algorithms
        ✓ Interactive exploration
        
        WHEN NOT TO CACHE:
        ✗ Data is only accessed once
        ✗ Very large datasets (memory constraints)
        ✗ Simple transformations
        
        """
        
        print(caching_guide)


class ErrorHandlingPatterns:
    """
    Error handling and recovery patterns
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_error_handling():
        """Show error handling patterns"""
        
        error_handling_guide = """
        
        ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║                  ERROR HANDLING PATTERNS                             ║
        ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        1. BATCH MODE ERROR HANDLING
        ─────────────────────────────
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import *
        
        # Separate good and bad records
        def process_with_error_handling(df):
            # Add error column
            processed = df.withColumn(
                "is_valid",
                when(
                    (col("amount").isNotNull()) & 
                    (col("amount") > 0),
                    True
                ).otherwise(False)
            )
            
            # Split into good and bad
            good_records = processed.filter(col("is_valid"))
            bad_records = processed.filter(~col("is_valid"))
            
            # Write to different locations
            good_records.write.parquet("s3://bucket/good/")
            bad_records.write.parquet("s3://bucket/errors/")
            
            return good_records, bad_records
        
        
        2. STREAMING ERROR HANDLING
        ────────────────────────────
        
        # Use foreachBatch for custom error handling
        def process_batch_with_errors(batch_df, batch_id):
            try:
                # Process batch
                processed = batch_df.transform(...)
                
                # Write successful records
                processed.write.format("delta").mode("append").save(...)
                
            except Exception as e:
                # Log error
                print(f"Error in batch {batch_id}: {e}")
                
                # Write failed batch to error location
                batch_df.write.format("parquet") \
                    .mode("append") \
                    .save(f"s3://bucket/errors/batch_{batch_id}/")
                
                # Optionally re-raise or continue
                # raise e
        
        query = df.writeStream \
            .foreachBatch(process_batch_with_errors) \
            .option("checkpointLocation", checkpoint_path) \
            .start()
        
        
        3. RETRY LOGIC
        ──────────────
        
        from time import sleep
        
        def write_with_retry(df, path, max_retries=3):
            for attempt in range(max_retries):
                try:
                    df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(path)
                    print(f"Write successful on attempt {attempt + 1}")
                    break
                except Exception as e:
                    if attempt < max_retries - 1:
                        print(f"Attempt {attempt + 1} failed: {e}. Retrying...")
                        sleep(2 ** attempt)  # Exponential backoff
                    else:
                        print(f"All {max_retries} attempts failed")
                        raise
        
        
        4. DEAD LETTER QUEUE PATTERN
        ─────────────────────────────
        
        def process_with_dlq(df):
            from pyspark.sql.functions import struct, to_json, current_timestamp
            
            # Try to process
            try:
                processed = df.transform(complex_transformation)
                processed.write.format("delta").save("s3://bucket/output/")
            except Exception as e:
                # Send to dead letter queue
                error_record = df.withColumn(
                    "error_info",
                    struct(
                        lit(str(e)).alias("error_message"),
                        current_timestamp().alias("error_timestamp")
                    )
                )
                
                error_record.write \
                    .format("parquet") \
                    .mode("append") \
                    .save("s3://bucket/dlq/")
        
        
        5. CIRCUIT BREAKER PATTERN
        ───────────────────────────
        
        class CircuitBreaker:
            def __init__(self, failure_threshold=5, timeout=60):
                self.failure_count = 0
                self.failure_threshold = failure_threshold
                self.timeout = timeout
                self.last_failure_time = None
                self.state = "CLOSED"  # CLOSED, OPEN, HALF_OPEN
            
            def call(self, func, *args, **kwargs):
                if self.state == "OPEN":
                    if time.time() - self.last_failure_time > self.timeout:
                        self.state = "HALF_OPEN"
                    else:
                        raise Exception("Circuit breaker is OPEN")
                
                try:
```python
                try:
                    result = func(*args, **kwargs)
                    if self.state == "HALF_OPEN":
                        self.state = "CLOSED"
                        self.failure_count = 0
                    return result
                except Exception as e:
                    self.failure_count += 1
                    self.last_failure_time = time.time()
                    
                    if self.failure_count >= self.failure_threshold:
                        self.state = "OPEN"
                    
                    raise e
        
        # Usage
        breaker = CircuitBreaker()
        
        def write_to_external_system(df):
            breaker.call(df.write.jdbc, url, table, properties)
        
        
        BEST PRACTICES:
        ✓ Always validate input data
        ✓ Separate good and bad records
        ✓ Implement retry logic with exponential backoff
        ✓ Use dead letter queues for failed records
        ✓ Monitor error rates and set up alerts
        ✓ Log errors with sufficient context
        ✓ Implement circuit breakers for external dependencies
        
        """
        
        print(error_handling_guide)


class DataQualityPatterns:
    """
    Data quality validation patterns
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def demonstrate_data_quality_checks():
        """Show data quality validation patterns"""
        
        quality_guide = """
        
        ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║                  DATA QUALITY PATTERNS                               ║
        ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        1. SCHEMA VALIDATION
        ────────────────────
        
        from pyspark.sql.types import *
        
        # Define expected schema
        expected_schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("date", DateType(), True)
        ])
        
        # Validate schema
        def validate_schema(df, expected_schema):
            if df.schema != expected_schema:
                raise ValueError(f"Schema mismatch: {df.schema} != {expected_schema}")
            return df
        
        # Read with schema enforcement
        df = spark.read.schema(expected_schema).csv("data.csv")
        
        
        2. NULL CHECKS
        ──────────────
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import *
        
        # Check for nulls
        def check_nulls(df, columns):
            null_counts = df.select([
                sum(col(c).isNull().cast("int")).alias(c)
                for c in columns
            ]).collect()[0]
            
            for col_name, null_count in null_counts.asDict().items():
                if null_count > 0:
                    print(f"Warning: {null_count} nulls in {col_name}")
            
            return df
        
        # Filter out nulls
        df_clean = df.filter(
            col("id").isNotNull() & 
            col("amount").isNotNull()
        )
        
        
        3. RANGE VALIDATION
        ───────────────────
        
        def validate_ranges(df):
            # Add validation flags
            validated = df.withColumn(
                "is_valid",
                (col("amount") >= 0) & 
                (col("amount") <= 1000000) &
                (col("quantity") > 0) &
                (year(col("date")) >= 2020)
            )
            
            # Count invalid records
            invalid_count = validated.filter(~col("is_valid")).count()
            total_count = validated.count()
            
            print(f"Invalid records: {invalid_count}/{total_count} "
                  f"({invalid_count/total_count*100:.2f}%)")
            
            return validated.filter(col("is_valid")).drop("is_valid")
        
        
        4. DUPLICATE DETECTION
        ──────────────────────
        
        # Check for duplicates
        def check_duplicates(df, key_columns):
            duplicate_count = df.groupBy(key_columns) \
                .count() \
                .filter(col("count") > 1) \
                .count()
            
            if duplicate_count > 0:
                print(f"Found {duplicate_count} duplicate keys")
            
            return df
        
        # Remove duplicates
        df_dedup = df.dropDuplicates(["id", "date"])
        
        # Keep first/last occurrence
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("id").orderBy(desc("timestamp"))
        df_latest = df.withColumn("rank", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
            .filter(col("rank") == 1) \
            .drop("rank")
        
        
        5. REFERENTIAL INTEGRITY
        ────────────────────────
        
        def check_referential_integrity(fact_df, dim_df, key_column):
            # Left anti join to find orphaned records
            orphaned = fact_df.join(
                dim_df,
                fact_df[key_column] == dim_df[key_column],
                "left_anti"
            )
            
            orphaned_count = orphaned.count()
            if orphaned_count > 0:
                print(f"Warning: {orphaned_count} orphaned records found")
                orphaned.write.parquet("s3://bucket/orphaned_records/")
            
            # Inner join to keep only valid records
            return fact_df.join(dim_df, key_column, "inner")
        
        
        6. STATISTICAL VALIDATION
        ──────────────────────────
        
        def statistical_validation(df, column):
            stats = df.select(
                mean(col(column)).alias("mean"),
                stddev(col(column)).alias("stddev"),
                min(col(column)).alias("min"),
                max(col(column)).alias("max")
            ).collect()[0]
            
            # Detect outliers (3 sigma rule)
            lower_bound = stats["mean"] - 3 * stats["stddev"]
            upper_bound = stats["mean"] + 3 * stats["stddev"]
            
            outliers = df.filter(
                (col(column) < lower_bound) | 
                (col(column) > upper_bound)
            )
            
            outlier_count = outliers.count()
            print(f"Outliers detected: {outlier_count}")
            
            return df.filter(
                (col(column) >= lower_bound) & 
                (col(column) <= upper_bound)
            )
        
        
        7. COMPREHENSIVE QUALITY REPORT
        ────────────────────────────────
        
        def generate_quality_report(df):
            report = {
                "total_records": df.count(),
                "columns": len(df.columns),
                "null_counts": {},
                "duplicate_count": 0,
                "schema": str(df.schema)
            }
            
            # Null counts per column
            for column in df.columns:
                null_count = df.filter(col(column).isNull()).count()
                report["null_counts"][column] = null_count
            
            # Duplicate check
            report["duplicate_count"] = df.count() - df.dropDuplicates().count()
            
            # Summary statistics
            report["summary_stats"] = df.describe().toPandas().to_dict()
            
            return report
        
        
        QUALITY METRICS TO TRACK:
        ✓ Completeness (null percentage)
        ✓ Uniqueness (duplicate percentage)
        ✓ Validity (range compliance)
        ✓ Accuracy (data correctness)
        ✓ Consistency (cross-field validation)
        ✓ Timeliness (data freshness)
        
        """
        
        print(quality_guide)


class PerformanceBenchmarking:
    """
    Performance benchmarking utilities
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def benchmark_pattern(pattern_name, pattern_func, iterations=3):
        """Benchmark a specific pattern"""
        
        print(f"\n{'='*70}")
        print(f" BENCHMARKING: {pattern_name}")
        print(f"{'='*70}")
        
        execution_times = []
        
        for i in range(iterations):
            print(f"\nIteration {i+1}/{iterations}...")
            start_time = time.time()
            
            try:
                pattern_func()
                end_time = time.time()
                execution_time = end_time - start_time
                execution_times.append(execution_time)
                print(f"Execution time: {execution_time:.2f} seconds")
            except Exception as e:
                print(f"Error: {e}")
                execution_times.append(None)
        
        # Calculate statistics
        valid_times = [t for t in execution_times if t is not None]
        
        if valid_times:
            avg_time = sum(valid_times) / len(valid_times)
            min_time = min(valid_times)
            max_time = max(valid_times)
            
            print(f"\n{'='*70}")
            print(f" BENCHMARK RESULTS")
            print(f"{'='*70}")
            print(f"Average time: {avg_time:.2f} seconds")
            print(f"Min time:     {min_time:.2f} seconds")
            print(f"Max time:     {max_time:.2f} seconds")
            print(f"Success rate: {len(valid_times)}/{iterations}")
        else:
            print("\n⚠ All iterations failed")
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_patterns_performance():
        """Compare performance of different patterns"""
        
        comparison_guide = """
        
        ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
        ║              PERFORMANCE COMPARISON GUIDE                            ║
        ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
        
        TYPICAL PERFORMANCE CHARACTERISTICS:
        
        Pattern          | Latency    | Throughput | Resource Usage
        ─────────────────┼────────────┼────────────┼────────────────
        Interactive      | Low        | Medium     | Low-Medium
        Batch            | High       | Very High  | High
        Streaming        | Low-Medium | High       | Medium-High
        Hybrid           | Variable   | Very High  | Very High
        Real-Time        | Very Low   | Medium     | Medium
        Near Real-Time   | Low        | High       | Medium-High
        
        
        OPTIMIZATION PRIORITIES:
        
        Interactive Mode:
        ├─ Query response time
        ├─ Memory efficiency
        └─ Cache hit ratio
        
        Batch Mode:
        ├─ Total job duration
        ├─ Data throughput (GB/hour)
        └─ Resource utilization
        
        Streaming Mode:
        ├─ Processing rate (records/sec)
        ├─ End-to-end latency
        └─ State store efficiency
        
        Hybrid Mode:
        ├─ Batch layer throughput
        ├─ Speed layer latency
        └─ Serving layer query performance
        
        Real-Time Mode:
        ├─ Event processing latency (p99)
        ├─ Throughput consistency
        └─ Resource stability
        
        Near Real-Time Mode:
        ├─ Micro-batch duration
        ├─ Trigger interval adherence
        └─ Aggregation accuracy
        
        """
        
        print(comparison_guide)
