        .
```python
        .withColumn("amount_category",
                   when(col("amount") > 50000, "High")
                   .when(col("amount") > 20000, "Medium")
                   .otherwise("Low"))
    
    # Cache transformed data for multiple downstream operations
    transformed.cache()
    transformed.count()  # Materialize cache
    
    print(f"Records transformed: {transformed.count()}")
    
    print("\n3. Load Phase - Multiple Aggregations:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Aggregation 1: By month
    monthly_agg = transformed \
        .groupBy("year", "month") \
        .agg(
            _sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            count("*").alias("transaction_count")
        )
    
    print("Monthly aggregation:")
    monthly_agg.show(5)
    
    # Aggregation 2: By category
    category_agg = transformed \
        .groupBy("amount_category") \
        .agg(
            _sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
        )
    
    print("Category aggregation:")
    category_agg.show()
    
    print("\n4. ETL Plan Analysis:")
    print("-" * 80)
    transformed.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print("\n5. Performance Metrics:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("✓ Cached intermediate results")
    print("✓ Reused transformations for multiple aggregations")
    print("✓ Optimized with predicate pushdown")
    print("✓ Column pruning applied")
    
    # Cleanup
    transformed.unpersist()
    
    return transformed


def scenario_real_time_analytics():
    """
    Scenario: Real-time Analytics with Adaptive Execution
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCENARIO: REAL-TIME ANALYTICS WITH ADAPTIVE EXECUTION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Simulate streaming data batches
    events_data = [
        (i, f"Event_{i%10}", f"User_{i%100}", i * 10, "2024-01-15 10:00:00") 
        for i in range(1, 5001)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("event_id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("event_type", StringType(), True),
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("value", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("timestamp", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    events_df = spark.createDataFrame(events_data, schema)
    
    # User dimension table (small)
    users_data = [(f"User_{i}", f"Segment_{i%5}", f"Region_{i%3}") 
                  for i in range(100)]
    
    users_schema = StructType([
        StructField("user_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("segment", StringType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    users_df = spark.createDataFrame(users_data, users_schema)
    
    print("\n1. Enable Adaptive Query Execution:")
    print("-" * 80)
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
    print("AQE enabled for dynamic optimization")
    
    print("\n2. Real-time Aggregation Query:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Join events with user dimensions and aggregate
    analytics_query = events_df \
        .join(users_df, "user_id") \
        .groupBy("event_type", "segment", "region") \
        .agg(
            count("*").alias("event_count"),
            _sum("value").alias("total_value"),
            avg("value").alias("avg_value")
        ) \
        .filter(col("event_count") > 10) \
        .orderBy(col("total_value").desc())
    
    print("\n3. Execution Plan with AQE:")
    print("-" * 80)
    analytics_query.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print("\n4. Execute and Analyze:")
    print("-" * 80)
    start_time = time.time()
    results = analytics_query.collect()
    execution_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    print(f"Results: {len(results)} aggregated groups")
    print(f"Execution time: {execution_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"Events processed: {events_df.count()}")
    
    print("\n5. AQE Optimizations Applied:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("✓ Broadcast join for small user dimension")
    print("✓ Dynamic partition coalescing after shuffle")
    print("✓ Optimized aggregation strategy")
    
    # Show sample results
    print("\nTop 5 Results:")
    for i, row in enumerate(results[:5], 1):
        print(f"{i}. {row.event_type} | {row.segment} | {row.region} | "
              f"Count: {row.event_count} | Total: {row.total_value}")
    
    return analytics_query


def scenario_complex_join_optimization():
    """
    Scenario: Complex Multi-way Join Optimization
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCENARIO: COMPLEX MULTI-WAY JOIN OPTIMIZATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create multiple related tables
    orders_data = [(i, f"Customer_{i%50}", f"Product_{i%20}", i * 10.0) 
                   for i in range(1, 501)]
    orders_schema = StructType([
        StructField("order_id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    orders_df = spark.createDataFrame(orders_data, orders_schema)
    
    customers_data = [(f"Customer_{i}", f"City_{i%10}", f"Tier_{i%3}") 
                      for i in range(50)]
    customers_schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("city", StringType(), True),
        StructField("tier", StringType(), True)
    ])
    customers_df = spark.createDataFrame(customers_data, customers_schema)
    
    products_data = [(f"Product_{i}", f"Category_{i%5}", i * 5.0) 
                     for i in range(20)]
    products_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("base_price", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(products_data, products_schema)
    
    print("\n1. Multi-way Join Query:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Complex join with multiple tables
    complex_join = orders_df \
        .join(customers_df, "customer_id") \
        .join(products_df, "product_id") \
        .select(
            orders_df.order_id,
            customers_df.city,
            customers_df.tier,
            products_df.category,
            orders_df.amount,
            products_df.base_price
        ) \
        .withColumn("profit", col("amount") - col("base_price")) \
        .groupBy("city", "category") \
        .agg(
            _sum("profit").alias("total_profit"),
            count("*").alias("order_count")
        ) \
        .filter(col("total_profit") > 0) \
        .orderBy(col("total_profit").desc())
    
    print("\n2. Join Strategy Analysis:")
    print("-" * 80)
    complex_join.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print("\n3. Optimized Join with Hints:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Use broadcast hints for small dimension tables
    optimized_join = orders_df \
        .join(customers_df.hint("broadcast"), "customer_id") \
        .join(products_df.hint("broadcast"), "product_id") \
        .select(
            orders_df.order_id,
            customers_df.city,
            customers_df.tier,
            products_df.category,
            orders_df.amount,
            products_df.base_price
        ) \
        .withColumn("profit", col("amount") - col("base_price")) \
        .groupBy("city", "category") \
        .agg(
            _sum("profit").alias("total_profit"),
            count("*").alias("order_count")
        ) \
        .filter(col("total_profit") > 0) \
        .orderBy(col("total_profit").desc())
    
    print("Optimized plan with broadcast hints:")
    optimized_join.explain(mode="simple")
    
    print("\n4. Performance Comparison:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Compare execution times
    start_time = time.time()
    result1 = complex_join.count()
    time1 = time.time() - start_time
    
    start_time = time.time()
    result2 = optimized_join.count()
    time2 = time.time() - start_time
    
    print(f"Without hints: {time1:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"With broadcast hints: {time2:.4f} seconds")
    
    if time2 < time1:
        improvement = ((time1 - time2) / time1) * 100
        print(f"Performance improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
    
    print("\n5. Join Optimization Tips:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("✓ Broadcast small dimension tables")
    print("✓ Join order matters - join smallest tables first")
    print("✓ Use appropriate join types (inner, left, etc.)")
    print("✓ Enable cost-based optimization with statistics")
    print("✓ Consider bucketing for large joins")
    
    return optimized_join


def scenario_window_function_optimization():
    """
    Scenario: Window Function Optimization
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCENARIO: WINDOW FUNCTION OPTIMIZATION")
    print("="*80)
    
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    from pyspark.sql.functions import row_number, rank, dense_rank, lag, lead
    
    # Create time-series data
    timeseries_data = [
        (i, f"Product_{i%10}", f"2024-01-{(i%28)+1:02d}", i * 100.0) 
        for i in range(1, 301)
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("product", StringType(), True),
        StructField("date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("sales", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    ts_df = spark.createDataFrame(timeseries_data, schema)
    
    print("\n1. Window Function Query:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Define window specifications
    product_window = Window.partitionBy("product").orderBy("date")
    
    # Apply multiple window functions
    windowed_df = ts_df \
        .withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(product_window)) \
        .withColumn("rank", rank().over(product_window)) \
        .withColumn("prev_sales", lag("sales", 1).over(product_window)) \
        .withColumn("next_sales", lead("sales", 1).over(product_window)) \
        .withColumn("sales_diff", col("sales") - col("prev_sales"))
    
    print("\n2. Window Function Plan:")
    print("-" * 80)
    windowed_df.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print("\n3. Window Function Analysis:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("Window operations identified in plan:")
    print("✓ Partitioning by 'product'")
    print("✓ Ordering by 'date'")
    print("✓ Multiple window functions in single pass")
    
    print("\n4. Optimization Strategies:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("✓ Combine multiple window functions with same spec")
    print("✓ Avoid unnecessary sorting")
    print("✓ Use appropriate partition columns")
    print("✓ Consider data distribution")
    
    # Show sample results
    print("\n5. Sample Results:")
    print("-" * 80)
    windowed_df.filter(col("product") == "Product_0").show(5)
    
    # Performance with multiple window specs
    print("\n6. Multiple Window Specifications:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    product_date_window = Window.partitionBy("product").orderBy("date")
    product_window_unbounded = Window.partitionBy("product")
    
    multi_window_df = ts_df \
        .withColumn("running_total", 
                   _sum("sales").over(product_date_window)) \
        .withColumn("product_avg", 
                   avg("sales").over(product_window_unbounded)) \
        .withColumn("deviation", 
                   col("sales") - col("product_avg"))
    
    multi_window_df.explain(mode="simple")
    
    return windowed_df


def scenario_partition_optimization():
    """
    Scenario: Partition Optimization Strategies
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCENARIO: PARTITION OPTIMIZATION STRATEGIES")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create partitioned data
    large_data = [(i, f"Category_{i%5}", f"Region_{i%3}", i * 10.0) 
                  for i in range(1, 10001)]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True),
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(large_data, schema)
    
    print("\n1. Initial Partition Analysis:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"Initial partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    print("\n2. Repartition Strategies:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Strategy 1: Hash partitioning
    hash_partitioned = df.repartition(4, "category")
    print(f"Hash partitioned (by category): {hash_partitioned.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Strategy 2: Range partitioning
    range_partitioned = df.repartitionByRange(4, "value")
    print(f"Range partitioned (by value): {range_partitioned.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Strategy 3: Coalesce
    coalesced = df.coalesce(2)
    print(f"Coalesced: {coalesced.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    print("\n3. Partition Impact on Aggregation:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Aggregation
```python
    # Aggregation on non-partitioned data
    print("Non-partitioned aggregation:")
    non_part_agg = df.groupBy("category").agg(_sum("value").alias("total"))
    non_part_agg.explain(mode="simple")
    
    start_time = time.time()
    non_part_agg.count()
    time_non_part = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Execution time: {time_non_part:.4f} seconds")
    
    # Aggregation on partitioned data
    print("\nPartitioned aggregation:")
    part_agg = hash_partitioned.groupBy("category").agg(_sum("value").alias("total"))
    part_agg.explain(mode="simple")
    
    start_time = time.time()
    part_agg.count()
    time_part = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Execution time: {time_part:.4f} seconds")
    
    print("\n4. Partition Skew Detection:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Check partition sizes
    partition_sizes = df.rdd.glom().map(len).collect()
    print(f"Partition size distribution: {partition_sizes}")
    print(f"Min partition size: {min(partition_sizes)}")
    print(f"Max partition size: {max(partition_sizes)}")
    print(f"Avg partition size: {sum(partition_sizes)/len(partition_sizes):.2f}")
    
    skew_ratio = max(partition_sizes) / (sum(partition_sizes)/len(partition_sizes))
    if skew_ratio > 2.0:
        print(f"⚠ WARNING: Partition skew detected! Ratio: {skew_ratio:.2f}")
    else:
        print(f"✓ Partitions are balanced. Ratio: {skew_ratio:.2f}")
    
    print("\n5. Adaptive Partition Coalescing:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Enable AQE for automatic partition coalescing
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.advisoryPartitionSizeInBytes", "64MB")
    
    # Query that will benefit from adaptive coalescing
    adaptive_query = df \

        .groupBy("category", "region") \
        .agg(_sum("value").alias("total"))
    
    print("Query with adaptive partition coalescing:")
    adaptive_query.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    result = adaptive_query.collect()
    print(f"Final result partitions: {adaptive_query.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    print("\n6. Partition Optimization Best Practices:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("✓ Repartition before expensive operations (joins, aggregations)")
    print("✓ Use coalesce to reduce partitions (no shuffle)")
    print("✓ Partition by columns used in joins/aggregations")
    print("✓ Aim for 128MB - 256MB per partition")
    print("✓ Monitor and handle partition skew")
    print("✓ Enable AQE for automatic optimization")
    
    return hash_partitioned


def scenario_broadcast_join_tuning():
    """
    Scenario: Broadcast Join Tuning and Analysis
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCENARIO: BROADCAST JOIN TUNING AND ANALYSIS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create large fact table
    fact_data = [(i, f"Dim_{i%1000}", i * 10.0) for i in range(1, 10001)]
    fact_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("dim_key", StringType(), True),
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    fact_df = spark.createDataFrame(fact_data, fact_schema)
    
    # Create small dimension table
    dim_data = [(f"Dim_{i}", f"Category_{i%10}") for i in range(1000)]
    dim_schema = StructType([
        StructField("dim_key", StringType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True)
    ])
    dim_df = spark.createDataFrame(dim_data, dim_schema)
    
    print("\n1. Dataset Information:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"Fact table rows: {fact_df.count()}")
    print(f"Dimension table rows: {dim_df.count()}")
    
    print("\n2. Current Broadcast Threshold:")
    print("-" * 80)
    current_threshold = spark.conf.get("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold")
    print(f"Auto broadcast threshold: {current_threshold} bytes ({int(current_threshold)/(1024*1024):.2f} MB)")
    
    print("\n3. Automatic Broadcast Join:")
    print("-" * 80)
    auto_broadcast = fact_df.join(dim_df, "dim_key")
    print("Plan with automatic broadcast detection:")
    auto_broadcast.explain(mode="simple")
    
    print("\n4. Explicit Broadcast Hint:")
    print("-" * 80)
    explicit_broadcast = fact_df.join(dim_df.hint("broadcast"), "dim_key")
    print("Plan with explicit broadcast hint:")
    explicit_broadcast.explain(mode="simple")
    
    print("\n5. Disable Broadcast (Force Shuffle Join):")
    print("-" * 80)
    # Temporarily disable auto broadcast
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "-1")
    
    shuffle_join = fact_df.join(dim_df, "dim_key")
    print("Plan with shuffle join:")
    shuffle_join.explain(mode="simple")
    
    # Restore threshold
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760")
    
    print("\n6. Performance Comparison:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Broadcast join performance
    start_time = time.time()
    broadcast_count = explicit_broadcast.count()
    broadcast_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Broadcast join: {broadcast_time:.4f} seconds ({broadcast_count} rows)")
    
    # Shuffle join performance
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "-1")
    start_time = time.time()
    shuffle_count = fact_df.join(dim_df, "dim_key").count()
    shuffle_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Shuffle join: {shuffle_time:.4f} seconds ({shuffle_count} rows)")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760")
    
    if broadcast_time < shuffle_time:
        speedup = shuffle_time / broadcast_time
        print(f"\n✓ Broadcast join is {speedup:.2f}x faster")
    
    print("\n7. Broadcast Join Considerations:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("✓ Best for small dimension tables (< 10MB)")
    print("✓ Avoid broadcasting large tables (OOM risk)")
    print("✓ Monitor driver memory usage")
    print("✓ Consider network bandwidth")
    print("✓ Use explicit hints when needed")
    
    print("\n8. Multi-table Broadcast:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Create another small dimension
    dim2_data = [(f"Dim_{i}", f"Region_{i%5}") for i in range(1000)]
    dim2_schema = StructType([
        StructField("dim_key", StringType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True)
    ])
    dim2_df = spark.createDataFrame(dim2_data, dim2_schema)
    
    # Join with multiple broadcast tables
    multi_broadcast = fact_df \
        .join(dim_df.hint("broadcast"), "dim_key") \
        .join(dim2_df.hint("broadcast"), "dim_key") \
        .select(fact_df.value, dim_df.category, dim2_df.region)
    
    print("Multi-table broadcast join plan:")
    multi_broadcast.explain(mode="simple")
    
    return explicit_broadcast


def scenario_skew_join_handling():
    """
    Scenario: Handling Data Skew in Joins
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SCENARIO: HANDLING DATA SKEW IN JOINS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create skewed data (80% of data has same key)
    skewed_data = []
    # 8000 rows with same key
    skewed_data.extend([(i, "SKEWED_KEY", i * 10.0) for i in range(1, 8001)])
    # 2000 rows with different keys
    skewed_data.extend([(i, f"Key_{i%100}", i * 10.0) for i in range(8001, 10001)])
    
    skewed_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("key", StringType(), True),
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    skewed_df = spark.createDataFrame(skewed_data, skewed_schema)
    
    # Create dimension table
    dim_data = [(f"Key_{i}", f"Info_{i}") for i in range(100)]
    dim_data.append(("SKEWED_KEY", "Skewed_Info"))
    
    dim_schema = StructType([
        StructField("key", StringType(), True),
        StructField("info", StringType(), True)
    ])
    dim_df = spark.createDataFrame(dim_data, dim_schema)
    
    print("\n1. Detect Data Skew:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Analyze key distribution
    key_distribution = skewed_df.groupBy("key").count().orderBy(col("count").desc())
    print("Top 5 keys by frequency:")
    key_distribution.show(5)
    
    print("\n2. Standard Join (with skew):")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    standard_join = skewed_df.join(dim_df, "key")
    print("Standard join plan:")
    standard_join.explain(mode="simple")
    
    start_time = time.time()
    standard_result = standard_join.count()
    standard_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Standard join time: {standard_time:.4f} seconds")
    
    print("\n3. Adaptive Skew Join (AQE):")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Enable AQE skew join optimization
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionFactor", "5")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.skewedPartitionThresholdInBytes", "256MB")
    
    aqe_join = skewed_df.join(dim_df, "key")
    print("AQE skew join plan:")
    aqe_join.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    start_time = time.time()
    aqe_result = aqe_join.count()
    aqe_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"AQE skew join time: {aqe_time:.4f} seconds")
    
    print("\n4. Salting Technique:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import concat, lit, rand, floor
    
    # Add salt to skewed table
    salt_num = 10
    salted_skewed = skewed_df.withColumn(
        "salted_key",
        concat(col("key"), lit("_"), floor(rand() * salt_num).cast("int"))
    )
    
    # Replicate dimension table
    from pyspark.sql.functions import explode, array
    
    salt_array = array([lit(i) for i in range(salt_num)])
    replicated_dim = dim_df.withColumn("salt", explode(salt_array)) \
        .withColumn("salted_key", concat(col("key"), lit("_"), col("salt")))
    
    # Join on salted keys
    salted_join = salted_skewed.join(replicated_dim, "salted_key") \
        .select(salted_skewed.id, salted_skewed.key, 
                salted_skewed.value, replicated_dim.info)
    
    print("Salted join plan:")
    salted_join.explain(mode="simple")
    
    start_time = time.time()
    salted_result = salted_join.count()
    salted_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Salted join time: {salted_time:.4f} seconds")
    
    print("\n5. Performance Comparison:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"Standard join: {standard_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"AQE skew join: {aqe_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"Salted join: {salted_time:.4f} seconds")
    
    best_time = min(standard_time, aqe_time, salted_time)
    if best_time == aqe_time:
        print("\n✓ AQE skew join performed best")
    elif best_time == salted_time:
        print("\n✓ Salted join performed best")
    else:
        print("\n✓ Standard join performed best (no significant skew impact)")
    
    print("\n6. Skew Handling Strategies:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print("✓ Enable AQE skew join optimization")
    print("✓ Use salting for extreme skew")
    print("✓ Consider broadcast join for small dimension")
    print("✓ Isolate and handle skewed keys separately")
    print("✓ Monitor partition sizes and task execution times")
    
    return aqe_join

def test_all_patterns():

        ("Logical Plan Pattern", lambda: logical_plan_pattern(sales_df, store_df)),

        ("Optimized Plan Pattern", lambda: optimized_plan_pattern(sales_df, store_df)),
        ("Executed Plan Pattern", lambda: executed_plan_pattern(sales_df, store_df)),
        ("Adaptive Plan Pattern", lambda: adaptive_plan_pattern(sales_df, store_df)),
        ("Plan Caching Pattern", lambda: plan_caching_pattern(sales_df, store_df))
    ]
    
    results = {}
    
    for pattern_name, pattern_func in patterns:
        try:
            print(f"\nTesting: {pattern_name}")
            start_time = time.time()
            result = pattern_func()
            execution_time = time.time() - start_time
            results[pattern_name] = {
                'status': 'SUCCESS',
                'time': execution_time,
                'result': result
            }
            print(f"✓ {pattern_name} completed in {execution_time:.4f} seconds")
        except Exception as e:
            results[pattern_name] = {
                'status': 'FAILED',
                'error': str(e)
            }

    # Print summary

    print("TEST SUMMARY")

    total_count = len(results)
    
    print(f"\nTests Passed: {success_count}/{total_count}")
    
    for pattern_name, result in results.items():
        status_symbol = "✓" if result['status'] == 'SUCCESS' else "✗"

        if result['status'] == 'SUCCESS':

def generate_performance_report(sales_df, store_df):
    """
    Generate comprehensive performance report
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COMPREHENSIVE PERFORMANCE REPORT")
    print("="*80)
    
    report = {
        'queries': [],
        'optimizations': [],
        'recommendations': []
    }
    
    # Test Query 1: Simple aggregation
    print("\n1. Testing Simple Aggregation...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    simple_agg = sales_df.groupBy("product").agg(_sum("revenue").alias("total"))
    
    start_time = time.time()
    simple_result = simple_agg.count()
    simple_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    report['queries'].append({
        'name': 'Simple Aggregation',
        'time': simple_time,
        'rows': simple_result,
        'partitions': simple_agg.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    })
    
    print(f"Time: {simple_time:.4f}s | Rows: {simple_result} | Partitions: {simple_agg.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Test Query 2: Join with aggregation
    print("\n2. Testing Join with Aggregation...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    join_agg = sales_df.join(store_df, sales_df.store == store_df.store_id) \
        .groupBy("region").agg(_sum("revenue").alias("total"))
    
    start_time = time.time()
    join_result = join_agg.count()
    join_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    report['queries'].append({
        'name': 'Join with Aggregation',
        'time': join_time,
        'rows': join_result,
        'partitions': join_agg.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    })
    
    print(f"Time: {join_time:.4f}s | Rows: {join_result} | Partitions: {join_agg.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Test Query 3: Complex multi-stage query
    print("\n3. Testing Complex Multi-Stage Query...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    complex_query = sales_df \
        .filter(col("quantity") > 50) \
        .join(store_df, sales_df.store == store_df.store_id) \
        .groupBy("region", "product") \
        .agg(
            _sum("revenue").alias("total_revenue"),
            avg("quantity").alias("avg_quantity")
        ) \
        .filter(col("total_revenue") > 100) \
        .orderBy(col("total_revenue").desc())
    
    start_time = time.time()
    complex_result = complex_query.count()
    complex_time = time.time() - start_time
    
    report['queries'].append({
        'name': 'Complex Multi-Stage Query',
        'time': complex_time,
        'rows': complex_result,
        'partitions': complex_query.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    })
    
    print(f"Time: {complex_time:.4f}s | Rows: {complex_result} | Partitions: {complex_query.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Analyze optimizations
    print("\n4. Analyzing Applied Optimizations...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    plan_str = complex_query._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    
    optimizations = {
        'Predicate Pushdown': 'Filter' in plan_str,
        'Broadcast Join': 'Broadcast' in plan_str,
        'Column Pruning': True,  # Always applied by Catalyst
        'Whole-Stage Codegen': 'WholeStageCodegen' in plan_str,
        'Adaptive Execution': spark.conf.get('spark.sql.adaptive.enabled') == 'true'
    }
    
    for opt_name, applied in optimizations.items():
        status = "✓ Applied" if applied else "✗ Not Applied"
        print(f"{status}: {opt_name}")
        report['optimizations'].append({
            'name': opt_name,
            'applied': applied
        })
    
    # Generate recommendations
    print("\n5. Performance Recommendations...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    recommendations = []
    
    # Check AQE
    if not optimizations['Adaptive Execution']:
        rec = "Enable Adaptive Query Execution for better runtime optimization"
        recommendations.append(rec)
        print(f"• {rec}")
    
    # Check broadcast
    if not optimizations['Broadcast Join']:
        rec = "Consider using broadcast hints for small dimension tables"
        recommendations.append(rec)
        print(f"• {rec}")
    
    # Check partition count
    avg_partitions = sum(q['partitions'] for q in report['queries']) / len(report['queries'])
    if avg_partitions > 200:
        rec = f"High partition count ({avg_partitions:.0f} avg) - consider reducing"
        recommendations.append(rec)
        print(f"• {rec}")
    
    # Check execution times
    slowest_query = max(report['queries'], key=lambda x: x['time'])
    if slowest_query['time'] > 1.0:
        rec = f"Slowest query '{slowest_query['name']}' took {slowest_query['time']:.4f}s - investigate further"
        recommendations.append(rec)
        print(f"• {rec}")
    
    if not recommendations:
        print("✓ No major performance issues detected")
    
    report['recommendations'] = recommendations
    
    # Summary
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("REPORT SUMMARY")
    print("="*80)
    
    total_time = sum(q['time'] for q in report['queries'])
    total_rows = sum(q['rows'] for q in report['queries'])
    
    print(f"\nTotal Queries Tested: {len(report['queries'])}")
    print(f"Total Execution Time: {total_time:.4f} seconds")
    print(f"Total Rows Processed: {total_rows}")
    print(f"Optimizations Applied: {sum(1 for o in report['optimizations'] if o['applied'])}/{len(report['optimizations'])}")
    print(f"Recommendations: {len(recommendations)}")
    
    return report

def export_plan_to_file(df, filename, mode="formatted"):
    """
    Export execution plan to a text file
    """
    try:
        import io
        import sys
        
        # Capture explain output
        old_stdout = sys.stdout
        sys.stdout = buffer = io.StringIO()
        
        df.explain(mode=mode)
        
        output = buffer.getvalue()
        sys.stdout = old_stdout
        
        # Write to file
        with open(filename, 'w') as f:
            f.write(f"Execution Plan - Mode: {mode}\n")
            f.write("=" * 80 + "\n\n")
            f.write(output)
        
        print(f"✓ Plan exported to {filename}")
        return True
        
    except Exception as e:
        print(f"✗ Failed to export plan: {str(e)}")
        return False

def monitor_query_execution(df, query_name="Query"):
    """
    Monitor query execution with detailed metrics
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print(f"MONITORING QUERY EXECUTION: {query_name}")
    print("="*80)
    
    from datetime import datetime
    
    # Pre-execution info
    print(f"\n[{datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] Starting execution...")
    print(f"Initial partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
    
    # Show plan
    print("\nExecution Plan:")
    print("-" * 80)
    df.explain(mode="simple")
    
    # Execute with timing
    print(f"\n[{datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] Executing query...")
    start_time = time.time()
    
    try:
        result = df.collect()
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        
        print(f"[{datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] Execution completed")
        print("\nExecution Metrics:")
        print("-" * 80)
        print(f"✓ Status: SUCCESS")
        print(f"✓ Execution time: {execution_time:.4f} seconds")
        print(f"✓ Rows returned: {len(result)}")
        print(f"✓ Final partitions: {df.rdd.getNumPartitions()}")
        
        # Estimate throughput
        if execution_time > 0:
            throughput = len(result) / execution_time
            print(f"✓ Throughput: {throughput:.2f} rows/second")
        
        return {
            'status': 'SUCCESS',
            'time': execution_time,
            'rows': len(result),
            'result': result
        }
        
    except Exception as e:
        execution_time = time.time() - start_time
        print(f"[{datetime.now().strftime('%H:%M:%S')}] Execution failed")
        print("\nExecution Metrics:")
        print("-" * 80)
        print(f"✗ Status: FAILED")
        print(f"✗ Error: {str(e)}")
        print(f"✗ Time before failure: {execution_time:.4f} seconds")
        
        return {
            'status': 'FAILED',
            'time': execution_time,
            'error': str(e)
        }


def create_plan_visualization_data(df):
    """
    Create data structure for plan visualization
    """
    plan_str = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    
    nodes = []
    edges = []
    node_id = 0
    stack = []
    
    for line in plan_str.split('\n'):
        if not line.strip():
            continue
        
        # Calculate depth based on indentation
        depth = (len(line) - len(line.lstrip())) // 3
        
        # Extract node information
        node_text = line.strip()
        node_type = node_text.split('[')[0].strip() if '[' in node_text else node_text
        
        # Create node
        node = {
            'id': node_id,
            'type': node_type,
            'text': node_text,
            'depth': depth
        }
        nodes.append(node)
        
        # Create edge to parent
        if depth > 0 and stack:
            parent_id = stack[depth - 1]
            edges.append({
                'from': parent_id,
                'to': node_id
            })
        
        # Update stack
        if len(stack) <= depth:
            stack.append(node_id)
        else:
            stack[depth] = node_id
        
        node_id += 1
    
    return {
        'nodes': nodes,
        'edges': edges
    }


def analyze_shuffle_operations(df):
    """
    Analyze and report on shuffle operations in the plan
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("SHUFFLE OPERATIONS ANALYSIS")
    print("="*80)
    
    plan_str = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    
    # Find all Exchange operations
    shuffles = []
    for i, line in enumerate(plan_str.split('\n')):
        if 'Exchange' in line:
            shuffles.append({
                'line_num': i,
                'operation': line.strip(),
                'type': 'Hash' if 'hashpartitioning' in line.lower() else 'Range' if 'rangepartitioning' in line.lower() else 'Unknown'
            })
    
    print(f"\nTotal Shuffle Operations: {len(shuffles)}")
    
    if shuffles:
        print("\nShuffle Details:")
        print("-" * 80)
        for i, shuffle in enumerate(shuffles, 1):
            print(f"\n{i}. Type: {shuffle['type']}")
            print(f"   Operation: {shuffle['operation']}")
        
        print("\n" + "-" * 80)
        print("Shuffle Impact:")
        print("✓ Each shuffle writes data to disk and reads from network")
        print("✓ Shuffles are expensive operations")
        print(f"✓ This query has {len(shuffles)} shuffle(s)")
        
        if len(shuffles) > 3:
            print("\n⚠ WARNING: High number of shuffles detected!")
            print("  Consider:")
            print("  - Reducing repartition operations")
            print("  - Using broadcast joins for small tables")
            print("  - Enabling Adaptive Query Execution")
    else:
        print("\n✓ No shuffle operations detected")
        print("  This is optimal for performance")
    
    return shuffles


def benchmark_query_variations(base_df, variations):
    """
    Benchmark multiple variations of a query
    
    Args:
        base_df: Base DataFrame
        variations: List of tuples (name, transformation_function)
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("QUERY VARIATIONS BENCHMARK")
    print("="*80)
    
    results = []
    
    for name, transform_func in variations:
        print(f"\nBenchmarking: {name}")
        print("-" * 80)
        
        # Apply transformation
        df = transform_func(base_df)
        
        # Warm-up run
        df.count()
        
        # Timed runs
        times = []
        num_runs = 3
        
        for run in range(num_runs):
            start_time = time.time()
            count = df.count()
            elapsed = time.time() - start_time
            times.append(elapsed)
            print(f"  Run {run + 1}: {elapsed:.4f}s")
        
        avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
        min_time = min(times)
        max_time = max(times)
        
        results.append({
            'name': name,
            'avg_time': avg_time,
            'min_time': min_time,
            'max_time': max_time,
            'row_count': count
        })
        
        print(f"  Average: {avg_time:.4f}s")
    
    # Print comparison
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("BENCHMARK RESULTS")
    print("="*80)
    
    print(f"\n{'Variation':<40} {'Avg Time':<15} {'Min Time':<15} {'Max Time':<15}")
    print("-" * 85)
    
    for result in sorted(results, key=lambda x: x['avg_time']):
        print(f"{result['name']:<40} {result['avg_time']:<15.4f} {result['min_time']:<15.4f} {result['max_time']:<15.4f}")
    
    # Find best
    best = min(results, key=lambda x: x['avg_time'])
    worst = max(results, key=lambda x: x['avg_time'])
    
    print("\n" + "-" * 85)
    print(f"✓ Best: {best['name']} ({best['avg_time']:.4f}s)")
    print(f"✗ Worst: {worst['name']} ({worst['avg_time']:.4f}s)")
    
    if worst['avg_time'] > 0:
        speedup = worst['avg_time'] / best['avg_time']
        print(f"⚡ Speedup: {speedup:.2f}x")
    
    return results

def demonstrate_plan_stability():
    """
    Demonstrate plan stability across executions
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PLAN STABILITY ANALYSIS")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create test data
    data = [(i, f"Key_{i%100}", i * 10.0) for i in range(1, 1001)]
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("key", StringType(), True),
        StructField("value", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    # Define query
    query = df.groupBy("key").agg(_sum("value").alias("total"))
    
    print("\n1. Executing query multiple times...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    plans = []
    times = []
    
    for i in range(5):
        # Get plan
        import io
        import sys
        
        old_stdout = sys.stdout
        sys.stdout = buffer = io.StringIO()
        query.explain(mode="simple")
        plan = buffer.getvalue()
        sys.stdout = old_stdout
        
        plans.append(plan)
        
        # Execute
        start_time = time.time()
        query.count()
        exec_time = time.time() - start_time
        times.append(exec_time)
        
        print(f"Execution {i+1}: {exec_time:.4f}s")
    
    print("\n2. Plan Consistency Check:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Check if all plans are identical
    all_same = all(p == plans[0] for p in plans)
    
    if all_same:
        print("✓ All execution plans are identical")
        print("✓ Plan is stable across executions")
    else:
        print("⚠ Plans differ across executions")
        print("⚠ This may indicate non-deterministic optimization")
    
    print("\n3. Execution Time Consistency:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
    std_dev = (sum((t - avg_time) ** 2 for t in times) / len(times)) ** 0.5
    coefficient_of_variation = (std_dev / avg_time * 100) if avg_time > 0 else 0
    
    print(f"Average time: {avg_time:.4f}s")
    print(f"Std deviation: {std_dev:.4f}s")
    print(f"Coefficient of variation: {coefficient_of_variation:.2f}%")
    
    if coefficient_of_variation < 10:
        print("✓ Execution times are consistent")
    else:
        print("⚠ High variance in execution times")
    
    return plans, times


def demonstrate_cost_based_join_selection():
    """
    Demonstrate how CBO selects join strategies
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("COST-BASED JOIN STRATEGY SELECTION")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create tables of different sizes
    small_data = [(i, f"Small_{i}") for i in range(1, 101)]
    medium_data = [(i, f"Medium_{i}") for i in range(1, 1001)]
    large_data = [(i, f"Large_{i}") for i in range(1, 10001)]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("value", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    small_df = spark.createDataFrame(small_data, schema)
    medium_df = spark.createDataFrame(medium_data, schema)
    large_df = spark.createDataFrame(large_data, schema)
    
    print("\n1. Dataset Sizes:")
    print("-" * 80)
    print(f"Small table: {small_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Medium table: {medium_df.count()} rows")
    print(f"Large table: {large_df.count()} rows")
    
    # Register tables for statistics
    small_df.createOrReplaceTempView("small_table")
    medium_df.createOrReplaceTempView("medium_table")
    large_df.createOrReplaceTempView("large_table")
    
    # Compute statistics
    print("\n2. Computing Statistics...")
    print("-" * 80)
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE small_table COMPUTE STATISTICS")
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE medium_table COMPUTE STATISTICS")
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE large_table COMPUTE STATISTICS")
    print("✓ Statistics computed")
    
    # Test different join combinations
    print("\n3. Join Strategy Selection:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Small x Large (should use broadcast)
    print("\nSmall x Large Join:")
    join1 = spark.sql("""
        SELECT l.id, l.value as large_val, s.value as small_val
        FROM large_table l
        JOIN small_table s ON l.id = s.id
    """)
    join1.explain(mode="simple")
    
    # Medium x Medium (should use sort-merge or shuffle hash)
    print("\nMedium x Medium Join:")
    join2 = spark.sql("""
        SELECT m1.id, m1.value as val1, m2.value as val2
        FROM medium_table m1
        JOIN medium_table m2 ON m1.id = m2.id
    """)
    join2.explain(mode="simple")
    
    # Large x Large (should use sort-merge)
    print("\nLarge x Large Join:")
    join3 = spark.sql("""
        SELECT l1.id, l1.value as val1, l2.value as val2
        FROM large_table l1
        JOIN large_table l2 ON l1.id = l2.id
    """)
    join3.explain(mode="simple")
    
    print("\n4. Join Strategy Analysis:")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    def detect_join_strategy(df):
        plan_str = df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
        if 'BroadcastHashJoin' in plan_str:
            return 'Broadcast Hash Join'
        elif 'ShuffleHashJoin' in plan_str:
            return 'Shuffle Hash Join'
        elif 'SortMergeJoin' in plan_str:
            return 'Sort Merge Join'
        else:
            return 'Unknown'
    
    print(f"Small x Large: {detect_join_strategy(join1)}")
    print(f"Medium x Medium: {detect_join_strategy(join2)}")
    print(f"Large x Large: {detect_join_strategy(join3)}")
    
    # Cleanup
    spark.catalog.dropTempView("small_table")
    spark.catalog.dropTempView("medium_table")
    spark.catalog.dropTempView("large_table")
    
    return join1, join2, join3


def create_execution_plan_cheatsheet():
    """
    Create a comprehensive cheatsheet for execution plans
    """
    cheatsheet = """
    
    ╔══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║                  PYSPARK EXECUTION PLAN CHEATSHEET                       ║
    ╚══════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ EXPLAIN MODES                                                            │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    df.explain()                           # Simple physical plan
    df.explain(True)                       # All plans (parsed, analyzed, optimized, physical)
    df.explain(mode="simple")              # Physical plan only
    df.explain(mode="extended")            # All plans with details
    df.explain(mode="codegen")             # Generated code
    df.explain(mode="cost")                # With cost information
    df.explain(mode="formatted")           # Formatted tree structure
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ COMMON OPERATORS IN PLANS                                                │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    Exchange                               # Shuffle operation (expensive!)
    BroadcastExchange                      # Broadcast data to all executors
    HashAggregate                          # Hash-based aggregation
    SortAggregate                          # Sort-based aggregation
    BroadcastHashJoin                      # Broadcast join (fast for small tables)
    SortMergeJoin                          # Sort-merge join (for large tables)
    ShuffleHashJoin                        # Shuffle hash join
    Project                                # Column selection/transformation
    Filter                                 # Row filtering
    Sort                                   # Sorting operation
    WholeStageCodegen                      # Code generation optimization
    ColumnarToRow / RowToColumnar          # Format conversion
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ JOIN STRATEGIES                                                          │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    Broadcast Hash Join:
      • Best for: Small dimension tables (< 10MB)
      • Pros: No shuffle, fastest
      • Cons: Limited by broadcast size
      • Hint: df.hint("broadcast")
    
    Shuffle Hash Join:
      • Best for: Medium-sized tables
      • Pros: Memory efficient
      • Cons: Requires shuffle
      • Hint: df.hint("shuffle_hash")
    
    Sort Merge Join:
      • Best for: Large tables
      • Pros: Most scalable
      • Cons: Requires sort + shuffle
      • Hint: df.hint("merge")
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES                                                  │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    1. Predicate Pushdown
       • Filters pushed to data source
       • Reduces data read
       • Automatic in most cases
    
    2. Column Pruning
       • Only required columns read
       • Reduces I/O and memory
       • Automatic with Catalyst
    
    3. Constant Folding
       • Compile-time constant evaluation
       • Example: WHERE col > 10 + 5 → WHERE col > 15
    
    4. Partition Pruning
       • Skip irrelevant partitions
       • Requires partitioned data
       • Huge performance gain
    
    5. Whole-Stage Code Generation
       • Generates optimized JVM bytecode
       • Fuses operators
       • 2-10x performance improvement
    
    6. Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)
       • Runtime optimization
       • Dynamic partition coalescing
       • Dynamic join strategy switching
       • Skew join optimization
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ CONFIGURATION PARAMETERS                                                 │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    # Adaptive Query Execution
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
    
    # Broadcast Join Threshold
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760")  # 10MB
    
    # Shuffle Partitions
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
    
    # Code Generation
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.codegen.wholeStage", "true")
    
    # Cost-Based Optimization
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.enabled",
```python
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.cbo.joinReorder.enabled", "true")
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ PERFORMANCE TUNING CHECKLIST                                             │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    □ Enable AQE for runtime optimization
    □ Use appropriate join hints for small tables
    □ Cache frequently accessed DataFrames
    □ Optimize partition count (128-256MB per partition)
    □ Use broadcast joins for dimension tables
    □ Avoid UDFs when possible (use built-in functions)
    □ Compute table statistics for CBO
    □ Monitor shuffle operations (minimize them)
    □ Use column pruning (select only needed columns)
    □ Push filters as early as possible
    □ Repartition before expensive operations
    □ Handle data skew (salting, AQE)
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ TROUBLESHOOTING GUIDE                                                    │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    Problem: Too many shuffles
    Solution:
      • Check for excessive repartition() calls
      • Use coalesce() instead of repartition() when reducing partitions
      • Enable AQE for automatic partition coalescing
      • Combine operations to reduce shuffle stages
    
    Problem: Slow joins
    Solution:
      • Use broadcast hint for small tables
      • Enable CBO and compute statistics
      • Check for data skew
      • Consider join order (smallest table first)
    
    Problem: Out of memory
    Solution:
      • Reduce partition size
      • Increase executor memory
      • Use appropriate storage level for cache
      • Unpersist unused cached data
      • Check for data skew
    
    Problem: Data skew
    Solution:
      • Enable spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled
      • Use salting technique for extreme skew
      • Repartition on skewed keys
      • Isolate skewed keys and handle separately
    
    Problem: Slow aggregations
    Solution:
      • Ensure proper partitioning
      • Use partial aggregations
      • Consider approximate aggregations for large datasets
      • Check if predicate pushdown is working
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ CACHING STRATEGIES                                                       │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    from pyspark.storagelevel import StorageLevel
    
    # Memory only (fastest, but limited)
    df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY)
    
    # Memory and disk (spills to disk if needed)
    df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_AND_DISK)
    
    # Serialized in memory (saves space)
    df.persist(StorageLevel.MEMORY_ONLY_SER)
    
    # Disk only (slowest, but reliable)
    df.persist(StorageLevel.DISK_ONLY)
    
    # Off-heap memory
    df.persist(StorageLevel.OFF_HEAP)
    
    # Default cache (MEMORY_AND_DISK)
    df.cache()
    
    # Unpersist when done
    df.unpersist()
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ ANALYZING TABLE STATISTICS                                               │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    # Compute table statistics
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE table_name COMPUTE STATISTICS")
    
    # Compute column statistics
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE table_name COMPUTE STATISTICS FOR COLUMNS col1, col2")
    
    # View statistics
    spark.sql("DESCRIBE EXTENDED table_name").show()
    
    # Drop statistics
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE table_name DROP STATISTICS")
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ PARTITION OPTIMIZATION                                                   │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    # Hash partitioning
    df.repartition(10, "column_name")
    
    # Range partitioning
    df.repartitionByRange(10, "column_name")
    
    # Reduce partitions (no shuffle)
    df.coalesce(5)
    
    # Check partition count
    df.rdd.getNumPartitions()
    
    # Check partition distribution
    df.rdd.glom().map(len).collect()
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ MONITORING AND DEBUGGING                                                 │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    # Access Spark UI
    # http://localhost:4040
    
    # Get query execution plan
    df._jdf.queryExecution().toString()
    
    # Get logical plan
    df._jdf.queryExecution().logical().toString()
    
    # Get optimized plan
    df._jdf.queryExecution().optimizedPlan().toString()
    
    # Get physical plan
    df._jdf.queryExecution().executedPlan().toString()
    
    # Get query ID
    df._jdf.queryExecution().executionId()
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ BEST PRACTICES                                                           │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    1. Always use df.explain() to understand query execution
    2. Enable AQE for production workloads
    3. Cache intermediate results used multiple times
    4. Use broadcast joins for small dimension tables
    5. Partition data appropriately (128-256MB per partition)
    6. Compute statistics for cost-based optimization
    7. Monitor Spark UI for bottlenecks
    8. Avoid wide transformations when possible
    9. Use built-in functions instead of UDFs
    10. Test queries with representative data volumes
    
    
    ┌──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ QUICK REFERENCE: PLAN INTERPRETATION                                     │
    └──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    Good Signs in Plan:
      ✓ BroadcastHashJoin for dimension tables
      ✓ Filter operations near data source
      ✓ WholeStageCodegen present
      ✓ Few Exchange operations
      ✓ Column pruning applied
      ✓ Partition pruning applied
    
    Warning Signs in Plan:
      ⚠ Multiple Exchange operations
      ⚠ CartesianProduct (cross join)
      ⚠ No predicate pushdown
      ⚠ Sort operations on large data
      ⚠ High partition counts
      ⚠ No broadcast for small tables
    
    """
    
    print(cheatsheet)
    return cheatsheet


def final_comprehensive_example():
    """
    Final comprehensive example combining all patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("FINAL COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLE - ALL PATTERNS COMBINED")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Create realistic dataset
    print("\n1. Creating Realistic Dataset...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    # Sales transactions
    sales_data = [
        (i, 
         f"Customer_{i%500}", 
         f"Product_{i%100}", 
         f"Store_{i%20}",
         f"2024-01-{(i%28)+1:02d}",
         i * 10.0,
         i % 10) 
        for i in range(1, 10001)
    ]
    
    sales_schema = StructType([
        StructField("transaction_id", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("store_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("date", StringType(), True),
        StructField("amount", DoubleType(), True),
        StructField("quantity", IntegerType(), True)
    ])
    
    sales_df = spark.createDataFrame(sales_data, sales_schema)
    
    # Customer dimension
    customer_data = [(f"Customer_{i}", f"Segment_{i%5}", f"Region_{i%3}") 
                     for i in range(500)]
    customer_schema = StructType([
        StructField("customer_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("segment", StringType(), True),
        StructField("region", StringType(), True)
    ])
    customers_df = spark.createDataFrame(customer_data, customer_schema)
    
    # Product dimension
    product_data = [(f"Product_{i}", f"Category_{i%10}", i * 5.0) 
                    for i in range(100)]
    product_schema = StructType([
        StructField("product_id", StringType(), True),
        StructField("category", StringType(), True),
        StructField("unit_price", DoubleType(), True)
    ])
    products_df = spark.createDataFrame(product_data, product_schema)
    
    print(f"✓ Sales transactions: {sales_df.count()}")
    print(f"✓ Customers: {customers_df.count()}")
    print(f"✓ Products: {products_df.count()}")
    
    # Enable all optimizations
    print("\n2. Enabling All Optimizations...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.adaptive.skewJoin.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.cbo.enabled", "true")
    spark.conf.set("spark.sql.autoBroadcastJoinThreshold", "10485760")
    
    print("✓ Adaptive Query Execution enabled")
    print("✓ Cost-Based Optimization enabled")
    print("✓ Auto broadcast threshold set")
    
    # Compute statistics
    print("\n3. Computing Statistics...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    sales_df.createOrReplaceTempView("sales")
    customers_df.createOrReplaceTempView("customers")
    products_df.createOrReplaceTempView("products")
    
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE sales COMPUTE STATISTICS")
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE customers COMPUTE STATISTICS")
    spark.sql("ANALYZE TABLE products COMPUTE STATISTICS")
    
    print("✓ Statistics computed for all tables")
    
    # Complex analytical query
    print("\n4. Building Complex Analytical Query...")
    print("-" * 80)
    
    from pyspark.sql.functions import to_date, month, year
    
    # Cache intermediate result
    enriched_sales = sales_df \
        .join(customers_df.hint("broadcast"), "customer_id") \
        .join(products_df.hint("broadcast"), "product_id") \
        .withColumn("date_parsed", to_date(col("date"), "yyyy-MM-dd")) \
        .withColumn("month", month(col("date_parsed"))) \
        .withColumn("year", year(col("date_parsed"))) \

"""
PySpark Data Clustering Patterns Implementation
Author: Expert Code Generation Assistant
Description: Comprehensive clustering patterns for big data processing

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from pyspark.ml.feature import VectorAssembler, StandardScaler
from pyspark.ml.clustering import KMeans, BisectingKMeans
from pyspark.ml.linalg import Vectors, VectorUDT
import numpy as np
from typing import List, Tuple
import math

# Initialize Spark Session
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("DataClusteringPatterns") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.coalescePartitions.enabled", "true") \
    .getOrCreate()

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: K-MEANS CLUSTERING PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class KMeansClusteringPattern:
    """
    K-Means clustering for partitioning data into K distinct clusters.
    Best for: Spherical clusters, known number of clusters
    """
    
    def __init__(self, k: int = 3, max_iter: int = 20, seed: int = 42):
        """
        Initialize K-Means clustering
        
        Args:
            k: Number of clusters
            max_iter: Maximum iterations for convergence
            seed: Random seed for reproducibility
        """
        self.k = k
        self.max_iter = max_iter
        self.seed = seed
        self.model = None
        
    def prepare_features(self, df, feature_cols: List[str]):
        """
        Prepare features for clustering
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            feature_cols: List of feature column names
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with assembled and scaled features
        """
        # Assemble features into a single vector
        assembler = VectorAssembler(
            inputCols=feature_cols,
            outputCol="features_raw"
        )
        df_assembled = assembler.transform(df)
        
        # Scale features for better clustering
        scaler = StandardScaler(
            inputCol="features_raw",
            outputCol="features",
            withStd=True,
            withMean=True
        )
        scaler_model = scaler.fit(df_assembled)
        df_scaled = scaler_model.transform(df_assembled)
        
        return df_scaled, scaler_model
    
    def fit_predict(self, df, feature_cols: List[str]):
        """
        Fit K-Means model and predict clusters
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            feature_cols: List of feature column names
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with cluster predictions
        """
        # Prepare features
        df_prepared, scaler_model = self.prepare_features(df, feature_cols)
        
        # Train K-Means model
        kmeans = KMeans(
            k=self.k,
            maxIter=self.max_iter,
            seed=self.seed,
            featuresCol="features",
            predictionCol="cluster"
        )
        
        self.model = kmeans.fit(df_prepared)
        
        # Make predictions
        df_clustered = self.model.transform(df_prepared)
        
        # Calculate cluster statistics
        cluster_stats = df_clustered.groupBy("cluster").agg(
            count("*").alias("count"),
            avg("features").alias("centroid")
        )
        
        return df_clustered, cluster_stats
    
    def evaluate(self, df_clustered):
        """
        Evaluate clustering quality using silhouette score and WSSSE
        
        Args:
            df_clustered: DataFrame with cluster predictions
            
        Returns:
            Dictionary with evaluation metrics
        """
        from pyspark.ml.evaluation import ClusteringEvaluator
        
        # Within Set Sum of Squared Errors
        wssse = self.model.summary.trainingCost
        
        # Silhouette score
        evaluator = ClusteringEvaluator(
            featuresCol="features",
            predictionCol="cluster",
            metricName="silhouette"
        )
        silhouette = evaluator.evaluate(df_clustered)
        
        return {
            "wssse": wssse,
            "silhouette": silhouette,
            "num_clusters": self.k
        }


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 2: HIERARCHICAL CLUSTERING PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class HierarchicalClusteringPattern:
    """
    Hierarchical clustering using Bisecting K-Means (divisive approach).
    Best for: Tree-like cluster structures, variable granularity
    """
    
    def __init__(self, k: int = 5, max_iter: int = 20, seed: int = 42):
        """
        Initialize Hierarchical clustering
        
        Args:
            k: Number of leaf clusters
            max_iter: Maximum iterations per split
            seed: Random seed
        """
        self.k = k
        self.max_iter = max_iter
        self.seed = seed
        self.model = None
        
    def fit_predict(self, df, feature_cols: List[str]):
        """
        Fit hierarchical clustering model
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            feature_cols: List of feature column names
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with hierarchical cluster assignments
        """
        # Prepare features
        assembler = VectorAssembler(
            inputCols=feature_cols,
            outputCol="features_raw"
        )
        df_assembled = assembler.transform(df)
        
        # Scale features
        scaler = StandardScaler(
            inputCol="features_raw",
            outputCol="features",
            withStd=True,
            withMean=True
        )
        scaler_model = scaler.fit(df_assembled)
        df_scaled = scaler_model.transform(df_assembled)
        
        # Train Bisecting K-Means (hierarchical divisive clustering)
        bkm = BisectingKMeans(
            k=self.k,
            maxIter=self.max_iter,
            seed=self.seed,
            featuresCol="features",
            predictionCol="cluster"
        )
        
        self.model = bkm.fit(df_scaled)
        
        # Make predictions
        df_clustered = self.model.transform(df_scaled)
        
        # Get cluster hierarchy information
        cluster_centers = self.model.clusterCenters()
        
        return df_clustered, cluster_centers
    
    def get_cluster_hierarchy(self):
        """
        Extract cluster hierarchy tree structure
        
        Returns:
            Dictionary representing the cluster tree
        """
        if self.model is None:
            raise ValueError("Model not fitted yet")
        
        # Get cluster centers at each level
        centers = self.model.clusterCenters()
        
        hierarchy = {
            "num_levels": int(math.log2(self.k)) + 1,
            "leaf_clusters": self.k,
            "centers": [center.toArray().tolist() for center in centers]
        }
        
        return hierarchy


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 3: DENSITY-BASED CLUSTERING PATTERN (DBSCAN-like)
# ============================================================================

class DensityBasedClusteringPattern:
    """
    Density-based clustering implementation for PySpark.
    Best for: Arbitrary shaped clusters, noise detection
    """
    
    def __init__(self, eps: float = 0.5, min_points: int = 5):
        """
        Initialize density-based clustering
        
        Args:
            eps: Maximum distance between two samples for neighborhood
            min_points: Minimum points in neighborhood to form dense region
        """
        self.eps = eps
        self.min_points = min_points
        
    def fit_predict(self, df, feature_cols: List[str]):
        """
        Fit density-based clustering (DBSCAN-like algorithm)
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            feature_cols: List of feature column names
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with cluster assignments (-1 for noise)
        """
        # Prepare features
        assembler = VectorAssembler(
            inputCols=feature_cols,
            outputCol="features"
        )
        df_assembled = assembler.transform(df)
        
        # Add unique ID for each point
        df_with_id = df_assembled.withColumn("point_id", monotonically_increasing_id())
        
        # Broadcast epsilon for distance calculation
        eps_broadcast = self.eps
        min_pts_broadcast = self.min_points
        
        # UDF to calculate Euclidean distance
        @udf(DoubleType())
        def euclidean_distance(v1, v2):
            arr1 = np.array(v1.toArray())
            arr2 = np.array(v2.toArray())
            return float(np.sqrt(np.sum((arr1 - arr2) ** 2)))
        
        # Self-join to find neighbors within eps distance
        df_cross = df_with_id.alias("a").crossJoin(
            df_with_id.alias("b")
        ).where(col("a.point_id") != col("b.point_id"))
        
        # Calculate distances and find neighbors
        df_neighbors = df_cross.withColumn(
            "distance",
            euclidean_distance(col("a.features"), col("b.features"))
        ).where(col("distance") <= eps_broadcast)
        
        # Count neighbors for each point
        neighbor_counts = df_neighbors.groupBy("a.point_id").agg(
            count("*").alias("neighbor_count")
        )
        
        # Identify core points (points with >= min_points neighbors)
        df_labeled = df_with_id.join(
            neighbor_counts,
            df_with_id.point_id == neighbor_counts["a.point_id"],
            "left"
        ).withColumn(
            "is_core",
            when(col("neighbor_count") >= min_pts_broadcast, True).otherwise(False)
        ).withColumn(
            "cluster",
            when(col("is_core"), col("point_id")).otherwise(-1)
        )
        
        # Simplified cluster assignment (for demonstration)
        # In production, implement full DBSCAN with connected components
        df_clustered = df_labeled.select(
            "*",
            when(col("is_core"), col("cluster")).otherwise(-1).alias("final_cluster")
        )
        
        return df_clustered


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: GRID-BASED CLUSTERING PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class GridBasedClusteringPattern:
    """
    Grid-based clustering for spatial data.
    Best for: Large datasets, spatial data, fast clustering
    """
    
    def __init__(self, grid_size: float = 1.0, min_points: int = 5):
        """
        Initialize grid-based clustering
        
        Args:
            grid_size: Size of each grid cell
            min_points: Minimum points in grid cell to form cluster
        """
        self.grid_size = grid_size
        self.min_points = min_points
        
    def fit_predict(self, df, feature_cols: List[str]):
        """
        Fit grid-based clustering
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            feature_cols: List of feature column names (typically 2D coordinates)
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with grid-based cluster assignments
        """
        # Calculate grid cell for each point
        df_gridded = df
        
        for i, col_name in enumerate(feature_cols):
            grid_col_name = f"grid_{col_name}"
            df_gridded = df_gridded.withColumn(
                grid_col_name,
                floor(col(col_name) / self.grid_size)
            )
        
        # Create grid cell ID
        grid_cols = [f"grid_{col_name}" for col_name in feature_cols]
        df_gridded = df_gridded.withColumn(
            "grid_cell",
            concat_ws("_", *grid_cols)
        )
        
        # Count points in each grid cell
        grid_counts = df_gridded.groupBy("grid_cell").agg(
            count("*").alias("cell_count")
        )
        
        # Join back and assign clusters
        df_clustered = df_gridded.join(grid_counts, "grid_cell")
        
        # Assign cluster ID based on dense cells
        df_clustered = df_clustered.withColumn(
            "cluster",
            when(col("cell_count") >= self.min_points, 
                 dense_rank().over(Window.orderBy("grid_cell")) - 1
            ).otherwise(-1)  # Noise points
        )
        
        # Add cluster statistics
        cluster_stats = df_clustered.filter(col("cluster") != -1).groupBy("cluster").agg(
            count("*").alias("cluster_size"),
            *[avg(col_name).alias(f"centroid_{col_name}") for col_name in feature_cols]
        )
        
        return df_clustered, cluster_stats

# PATTERN 5: Z-ORDER CLUSTERING PATTERN (REFINED)
# ============================================================================

class ZOrderClusteringPattern:
    """
    Z-Order (Morton) curve clustering for multi-dimensional data.
    Best for: Range queries, spatial indexing, data skipping
    """
    
    def __init__(self, num_bits: int = 16, num_clusters: int = 10):
        """
        Initialize Z-Order clustering
        
        Args:
            num_bits: Number of bits for Z-order encoding
            num_clusters: Number of clusters to create
        """
        self.num_bits = num_bits
        self.num_clusters = num_clusters
        
    def interleave_bits(self, x: int, y: int) -> int:
        """
        Interleave bits of two integers to create Z-order value
        
        Args:
            x, y: Integer coordinates
            
        Returns:
            Z-order value
        """
        z = 0
        for i in range(self.num_bits):
            z |= ((x & (1 << i)) << i) | ((y & (1 << i)) << (i + 1))
        return z
    
    def fit_predict(self, df, feature_cols: List[str]):
        """
        Fit Z-Order clustering
        
        Args:
            df: Input DataFrame
            feature_cols: List of feature column names (2 dimensions)
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with Z-order cluster assignments
        """
        if len(feature_cols) != 2:
            raise ValueError("Z-Order clustering requires exactly 2 feature columns")
        
        # Normalize features to integer range [0, 2^num_bits - 1]
        max_val = (1 << self.num_bits) - 1
        
        # Get min/max for normalization
        stats = df.agg(
            min(feature_cols[0]).alias("min_x"),
            max(feature_cols[0]).alias("max_x"),
            min(feature_cols[1]).alias("min_y"),
            max(feature_cols[1]).alias("max_y")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        min_x, max_x = stats["min_x"], stats["max_x"]
        min_y, max_y = stats["min_y"], stats["max_y"]
        
        # Normalize and convert to integers
        df_normalized = df.withColumn(
            "
```python
            "x_normalized",
            ((col(feature_cols[0]) - min_x) / (max_x - min_x) * max_val).cast(IntegerType())
        ).withColumn(
            "y_normalized",
            ((col(feature_cols[1]) - min_y) / (max_y - min_y) * max_val).cast(IntegerType())
        )
        
        # UDF to calculate Z-order value
        @udf(LongType())
        def calculate_z_order(x, y):
            if x is None or y is None:
                return None
            z = 0
            for i in range(self.num_bits):
                z |= ((x & (1 << i)) << i) | ((y & (1 << i)) << (i + 1))
            return int(z)
        
        # Calculate Z-order value for each point
        df_z_order = df_normalized.withColumn(
            "z_order",
            calculate_z_order(col("x_normalized"), col("y_normalized"))
        )
        
        # Sort by Z-order value
        df_sorted = df_z_order.orderBy("z_order")
        
        # Assign clusters based on Z-order ranges
        # Calculate cluster boundaries
        total_count = df_sorted.count()
        points_per_cluster = total_count // self.num_clusters
        
        # Add row number and assign cluster
        df_clustered = df_sorted.withColumn(
            "row_num",
            row_number().over(Window.orderBy("z_order"))
        ).withColumn(
            "cluster",
            (col("row_num") / points_per_cluster).cast(IntegerType())
        ).withColumn(
            "cluster",
            when(col("cluster") >= self.num_clusters, self.num_clusters - 1)
            .otherwise(col("cluster"))
        )
        
        # Calculate cluster statistics
        cluster_stats = df_clustered.groupBy("cluster").agg(
            count("*").alias("cluster_size"),
            min("z_order").alias("z_order_min"),
            max("z_order").alias("z_order_max"),
            avg(feature_cols[0]).alias(f"centroid_{feature_cols[0]}"),
            avg(feature_cols[1]).alias(f"centroid_{feature_cols[1]}")
        )
        
        return df_clustered, cluster_stats
    
    def optimize_for_range_queries(self, df_clustered):
        """
        Optimize DataFrame for range queries using Z-order
        
        Args:
            df_clustered: DataFrame with Z-order clustering
            
        Returns:
            Optimized DataFrame
        """
        # Repartition by cluster for better locality
        df_optimized = df_clustered.repartition("cluster")
        
        # Sort within partitions by Z-order
        df_optimized = df_optimized.sortWithinPartitions("z_order")
        
        return df_optimized
