# PATTERN 1: EARLY FILTER PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Apply filters as early as possible in the pipeline to reduce data volume
# Benefits: Minimizes data shuffling, reduces memory usage, improves performance

def early_filter_pattern(transactions_df):
    """
    Apply filters immediately after reading data, before any transformations.
    This reduces the amount of data processed in subsequent operations.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 1: EARLY FILTER PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    # BAD PRACTICE: Late filtering after expensive operations
    print("\n--- Bad Practice (Late Filtering) ---")
    start_time = time.time()
    
    bad_result = transactions_df \
        .withColumn("amount_with_tax", col("amount") * 1.1) \
        .withColumn("year", year(to_date(col("date")))) \
        .withColumn("month", month(to_date(col("date")))) \
        .groupBy("category", "country") \
        .agg(
            sum("amount_with_tax").alias("total_amount"),
            count("*").alias("transaction_count")
        ) \
        .filter(col("country") == "US") \
        .filter(col("total_amount") > 10000)
    
    bad_count = bad_result.count()
    bad_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Records processed (late filter): {bad_count}")
    print(f"Time taken: {bad_time:.2f} seconds")
    
    # GOOD PRACTICE: Early filtering before transformations
    print("\n--- Good Practice (Early Filtering) ---")
    start_time = time.time()
    
    good_result = transactions_df \
        .filter(col("country") == "US") \
        .filter(col("status") == "active") \
        .withColumn("amount_with_tax", col("amount") * 1.1) \
        .withColumn("year", year(to_date(col("date")))) \
        .withColumn("month", month(to_date(col("date")))) \
        .groupBy("category", "country") \
        .agg(
            sum("amount_with_tax").alias("total_amount"),
            count("*").alias("transaction_count")
        ) \
        .filter(col("total_amount") > 10000)
    
    good_count = good_result.count()
    good_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Records processed (early filter): {good_count}")
    print(f"Time taken: {good_time:.2f} seconds")
    print(f"Performance improvement: {((bad_time - good_time) / bad_time * 100):.2f}%")
    
    good_result.show(5)
    
    return good_result

# PATTERN 2: LATE FILTER PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Apply filters after aggregations when filtering on aggregated values
# Use Case: When filter conditions depend on computed/aggregated values

def late_filter_pattern(transactions_df):
    """
    Apply filters after aggregations when the filter criteria
    depends on aggregated results.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 2: LATE FILTER PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Use case: Find categories with high average transaction amounts
    # Filter must be applied AFTER aggregation
    
    print("\n--- Correct Usage of Late Filter ---")
    
    result = transactions_df \
        .filter(col("status") == "active") \
        .groupBy("category", "country") \
        .agg(
            avg("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
            sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
            count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
            max("amount").alias("max_amount"),
            min("amount").alias("min_amount")
        ) \
        .filter(col("avg_amount") > 500) \
        .filter(col("transaction_count") > 100) \
        .orderBy(col("avg_amount").desc())
    
    print("\nCategories with avg transaction > 500 and count > 100:")
    result.show()
    
    # Window function example with late filter
    print("\n--- Late Filter with Window Functions ---")
    
    from pyspark.sql.window import Window
    
    window_spec = Window.partitionBy("category").orderBy(col("amount").desc())
    
    ranked_result = transactions_df \
        .filter(col("status") == "active") \
        .withColumn("rank", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
        .withColumn("dense_rank", dense_rank().over(window_spec)) \
        .filter(col("rank") <= 5)  # Late filter on window function result
    
    print("\nTop 5 transactions per category:")
    ranked_result.select("category", "amount", "rank", "country").show(20)
    
    return result

# PATTERN 3: PREDICATE FILTER PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Use predicate pushdown to optimize filtering at the data source level
# Benefits: Reduces data read from storage, leverages database/file optimizations

def predicate_filter_pattern():
    """
    Demonstrate predicate pushdown optimization where filters are pushed
    to the data source (database, parquet files, etc.)
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 3: PREDICATE FILTER PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Save sample data as parquet for demonstration
    transactions_df, _ = create_sample_data()
    
    # Partition data for better predicate pushdown
    output_path = "/tmp/transactions_partitioned"
    transactions_df.write \
        .partitionBy("country", "category") \
        .mode("overwrite") \
        .parquet(output_path)
    
    print(f"\n--- Reading with Predicate Pushdown ---")
    
    # Filters are pushed down to parquet reader
    # Only relevant partitions and row groups are read
    filtered_df = spark.read.parquet(output_path) \
        .filter(col("country") == "US") \
        .filter(col("category") == "Electronics") \
        .filter(col("amount") > 1000) \
        .filter(col("status") == "active")
    
    # Check physical plan to see predicate pushdown
    print("\nPhysical Plan (notice PushedFilters):")
    filtered_df.explain(mode="formatted")
    
    print("\nFiltered Results:")
    filtered_df.show(10)
    
    # Complex predicate example
    print("\n--- Complex Predicate Filters ---")
    
    complex_filter = (
        ((col("country") == "US") & (col("amount") > 1000)) |
        ((col("country") == "UK") & (col("amount") > 500))
    ) & (col("status") == "active")
    
    complex_result = spark.read.parquet(output_path) \
        .filter(complex_filter)
    
    print("\nComplex filter results:")
    complex_result.show(10)
    
    return filtered_df

        if "custom_filters" in config:
            for custom_filter in config["custom_filters"]:

                filtered_df = filtered_df.filter(expr(custom_filter))
        
        return filtered_df

```python
# Benefits: Reduces expensive joins, fast lookup for large datasets
# Note: May have false positives but no false negatives

def bloom_filter_pattern(transactions_df, customers_df):
    """
    Implement Bloom Filter for efficient semi-join operations.
    Useful for filtering large datasets based on membership in another dataset.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 5: BLOOM FILTER PATTERN (Refined)")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Method 1: Using Spark's built-in Bloom Filter (Spark 3.0+)
    print("\n--- Method 1: Spark Built-in Bloom Filter ---")
    
    # Create a bloom filter from the smaller dataset
    # This is useful for semi-joins where we only need to check membership
    
    # Scenario: Filter transactions for premium customers only
    premium_customers = customers_df.filter(col("tier") == "premium")
    
    # Traditional approach with join
    print("\nTraditional Join Approach:")
    start_time = time.time()
    
    traditional_result = transactions_df \
        .join(premium_customers.select("customer_id"), 
              transactions_df.transaction_id == premium_customers.customer_id,
              "inner")
    
    traditional_count = traditional_result.count()
    traditional_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Records: {traditional_count}, Time: {traditional_time:.2f}s")
    
    # Bloom filter approach using broadcast
    print("\nBloom Filter Approach (using broadcast):")
    start_time = time.time()
    
    # Collect premium customer IDs for bloom filter
    premium_ids = [row.customer_id for row in premium_customers.select("customer_id").collect()]
    
    # Broadcast the set for efficient filtering
    premium_ids_broadcast = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(set(premium_ids))
    
    # Create UDF to check membership
    def is_premium_customer(transaction_id):
        return transaction_id in premium_ids_broadcast.value
    
    is_premium_udf = udf(is_premium_customer, BooleanType())
    
    bloom_result = transactions_df \
        .filter(is_premium_udf(col("transaction_id")))
    
    bloom_count = bloom_result.count()
    bloom_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Records: {bloom_count}, Time: {bloom_time:.2f}s")
    
    # Method 2: Custom Bloom Filter Implementation
    print("\n--- Method 2: Custom Bloom Filter Implementation ---")
    
    class SimpleBloomFilter:
        """
        Simple Bloom Filter implementation for demonstration.
        Uses multiple hash functions to minimize false positives.
        """
        
        def __init__(self, size=10000, hash_count=3):
            self.size = size
            self.hash_count = hash_count
            self.bit_array = [False] * size
        
        def _hash(self, item, seed):
            """Generate hash for an item with given seed"""
            hash_str = f"{item}_{seed}"
            hash_val = int(hashlib.md5(hash_str.encode()).hexdigest(), 16)
            return hash_val % self.size
        
        def add(self, item):
            """Add item to bloom filter"""
            for seed in range(self.hash_count):
                index = self._hash(item, seed)
                self.bit_array[index] = True
        
        def contains(self, item):
            """Check if item might be in the set (may have false positives)"""
            for seed in range(self.hash_count):
                index = self._hash(item, seed)
                if not self.bit_array[index]:
                    return False  # Definitely not in set
            return True  # Probably in set
        
        def add_multiple(self, items):
            """Add multiple items to bloom filter"""
            for item in items:
                self.add(item)
    
    # Create bloom filter with premium customer IDs
    bloom_filter = SimpleBloomFilter(size=50000, hash_count=5)
    bloom_filter.add_multiple(premium_ids)
    
    # Broadcast the bloom filter
    bloom_filter_broadcast = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(bloom_filter)
    
    # Create UDF using bloom filter
    def bloom_filter_check(transaction_id):
        return bloom_filter_broadcast.value.contains(transaction_id)
    
    bloom_check_udf = udf(bloom_filter_check, BooleanType())
    
    start_time = time.time()
    custom_bloom_result = transactions_df \
        .filter(bloom_check_udf(col("transaction_id")))
    
    custom_bloom_count = custom_bloom_result.count()
    custom_bloom_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Records: {custom_bloom_count}, Time: {custom_bloom_time:.2f}s")
    
    # Method 3: Using Spark SQL Bloom Filter Join Hint (Spark 3.3+)
    print("\n--- Method 3: Bloom Filter Join Hint ---")
    
    # Register DataFrames as temp views
    transactions_df.createOrReplaceTempView("transactions")
    premium_customers.createOrReplaceTempView("premium_customers")
    
    # Use bloom filter join hint in SQL
    bloom_join_sql = """
        SELECT /*+ BLOOM_FILTER(t, p, 'customer_id') */ 
            t.*
        FROM transactions t
        INNER JOIN premium_customers p
        ON t.transaction_id = p.customer_id
    """
    
    start_time = time.time()
    sql_bloom_result = spark.sql(bloom_join_sql)
    sql_bloom_count = sql_bloom_result.count()
    sql_bloom_time = time.time() - start_time
    print(f"Records: {sql_bloom_count}, Time: {sql_bloom_time:.2f}s")
    
    # Method 4: Practical Bloom Filter Use Case - Deduplication
    print("\n--- Method 4: Bloom Filter for Deduplication ---")
    
    # Scenario: Filter out transactions that have already been processed
    processed_transaction_ids = list(range(1, 5001))  # Simulate processed IDs
    
    dedup_bloom = SimpleBloomFilter(size=100000, hash_count=5)
    dedup_bloom.add_multiple(processed_transaction_ids)
    
    dedup_bloom_broadcast = spark.sparkContext.broadcast(dedup_bloom)
    
    def is_new_transaction(transaction_id):
        return not dedup_bloom_broadcast.value.contains(transaction_id)
    
    is_new_udf = udf(is_new_transaction, BooleanType())
    
    new_transactions = transactions_df \
        .filter(is_new_udf(col("transaction_id")))
    
    print(f"\nNew transactions to process: {new_transactions.count()}")
    new_transactions.show(5)
    
    # Performance comparison summary
    print("\n--- Performance Summary ---")
    print(f"Traditional Join: {traditional_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"Broadcast Set Filter: {bloom_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"Custom Bloom Filter: {custom_bloom_time:.2f}s")
    print(f"SQL Bloom Filter Hint: {sql_bloom_time:.2f}s")
    
    return bloom_result

# PATTERN 6: RUNTIME FILTER PATTERN
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Generate filters at runtime based on data characteristics
# Benefits: Adaptive filtering, dynamic optimization based on actual data

def runtime_filter_pattern(transactions_df, customers_df):
    """
    Implement runtime filters that are generated dynamically based on
    data statistics and characteristics discovered during execution.
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("PATTERN 6: RUNTIME FILTER PATTERN")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Method 1: Statistical Runtime Filters
    print("\n--- Method 1: Statistical Runtime Filters ---")
    
    # Analyze data to determine optimal filter thresholds
    stats = transactions_df.select(
        avg("amount").alias("avg_amount"),
        stddev("amount").alias("stddev_amount"),
        percentile_approx("amount", 0.75).alias("p75_amount"),
        percentile_approx("amount", 0.90).alias("p90_amount"),
        percentile_approx("amount", 0.95).alias("p95_amount")
    ).collect()[0]
    
    print(f"\nData Statistics:")
    print(f"Average Amount: ${stats['avg_amount']:.2f}")
    print(f"Std Dev: ${stats['stddev_amount']:.2f}")
    print(f"75th Percentile: ${stats['p75_amount']:.2f}")
    print(f"90th Percentile: ${stats['p90_amount']:.2f}")
    print(f"95th Percentile: ${stats['p95_amount']:.2f}")
    
    # Create runtime filter based on statistics
    # Filter for outliers (above 95th percentile)
    runtime_threshold = stats['p95_amount']
    
    print(f"\nApplying runtime filter: amount > ${runtime_threshold:.2f}")
    outlier_transactions = transactions_df.filter(col("amount") > runtime_threshold)
    
    print(f"Outlier transactions found: {outlier_transactions.count()}")
    outlier_transactions.show(5)
    
    # Method 2: Adaptive Runtime Filters Based on Cardinality
    print("\n--- Method 2: Adaptive Cardinality-Based Filters ---")
    
    # Count distinct values to decide filter strategy
    category_counts = transactions_df.groupBy("category") \
        .agg(count("*").alias("count")) \
        .collect()
    
    print("\nCategory Distribution:")
    for row in category_counts:
        print(f"{row['category']}: {row['count']} transactions")
    
    # Dynamically select high-volume categories

    class RuntimeFilterBuilder:
        """
        Builder pattern for composing runtime filters dynamically
        """
        
        def __init__(self, df):
            self.df = df
            self.filters = []
        
        def add_percentile_filter(self, column, percentile, operator=">"):

            threshold = self.df.select(
                percentile_approx(
```python

            ).collect()[0][0]
            
            if operator == ">":
                self.filters.append(col(column) > threshold)
            elif operator == "<":
                self.filters.append(col(column) < threshold)
            elif operator == ">=":
                self.filters.append(col(column) >= threshold)
            elif operator == "<=":
                self.filters.append(col(column) <= threshold)
            
            print(f"Added percentile filter: {column} {operator} {threshold}")
            return self
        
        def add_frequency_filter(self, column, min_frequency):
            """Add filter based on value frequency"""
            freq_df = self.df.groupBy(column).count()
            high_freq_values = [row[column] for row in freq_df.collect() 
                               if row['count'] >= min_frequency]
            
            self.filters.append(col(column).isin(high_freq_values))
            print(f"Added frequency filter: {column} with min frequency {min_frequency}")
            return self
        
        def add_recency_filter(self, date_column, days_back):
            """Add filter for recent data"""
            max_date = self.df.agg(max(date_column)).collect()[0][0]
            max_date_obj = datetime.strptime(max_date, "%Y-%m-%d")
            cutoff_date = (max_date_obj - timedelta(days=days_back)).strftime("%Y-%m-%d")
            
            self.filters.append(col(date_column) >= cutoff_date)
            print(f"Added recency filter: {date_column} >= {cutoff_date}")
            return self
        
        def add_outlier_filter(self, column, std_devs=2):
            """Add filter to include/exclude outliers"""
            stats = self.df.select(
                avg(column).alias("mean"),
                stddev(column).alias("std")
            ).collect()[0]
            
            lower_bound = stats['mean'] - (std_devs * stats['std'])
            upper_bound = stats['mean'] + (std_devs * stats['std'])
            
            self.filters.append(
                (col(column) >= lower_bound) & (col(column) <= upper_bound)
            )
            print(f"Added outlier filter: {column} within {std_devs} std devs")
            return self
        
        def build(self):
            """Apply all filters and return filtered DataFrame"""
            result_df = self.df
            for filter_condition in self.filters:
                result_df = result_df.filter(filter_condition)
            return result_df

            """Apply filter and collect metrics"""
            self.df = self.df.filter(filter_condition)
            current_count = self.df.count()
            reduction = ((self.initial_count - current_count) / self.initial_count) * 100
            
            self.metrics['filters_applied'].append(filter_name)
            self.metrics['reduction_percentages'].append(reduction)
            
            print(f"\nFilter: {filter_name}")
            print(f"Records remaining: {current_count}")
            print(f"Total reduction: {reduction:.2f}%")
            
            return self
        
        def get_result(self):
            """Get filtered DataFrame and metrics"""
            return self.df, self.metrics
        
        def print_summary(self):

            print(f"Total filters applied: {len(self.metrics['filters_applied'])}")
            print("\nFilter breakdown:")

def advanced_filtering_examples():
    """
    Advanced real-world filtering scenarios combining multiple patterns
    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("ADVANCED FILTERING EXAMPLES")
    print("="*80)
    
    transactions_df, customers_df = create_sample_data()
    
    # Example 1: Multi-stage filtering pipeline
    print("\n--- Example 1: Multi-stage Filtering Pipeline ---")
    
    def multi_stage_filter(df):
        """
        Implement a multi-stage filtering strategy that combines
        early filters, runtime statistics, and dynamic optimization
        """
        # Stage 1: Early coarse-grained filter
        stage1 = df.filter(col("status") == "active")
        print(f"Stage 1 (status filter): {stage1.count()} records")
        
        # Stage 2: Runtime statistical filter
        stats = stage1.select(
            percentile_approx("amount", 0.5).alias("median")
        ).collect()[0]
        
        stage2 = stage1.filter(col("amount") > stats['median'])
        print(f"Stage 2 (above median): {stage2.count()} records")
        
        # Stage 3: Dynamic category filter based on frequency
        category_freq = stage2.groupBy("category").count()
        top_categories = [row['category'] for row in 
                         category_freq.orderBy(col("count").desc()).limit(2).collect()]
        
        stage3 = stage2.filter(col("category").isin(top_categories))
        print(f"Stage 3 (top categories): {stage3.count()} records")
        
        return stage3
    
    multi_stage_result = multi_stage_filter(transactions_df)
    multi_stage_result.show(5)
    
    # Example 2: Conditional filtering based on data characteristics
    print("\n--- Example 2: Adaptive Filtering Strategy ---")
    
    def adaptive_filter(df, target_reduction=0.9):
        """
        Adaptively apply filters to achieve target data reduction
        """
        initial_count = df.count()
        target_count = int(initial_count * (1 - target_reduction))
        
        print(f"Initial: {initial_count}, Target: {target_count}")
        
        filtered_df = df
        current_count = initial_count
        
        # Try filters in order of selectivity
        filters = [
            ("status = 'active'", col("status") == "active"),
            ("amount > 1000", col("amount") > 1000),
            ("category = 'Electronics'", col("category") == "Electronics"),
            ("country = 'US'", col("country") == "US")
        ]
        
        for filter_name, filter_condition in filters:
            if current_count <= target_count:
                break
            
            test_df = filtered_df.filter(filter_condition)
            test_count = test_df.count()
            
            if test_count >= target_count:
                filtered_df = test_df
                current_count = test_count
                print(f"Applied: {filter_name}, Count: {current_count}")
            else:
                print(f"Skipped: {filter_name} (would over-filter)")
        
        return filtered_df
    
    adaptive_result = adaptive_filter(transactions_df, target_reduction=0.8)
    adaptive_result.show(5)
    
    # Example 3: Intelligent caching with filtering
    print("\n--- Example 3: Smart Cache with Filters ---")
    
    # Cache filtered hot data for repeated queries
    hot_data_filter = (col("amount") > 1000) & \
                     (col("category") == "Electronics") & \
                     (col("status") == "active")
    
    hot_data = transactions_df.filter(hot_data_filter).cache()
    hot_count = hot_data.count()
    print(f"Cached hot data: {hot_count} records")
    
    # Multiple queries on hot data (will use cache)
    query1 = hot_data.filter(col("country") == "US").count()
    query2 = hot_data.groupBy("country").count().count()
    
    print(f"Query 1 result: {query1}")
    print(f"Query 2 result: {query2}")
    
    # Unpersist when done
    hot_data.unpersist()

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession
from pyspark.sql.types import *
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from datetime import datetime
import json
from typing import Dict, List, Optional

# Initialize Spark Session with appropriate configurations
spark = SparkSession.builder \
    .appName("DataFormatCompatibilityPatterns") \
    .config("spark.sql.sources.partitionOverwriteMode", "dynamic") \

# PATTERN 1: Schema Evolution Support Pattern
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Handle schema changes over time while maintaining data compatibility
# Use Case: Adding/removing columns, changing data types safely

class SchemaEvolutionManager:
    """
    Manages schema evolution with backward and forward compatibility.
    Supports: Column addition, column removal, type promotion, nested schema changes
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.schema_registry = {}
        
    def register_schema_version(self, table_name: str, version: int, schema: StructType):
        """Register a schema version for tracking"""
        key = f"{table_name}_v{version}"
        self.schema_registry[key] = {
            'version': version,
            'schema': schema,
            'timestamp': datetime.now()
        }
        
    def evolve_schema_add_columns(self, df, new_columns: Dict[str, any]):
        """
        Safely add new columns with default values
        
        Args:
            df: Source DataFrame
            new_columns: Dict of {column_name: default_value}
        """
        evolved_df = df
        for col_name, default_value in new_columns.items():
            if col_name not in df.columns:
                evolved_df = evolved_df.withColumn(col_name, lit(default_value))
        return evolved_df
    
    def evolve_schema_remove_columns(self, df, columns_to_remove: List[str]):
        """Safely remove columns"""
        remaining_cols = [col for col in df.columns if col not in columns_to_remove]
        return df.select(remaining_cols)
    
    def evolve_schema_rename_columns(self, df, column_mapping: Dict[str, str]):
        """
        Rename columns while maintaining compatibility
        
        Args:
            column_mapping: Dict of {old_name: new_name}
        """
        evolved_df = df
        for old_name, new_name in column_mapping.items():
            if old_name in df.columns:
                evolved_df = evolved_df.withColumnRenamed(old_name, new_name)
        return evolved_df
    
    def promote_data_types(self, df, type_promotions: Dict[str, str]):
        """
        Safely promote data types (e.g., int -> long, float -> double)
        
        Args:
            type_promotions: Dict of {column_name: new_type}
        """
        evolved_df = df
        for col_name, new_type in type_promotions.items():
            if col_name in df.columns:
                evolved_df = evolved_df.withColumn(
                    col_name, 
                    col(col_name).cast(new_type)
                )
        return evolved_df
    
    def merge_schemas(self, schema1: StructType, schema2: StructType) -> StructType:
        """Merge two schemas, taking union of all fields"""
        fields_dict = {}
        
        # Add fields from schema1
        for field in schema1.fields:
            fields_dict[field.name] = field
            
        # Add fields from schema2 (newer schema takes precedence)
        for field in schema2.fields:
            fields_dict[field.name] = field
            
        return StructType(list(fields_dict.values()))
    
    def write_with_schema_evolution(self, df, path: str, mode: str = "append"):
        """
        Write data with schema evolution support (Parquet)
        Automatically merges schemas when appending
        """
        df.write \
            .mode(mode) \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .parquet(path)
    
    def read_with_schema_evolution(self, path: str):
        """Read data with merged schema from all files"""
        return self.spark.read \
            .option("mergeSchema", "true") \
            .parquet(path)


# Example Usage: Schema Evolution

# Purpose: Maintain multiple versions of data formats simultaneously
# Use Case: API versioning, gradual migration, A/B testing

class VersionCompatibilityManager:
    """
    Manages multiple versions of data formats with compatibility layers
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.version_transformers = {}
        
    def register_version_transformer(self, from_version: int, to_version: int, 
                                    transform_func):
        """Register transformation function between versions"""
        key = f"v{from_version}_to_v{to_version}"
        self.version_transformers[key] = transform_func
        
    def add_version_metadata(self, df, version: int):
        """Add version tracking metadata to DataFrame"""
        return df.withColumn("_version", lit(version)) \
                 .withColumn("_version_timestamp", current_timestamp())
    
    def transform_to_version(self, df, current_version: int, target_version: int):
        """Transform data from one version to another"""
        key = f"v{current_version}_to_v{target_version}"
        if key in self.version_transformers:
            return self.version_transformers[key](df)
        else:
            raise ValueError(f"No transformer registered for {key}")
    
    def write_versioned_data(self, df, base_path: str, version: int, 
                            format_type: str = "parquet"):
        """Write data with version partitioning"""
        versioned_df = self.add_version_metadata(df, version)
        path = f"{base_path}/version={version}"
        
        versioned_df.write \
            .mode("overwrite") \
            .format(format_type) \
            .save(path)
        
        # Write version metadata
        version_info = {
            'version': version,
            'timestamp': datetime.now().isoformat(),
            'schema': df.schema.json(),
            'record_count': df.count()
        }
        
        metadata_path = f"{base_path}/version={version}/_metadata.json"
        with open(metadata_path.replace("file://", ""), 'w') as f:
            json.dump(version_info, f, indent=2)
    
    def read_versioned_data(self, base_path: str, version: Optional[int] = None):
        """Read data from specific version or latest"""
        if version:
            path = f"{base_path}/version={version}"
        else:
            path = base_path
            
        return self.spark.read.parquet(path)
    
    def create_compatibility_layer(self, df, source_version: int, 
                                   target_version: int):
        """
        Create compatibility layer for reading old data with new schema
        """
        if source_version < target_version:
            # Forward compatibility: add missing fields
            return self.transform_to_version(df, source_version, target_version)
        elif source_version > target_version:
            # Backward compatibility: remove extra fields
            return self.transform_to_version(df, source_version, target_version)
        else:
            return df


# Example Usage: Version Compatibility
def demo_version_compatibility():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 2: Version Compatibility Pattern")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    manager = VersionCompatibilityManager(spark)
    
    # Version 1 data structure
    data_v1 = [
        (1, "Product A", 100.0),
        (2, "Product B", 200.0)
    ]
    df_v1 = spark.createDataFrame(data_v1, ["id", "name", "price"])
    
    print("\n--- Version 1 Data ---")
    df_v1.show()
    
    # Define transformer from v1 to v2
    def transform_v1_to_v2(df):
        return df.withColumn("currency", lit("USD")) \
                 .withColumn("tax_rate", lit(0.1)) \
                 .withColumn("price_with_tax", col("price") * 1.1)
    
    manager.register_version_transformer(1, 2, transform_v1_to_v2)
    
    # Transform to Version 2
    df_v2 = manager.transform_to_version(df_v1, 1, 2)
    print("\n--- Version 2 Data (Transformed) ---")
    df_v2.show()
    
    # Define transformer from v2 to v3
    def transform_v2_to_v3(df):
        return df.withColumn("category", lit("General")) \
                 .withColumn("discount_eligible", lit(True)) \
                 .withColumn("final_price", 
                           when(col("discount_eligible"), col("price_with_tax") * 0.9)
                           .otherwise(col("price_with_tax")))
    
    manager.register_version_transformer(2, 3, transform_v2_to_v3)
    
    # Transform to Version 3
    df_v3 = manager.transform_to_version(df_v2, 2, 3)
    print("\n--- Version 3 Data (Transformed) ---")
    df_v3.show()
    
    # Write versioned data
    base_path = "/tmp/versioned_data"
    manager.write_versioned_data(df_v1, base_path, 1)
    manager.write_versioned_data(df_v2, base_path, 2)
    manager.write_versioned_data(df_v3, base_path, 3)
    
    # Read specific version
    df_read_v2 = manager.read_versioned_data(base_path, version=2)
    print("\n--- Read Version 2 ---")
    df_read_v2.show()

# PATTERN 3: Cross-Format Compatibility Pattern
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Convert between different file formats while preserving data integrity
# Use Case: Format migration, multi-format support, interoperability

class CrossFormatCompatibility:
    """
    Handle conversions between different data formats (Parquet, Avro, JSON, CSV, ORC)
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.format_configs = {
            'parquet': {
                'compression': 'snappy',
                'options': {}
            },
            'avro': {
                'compression': 'snappy',
                'options': {}
            },
            'json': {
                'compression': 'gzip',
                'options': {'multiLine': 'true'}
            },
            'csv': {
                'compression': 'gzip',
                'options': {'header': 'true', 'inferSchema': 'true'}
            },
            'orc': {
                'compression': 'zlib',
                'options': {}
            }
        }
    
    def convert_format(self, input_path: str, output_path: str, 
                      source_format: str, target_format: str,
                      schema: Optional[StructType] = None):
        """
        Convert data from one format to another
        
        Args:
            input_path: Source data path
            output_path: Destination path
            source_format: Source format (parquet, avro, json, csv, orc)
            target_format: Target format
            schema: Optional explicit schema
        """
        # Read from source format
        reader = self.spark.read.format(source_format)
        
        if schema:
            reader = reader.schema(schema)
            
        if source_format in self.format_configs:
            for key, value in self.format_configs[source_format]['options'].items():
                reader = reader.option(key, value)
        
        df = reader.load(input_path)
        
        # Write to target format
        writer = df.write.mode("overwrite").format(target_format)
        
        if target_format in self.format_configs:
            compression = self.format_configs[target_format]['compression']
            writer = writer.option("compression", compression)
            
            for key
```python
            for key, value in self.format_configs[target_format]['options'].items():
                writer = writer.option(key, value)
        
        writer.save(output_path)
        print(f"Converted {source_format} to {target_format}: {input_path} -> {output_path}")
        
        return df
    
    def batch_convert_formats(self, input_path: str, output_base_path: str,
                             source_format: str, target_formats: List[str]):
        """Convert single source to multiple target formats"""
        df = self.spark.read.format(source_format).load(input_path)
        
        results = {}
        for target_format in target_formats:
            output_path = f"{output_base_path}/{target_format}"
            self.convert_format(input_path, output_path, source_format, target_format)
            results[target_format] = output_path
            
        return results
    
    def create_format_agnostic_reader(self, path: str, format_hint: Optional[str] = None):
        """
        Read data regardless of format (auto-detect or use hint)
        """
        if format_hint:
            return self.spark.read.format(format_hint).load(path)
        
        # Try different formats
        formats_to_try = ['parquet', 'avro', 'json', 'csv', 'orc']
        
        for fmt in formats_to_try:
            try:
                df = self.spark.read.format(fmt).load(path)
                print(f"Successfully read as {fmt}")
                return df
            except Exception as e:
                continue
        
        raise ValueError(f"Could not read data from {path} with any supported format")
    
    def ensure_format_compatibility(self, df, target_format: str):
        """
        Ensure DataFrame is compatible with target format
        Handle format-specific limitations
        """
        if target_format == 'csv':
            # CSV doesn't support nested structures - flatten if needed
            # Check for nested columns
            nested_cols = [f.name for f in df.schema.fields 
                          if isinstance(f.dataType, (StructType, ArrayType, MapType))]
            
            if nested_cols:
                print(f"Warning: CSV format doesn't support nested types. "
                      f"Flattening columns: {nested_cols}")
                for col_name in nested_cols:
                    df = df.withColumn(col_name, to_json(col(col_name)))
        
        elif target_format == 'avro':
            # Avro has specific type requirements
            # Convert decimal types if needed
            pass
        
        return df
    
    def create_universal_format_wrapper(self, df, output_base_path: str):
        """
        Write data in multiple formats for maximum compatibility
        """
        formats = ['parquet', 'json', 'csv']
        paths = {}
        
        for fmt in formats:
            compatible_df = self.ensure_format_compatibility(df, fmt)
            path = f"{output_base_path}/{fmt}"
            
            writer = compatible_df.write.mode("overwrite").format(fmt)
            
            if fmt in self.format_configs:
                compression = self.format_configs[fmt]['compression']
                writer = writer.option("compression", compression)
                
                for key, value in self.format_configs[fmt]['options'].items():
                    writer = writer.option(key, value)
            
            writer.save(path)
            paths[fmt] = path
            
        return paths


# Example Usage: Cross-Format Compatibility
def demo_cross_format_compatibility():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 3: Cross-Format Compatibility Pattern")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    manager = CrossFormatCompatibility(spark)
    
    # Create sample data
    data = [
        (1, "Alice", 30, {"city": "New York", "country": "USA"}),
        (2, "Bob", 25, {"city": "London", "country": "UK"}),
        (3, "Charlie", 35, {"city": "Tokyo", "country": "Japan"})
    ]
    
    schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("age", IntegerType(), True),
        StructField("address", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
    ])
    
    df = spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    print("\n--- Original Data ---")
    df.show()
    df.printSchema()
    
    # Write in Parquet format first
    parquet_path = "/tmp/cross_format/parquet"
    df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(parquet_path)
    
    # Convert Parquet to other formats
    print("\n--- Converting Formats ---")
    
    # Parquet to JSON
    json_path = "/tmp/cross_format/json"
    manager.convert_format(parquet_path, json_path, 'parquet', 'json')
    
    # Parquet to CSV (with nested data flattened)
    csv_path = "/tmp/cross_format/csv"
    df_flat = df.withColumn("address_str", to_json(col("address"))).drop("address")
    df_flat.write.mode("overwrite").option("header", "true").csv(csv_path)
    
    # Parquet to ORC
    orc_path = "/tmp/cross_format/orc"
    manager.convert_format(parquet_path, orc_path, 'parquet', 'orc')
    
    # Batch conversion
    print("\n--- Batch Format Conversion ---")
    target_formats = ['json', 'orc']
    results = manager.batch_convert_formats(
        parquet_path, 
        "/tmp/cross_format/batch", 
        'parquet', 
        target_formats
    )
    print(f"Batch conversion results: {results}")
    
    # Read back in different formats
    print("\n--- Reading Different Formats ---")
    
    df_from_json = spark.read.json(json_path)
    print("From JSON:")
    df_from_json.show()
    
    df_from_orc = spark.read.orc(orc_path)
    print("From ORC:")
    df_from_orc.show()
    
    # Universal format wrapper
    print("\n--- Universal Format Wrapper ---")
    universal_paths = manager.create_universal_format_wrapper(
        df, 
        "/tmp/cross_format/universal"
    )
    print(f"Data written in multiple formats: {universal_paths}")


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 4: Backward Compatible Format Pattern
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Ensure new data formats can be read by older systems
# Use Case: System upgrades, maintaining legacy support

class BackwardCompatibilityManager:
    """
    Ensure new data can be read by older versions of applications
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        self.compatibility_rules = {}
        
    def register_compatibility_rule(self, rule_name: str, rule_func):
        """Register a backward compatibility rule"""
        self.compatibility_rules[rule_name] = rule_func
    
    def ensure_backward_compatible_schema(self, df, legacy_schema: StructType):
        """
        Ensure DataFrame schema is compatible with legacy schema
        - Remove new columns not in legacy schema
        - Ensure column order matches
        - Convert types if needed
        """
        legacy_columns = [field.name for field in legacy_schema.fields]
        
        # Select only columns that exist in legacy schema
        compatible_df = df.select(*[col for col in legacy_columns if col in df.columns])
        
        # Add missing columns with null values
        for field in legacy_schema.fields:
            if field.name not in compatible_df.columns:
                compatible_df = compatible_df.withColumn(
                    field.name, 
                    lit(None).cast(field.dataType)
                )
        
        # Reorder columns to match legacy schema
        compatible_df = compatible_df.select(*legacy_columns)
        
        # Cast types to match legacy schema
        for field in legacy_schema.fields:
            if field.name in compatible_df.columns:
                compatible_df = compatible_df.withColumn(
                    field.name,
                    col(field.name).cast(field.dataType)
                )
        
        return compatible_df
    
    def write_with_backward_compatibility(self, df, path: str, 
                                         legacy_schema: Optional[StructType] = None,
                                         keep_new_data: bool = True):
        """
        Write data maintaining backward compatibility
        
        Args:
            df: DataFrame to write
            path: Output path
            legacy_schema: Schema of legacy system
            keep_new_data: If True, write both compatible and full versions
        """
        if legacy_schema:
            compatible_df = self.ensure_backward_compatible_schema(df, legacy_schema)
            compatible_path = f"{path}/compatible"
            compatible_df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(compatible_path)
            print(f"Backward compatible data written to: {compatible_path}")
        
        if keep_new_data:
            full_path = f"{path}/full"
            df.write.mode("overwrite").parquet(full_path)
            print(f"Full data written to: {full_path}")
    
    def apply_default_values_for_new_columns(self, df, default_values: Dict[str, any]):
        """
        Apply default values for columns that don't exist in legacy data
        """
        result_df = df
        for col_name, default_val in default_values.items():
            if col_name not in df.columns:
                result_df = result_df.withColumn(col_name, lit(default_val))
        return result_df
    
    def create_compatibility_view(self, df, view_name: str, legacy_columns: List[str]):
        """
        Create a view that shows only legacy-compatible columns
        """
        compatible_df = df.select(*[c for c in legacy_columns if c in df.columns])
        compatible_df.createOrReplaceTempView(view_name)
        print(f"Created backward-compatible view: {view_name}")
        return compatible_df
    
    def validate_backward_compatibility(self, new_df, legacy_schema: StructType) -> bool:
        """
        Validate if new DataFrame is backward compatible
        """
        legacy_columns = set([field.name for field in legacy_schema.fields])
        new_columns = set(new_df.columns)
        
        # Check if all legacy columns exist
        missing_columns = legacy_columns - new_columns
        if missing_columns:
            print(f"Warning: Missing legacy columns: {missing_columns}")
            return False
        
        # Check data types
        for field in legacy_schema.fields:
            if field.name in new_df.columns:
                new_type = [f.dataType for f in new_df.schema.fields 
                           if f.name == field.name][0]
                if new_type != field.dataType:
                    print(f"Warning: Type mismatch for {field.name}: "
                          f"{new_type} vs {field.dataType}")
                    return False
        
        print("✓ Backward compatibility validated successfully")
        return True
    
    def downgrade_schema(self, df, target_version_schema: StructType):
        """
        Downgrade current schema to match target version
        """
        return self.ensure_backward_compatible_schema(df, target_version_schema)


# Example Usage: Backward Compatibility
def demo_backward_compatibility():
    print("\n" + "=" * 80)
    print("PATTERN 4: Backward Compatible Format Pattern")
    print("=" * 80)
    
    manager = BackwardCompatibilityManager(spark)
    
    # Legacy schema (Version 1)
    legacy_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("email", StringType(), True)
    ])
    
    # New schema (Version 2) - has additional fields
    new_data = [
        (1, "Alice", "alice@example.com", "Premium", 100, True),
        (2, "Bob", "bob@example.com", "Standard", 50, False),
        (3, "Charlie", "charlie@example.com", "Premium", 150, True)
    ]
    
    new_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), True),
        StructField("email", StringType(), True),
        StructField("subscription_type", StringType(), True),  # New field
        StructField("credits", IntegerType(), True),  # New field
        StructField("is_verified", BooleanType(), True)  # New field
    ])
    
    df_new = spark.createDataFrame(new_data, new_schema)
    
    print("\n--- New Version Data (V2) ---")
    df_new.show()
    df_new.printSchema()
    
    # Validate backward compatibility
    print("\n--- Validating Backward Compatibility ---")
    is_compatible = manager.validate_backward_compatibility(df_new, legacy_schema)
    
    # Create backward compatible version
    print("\n--- Creating Backward Compatible Version ---")
    df_compatible = manager.ensure_backward_compatible_schema(df_new, legacy_schema)
    print("Backward Compatible Data:")
    df_compatible.show()
    df_compatible.printSchema()
    
    # Write with backward compatibility
    output_path = "/tmp/backward_compatible"
    manager.write_with_backward_compatibility(
        df_new, 
        output_path, 
        legacy_schema, 
        keep_new_data=True
    )
    
    # Create compatibility view
    legacy_columns = ["id", "name", "email"]
    manager.create_compatibility_view(df_new, "legacy_users_view", legacy_columns)
    
    # Query the compatibility view
    print("\n--- Querying Compatibility View ---")
    legacy_view_df = spark.sql("SELECT * FROM legacy_users_view")
    legacy_view_df.show()
    
    # Demonstrate reading legacy data and adding new columns with defaults
    print("\n--- Reading Legacy Data and Adding Defaults ---")
    df_legacy = spark.createDataFrame(
        [(4, "David", "david@example.com")],
        legacy_schema
    )
    
    default_values = {
        "subscription_type": "Standard",
        "credits": 0,
        "is_verified": False
    }
    
    df_upgraded = manager.apply_default_values_for_new_columns(df_legacy, default_values)
    print("Legacy data with default values for new columns:")
    df_upgraded.show()
    df_upgraded.printSchema()


# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 5: Forward Compatible Format Pattern
# ============================================================================
# Purpose: Ensure current data formats can handle future schema changes
# Use Case: Future-proofing, extensibility, graceful degradation

class ForwardCompatibilityManager:
    """
    Design data formats to handle future unknown fields gracefully
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def add_extension_column(self, df, extension_col_name: str = "extensions"):
        """
        Add a flexible extension column (Map type) for future fields
        """
        if extension_col_name not in df.columns:
            df = df.with
```python
            df = df.withColumn(extension_col_name, lit(None).cast(MapType(StringType(), StringType())))
        return df
    
    def add_metadata_column(self, df, metadata_col_name: str = "metadata"):
        """
        Add metadata column for versioning and future compatibility
        """
        metadata = struct(
            lit("1.0").alias("schema_version"),
            current_timestamp().alias("created_at"),
            lit(None).cast(StringType()).alias("source_system"),
            lit(None).cast(MapType(StringType(), StringType())).alias("custom_fields")
        )
        
        return df.withColumn(metadata_col_name, metadata)
    
    def create_extensible_schema(self, base_schema: StructType, 
                                 include_extensions: bool = True,
                                 include_metadata: bool = True) -> StructType:
        """
        Create a schema with extension and metadata fields for forward compatibility
        """
        fields = list(base_schema.fields)
        
        if include_extensions:
            fields.append(
                StructField("extensions", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
            )
        
        if include_metadata:
            metadata_schema = StructType([
                StructField("schema_version", StringType(), True),
                StructField("created_at", TimestampType(), True),
                StructField("source_system", StringType(), True),
                StructField("custom_fields", MapType(StringType(), StringType()), True)
            ])
            fields.append(StructField("metadata", metadata_schema, True))
        
        return StructType(fields)
    
    def add_unknown_fields_to_extensions(self, df, known_columns: List[str],
                                        extension_col_name: str = "extensions"):
        """
        Move unknown/future fields into extensions column
        """
        unknown_columns = [col for col in df.columns if col not in known_columns]
        
        if not unknown_columns:
            return self.add_extension_column(df, extension_col_name)
        
        # Create map from unknown columns
        extension_map = create_map(
            *[lit(col_name) for col_name in unknown_columns 
              for item in [col_name, col(col_name).cast(StringType())]]
        )
        
        # Add extensions column and drop unknown columns
        df = df.withColumn(extension_col_name, extension_map)
        df = df.drop(*unknown_columns)
        
        return df
    
    def extract_from_extensions(self, df, field_name: str, 
                               extension_col_name: str = "extensions",
                               target_type: str = "string"):
        """
        Extract a field from extensions column into a proper column
        """
        if extension_col_name in df.columns:
            df = df.withColumn(
                field_name,
                col(f"{extension_col_name}.{field_name}").cast(target_type)
            )
        return df
    
    def write_with_forward_compatibility(self, df, path: str, 
                                        known_columns: List[str],
                                        format_type: str = "parquet"):
        """
        Write data with forward compatibility features
        """
        # Add extension and metadata columns
        forward_compatible_df = self.add_extension_column(df)
        forward_compatible_df = self.add_metadata_column(forward_compatible_df)
        
        # Move unknown fields to extensions
        forward_compatible_df = self.add_unknown_fields_to_extensions(
            forward_compatible_df,
            known_columns + ["extensions", "metadata"]
        )
        
        # Write data
        forward_compatible_df.write.mode("overwrite").format(format_type).save(path)
        
        print(f"Data written with forward compatibility to: {path}")
        return forward_compatible_df
    
    def read_with_forward_compatibility(self, path: str, 
                                       extract_extensions: bool = True):
        """
        Read data and optionally extract known fields from extensions
        """
        df = self.spark.read.parquet(path)
        
        if extract_extensions and "extensions" in df.columns:
            # Get all keys from extensions map
            extensions_keys = df.select(explode(col("extensions").getField("key"))) \
                               .distinct() \
                               .rdd.flatMap(lambda x: x).collect()
            
            # Extract each extension field
            for key in extensions_keys:
                df = self.extract_from_extensions(df, key)
        
        return df
    
    def create_schema_with_optional_fields(self, required_fields: List[StructField],
                                          optional_fields: List[StructField]) -> StructType:
        """
        Create schema distinguishing required vs optional fields for future flexibility
        """
        all_fields = []
        
        # Required fields (nullable=False)
        for field in required_fields:
            all_fields.append(StructField(field.name, field.dataType, False))
        
        # Optional fields (nullable=True)
        for field in optional_fields:
            all_fields.append(StructField(field.name, field.dataType, True))
        
        return StructType(all_fields)
    
    def validate_forward_compatibility(self, df) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Validate that DataFrame has forward compatibility features
        """
        validation_results = {
            'has_extensions': 'extensions' in df.columns,
            'has_metadata': 'metadata' in df.columns,
            'is_forward_compatible': False
        }
        
        if validation_results['has_extensions'] and validation_results['has_metadata']:
            validation_results['is_forward_compatible'] = True
            print("✓ DataFrame is forward compatible")
        else:
            missing = []
            if not validation_results['has_extensions']:
                missing.append('extensions')
            if not validation_results['has_metadata']:
                missing.append('metadata')
            print(f"⚠ DataFrame missing forward compatibility features: {missing}")
        
        return validation_results
    
    def migrate_to_forward_compatible_format(self, df, known_columns: List[str]):
        """
        Migrate existing DataFrame to forward-compatible format
        """
        # Identify unknown columns
        unknown_cols = [c for c in df.columns if c not in known_columns]
        
        # Add extensions column with unknown fields
        if unknown_cols:
            extension_map = create_map(
                *[item for col_name in unknown_cols 
                  for item in [lit(col_name), col(col_name).cast(StringType())]]
            )
            df = df.withColumn("extensions", extension_map)
            df = df.drop(*unknown_cols)
        else:
            df = self.add_extension_column(df)
        
        # Add metadata
        df = self.add_metadata_column(df)
        
        return df
    
    def handle_schema_evolution_gracefully(self, old_df, new_df):
        """
        Merge old and new DataFrames with different schemas gracefully
        """
        # Get all columns from both DataFrames
        old_cols = set(old_df.columns)
        new_cols = set(new_df.columns)
        
        # Columns only in old DataFrame
        old_only = old_cols - new_cols
        # Columns only in new DataFrame
        new_only = new_cols - old_cols
        # Common columns
        common = old_cols & new_cols
        
        print(f"Common columns: {common}")
        print(f"Old-only columns: {old_only}")
        print(f"New-only columns: {new_only}")
        
        # Add missing columns to old DataFrame
        for col_name in new_only:
            col_type = [f.dataType for f in new_df.schema.fields if f.name == col_name][0]
            old_df = old_df.withColumn(col_name, lit(None).cast(col_type))
        
        # Add missing columns to new DataFrame
        for col_name in old_only:
            col_type = [f.dataType for f in old_df.schema.fields if f.name == col_name][0]
            new_df = new_df.withColumn(col_name, lit(None).cast(col_type))
        
        # Union the DataFrames
        return old_df.unionByName(new_df)

# UTILITY FUNCTIONS AND HELPERS

class CompatibilityUtils:
    """
    Utility functions for compatibility management
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def compare_schemas(schema1: StructType, schema2: StructType) -> Dict[str, any]:
        """
        Compare two schemas and return differences
        """
        fields1 = {f.name: f for f in schema1.fields}
        fields2 = {f.name: f for f in schema2.fields}
        
        added = set(fields2.keys()) - set(fields1.keys())
        removed = set(fields1.keys()) - set(fields2.keys())
        common = set(fields1.keys()) & set(fields2.keys())
        
        type_changes = []
        for field_name in common:
            if fields1[field_name].dataType != fields2[field_name].dataType:
                type_changes.append({
                    'field': field_name,
                    'old_type': str(fields1[field_name].dataType),
                    'new_type': str(fields2[field_name].dataType)
                })
        
        return {
            'added_fields': list(added),
            'removed_fields': list(removed),
            'type_changes': type_changes,
            'is_compatible': len(removed) == 0  # Compatible if no fields removed
        }
    
    @staticmethod
    def generate_schema_fingerprint(schema: StructType) -> str:
        """
        Generate a unique fingerprint for a schema
        """
        import hashlib
        schema_str = schema.json()
        return hashlib.md5(schema_str.encode()).hexdigest()
    
    @staticmethod
    def create_schema_changelog(old_schema: StructType, new_schema: StructType) -> str:
        """
        Create a human-readable changelog between schemas
        """
        diff = CompatibilityUtils.compare_schemas(old_schema, new_schema)
        
        changelog = ["Schema Changes:"]
        changelog.append("-" * 50)
        
        if diff['added_fields']:
            changelog.append(f"Added Fields: {', '.join(diff['added_fields'])}")
        
        if diff['removed_fields']:
            changelog.append(f"Removed Fields: {', '.join(diff['removed_fields'])}")
        
        if diff['type_changes']:
            changelog.append("Type Changes:")
            for change in diff['type_changes']:
                changelog.append(f"  - {change['field']}: {change['old_type']} → {change['new_type']}")
        
        if not (diff['added_fields'] or diff['removed_fields'] or diff['type_changes']):
            changelog.append("No changes detected")
        
        return "\n".join(changelog)
    
    @staticmethod
    def suggest_compatibility_strategy(old_schema: StructType, new_schema: StructType) -> str:
        """
        Suggest compatibility strategy based on schema differences
        """
        diff = CompatibilityUtils.compare_schemas(old_schema, new_schema)
        
        if diff['removed_fields']:
            return "BREAKING CHANGE: Use Version Compatibility Pattern with separate versions"
        elif diff['type_changes']:
            has_unsafe_changes = any(
                not CompatibilityUtils.is_safe_type_promotion(tc['old_type'], tc['new_type'])
                for tc in diff['type_changes']
            )
            if has_unsafe_changes:
                return "CAUTION: Use Backward Compatibility Pattern with type conversion"
            else:
                return "SAFE: Use Schema Evolution Pattern with type promotion"
        elif diff['added_fields']:
            return "SAFE: Use Forward Compatibility Pattern with optional fields"
        else:
            return "NO CHANGES: Schemas are identical"
    
    @staticmethod
    def is_safe_type_promotion(old_type: str, new_type: str) -> bool:
        """
        Check if type change is a safe promotion
        """
        safe_promotions = {
            'IntegerType': ['LongType', 'DoubleType', 'DecimalType'],
            'FloatType': ['DoubleType'],
            'ShortType': ['IntegerType', 'LongType', 'DoubleType'],
            'ByteType': ['ShortType', 'IntegerType', 'LongType', 'DoubleType']
        }
        
        for old, allowed_new in safe_promotions.items():
            if old in old_type and any(new in new_type for new in allowed_new):
                return True
        
        return False

"""
BEST PRACTICES FOR DATA FORMAT COMPATIBILITY:

1. SCHEMA EVOLUTION:
   - Always use nullable fields for new columns
   - Provide default values for backward compatibility
   - Document schema changes in metadata
   - Use schema registry for centralized management

2. VERSION COMPATIBILITY:
   - Maintain version numbers in data and code
   - Keep transformation logic for all version transitions
   - Test compatibility between all version pairs
   - Deprecate old versions gracefully with warnings

3. CROSS-FORMAT COMPATIBILITY:
   - Choose formats based on use case (Parquet for analytics, Avro for streaming)
   - Be aware of format limitations (CSV for nested data)
   - Use compression consistently across formats
   - Validate data integrity after format conversions

4. BACKWARD COMPATIBILITY:
   - Never remove required fields without major version bump
   - Maintain old column names as aliases
   - Provide migration scripts for breaking changes
   - Test with actual legacy systems

5. FORWARD COMPATIBILITY:
   - Use extension/metadata columns for unknown fields
   - Design schemas with optional fields
   - Version your schema definitions
   - Plan for future requirements during initial design

6. GENERAL RECOMMENDATIONS:
   - Use Parquet for long-term storage (columnar, efficient)
   - Use Avro for schema evolution in streaming
   - Implement schema validation in pipelines
   - Monitor schema drift in production
   - Automate compatibility testing in CI/CD
   - Document all schema changes and compatibility decisions
   - Use Delta Lake for ACID transactions and time travel
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession

import time
from functools import wraps

# Initialize Spark Session with optimization configurations
spark = SparkSession.builder \

    .config("spark.sql.adaptive.enabled", "true") \
