# Utility decorator for timing execution
def timing_decorator(func):
    @wraps(func)
    def wrapper(*args, **kwargs):
        start_time = time.time()
        result = func(*args, **kwargs)
        end_time = time.time()
        print(f"\n{func.__name__} execution time: {end_time - start_time:.4f} seconds")
        return result
    return wrapper

# ============================================================================
# Pattern 1: FUSION OPTIMIZATION PATTERN
# Combines multiple transformations into a single operation to reduce passes
# ============================================================================

class FusionOptimizationPattern:
    """
    Fusion Pattern combines multiple operations into fewer passes over the data.
    This reduces I/O and improves performance by minimizing intermediate results.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    @timing_decorator
    def unoptimized_multiple_passes(self, df):
        """
        BAD: Multiple separate transformations causing multiple passes
        Each operation creates a new DataFrame and requires a separate pass
        """
        print("\n=== Unoptimized: Multiple Passes ===")
        
        # First pass: filter
        filtered_df = df.filter(col("age") > 18)
        
        # Second pass: select
        selected_df = filtered_df.select("name", "age", "salary")
        
        # Third pass: add column
        with_bonus_df = selected_df.withColumn("bonus", col("salary") * 0.1)
        
        # Fourth pass: filter again
        final_df = with_bonus_df.filter(col("salary") > 50000)
        
        return final_df
    
    @timing_decorator
    def optimized_fused_operations(self, df):
        """
        GOOD: Fused operations in a single transformation chain
        All operations are combined and executed in minimal passes
        """
        print("\n=== Optimized: Fused Operations ===")
        
        # All operations fused into a single transformation chain
        final_df = df \
            .filter(col("age") > 18) \
            .select("name", "age", "salary") \
            .withColumn("bonus", col("salary") * 0.1) \
            .filter(col("salary") > 50000)
        
        return final_df
    
    @timing_decorator
    def advanced_fusion_with_expressions(self, df):
        """
        ADVANCED: Fuse complex expressions and aggregations
        """
        print("\n=== Advanced Fusion: Complex Expressions ===")
        
        # Fuse multiple column derivations and filters
        result = df.select(
            col("name"),
            col("age"),
            col("salary"),
            # Fuse multiple calculations in single select
            (col("salary") * 0.1).alias("bonus"),
            (col("salary") * 1.1).alias("total_compensation"),
            when(col("age") > 30, "Senior").otherwise("Junior").alias("level")
        ).filter(
            (col("age") > 18) & (col("salary") > 50000)
        )
        
        return result

# ============================================================================
# Pattern 2: ELIMINATION OPTIMIZATION PATTERN
# Removes unnecessary operations and redundant transformations
# ============================================================================

class EliminationOptimizationPattern:
    """
    Elimination Pattern removes unnecessary operations that don't affect results.
    This includes redundant filters, unused columns, and duplicate operations.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    @timing_decorator
    def unoptimized_with_redundancy(self, df):
        """
        BAD: Contains redundant operations and unnecessary columns
        """
        print("\n=== Unoptimized: With Redundancy ===")
        
        # Select all columns (unnecessary)
        step1 = df.select("*")
        
        # Filter that will be overridden
        step2 = step1.filter(col("age") > 20)
        
        # Redundant filter (more restrictive)
        step3 = step2.filter(col("age") > 25)
        
        # Select many columns, only to use few later
        step4 = step3.select("name", "age", "salary", "department", "hire_date", "address")
        
        # Finally only use these columns
        final = step4.select("name", "age", "salary")
        
        return final
    
    @timing_decorator
    def optimized_eliminated_redundancy(self, df):
        """
        GOOD: Eliminated redundant operations
        """
        print("\n=== Optimized: Eliminated Redundancy ===")
        
        # Direct transformation with only necessary operations
        final = df \
            .filter(col("age") > 25) \
            .select("name", "age", "salary")
        
        return final
    
    @timing_decorator
    def eliminate_unused_joins(self, df1, df2):
        """
        ADVANCED: Eliminate unnecessary join columns
        """
        print("\n=== Eliminate Unused Join Columns ===")
        
        # BAD: Join with all columns, then select few
        # bad_result = df1.join(df2, "id").select(df1.name, df1.salary)
        
        # GOOD: Select only needed columns before join
        df1_filtered = df1.select("id", "name", "salary")
        df2_filtered = df2.select("id", "department")
        good_result = df1_filtered.join(df2_filtered, "id")
        
        return good_result

# ============================================================================
# Pattern 3: SIMPLIFICATION PATTERN
# Simplifies complex expressions and transformations
# ============================================================================

class SimplificationPattern:
    """
    Simplification Pattern reduces complex operations to simpler equivalents.
    This improves readability and often performance.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    @timing_decorator
    def unoptimized_complex_logic(self, df):
        """
        BAD: Overly complex nested conditions and expressions
        """
        print("\n=== Unoptimized: Complex Logic ===")
        
        # Complex nested when/otherwise
        result = df.withColumn(
            "category",
            when(col("age") >= 18, 
                when(col("age") >= 30,
                    when(col("age") >= 50, "Senior")
                    .otherwise("Mid-Career"))
                .otherwise("Young Adult"))
            .otherwise("Minor")
        ).withColumn(
            "tax_rate",
            when(col("salary") > 100000, 0.3)
            .when(col("salary") > 75000, 0.25)
            .when(col("salary") > 50000, 0.20)
            .when(col("salary") > 25000, 0.15)
            .otherwise(0.10)
        )
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def optimized_simplified_logic(self, df):
        """
        GOOD: Simplified using cleaner logic and bucketing
        """
        print("\n=== Optimized: Simplified Logic ===")
        
        # Simplified age categorization
        result = df.withColumn(
            "category",
            when(col("age") >= 50, "Senior")
            .when(col("age") >= 30, "Mid-Career")
            .when(col("age") >= 18, "Young Adult")
            .otherwise("Minor")
        )
        
        # Use array lookup for tax rates (more maintainable)
        tax_brackets = [(100000, 0.3), (75000, 0.25), (50000, 0.20), 
                       (25000, 0.15), (0, 0.10)]
        
        tax_expr = when(col("salary") > tax_brackets[0][0], tax_brackets[0][1])
        for bracket, rate in tax_brackets[1:]:
            tax_expr = tax_expr.when(col("salary") > bracket, rate)
        
        result = result.withColumn("tax_rate", tax_expr)
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def simplify_with_sql_expressions(self, df):
        """
        ADVANCED: Use SQL expressions for complex logic
        """
        print("\n=== Simplified with SQL Expressions ===")
        
        df.createOrReplaceTempView("employees")
        
        # Complex logic simplified using SQL CASE
        result = self.spark.sql("""
            SELECT 
                name,
                age,
                salary,
                CASE 
                    WHEN age >= 50 THEN 'Senior'
                    WHEN age >= 30 THEN 'Mid-Career'
                    WHEN age >= 18 THEN 'Young Adult'
                    ELSE 'Minor'
                END as category,
                CASE 
                    WHEN salary > 100000 THEN 0.3
                    WHEN salary > 75000 THEN 0.25
                    WHEN salary > 50000 THEN 0.20
                    WHEN salary > 25000 THEN 0.15
                    ELSE 0.10
                END as tax_rate
            FROM employees
        """)
        
        return result

# ============================================================================
# Pattern 4: CONSTANT PROPAGATION PATTERN
# Propagates constant values to eliminate runtime computations
# ============================================================================

class ConstantPropagationPattern:
    """
    Constant Propagation Pattern identifies and propagates constant values
    to reduce runtime computations and enable further optimizations.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    @timing_decorator
    def unoptimized_runtime_constants(self, df):
        """
        BAD: Computing constants at runtime for each row
        """
        print("\n=== Unoptimized: Runtime Constants ===")
        
        # These calculations are repeated for every row
        result = df.withColumn(
            "annual_salary", col("salary") * lit(12)
        ).withColumn(
            "tax_amount", col("annual_salary") * lit(0.25)
        ).withColumn(
            "bonus_multiplier", lit(1.0) + lit(0.1)
        ).withColumn(
            "total_with_bonus", col("annual_salary") * col("bonus_multiplier")
        )
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def optimized_propagated_constants(self, df):
        """
        GOOD: Pre-computed constants propagated
        """
        print("\n=== Optimized: Propagated Constants ===")
        
        # Pre-compute constants
        MONTHS_PER_YEAR = 12
        TAX_RATE = 0.25
        BONUS_MULTIPLIER = 1.1  # Pre-computed 1.0 + 0.1
        
        # Use pre-computed constants
        result = df.withColumn(
            "annual_salary", col("salary") * MONTHS_PER_YEAR
        ).withColumn(
            "tax_amount", col("salary") * MONTHS_PER_YEAR * TAX_RATE
        ).withColumn(
            "total_with_bonus", col("salary") * MONTHS_PER_YEAR * BONUS_MULTIPLIER
        )
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def advanced_constant_folding(self, df):
        """
        ADVANCED: Constant folding in complex expressions
        """
        print("\n=== Advanced: Constant Folding ===")
        
        # Define constants once
        BASE_SALARY_MULTIPLIER = 12
        STANDARD_TAX_RATE = 0.25
        HIGH_EARNER_THRESHOLD = 100000
        HIGH_EARNER_TAX_RATE = 0.35
        BONUS_RATE = 0.1
        
        # Pre-compute derived constants
        EFFECTIVE_MULTIPLIER = BASE_SALARY_MULTIPLIER * (1 + BONUS_RATE)
        
        result = df.select(
            col("name"),
            col("salary"),
            (col("salary") * EFFECTIVE_MULTIPLIER).alias("total_annual_comp"),
            when(
                col("salary") * BASE_SALARY_MULTIPLIER > HIGH_EARNER_THRESHOLD,
                col("salary") * BASE_SALARY_MULTIPLIER * HIGH_EARNER_TAX_RATE
            ).otherwise(
                col("salary") * BASE_SALARY_MULTIPLIER * STANDARD_TAX_RATE
            ).alias("tax_amount")
        )
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def broadcast_constants_pattern(self, df):
        """
        ADVANCED: Using broadcast variables for complex constant structures
        """
        print("\n=== Broadcast Constants Pattern ===")
        
        # Complex constant structure
        tax_config = {
            'standard_rate': 0.25,
            'high_earner_rate': 0.35,
            'threshold': 100000,
            'deductions': {
                'standard': 12000,
                'itemized': 15000
            }
        }
        
        # Broadcast for efficiency
        broadcast_config = self.spark.sparkContext.broadcast(tax_config)
        
        # Use broadcasted constants
        config = broadcast_config.value
        result = df.withColumn(
            "tax_rate",
            when(col("salary") > config['threshold'], 
                 lit(config['high_earner_rate']))
            .otherwise(lit(config['standard_rate']))
        ).withColumn(
            "standard_deduction", lit(config['deductions']['standard'])
        )
        
        return result

# ============================================================================
# Pattern 5: DEAD CODE ELIMINATION PATTERN
# Removes unused columns, transformations, and computations
# ============================================================================

class DeadCodeEliminationPattern:
    """
    Dead Code Elimination Pattern removes computations and columns that
    don't contribute to the final result, reducing processing overhead.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    @timing_decorator
    def unoptimized_with_dead_code(self, df):
        """
        BAD: Contains unused columns and computations
        """
        print("\n=== Unoptimized: With Dead Code ===")
        
        # Compute columns that are never used
        result = df.withColumn(
            "unused_calculation_1", col("salary") * 2
        ).withColumn(
            "unused_calculation_2", col("age") + 10
        ).withColumn(
            "unused_calculation_3", concat(col("name"), lit("_suffix"))
        ).withColumn(
            "needed_column", col("salary") * 1.1
        ).select(
            "name", "needed_column"  # Only these are actually used
        )
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def optimized_dead_code_eliminated(self, df):
        """
        GOOD: Only necessary computations
        """
        print("\n=== Optimized: Dead Code Eliminated ===")
        
        # Only compute what's needed
        result = df.select(
            col
```python
            col("name"),
            (col("salary") * 1.1).alias("needed_column")
        )
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def eliminate_unused_aggregations(self, df):
        """
        ADVANCED: Eliminate unused aggregation computations
        """
        print("\n=== Eliminate Unused Aggregations ===")
        
        # BAD: Computing aggregations that aren't used
        # bad_result = df.groupBy("department").agg(
        #     avg("salary").alias("avg_salary"),
        #     max("salary").alias("max_salary"),
        #     min("salary").alias("min_salary"),
        #     count("*").alias("count"),
        #     sum("salary").alias("total_salary")
        # ).select("department", "avg_salary")  # Only using avg_salary
        
        # GOOD: Only compute needed aggregations
        good_result = df.groupBy("department").agg(
            avg("salary").alias("avg_salary")
        )
        
        return good_result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def eliminate_unused_joins(self, df1, df2, df3):
        """
        ADVANCED: Eliminate unnecessary joins
        """
        print("\n=== Eliminate Unused Joins ===")
        
        # BAD: Join with tables whose columns aren't used
        # bad_result = df1.join(df2, "id").join(df3, "id").select(df1.name, df1.salary)
        
        # GOOD: Only join what's needed
        good_result = df1.select("name", "salary")
        
        return good_result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def eliminate_redundant_caching(self, df):
        """
        ADVANCED: Eliminate unnecessary cache/persist operations
        """
        print("\n=== Eliminate Redundant Caching ===")
        
        # BAD: Caching DataFrames that are only used once
        # cached_df = df.filter(col("age") > 25).cache()
        # result = cached_df.select("name", "salary")
        # cached_df.unpersist()
        
        # GOOD: No caching for single-use DataFrames
        result = df.filter(col("age") > 25).select("name", "salary")
        
        return result

# ============================================================================
# COMPREHENSIVE EXAMPLE: Combining All Patterns
# ============================================================================

class CombinedOptimizationPatterns:
    """
    Demonstrates how to combine all optimization patterns for maximum efficiency
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        
        # Constants (Constant Propagation)
        self.TAX_RATE = 0.25
        self.BONUS_RATE = 0.1
        self.SENIOR_AGE_THRESHOLD = 50
        self.HIGH_SALARY_THRESHOLD = 100000
    
    @timing_decorator
    def unoptimized_comprehensive(self, employees_df, departments_df):
        """
        BAD: No optimization patterns applied
        """
        print("\n=== Unoptimized: No Patterns Applied ===")
        
        # Multiple passes (no fusion)
        step1 = employees_df.select("*")
        step2 = step1.filter(col("age") > 18)
        step3 = step2.filter(col("age") > 25)  # Redundant filter
        
        # Unused calculations (dead code)
        step4 = step3.withColumn("unused1", col("salary") * 2)
        step5 = step4.withColumn("unused2", col("age") + 100)
        
        # Runtime constants (no constant propagation)
        step6 = step5.withColumn("bonus", col("salary") * lit(0.1))
        step7 = step6.withColumn("tax", col("salary") * lit(0.25))
        
        # Complex logic (no simplification)
        step8 = step7.withColumn(
            "category",
            when(col("age") >= 18,
                when(col("age") >= 30,
                    when(col("age") >= 50, "Senior")
                    .otherwise("Mid"))
                .otherwise("Young"))
            .otherwise("Minor")
        )
        
        # Join with all columns (no elimination)
        step9 = step8.join(departments_df, "dept_id")
        
        # Finally select what we need
        result = step9.select("name", "salary", "bonus", "tax", "category", "dept_name")
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def optimized_comprehensive(self, employees_df, departments_df):
        """
        GOOD: All optimization patterns applied
        """
        print("\n=== Optimized: All Patterns Applied ===")
        
        # Apply all patterns:
        # 1. Fusion: Chain all operations
        # 2. Elimination: Remove redundant filters and unused columns
        # 3. Simplification: Simplified logic
        # 4. Constant Propagation: Use pre-computed constants
        # 5. Dead Code Elimination: Only compute what's needed
        
        # Select only needed columns before join (Elimination)
        employees_filtered = employees_df.select("name", "salary", "age", "dept_id")
        departments_filtered = departments_df.select("dept_id", "dept_name")
        
        # Fused transformation chain
        result = employees_filtered \
            .filter(col("age") > 25) \
            .join(departments_filtered, "dept_id") \
            .select(
                col("name"),
                col("salary"),
                (col("salary") * self.BONUS_RATE).alias("bonus"),
                (col("salary") * self.TAX_RATE).alias("tax"),
                when(col("age") >= self.SENIOR_AGE_THRESHOLD, "Senior")
                    .when(col("age") >= 30, "Mid")
                    .otherwise("Young").alias("category"),
                col("dept_name")
            )
        
        return result

def create_sample_data(spark):
    """

    """
    print("\n" + "="*80)
    print("Creating Sample Data")
    print("="*80)
    
    # Employee data
    employees_data = [
        (1, "Alice", 25, 60000, "HR", "2020-01-15", "123 Main St"),
        (2, "Bob", 35, 80000, "IT", "2018-03-20", "456 Oak Ave"),
        (3, "Charlie", 45, 95000, "Finance", "2015-07-10", "789 Pine Rd"),
        (4, "David", 55, 120000, "IT", "2010-05-01", "321 Elm St"),
        (5, "Eve", 28, 70000, "HR", "2019-09-12", "654 Maple Dr"),
        (6, "Frank", 32, 85000, "Finance", "2017-11-30", "987 Cedar Ln"),
        (7, "Grace", 42, 110000, "IT", "2014-02-28", "147 Birch Ct"),
        (8, "Henry", 29, 75000, "HR", "2018-08-15", "258 Spruce Way"),
        (9, "Iris", 38, 90000, "Finance", "2016-04-22", "369 Willow Pl"),
        (10, "Jack", 52, 125000, "IT", "2012-12-05", "741 Ash Blvd"),
    ]
    
    employees_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("name", StringType(), False),
        StructField("age", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("salary", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("department", StringType(), False),
        StructField("hire_date", StringType(), False),
        StructField("address", StringType(), False),
    ])
    
    employees_df = spark.createDataFrame(employees_data, employees_schema)
    
    # Department data
    departments_data = [
        (1, "HR", "Human Resources"),
        (2, "IT", "Information Technology"),
        (3, "Finance", "Finance Department"),
    ]
    
    departments_schema = StructType([
        StructField("dept_id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("dept_code", StringType(), False),
        StructField("dept_name", StringType(), False),
    ])
    
    departments_df = spark.createDataFrame(departments_data, departments_schema)
    
    # Additional employee-department mapping
    emp_dept_data = [
        (1, 1), (2, 2), (3, 3), (4, 2), (5, 1),
        (6, 3), (7, 2), (8, 1), (9, 3), (10, 2),
    ]
    
    emp_dept_schema = StructType([
        StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
        StructField("dept_id", IntegerType(), False),
    ])
    
    emp_dept_df = spark.createDataFrame(emp_dept_data, emp_dept_schema)
    
    return employees_df, departments_df, emp_dept_df

def print_best_practices():
    """
    Print best practices for each optimization pattern
    """
    best_practices = """
    
    ╔══════════════════════════════
```python
════════════════════════════════════╗
    ║  OPTIMIZATION PATTERNS - BEST PRACTICES & RECOMMENDATIONS  ║
    ╚════════════════════════════════════════════════════════════╝
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ 1. FUSION OPTIMIZATION PATTERN                              │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    ✓ DO:
      • Chain transformations together in a single pipeline
      • Combine multiple filters into one compound condition
      • Use select() with multiple expressions instead of multiple withColumn()
      • Leverage Catalyst optimizer by keeping transformations together
      
    ✗ DON'T:
      • Break transformation chains unnecessarily
      • Create intermediate DataFrames for simple operations
      • Use multiple passes when one will suffice
      
    Example:
      # Good: Fused
      df.filter(cond1).filter(cond2).select(cols)
      
      # Better: Single filter
      df.filter(cond1 & cond2).select(cols)
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ 2. ELIMINATION OPTIMIZATION PATTERN                         │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    ✓ DO:
      • Remove redundant filters (keep most restrictive)
      • Select only needed columns early in the pipeline
      • Eliminate duplicate operations
      • Remove unnecessary joins
      
    ✗ DON'T:
      • Select all columns then filter later
      • Apply multiple filters that can be combined
      • Join tables whose columns aren't used
      
    Example:
      # Good: Select early
      df.select("id", "name").join(other, "id")
      
      # Bad: Select late
      df.join(other, "id").select("id", "name")
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ 3. SIMPLIFICATION PATTERN                                   │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    ✓ DO:
      • Use clear, linear when/otherwise chains
      • Leverage SQL expressions for complex logic
      • Extract complex conditions to variables
      • Use built-in functions over UDFs when possible
      
    ✗ DON'T:
      • Create deeply nested when/otherwise statements
      • Use complex lambda functions when SQL functions work
      • Over-complicate simple boolean logic
      
    Example:
      # Good: Clear chain
      when(col("age") >= 50, "Senior")
        .when(col("age") >= 30, "Mid")
        .otherwise("Junior")
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ 4. CONSTANT PROPAGATION PATTERN                             │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    ✓ DO:
      • Define constants at class/module level
      • Pre-compute derived constants
      • Use broadcast variables for complex constant structures
      • Document constant meanings and sources
      
    ✗ DON'T:
      • Compute constants in transformation chains
      • Use magic numbers without explanation
      • Recalculate the same constant multiple times
      
    Example:
      # Good: Pre-computed
      TAX_RATE = 0.25
      df.withColumn("tax", col("salary") * TAX_RATE)
      
      # Bad: Runtime computation
      df.withColumn("tax", col("salary") * lit(0.25))
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ 5. DEAD CODE ELIMINATION PATTERN                            │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    ✓ DO:
      • Only compute columns that will be used
      • Remove unused aggregations
      • Eliminate unnecessary caching
      • Profile to identify unused computations
      
    ✗ DON'T:
      • Compute columns "just in case"
      • Cache DataFrames used only once
      • Perform aggregations that won't be used
      
    Example:
      # Good: Only what's needed
      df.groupBy("dept").agg(avg("salary"))
      
      # Bad: Unused aggregations
      df.groupBy("dept").agg(
        avg("salary"), max("salary"), min("salary")
      ).select("dept", "avg_salary")
    
    ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
    │ GENERAL OPTIMIZATION TIPS                                   │
    └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
    
    1. Use explain() to understand query plans
    2. Monitor Spark UI for optimization opportunities
    3. Enable Adaptive Query Execution (AQE)
    4. Use appropriate partitioning strategies
    5. Leverage columnar formats (Parquet, ORC)
    6. Cache strategically (only when reused multiple times)
    7. Use broadcast joins for small tables
    8. Avoid UDFs when built-in functions suffice
    9. Use coalesce() instead of repartition() when reducing partitions
    10. Profile before and after optimization
    
    """
    print(best_practices)

class OptimizationAnalyzer:
    """
    Utility class to analyze and suggest optimizations
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def analyze_query_plan(self, df, query_name="Query"):
        """
        Analyze and print query plan with recommendations
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"Query Plan Analysis: {query_name}")
        print('='*80)
        
        # Physical plan
        print("\n--- Physical Plan ---")
        df.explain(mode="formatted")
        
        # Check for common anti-patterns
        plan_str = df._jdf.queryExecution().toString()
        
        recommendations = []
        
        if "Project" in plan_str and plan_str.count("Project") > 3:
            recommendations.append(
                "⚠ Multiple projections detected - Consider fusion optimization"
            )
        
        if "Filter" in plan_str and plan_str.count("Filter") > 2:
            recommendations.append(
                "⚠ Multiple filters detected - Consider combining filters"
            )
        
        if "BroadcastExchange" not in plan_str and "Join" in plan_str:
            recommendations.append(
                "💡 Consider broadcast join for small tables"
            )
        
        if recommendations:
            print("\n--- Recommendations ---")
            for rec in recommendations:
                print(rec)
        else:
            print("\n✓ No obvious optimization opportunities detected")
    
    def compare_plans(self, df1, df2, name1="Unoptimized", name2="Optimized"):
        """
        Compare two query plans side by side
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"Plan Comparison: {name1} vs {name2}")
        print('='*80)
        
        print(f"\n--- {name1} ---")
        df1.explain(mode="simple")
        
        print(f"\n--- {name2} ---")
        df2.explain(mode="simple")
    
    def measure_performance(self, func, df, iterations=3):
        """
        Measure average execution time over multiple iterations
        """
        import time
        times = []
        
        for i in range(iterations):
            start = time.time()
            result = func(df)
            result.count()  # Force evaluation
            end = time.time()
            times.append(end - start)
        
        avg_time = sum(times) / len(times)
        print(f"\nAverage execution time: {avg_time:.4f} seconds")
        print(f"Min: {min(times):.4f}s, Max: {max(times):.4f}s")
        
        return avg_time

class ECommerceOptimizationExample:
    """
    Real-world example applying all optimization patterns to e-commerce analytics
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        
        # Constants (Constant Propagation)
        self.PREMIUM_THRESHOLD = 1000
        self.DISCOUNT_RATE = 0.15
        self.TAX_RATE = 0.08
        self.SHIPPING_COST = 9.99
        self.FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD = 50
    
    def create_ecommerce_data(self):
        """
        Create sample e-commerce datasets
        """
        # Orders data
        orders_data = [
            (1, 101, "2024-01-15", 150.00, "completed"),
            (2, 102, "2024-01-16", 2500.00, "completed"),
            (3, 103, "2024-01-17", 75.50, "pending"),
            (4, 101, "2024-01-18", 450.00, "completed"),
            (5, 104, "2024-01-19", 1200.00, "completed"),
            (6, 105, "2024-01-20", 35.00, "cancelled"),
            (7, 102, "2024-01-21", 890.00, "completed"),
            (8, 103, "2024-01-22", 3200.00, "completed"),
            (9, 104, "2024-01-23", 125.00, "pending"),
            (10, 105, "2024-01-24", 67.00, "completed"),
        ]
        
        orders_schema = StructType([
            StructField("order_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("order_date", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("status", StringType(), False),
        ])
        
        orders_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(orders_data, orders_schema)
        
        # Customers data
        customers_data = [
            (101, "Alice", "Premium", "2020-01-01"),
            (102, "Bob", "Premium", "2019-06-15"),
            (103, "Charlie", "Standard", "2021-03-20"),
            (104, "David", "Premium", "2020-11-10"),
            (105, "Eve", "Standard", "2022-02-28"),
        ]
        
        customers_schema = StructType([
            StructField("customer_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("tier", StringType(), False),
            StructField("join_date", StringType(), False),
        ])
        
        customers_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(customers_data, customers_schema)
        
        return orders_df, customers_df
    
    @timing_decorator
    def unoptimized_analytics(self, orders_df, customers_df):
        """
        Unoptimized e-commerce analytics query
        """
        print("\n=== Unoptimized E-Commerce Analytics ===")
        
        # No optimization patterns applied
        step1 = orders_df.select("*")
        step2 = step1.filter(col("status") == "completed")
        step3 = step2.filter(col("status") == "completed")  # Redundant
        
        # Dead code - unused calculations
        step4 = step3.withColumn("unused_calc", col("amount") * 2)
        step5 = step4.withColumn("temp_value", col("amount") + 100)
        
        # Runtime constants
        step6 = step5.withColumn("tax", col("amount") * lit(0.08))
        step7 = step6.withColumn("discount", col("amount") * lit(0.15))
        
        # Complex nested logic
        step8 = step7.withColumn(
            "shipping",
            when(col("amount") > lit(50), lit(0))
            .otherwise(lit(9.99))
        )
        
        # Join with all columns
        step9 = step8.join(customers_df, "customer_id")
        
        # More complex logic
        step10 = step9.withColumn(
            "customer_category",
            when(col("tier") == "Premium",
                when(col("amount") > 1000, "High Value Premium")
                .otherwise("Regular Premium"))
            .otherwise("Standard")
        )
        
        # Finally select what we need
        result = step10.select(
            "order_id",
            "name",
            "amount",
            "tax",
            "shipping",
            "customer_category"
        )
        
        return result
    
    @timing_decorator
    def optimized_analytics(self, orders_df, customers_df):
        """
        Optimized e-commerce analytics with all patterns applied
        """
        print("\n=== Optimized E-Commerce Analytics ===")
        
        # Apply all optimization patterns:
        # 1. Elimination: Select only needed columns early
        # 2. Dead Code Elimination: No unused calculations
        # 3. Constant Propagation: Use pre-defined constants
        # 4. Simplification: Clear logic
        # 5. Fusion: Single transformation chain
        
        orders_filtered = orders_df.select("order_id", "customer_id", "amount") \
            .filter(col("status") == "completed")
        
        customers_filtered = customers_df.select("customer_id", "name", "tier")
        
        result = orders_filtered \
            .join(customers_filtered, "customer_id") \
            .select(
                col("order_id"),
                col("name"),
                col("amount"),
                (col("amount") * self.TAX_RATE).alias("tax"),
                when(col("amount") > self.FREE_SHIPPING_THRESHOLD, lit(0))
                    .otherwise(self.SHIPPING_COST).alias("shipping"),
                when(
                    (col("tier") == "Premium") & (col("amount") > self.PREMIUM_THRESHOLD),
                    "High Value Premium"
                ).when(
                    col("tier") == "Premium",
                    "Regular Premium"
                ).otherwise("Standard").alias("customer_category")
            )
        
        return result
    
    def run_complete_analysis(self):
        """
        Run complete optimization analysis
        """
        orders_df, customers_df = self.create_ecommerce_data()
        
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("E-COMMERCE ANALYTICS OPTIMIZATION EXAMPLE")
        print("="*80)
        
        print("\nSample Orders Data:")
        orders_df.show()
        
        print("\nSample Customers Data:")
        customers_df.show()
        
        # Run unoptimized version
        unopt_result = self.unoptimized_analytics(orders_df, customers_df)
        print("\nUnoptimized Result:")
        unopt_result.show()
        
        # Run optimized version
        opt_result = self.optimized_analytics(orders_df, customers_df)
        print("\nOptimized Result:")
        opt_result.show()
        
        # Compare plans
        analyzer = OptimizationAnalyzer(self.spark)
        analyzer.compare_plans(unopt_result

class PerformanceBenchmark:
    """
    Comprehensive performance benchmarking for all optimization patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        self.results = {}
    
    def create_large_dataset(self, num_rows=100000):
        """
        Create a larger dataset for realistic performance testing
        """
        print(f"\nGenerating dataset with {num_rows:,} rows...")
        
        from pyspark.sql.functions import rand, randn
        
        df = self.spark.range(0, num_rows) \
            .withColumn("name", concat(lit("User_"), col("id"))) \
            .withColumn("age", (rand() * 50 + 18).cast("int")) \
            .withColumn("salary", (rand() * 100000 + 30000).cast("int")) \
            .withColumn("department", 
                       when(col("id") % 3 == 0, "IT")
                       .when(col("id") % 3 == 1, "HR")
                       .otherwise("Finance")) \
            .withColumn("performance_score", randn() * 10 + 75) \
            .withColumn("years_employed", (rand() * 15).cast("int"))
        
        return df
    
    def benchmark_fusion_pattern(self, df):
        """
        Benchmark fusion optimization pattern
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("BENCHMARKING: Fusion Optimization Pattern")
        print("="*80)
        
        fusion = FusionOptimizationPattern(self.spark)
        
        # Unoptimized
        print("\nRunning unoptimized version...")
        start = time.time()
        unopt = fusion.unoptimized_multiple_passes(df)
        unopt_count = unopt.count()
        unopt_time = time.time() - start
        
        # Optimized
        print("\nRunning optimized version...")
        start = time.time()
        opt = fusion.optimized_fused_operations(df)
        opt_count = opt.count()
        opt_time = time.time() - start
        
        improvement = ((unopt_time - opt_time) / unopt_time) * 100
        
        self.results['Fusion'] = {
            'unoptimized': unopt_time,
            'optimized': opt_time,
            'improvement': improvement
        }
        
        print(f"\nResults:")
        print(f"  Unoptimized: {unopt_time:.4f}s ({unopt_count:,} rows)")
        print(f"  Optimized:   {opt_time:.4f}s ({opt_count:,} rows)")
        print(f"  Improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
    
    def benchmark_elimination_pattern(self, df):
        """
        Benchmark elimination optimization pattern
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("BENCHMARKING: Elimination Optimization Pattern")
        print("="*80)
        
        elimination = EliminationOptimizationPattern(self.spark)
        
        # Unoptimized
        print("\nRunning unoptimized version...")
        start = time.time()
        unopt = elimination.unoptimized_with_redundancy(df)
        unopt_count = unopt.count()
        unopt_time = time.time() - start
        
        # Optimized
        print("\nRunning optimized version...")
        start = time.time()
        opt = elimination.optimized_eliminated_redundancy(df)
        opt_count = opt.count()
        opt_time = time.time() - start
        
        improvement = ((unopt_time - opt_time) / unopt_time) * 100
        
        self.results['Elimination'] = {
            'unoptimized': unopt_time,
            'optimized': opt_time,
            'improvement': improvement
        }
        
        print(f"\nResults:")
        print(f"  Unoptimized: {unopt_time:.4f}s ({unopt_count:,} rows)")
        print(f"  Optimized:   {opt_time:.4f}s ({opt_count:,} rows)")
        print(f"  Improvement: {improvement:.2f}%")
    
    def benchmark_all_patterns(self, num_rows=100000):
        """
        Run comprehensive benchmark of all patterns
        """
        df = self.create_large_dataset(num_rows)
        df.cache()
        df.count()  # Force caching
        
        self.benchmark_fusion_pattern(df)
        self.benchmark_elimination_pattern(df)
        
        # Print summary
        self.print_benchmark_summary()
        
        df.unpersist()
    
    def print_benchmark_summary(self):
        """
        Print comprehensive benchmark summary
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("BENCHMARK SUMMARY")
        print("="*80)
        
        print("\n{:<20} {:>15} {:>15} {:>15}".format(
            "Pattern", "Unoptimized", "Optimized", "Improvement"
        ))
        print("-" * 70)
        
        for pattern, metrics in self.results.items():
            print("{:<20} {:>12.4f}s {:>12.4f}s {:>13.2f}%".format(
                pattern,
                metrics['unoptimized'],
                metrics['optimized'],
                metrics['improvement']
            ))
        
        if self.results:
            avg_improvement = sum(m['improvement'] for m in self.results.values()) / len(self.results)
            print("-" * 70)
            print(f"{'Average Improvement:':<20} {avg_improvement:>41.2f}%")

class OptimizationGuide:
    """
    Interactive guide to help identify optimization opportunities
    """
    
    @staticmethod
    def analyze_transformation_chain(df):
        """
        Analyze a DataFrame transformation chain for optimization opportunities
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("TRANSFORMATION CHAIN ANALYSIS")
        print("="*80)
        
        plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().toString()
        
        issues = []
        recommendations = []
        
        # Check for fusion opportunities
        project_count = plan.count("Project")
        if project_count > 3:
            issues.append(f"Found {project_count} projection operations")
            recommendations.append(
                "FUSION: Combine multiple withColumn() calls into a single select()"
            )
        
        # Check for elimination opportunities
        filter_count = plan.count("Filter")
        if filter_count > 2:
            issues.append(f"Found {filter_count} filter operations")
            recommendations.append(
                "ELIMINATION: Combine multiple filters into a single compound condition"
            )
        
        # Check for dead code
        if "Project" in plan:
            issues.append("Multiple projections detected")
            recommendations.append(
                "DEAD CODE: Ensure all projected columns are actually used"
            )
        
        # Print analysis
        if issues:
            print("\n⚠ Issues Detected:")
            for i, issue in enumerate(issues, 1):
                print(f"  {i}. {issue}")
            
            print("\n💡 Recommendations:")
            for i, rec in enumerate(recommendations, 1):
                print(f"  {i}. {rec}")
        else:
            print("\n✓ No obvious optimization issues detected!")
        
        return issues, recommendations
    
    @staticmethod
    def suggest_optimizations(code_snippet):
        """
        Analyze code snippet and suggest optimizations
        """
        suggestions = []
        
        # Check for common anti-patterns
        if ".select(\"*\")" in code_snippet:
            suggestions.append(
                "ELIMINATION: Avoid select('*'). Select only needed columns."
            )
        
        if code_snippet.count(".withColumn(") > 3:
            suggestions.append(
                "FUSION: Replace multiple withColumn() with single select() with aliases"
            )
        
        if code_snippet.count(".filter(") > 2:
            suggestions.append(
                "FUSION: Combine multiple filters using & or | operators"
            )
        
        if "lit(" in code_snippet and code_snippet.count("lit(") > 3:
            suggestions.append(
                "CONSTANT PROPAGATION: Define constants at module level"
            )
        
        return suggestions

class AdvancedFusionExamples:
    """
    Advanced fusion optimization examples for complex scenarios
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def fusion_with_window_functions(self, df):
        """
        Optimize window functions using fusion
        """
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        
        print("\n=== Fusion with Window Functions ===")
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Multiple window specifications
        window1 = Window.partitionBy("department").orderBy("salary")
        window2 = Window.partitionBy("department").orderBy("salary")  # Duplicate
        
        unopt = df \
            .withColumn("rank1", row_number().over(window1)) \
            .withColumn("rank2", dense_rank().over(window2))
        
        # OPTIMIZED: Single window specification, fused operations
        window = Window.partitionBy("department").orderBy("salary")
        
        opt = df.select(
            "*",
            row_number().over(window).alias("rank1"),
            dense_rank().over(window).alias("rank2")
        )
        
        print("Unoptimized:")
        unopt.show(5)
        print("\nOptimized:")
        opt.show(5)
        
        return opt
    
    def fusion_with_aggregations(self, df):
        """
        Fuse multiple aggregation operations
        """
        print("\n=== Fusion with Aggregations ===")
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Multiple groupBy operations
        avg_salary = df.groupBy("department").agg(avg("salary").alias("avg_sal"))
        max_salary = df.groupBy("department").agg(max("salary").alias("max_sal"))
        result_unopt = avg_salary.join(max_salary, "department")
        
        # OPTIMIZED: Single groupBy with multiple aggregations
        result_opt = df.groupBy("department").agg(
            avg("salary").alias("avg_sal"),
            max("salary").alias("max_sal"),
            min("salary").alias("min_sal"),
            count("*").alias("count")
        )
        
        print("Unoptimized:")
        result_unopt.show()
        print("\nOptimized:")
        result_opt.show()
        
        return result_opt
    
    def fusion_with_complex_transformations(self, df):
        """
        Fuse complex multi-step transformations
        """
        print("\n=== Fusion with Complex Transformations ===")
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Multiple separate transformation steps
        step1 = df.withColumn("annual_salary", col("salary") * 12)
        step2 = step1.withColumn("tax", col("annual_salary") * 0.25)
        step3 = step2.withColumn("net_income", col("annual_salary") - col("tax"))
        step4 = step3.withColumn("monthly_net", col("net_income") / 12)
        
        # OPTIMIZED: All calculations in single select
        result_opt = df.select(
            "*",
            (col("salary") * 12).alias("annual_salary"),
            (col("salary") * 12 * 0.25).alias("tax"),
            (col("salary") * 12 * 0.75).alias("net_income"),
            (col("salary") * 0.75).alias("monthly_net")
        )
        
        print("Optimized result:")
        result_opt.show(5)
        
        return result_opt

class AdvancedEliminationExamples:
    """
    Advanced elimination optimization examples
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def eliminate_redundant_filters_complex(self, df):
        """
        Eliminate complex redundant filter conditions
        """
        print("\n=== Eliminate Complex Redundant Filters ===")
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Redundant and overlapping filters
        unopt = df \
            .filter(col("age") > 20) \
            .filter(col("age") > 25) \
            .filter(col("salary") > 50000) \
            .filter(col("salary") > 60000) \
            .filter(col("age") < 65) \
            .filter(col("department").isin(["IT", "Finance", "HR"])) \
            .filter(col("department") != "Marketing")  # Redundant with isin
        
        # OPTIMIZED: Single compound filter with most restrictive conditions
        opt = df.filter(
            (col("age") > 25) & 
            (col("age") < 65) & 
            (col("salary") > 60000) & 
            (col("department").isin(["IT", "Finance", "HR"]))
        )
        
        print(f"Unoptimized count: {unopt.count()}")
        print(f"Optimized count: {opt.count()}")
        
        return opt
    
    def eliminate_unnecessary_distinct(self, df):
        """
        Eliminate unnecessary distinct operations
        """
        print("\n=== Eliminate Unnecessary Distinct ===")
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Distinct on already unique key
        unopt = df.select("id", "name").distinct()  # id is unique
        
        # OPTIMIZED: No distinct needed if key is unique
        opt = df.select("id", "name")
        
        print("Optimized - no unnecessary distinct operation")
        
        return opt
    
    def eliminate_self_joins(self, df):
        """
        Eliminate unnecessary self-joins using window functions
        """
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        
        print("\n=== Eliminate Self-Joins ===")
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Self-join to get max salary per department
        max_salaries = df.groupBy("department").agg(
            max("salary").alias("max_salary")
        )
        unopt = df.join(max_salaries, "department")
        
        # OPTIMIZED: Use window function instead
        window = Window.partitionBy("department")
        opt = df.withColumn("max_salary", max("salary").over(window))
        
        print("Eliminated self-join using window function")
        
        return opt

class AdvancedSimplificationExamples:
    """
    Advanced simplification pattern examples
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def simplify_nested_case_statements(self, df):
        """
        Simplify deeply nested case/when statements
        """
        print("\n=== Simplify Nested Case Statements ===")
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Deeply nested when/otherwise
        unopt = df.withColumn(
            "performance_rating",
            when(col("salary") > 100000,
                when(col("age") > 50, "Expert Senior")
                .when(col("age") > 40, "Senior Expert")
                .when(col("age") > 30, "Mid Expert")
                .otherwise("Junior Expert"))
            .when(col("salary") > 75000,
                when(col("age") > 50, "Advanced Senior")
                .when(col("age") > 40, "Senior Advanced")
                .otherwise("Mid Advanced"))
            .otherwise("Standard")
        )
        
        # OPTIMIZED: Flattened logic with clear conditions
        opt = df.withColumn(
            "salary_tier",
            when(col("salary") > 100000, "Expert")
            .when(col("salary") > 75000, "Advanced")
            .otherwise("Standard")
        ).withColumn(
            "age_tier",
            when(col("age") > 50, "Senior")
            .when(col("age") > 40, "Mid-Senior")
            .when(col("age") > 30, "Mid")
            .otherwise("Junior")
        ).withColumn(
            "performance_rating",
            concat(col("age_tier"), lit(" "), col("salary_tier"))
        ).drop("salary_tier", "age_tier")
        
        print("Simplified nested logic")
        opt.show(5)
        
        return opt
    
    def simplify_using_lookup_tables(self, df):
        """
        Simplify complex mappings using lookup tables
        """
        print("\n=== Simplify Using Lookup Tables ===")
        
        # Create lookup table for tax rates
        tax_lookup = self.spark.createDataFrame([
            (0, 25000, 0.10),
            (25001, 50000, 0.15),
            (50001, 75000, 0.20),
            (75001, 100000, 0.25),
            (100001, 999999999, 0.30)
        ], ["min_salary", "max_salary", "tax_rate"])
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Multiple when/otherwise
        unopt = df.withColumn(
            "tax_rate",
            when(col("salary") <= 25000, 0.10)
            .when(col("salary") <= 50000, 0.15)
            .when(col("salary") <= 75000, 0.20)
            .when(col("salary") <= 100000, 0.25)
            .otherwise(0.30)
        )
        
        # OPTIMIZED: Join with lookup table
        opt = df.join(
            tax_lookup,
            (df.salary >= tax_lookup.min_salary) & 
            (df.salary <= tax_lookup.max_salary)
        ).select(df["*"], tax_lookup.tax_rate)
        
        print("Simplified using lookup table")
        
        return opt

class AdvancedConstantPropagationExamples:
    """
    Advanced constant propagation examples
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        
        # Configuration constants
        self.CONFIG = {
            'tax': {
                'federal_rate': 0.22,
                'state_rate': 0.05,
                'local_rate': 0.02
            },
            'benefits': {
                'health_insurance': 500,
                'retirement_match': 0.06,
                'bonus_multiplier': 0.15
            },
            'thresholds': {
                'high_earner': 100000,
                'executive': 200000
            }
        }
    
    def propagate_nested_constants(self, df):
        """
        Propagate complex nested constant structures
        """
        print("\n=== Propagate Nested Constants ===")
        
        # Pre-compute all derived constants
        TOTAL_TAX_RATE = (
            self.CONFIG['tax']['federal_rate'] + 
            self.CONFIG['tax']['state_rate'] + 
            self.CONFIG['tax']['local_rate']
        )
        
        ANNUAL_BENEFITS = self.CONFIG['benefits']['health_insurance'] * 12
        
        # Use pre-computed constants
        result = df.select(
            "*",
            (col("salary") * TOTAL_TAX_RATE).alias("total_tax"),
            (col("salary") * self.CONFIG['benefits']['retirement_match']).alias("retirement"),
            lit(ANNUAL_BENEFITS).alias("health_benefits"),
            (col("salary") * self.CONFIG['benefits']['bonus_multiplier']).alias("bonus")
        )
        
        print("Constants propagated efficiently")
        result.show(5)
        
        return result
    
    def use_broadcast_for_constants(self, df):
        """
        Use broadcast variables for large constant structures
        """
        print("\n=== Broadcast Constants ===")
        
        # Broadcast configuration
        config_broadcast = self.spark.sparkContext.broadcast(self.CONFIG)
        
        # Access broadcasted config
        cfg = config_broadcast.value
        
        result = df.select(
            "*",
            (col("salary") * cfg['tax']['federal_rate']).alias("federal_tax"),
            (col("salary") * cfg['benefits']['retirement_match']).alias("retirement")
        )
        
        print("Using broadcast variables for constants")
        
        return result

class AdvancedDeadCodeExamples:
    """
    Advanced dead code elimination examples
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
    
    def eliminate_unused_window_operations(self, df):
        """
        Eliminate unused window function calculations
        """
        from pyspark.sql.window import Window
        
        print("\n=== Eliminate Unused Window Operations ===")
        
        window = Window.partitionBy("department").orderBy("salary")
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Calculate many window functions but use only one
        unopt = df.select(
            "*",
            row_number().over(window).alias("row_num"),
            rank().over(window).alias("rank"),
            dense_rank().over(window).alias("dense_rank"),
            percent_rank().over(window).alias("percent_rank"),
            ntile(4).over(window).alias("quartile")
        ).select("name", "department", "row_num")  # Only use row_num
        
        # OPTIMIZED: Only calculate what's needed
        opt = df.select(
            "name",
            "department",
            row_number().over(window).alias("row_num")
        )
        
        print("Eliminated unused window operations")
        
        return opt
    
    def eliminate_unused_explode_operations(self, df):
        """
        Eliminate unnecessary explode operations
        """
        print("\n=== Eliminate Unused Explode ===")
        
        # Create DataFrame with array column
        df_with_array = df.withColumn(
            "skills",
            array(lit("Python"), lit("SQL"), lit("Spark"))
        )
        
        # UNOPTIMIZED: Explode then aggregate back
        unopt = df_
```python
with_array \
            .select("id", "name", explode("skills").alias("skill")) \
            .groupBy("id", "name") \
            .agg(count("skill").alias("skill_count"))
        
        # OPTIMIZED: Use array size instead of explode
        opt = df_with_array.select(

        )

    def eliminate_redundant_persistence(self, df):

    def eliminate_unused_broadcast(self, df, small_df):

class ComplexDataPipelineOptimization:
    """
    Complex real-world scenario combining all optimization patterns
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark_session):
        self.spark = spark_session
        
        # Constants (Constant Propagation Pattern)
        self.BUSINESS_CONSTANTS = {
            'commission_rates': {
                'bronze': 0.05,
                'silver': 0.08,
                'gold': 0.12,
                'platinum': 0.15
            },
            'tier_thresholds': {
                'silver': 50000,
                'gold': 100000,
                'platinum': 200000
            },
            'tax_rates': {
                'standard': 0.20,
                'high_earner': 0.30
            },
            'deductions': {
                'standard': 12000,
                'health': 6000,
                'retirement': 0.10
            }
        }
    
    def create_complex_datasets(self):
        """
        Create complex datasets for demonstration
        """
        # Sales data
        sales_data = [
            (1, 101, "2024-01-15", 5000, "Electronics", "Online"),
            (2, 102, "2024-01-16", 15000, "Furniture", "Store"),
            (3, 103, "2024-01-17", 3000, "Electronics", "Online"),
            (4, 101, "2024-01-18", 25000, "Appliances", "Store"),
            (5, 104, "2024-01-19", 8000, "Electronics", "Online"),
            (6, 102, "2024-01-20", 45000, "Furniture", "Store"),
            (7, 105, "2024-01-21", 12000, "Electronics", "Online"),
            (8, 103, "2024-01-22", 60000, "Appliances", "Store"),
            (9, 104, "2024-01-23", 7000, "Electronics", "Online"),
            (10, 105, "2024-01-24", 95000, "Furniture", "Store"),
        ]
        
        sales_schema = StructType([
            StructField("sale_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("sales_person_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("sale_date", StringType(), False),
            StructField("amount", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("category", StringType(), False),
            StructField("channel", StringType(), False),
        ])
        
        sales_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(sales_data, sales_schema)
        
        # Sales person data
        sales_person_data = [
            (101, "Alice Johnson", "2020-01-01", "Active", "West"),
            (102, "Bob Smith", "2019-06-15", "Active", "East"),
            (103, "Charlie Brown", "2021-03-20", "Active", "North"),
            (104, "David Lee", "2020-11-10", "Active", "South"),
            (105, "Eve Martinez", "2022-02-28", "Active", "West"),
        ]
        
        sales_person_schema = StructType([
            StructField("sales_person_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("name", StringType(), False),
            StructField("hire_date", StringType(), False),
            StructField("status", StringType(), False),
            StructField("region", StringType(), False),
        ])
        
        sales_person_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(sales_person_data, sales_person_schema)
        
        # Product data
        product_data = [
            ("Electronics", 0.15, 30),
            ("Furniture", 0.25, 45),
            ("Appliances", 0.20, 60),
        ]
        
        product_schema = StructType([
            StructField("category", StringType(), False),
            StructField("margin", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("warranty_days", IntegerType(), False),
        ])
        
        product_df = self.spark.createDataFrame(product_data, product_schema)
        
        return sales_df, sales_person_df, product_df
    
    @timing_decorator
    def unoptimized_complex_pipeline(self, sales_df, sales_person_df, product_df):
        """
        UNOPTIMIZED: Complex pipeline with no optimization patterns
        """
        print("\n=== UNOPTIMIZED Complex Pipeline ===")
        
        # No pattern optimization applied
        
        # Step 1: Multiple redundant filters (No Elimination)
        sales_filtered = sales_df.select("*")
        sales_filtered = sales_filtered.filter(col("amount") > 1000)
        sales_filtered = sales_filtered.filter(col("amount") > 2000)  # Redundant
        sales_filtered = sales_filtered.filter(col("status") != "Cancelled")
        
        # Step 2: Dead code - unused calculations
        sales_with_calcs = sales_filtered.withColumn("unused1", col("amount") * 2)
        sales_with_calcs = sales_with_calcs.withColumn("unused2", col("amount") / 2)
        sales_with_calcs = sales_with_calcs.withColumn("unused3", col("amount") + 1000)
        
        # Step 3: Runtime constants (No Constant Propagation)
        sales_with_calcs = sales_with_calcs.withColumn(
            "commission_estimate", col("amount") * lit(0.10)
        )
        sales_with_calcs = sales_with_calcs.withColumn(
            "tax_estimate", col("amount") * lit(0.20)
        )
        
        # Step 4: Complex nested logic (No Simplification)
        sales_with_tier = sales_with_calcs.withColumn(
            "tier",
            when(col("amount") > 200000, "Platinum")
            .when(col("amount") > 100000,
                when(col("amount") > 150000, "Gold+")
                .otherwise("Gold"))
            .when(col("amount") > 50000, "Silver")
            .otherwise("Bronze")
        )
        
        # Step 5: Join with all columns (No Elimination)
        joined = sales_with_tier.join(sales_person_df, "sales_person_id")
        joined = joined.join(product_df, "category")
        
        # Step 6: Multiple separate withColumn (No Fusion)
        result = joined.withColumn("final_commission", col("amount") * lit(0.10))
        result = result.withColumn("net_amount", col("amount") - col("final_commission"))
        result = result.withColumn("tax", col("net_amount") * lit(0.20))
        result = result.withColumn("final_net", col("net_amount") - col("tax"))
        
        # Step 7: Finally select needed columns
        final = result.select(
            "sale_id", "name", "amount", "tier", 
            "final_commission", "final_net", "region"
        )
        
        return final
    
    @timing_decorator
    def optimized_complex_pipeline(self, sales_df, sales_person_df, product_df):
        """
        OPTIMIZED: Complex pipeline with ALL optimization patterns applied
        """
        print("\n=== OPTIMIZED Complex Pipeline ===")
        
        # ALL PATTERNS APPLIED:
        # 1. Elimination: Select only needed columns early, remove redundant filters
        # 2. Dead Code Elimination: No unused calculations
        # 3. Constant Propagation: Use pre-defined constants
        # 4. Simplification: Clear, simple logic
        # 5. Fusion: Single transformation chain
        
        # Pre-compute constants
        COMMISSION_RATE = 0.10
        TAX_RATE = 0.20
        NET_MULTIPLIER = 1 - COMMISSION_RATE  # Pre-computed
        FINAL_MULTIPLIER = NET_MULTIPLIER * (1 - TAX_RATE)  # Pre-computed
        
        # Select only needed columns before joins (Elimination)
        sales_selected = sales_df.select(
            "sale_id", "sales_person_id", "amount", "category"
        ).filter(col("amount") > 2000)  # Most restrictive filter only
        
        person_selected = sales_person_df.select(
            "sales_person_id", "name", "region"
        )
        
        product_selected = product_df.select("category", "margin")
        
        # Fused transformation chain with all calculations
        result = sales_selected \
            .join(person_selected, "sales_person_id") \
            .join(product_selected, "category") \
            .select(
                col("sale_id"),
                col("name"),
                col("amount"),
                col("region"),
                # Simplified tier logic
                when(col("amount") >= 200000, "Platinum")
                    .when(col("amount") >= 100000, "Gold")
                    .when(col("amount") >= 50000, "Silver")
                    .otherwise("Bronze").alias("tier"),
                # All calculations fused with pre-computed constants
                (col("amount") * COMMISSION_RATE).alias("final_commission"),
                (col("amount") * FINAL_MULTIPLIER).alias("final_net")
            )
        
        return result
    
    def run_optimization_comparison(self):
        """
        Run and compare both versions
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("COMPLEX DATA PIPELINE OPTIMIZATION COMPARISON")
        print("="*80)
        
        sales_df, sales_person_df, product_df = self.create_complex_datasets()
        
        print("\nSample Data:")
        print("\nSales:")
        sales_df.show(5)
        print("\nSales Persons:")
        sales_person_df.show()
        
        # Run unoptimized
        unopt_result = self.unoptimized_complex_pipeline(
            sales_df, sales_person_df, product_df
        )
        print("\nUnoptimized Result:")
        unopt_result.show()
        
        # Run optimized
        opt_result = self.optimized_complex_pipeline(
            sales_df, sales_person_df, product_df
        )
        print("\nOptimized Result:")
        opt_result.show()
        
        # Compare query plans
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("QUERY PLAN COMPARISON")
        print("="*80)
        
        print("\n--- UNOPTIMIZED PLAN ---")
        unopt_result.explain(mode="simple")
        
        print("\n--- OPTIMIZED PLAN ---")
        opt_result.explain(mode="simple")
        
        # Verify results match
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("VERIFICATION")
        print("="*80)
        print(f"Unoptimized row count: {unopt_result.count()}")
        print(f"Optimized row count: {opt_result.count()}")
        print(f"✓ Results match: {unopt_result.count() == opt_result.count()}")

        ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
        │ 7. TESTING & VALIDATION                                            │
        └────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
        
        □ Are optimized and unoptimized versions compared?
        □ Is performance measured before and after optimization?
        □ Are results validated to ensure correctness?
        □ Are edge cases tested?
        □ Is the optimization documented?
        
        """
        print(checklist)
    
    @staticmethod
    def analyze_dataframe(df, df_name="DataFrame"):
        """
        Analyze a DataFrame and provide optimization suggestions
        """
        print(f"\n{'='*80}")
        print(f"ANALYZING: {df_name}")
        print('='*80)
        
        # Get query plan
        plan = df._jdf.queryExecution().toString()
        
        suggestions = []
        warnings = []
        
        # Check for multiple projects
        project_count = plan.count("Project")
        if project_count > 3:
            warnings.append(
                f"⚠ Found {project_count} Project operations"
            )
            suggestions.append(
                "→ FUSION: Consider combining withColumn() calls into select()"
            )
        
        # Check for multiple filters
        filter_count = plan.count("Filter")
        if filter_count > 2:
            warnings.append(
                f"⚠ Found {filter_count} Filter operations"
            )
            suggestions.append(
                "→ FUSION/ELIMINATION: Combine filters into compound condition"
            )
        
        # Check for joins without broadcast
        if "Join" in plan and "BroadcastExchange" not in plan:
            warnings.append(
                "⚠ Join detected without broadcast"
            )
            suggestions.append(
                "→ Consider using broadcast() for small tables"
            )
        
        # Check for multiple exchanges
        exchange_count = plan.count("Exchange")
        if exchange_count > 2:
            warnings.append(
                f"⚠ Found {exchange_count} Exchange operations (shuffles)"
            )
            suggestions.append(
                "→ Review partitioning strategy to reduce shuffles"
            )
        
        # Print analysis
        if warnings:
            print("\n⚠ WARNINGS:")
            for w in warnings:
                print(f"  {w}")
        
        if suggestions:
            print("\n💡 SUGGESTIONS:")
            for s in suggestions:
                print(f"  {s}")
        
        if not warnings and not suggestions:
            print("\n✓ No obvious optimization issues detected!")
        
        return warnings, suggestions

"""
PySpark Memory Spill Patterns
=============================
This module demonstrates various memory spill patterns and optimization techniques
in Apache Spark to handle large-scale data processing efficiently.
"""

from pyspark.sql import SparkSession, DataFrame
from pyspark.sql.functions import *
from pyspark.sql.types import *

import random

# ============================================================================
# PATTERN 1: DISK SPILL PATTERN
# ============================================================================

class DiskSpillPattern:
    """
    Demonstrates how to detect, monitor, and handle disk spills in Spark.
    Disk spills occur when data doesn't fit in memory and is written to disk.
    """
    
    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):
        self.spark = spark
        
    def create_large_dataset(self, num_records: int = 10000000) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Creates a large dataset to trigger disk spills.
        
        Args:
            num_records: Number of records to generate
            
        Returns:
            DataFrame with large dataset
        """
        print(f"Creating dataset with {num_records:,} records...")
        
        # Generate data that will likely cause spills
        data = [
            (
                i,
                f"user_{i % 100000}",
                random.randint(1, 1000),
                random.random() * 10000,
                f"category_{i % 50}",
                datetime.now() - timedelta(days=random.randint(0, 365))
            )
            for i in range(num_records)
        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("user_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("product_id", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("amount", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("category", StringType(), False),
            StructField("timestamp", TimestampType(), False)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def demonstrate_disk_spill(self):
        """
        Demonstrates operations that may cause disk spills and how to monitor them.
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("DISK SPILL PATTERN DEMONSTRATION")
        print("="*80)
        
        # Create large dataset
        df = self.create_large_dataset()
        
        # Cache the dataframe - may cause spills if data doesn't fit in memory
        df.cache()
        
        # Perform operations that trigger materialization
        print("\nPerforming aggregation that may cause disk spills...")
        result = df.groupBy("user_id", "category") \
                   .agg(
                       sum("amount").alias("total_amount"),
                       count("*").alias("transaction_count"),
                       avg("amount").alias("avg_amount")
                   )
        
        # Force execution
        count = result.count()
        print(f"Result count: {count:,}")
        
        # Show sample results
        print("\nSample results:")
        result.show(10)
        
        # Unpersist to free memory
        df.unpersist()
        
        return result
    
    def configure_spill_settings(self):
        """
        Shows how to configure Spark settings to manage disk spills.
        """
        configs = {
            # Memory fraction for execution (shuffles, joins, sorts, aggregations)
            "spark.memory.fraction": "0.6",
            
            # Fraction of execution memory for storage
            "spark.memory.storageFraction": "0.5",
            
            # Threshold for spilling data to disk
            "spark.shuffle.spill.compress": "true",
            
            # Compression codec for spilled data
            "spark.io.compression.codec": "snappy",
            
            # Number of files to merge during shuffle
            "spark.shuffle.file.buffer": "32k"
        }
        
        print("\nRecommended Spill Configuration:")
        for key, value in configs.items():
            print(f"  {key} = {value}")
        
        return configs

class SortSpillPattern:
    """
    Demonstrates sort operations that can cause memory spills and optimization techniques.

    def __init__(self, spark: SparkSession):

        data = [

                random.randint(1, 1000000),

                f"group_{random.randint(1, 100)}"

        ]
        
        schema = StructType([
            StructField("sort_key", IntegerType(), False),
            StructField("record_id", StringType(), False),
            StructField("value", DoubleType(), False),
            StructField("group", StringType(), False)
        ])
        
        return self.spark.createDataFrame(data, schema)
    
    def demonstrate_sort_spill(self):
        """
        Demonstrates sort operations that may cause spills.
        """
        print("\n" + "="*80)
        print("SORT SPILL PATTERN DEMONSTRATION")
        print("="*80)
        
        df = self.create_unsorted_dataset()
        
        # Simple sort - may cause spills with large datasets
        print("\n1. Simple Sort (may cause spills):")
        sorted_df = df.orderBy("sort_key")
        print(f"   Sorted records count: {sorted_df.count():,}")
        sorted_df.show(5)
        
        # Multi-column sort - higher chance of spills
        print("\n2. Multi-column Sort:")
        multi_sorted = df.orderBy("group", "sort_key", "value")
        multi_sorted.show(5)
        
        # Sort with increased partitions to reduce spill
        print("\n3. Optimized Sort with Repartitioning:")
        optimized_sort = df.repartition(20, "group") \
                          .sortWithinPartitions("sort_key")
        optimized_sort.show(5)
        
        return optimized_sort
    
    def optimize_sort_operations(self, df: DataFrame) -> DataFrame:
        """
        Demonstrates techniques to optimize sort operations and reduce spills.
        """
        print("\n" + "-"*80)
        print("SORT OPTIMIZATION TECHNIQUES")
        print("-"*80)
        
        # Technique 1: Use sortWithinPartitions instead of global sort
        print("\n1. Using sortWithinPartitions (avoids global shuffle):")
        partitioned_sort = df.repartition(10, "group") \
                            .sortWithinPartitions("sort_key")
        
        # Technique 2: Use sampling for approximate sorting
        print("\n2. Sampling-based sort optimization:")
        # Increase shuffle partitions for better parallelism
        self.spark.conf.set("spark.sql.shuffle.partitions", "200")
        
        # Technique 3: Range partitioning for pre-sorted data
        print("\n3. Range partitioning:")
        range_partitioned = df.repartitionByRange(20, "sort_key")
        
        return partitioned_sort
    
    def window_function_sort_spill(self, df: DataFrame):
        """
        Demonstrates sort spills in window functions and optimizations.
        """
        print("\n" + "-"*80)
        print("WINDOW FUNCTION SORT OPTIMIZATION")
        print("-"*80)
        
        # Window function that requires sorting - can cause spills
        window_spec = Window.partitionBy("group").orderBy("sort_key")
        
        result = df.withColumn("row_num", row_number().over(window_spec)) \
                   .withColumn("rank", rank().over(window_spec)) \
                   .withColumn("running_total", sum("value").over(window_spec))
        
        print("\nWindow function results:")
        result.show(10)
        
        return result
